ideas.title: Verified send-to-session primitive
ideas.what_user_gets: One safe path that puts text into a running Claude session only when Loom knows it is at an idle prompt, and reports the true outcome (queued, pasted, delivered, outcome unknown). It is the shared foundation for queued prompts, the composer, review comments, canned PR/CI actions, side-answer hand-back and any later cross-session send, and it removes the 'switch to the terminal, paste, hope it was not a permission dialog' step.
ideas.mechanisms: 1) [PTY; TUI input is undocumented but Loom owns the PTY] State-gated bracketed paste with ONE writer per session (Superset serializes sends so a delayed Enter cannot submit another send's text). Refuse in Needs approval or any modal (permission prompt, picker, /resume menu). Offer 'draft only' (paste without Enter) as the zero-risk mode. Confirm delivery with the documented UserPromptSubmit hook; states queued / pasted / delivered (prompt observed) / outcome unknown; never retry blindly. Practical details from Orca: Claude needs a TYPED lead line before the bracketed paste (pasteNeedsTypedRequest), Enter goes in a separate write after a delay (Orca main path ~500 ms plus a size term; the 50 ms figure is only its renderer note path), and sanitize invisible Unicode yourself because Claude strips it on Enter and then sends nothing (leaves a draft). 2) [documented, complement] hook additionalContext at the next prompt/tool boundary/Stop for 'attach to the next turn' when busy; does nothing for an idle session so cannot be the only path. 3) [documented but young: mods 2.1.287+, API churn, unsandboxed, blockable by org policy] a Loom mod calling $.prompt.submit({text, asUser:true}) once idle, as an optional runtime-detected upgrade. 4) [pull-at-skill] paste a short constant slash command (e.g. /loom:review) and let the skill pull content from Loom's socket with !`cmd` (needs allowed-tools pre-approval; fails if disableSkillShellExecution or org policy). 5) [undocumented, avoid] hidden `claude --prefill` flag (absent from docs, launch-time only, same code path had an RCE fixed in 2.1.118).
ideas.debates: Fact-checks: 'exact hash verification' is overstated (hook prompt has pastes expanded or wrapped in <pasted_content id=...>, invisible chars removed; need normalization or a marker, and Loom does not retain prompt text); Orca's turn-start verifier is NOT used on its diff-note path (two terminal.send calls with status gating), and Orca removes delivered notes while its docs say the opposite; herdr's agent_blocked guard only fires when its scraper already classified the pane and its 5 s effect gate runs after the keystrokes are sent; issue #15553 is a feature request and its failing examples are slash commands (/clear, /model) swallowed by autocomplete, which weakens the 'short constant slash command sidesteps paste quirks' argument. Orca's blind write after timeout (onUnconfirmedDelivery) is the part not to copy. review-git-loop recommends pull-at-skill as default and PTY paste as fallback; the product reports mostly propose gated paste. Contract tension is minimal (input aid, not a UI replacement).

ideas.title: Per-session prompt queue with verified delivery
ideas.what_user_gets: Line up the next instruction(s) for a session you are not looking at (or that is still working) in a small strip above the terminal; edit, reorder, 'send now'; Loom delivers when the hooks say the session is Ready and shows queued -> delivered -> failed. Also a global quick-capture hotkey that picks a session and queues text. Removes the wait-then-retype loop across 3-5 sessions, and is the safe user-authorized core of any later cross-session send.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest: Loom-owned persisted queue (small file per session; several ordered items, not one slot) delivered by the Working->Ready/Stop hook event through I-01, marked delivered only when UserPromptSubmit shows the text; cancel or ask when the user types in the terminal meanwhile; refuse delivery into Needs approval; dropped or restored as drafts on Quit and said so (no daemon). Add an unsent-draft marker on the card (Conductor). Documented CLI behaviour to know: typed input already queues while Claude works, and Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+X Ctrl+S (chat:sendNow, v2.1.275+) sends queued messages now (moves backgroundable work to background since 2.1.281). Loom's added value is cross-session/offscreen queuing and editing.
ideas.debates: Overlap with the CLI's own queue. Competitor queues are a bug magnet: OpenChamber 2.3.0 hidden/out-of-order delivery, Vibe Kanban 'never fires, draft not cleared, single slot, lost on restart' (thinly sourced: #3416 has one top-level comment), Paseo's queue is memory-only. Conductor removed the queue setting in 0.86 but kept a 'waiting until Claude reads it' pending state (concept not gone). Needs captured-transcript tests for ordering and Escape/interrupt interplay.

ideas.title: Native composer overlay with per-session drafts and delivery receipt
ideas.what_user_gets: A native multi-line editor (shortcut) for long structured prompts: @file completion from the session cwd, pasted images saved to a file and referenced by path, a draft per session, optional auto-open when a session finishes. The card says 'submitted' only when the hook arrives, else 'not submitted yet, press Enter' with the draft kept.
ideas.mechanisms: NSTextView overlay that exists only while open; plain text only; send = I-01 (bracketed paste + separate Enter); drafts in memory, optionally persisted on quit; never opens or sends while Needs approval; receipt from UserPromptSubmit within a window, never auto-retry Enter. Image paste = file path (clipboard + Ctrl+V into the TUI is hacky). Warp auto-opens its rich input on InProgress/Success/Failed/Cancelled and closes it on Blocked.
ideas.debates: Contract tension: the user's rule that the terminal is never replaced; the overlay loses CLI vim mode and slash-command completion, so keep it optional. Claude input changes (mode-switch prefixes ! and &, paste-burst heuristics) forced Warp special cases. power-user-workflows lists 'a custom composer that replaces the CLI prompt' under do-not-build; this is the lighter helper variant. Confirmation timeout can false-alarm on slow hooks (UserPromptSubmit default timeout 30 s).

ideas.title: Input fidelity audit (image paste, drag-drop paths, dictation)
ideas.what_user_gets: Invisible correctness work: screenshots and files dropped or pasted into a Loom terminal reach Claude correctly; macOS system dictation works in the terminal and composer; no voice stack needed.
ideas.mechanisms: Audit-only first: check image paste, Finder drag-drop path quoting, dictation insertion and large-paste behaviour in the SwiftTerm view. System dictation instead of a hosted voice dependency (Happy's voice agent costs about $0.01/min via ElevenLabs and a hosted dependency).
ideas.debates: Low controversy. Whether Loom already handles all of it is unknown (reports did not read Loom code); treat as a check, not a build.

ideas.title: Read-only conversation view of the SAME session (chat-looking transcript, no new engine)
ideas.what_user_gets: A 'Conversation' tab or panel that renders Claude's own transcript as readable turns (markdown, tool calls folded per turn with expandable rows, diffs, questions), next to the terminal. Ended, stopped and idle records become readable and searchable without a live terminal or process, replacing the static ended-screen snapshot; it is the first safe step toward a chat-centred UI and the base for side chat, right panel and search.
ideas.mechanisms: Extend the existing read-only subagent transcript panel to the main session. Incremental FSEvents tail by byte offset + inode (already how Usage reads), bounded cold open (T3: about 75 rows / 1 MiB), windowed/virtualized rows, raw tool bodies loaded only when a row is expanded, render nothing when hidden, never mount all history (OpenChamber lesson), 'latest N steps' while a turn runs. [Transcript JSONL is CLI-internal per SDK typings: lenient decoder, unknown records shown as raw collapsed blocks, recorded fixtures per CLI version, drift detection, fall back to the terminal.] Final text of a turn should come from the Stop hook's last_assistant_message (documented) because transcript_path is written asynchronously and can lag. Order by hook timestamps + transcript sequence, not insertion time. Sending from an ended view = resume the real CLI session.
ideas.debates: Every chat proposal in the research starts here; chat-ui-paths ranks it A1, cheapest big win with zero billing/ownership risk; power-user-workflows calls it the safest chat-UI step. Debate is about WHEN (power-user says only after measuring) and how far a live session goes. Transcript lag means partial streaming output is unavailable (use 'last complete message'). Cost depends on a lenient decoder; Ghostex spends about 5.2k lines of Rust on Claude alone, Conductor/T3/Orca show ordering and scroll polish absorbs effort. Contract rule about never replacing the CLI is kept because it is a view.

ideas.title: Chat lens with composer over the live PTY (terminal and chat as two views of one process)
ideas.what_user_gets: Toggle Terminal <-> Chat on the same live session: rendered markdown, collapsed tool calls, approvals as cards, a real multi-line composer, history, Esc to interrupt; the real CLI (slash commands, skills, MCP, hooks, subagents, resume) stays authoritative and one click away. Gives the chat-centred feel the user is now open to without an SDK.
ideas.mechanisms: I-05 for reading, plus a composer that writes through I-01 (bracketed paste + submit) and enabled only in Ready/Idle; disabled in permission prompts, pickers and slash dialogs; Esc sends an interrupt; approvals and questions via documented hooks (I-15/I-16). Reject screen-scraping of dialogs (Ghostex-style: ~5.2k lines, comments pinned to CLI versions 2.1.268/2.1.280/2.1.284). chat-ui-paths 'A2' = acceptable only for a bounded subset (plain-text send, approve/deny, AskUserQuestion).
ideas.debates: Strongest convergence for 'chat but keep the real CLI'. Risks named by all: two input surfaces ('which has focus'), composer text lost or misdelivered when the TUI is modal, transcript lag for partial output, mode disagreement (plan/permission/dialog). Orca's two-architecture split (terminal + structured chat) is the cautionary tale; Agent of Empires (structured view is DEFAULT, ACP-based, tmux terminal) is not evidence for a stop-and-resume pattern. Ghostex README: raw CLI one hotkey away and your draft comes with you.

ideas.title: Optional 'Chat mode': Loom-owned stream-json child per session (no Node, SDK or ACP)
ideas.what_user_gets: A true structured chat session with typed events, authoritative state, tool/permission cards and side questions, chosen per session as an explicit mode, with the PTY as default and fallback. Mode switch = stop plus --resume; exactly one process owns a session id.
ideas.mechanisms: [Semi-documented] `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --replay-user-messages --permission-prompts host|none (2.1.259+) --include-hook-events --fork-session ...`; wire protocol typed only in the published SDK typings (about 38-40 control request subtypes; system/init carries `capabilities` for feature detection; unknown types pass through). Loom already sends one get_usage control_request this way (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudePlanLimits.swift), but only as a short-lived probe: no session-lifecycle code exists to reuse. Status: session_state_changed is OPT-IN via CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1 (not on by default). Side questions via the undocumented `side_question` control request (shape unknown, needs a recorded capture). Alternatives: documented `defer` PreToolUse flow; request_user_dialog for tool dialogs.
ideas.debates: Only chat-ui-paths proposes it; Conductor, T3, Zed, Paseo, Emdash and Orca all pay for SDK/ACP-class approaches (feature lag, pinned CLIs, billing exposure, plus adapter trees). Billing: support article 15036540 (Oct 7 2026) says -p/SDK/third-party apps still draw subscription limits; the May 13 metering change was paused June 15 'for now'; April 4 policy said it 'applies to all third-party harnesses'; the legal page says products using the Agent SDK should use API keys and allows the unmodified binary with the user's own login, so headless is where policy moved four times in ten months. Corrections: 230-260 MB is a parked spare's floor, not a measured chat-process cost; AoE is not a 'stop plus --resume' precedent; --bare is recommended for scripts and may become -p's default (skips OAuth, hooks, skills, MCP); plain -p runs project hooks and .mcp.json without a trust dialog; sdk-cli entrypoint sessions are hidden from terminal /resume. User question open: does Chat mode REPLACE the terminal in daily use (then needs parity) or is it a convenience view (then I-05 + I-09 may suffice)? Defer until I-05 proves use.

ideas.title: /btw side-question shortcut (lightest side chat)
ideas.what_user_gets: One key (e.g. Cmd+;) that focuses the composer and inserts the CLI's own /btw flow: a one-shot question with the full conversation as context, no tools, nothing written to the main thread, works while the main turn is running, cache-cheap.
ideas.mechanisms: [Documented in interactive-mode docs] /btw replays the newest 20 exchanges, no tool access, never enters history, terminal keeps it in memory, available mid-turn, 'f' forks it to a background subagent. Loom only binds the shortcut, types '/btw ' into the focused composer when the prompt is empty/idle, and keeps the overlay readable. Even lighter: no shortcut, just document it.
ideas.debates: chat-ui-paths rejects 'type /btw into the PTY' (SC3) because Loom gets no structured answer (overlay only, screen scraping to capture) and holds it as inferior to a Loom-owned fork; the other six reports treat it as the free step 1. Unverified: whether /btw writes to the JSONL or registry on disk. SubagentStop fires for Claude's internal agents including /btw side questions (hooks doc), so the subagent tracker must ignore those. /btw persists in the VS Code panel but not in the terminal or Desktop side chat. Cursor's 'side chat' also uses /btw as an alias but is a durable child conversation, a different behaviour.

ideas.title: Side chat as a forked real CLI session (the user's ChatGPT-style side thread)
ideas.what_user_gets: Ask about the current work without polluting or blocking the main thread: a child of the parent card (nested like subagents, hidden from the normal list), seeded with the parent's context, multi-turn, with 'promote to normal session', 'bring the answer back' (a user click pastes a summary into the main prompt) and 'discard' (verified deletion). Closed = nothing running.
ideas.mechanisms: 1) [Documented flags; verified in `claude --help` 2.1.300: --resume, --fork-session] A second Loom-owned PTY running `claude --resume <id> --fork-session` in its own run scope, started only on demand and stopped when the panel closes or the parent ends; ended-screen/transcript view when closed; feature-detect the flag and degrade with a drift notice. Fork from the last COMPLETED turn (T3, OpenChamber, Codex: a fork only sees what is flushed). Prefix the first message with a boundary instruction (OpenChamber BTW_BOUNDARY: inherited history is reference only, no subagents, no file changes unless asked; Codex SIDE_BOUNDARY_PROMPT) and default to plan/read-only permission mode or a restricted tool allowlist (Loom's own design; Codex enforces only at prompt level and permits user-requested mutation). Mark lineage in Loom's own store. 2) [headless variant, needs I-05/I-07 renderer] `claude -p --resume <id> --fork-session` with --permission-prompts none; deleted on close; forks are tagged programmatic so they stay out of /resume. 3) [undocumented] side_question control request on a Chat-mode process, feature-detected, falling back to 2. 4) Reject: copying the JSONL under a new id (Happy's forkSession) breaks on schema change.
ideas.debates: Highest-convergence idea AND the user's long-standing wish. Debates: PTY child (cheap, honest, no billing exposure, terminal UI) vs headless fork rendered in a chat panel (better look, multi-turn with read-only tools, billing exposure and needs a renderer); persistent child (Codex users ask for persistence, #26227; Cursor durable child) vs ephemeral (Desktop side chat is unsaved, Codex /side is ephemeral). Experiments chat-ui-paths wants before committing: does --fork-session work while the parent is mid-turn in another process; combine with --no-session-persistence; does the fork reuse the parent's prompt cache (cache_read_input_tokens); what junk is left under ~/.claude/projects for the deletion path to clean. Costs: a fork re-reads the full context (tokens, cache), double usage while both run; usage must be tagged to avoid double-counting; fork pollutes the registry and `claude --resume` lists unless grouped under the parent and cleaned by Loom's verified permanent delete; shares the working tree so only guidance or tool limits keep it read-only; do not fork mid-approval; users may expect the answer to flow back (it will not). T3's side chat is only an open PR (#18243), not shipped; OpenChamber #3755 (/btw fork inherited an active goal) is reported on 1.24.2 and likely mitigated, but shows metadata must be stripped. Fork-from-an-earlier-prompt (Happy) belongs here only if a documented CLI option exists; otherwise skip.

ideas.title: Right-hand context panel (subagents, side chat, changes, notes)
ideas.what_user_gets: A collapsible right panel (the user's long-standing wish) that hosts the secondary threads of the selected session: subagents/subtasks, the side chat, later Changes and an agent note. Nothing is drawn or watched when it is collapsed; closing a tab stops what it owns.
ideas.mechanisms: Shell first (M): a per-window collapsible pane with tabs, one owner process per tab, lifetime = panel open. T3 puts side chat in a right-panel tab sharing the composer (Esc returns to main), OpenChamber uses a slide-over above the composer collapsible to a chip, Paseo/Codex use a right-hand pane, Zed a side panel. Lighter alternative that needs no new rail: reuse Loom's existing 'click a subagent = read-only live transcript in place of the terminal' pattern and let a side-chat child open the same way. Collapsed panel must still surface a pending approval of the parent (OpenChamber v2.4.0 fix for a parent stuck on an unseen request).
ideas.debates: Standing decision D-34 (no left rail; right sidebar deferred, 'ideas such as a side chat come later') must be revisited with the user. In-place vs side-by-side is a UX decision; a side panel competes for width on a laptop and with the terminal's column count. No report measured the panel's idle cost; the design rule is that an unopened panel costs nothing.

ideas.title: Subagent tree upgrades (who is asking, per-subagent cost, no stuck 'running')
ideas.what_user_gets: Attribute a 'waiting for you' state and its approval box to the specific subagent that asked, show per-subagent tokens/tool counts/context, and guarantee finished subagents never stay 'running'.
ideas.mechanisms: Add agent id/type from hook payloads on PreToolUse/permission events if present (unverified for the interactive CLI; degrade to session-level state); optional subagentStatusLine for per-subagent tokens/context (documented; agentType needs 2.1.293+; needs the I-24 bridge); fixtures from claude-hud's agent-tracking bug history (background agents whose completion appears only as a queue-operation enqueue or queued_command attachment, notices with <task-id> but no <tool-use-id>, forked/resumed sessions, usage logged several times per response). Do not promise per-subagent Stop: ACP does it via SDK Query.stopTask and no safe TUI equivalent is confirmed.
ideas.debates: Hook fields for agent identity are unverified for the current CLI (the ACP adapter gets agentID from canUseTool, not necessarily hooks). Needs real transcripts of forked/resumed background-agent sessions that the explorer did not have. SubagentStop also fires for internal agents (prompt suggestions, /btw).

ideas.title: Status accuracy hardening and 'Why this status?'
ideas.what_user_gets: Fewer wrong dots on the cards the user trusts all day: a session with background work or running subagents never shows Finished/Idle; Failed is not silently downgraded; resume, /clear and compaction never show Finished unviewed; an interrupt does not leave Working stuck; and a pill popover (and `loom status --explain`) says which signal produced the state, when, and what it replaced.
ideas.mechanisms: Mostly an audit plus tests of Loom's transition table (reports did not read Loom code, so some cases may already be covered): (a) Stop/SubagentStop hook input has background_tasks (shell/subagent/monitor/workflow) and session_crons (documented in hooks reference; since 2.1.145): derive 'Waiting on background work' with elapsed time instead of Finished; keep a per-session set of unfinished background launch ids, no transcript rescan; (b) bind every hook event to session id + launch identity, ignore nested/foreign sessions that inherit env, keep the hook tiny and a no-op outside Loom (Superset #8120/#8131/#8245/#6243); (c) sticky Failed (Supacode: Notification after Stop-on-error must not downgrade it), compaction (PreCompact -> SessionStart source=compact) as Working, use the documented notification_type (permission_prompt only after ~6 s, idle_prompt ~60 s after finishing; PermissionRequest is the immediate signal) and never treat idle_prompt as 'needs you'; (d) 'Interrupted' state: Stop does not fire on user interrupt and there is no interrupt event (documented), so after Loom writes Esc/Ctrl-C into a Working session and no hook arrives within a short window mark Interrupted until the next UserPromptSubmit, one-shot timer only; (e) completion/state-change sequence guards so restore/resume never counts as a completion (herdr completion_seq), reconcile stale Working at launch from the registry + PID check (Paseo); (f) store the last transition reason (signal, time, previous state) and show it behind a pill click; surface unknown values as drift evidence. Regression tests with exact hook sequences.
ideas.debates: Corrections: Warp does NOT synthesize Cancelled on a local Ctrl-C (only for shared-session/Remote Control viewer writes), so Warp is not precedent for the local case, but the gap is real; cmux #14308 (idle_prompt -> needs-input) and #13024 are historical, at HEAD idle_prompt becomes an idleReminder and is suppressed for completed/background-pending sessions; Orca needs dozens of background-task/child-work tracker files, showing how much state logic this takes. herdr itself moved away from hook-driven state for Claude (stale blocked states, hook removals in users' settings) toward identity-only hooks plus screen manifests, so hook hygiene matters. A Ctrl-C can also just dismiss input, so require Working and no later event; the ~2 s window is a heuristic to tune. Hook field names should be verified against the installed CLI through drift detection.

ideas.title: Receive OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol) as a second in-band state source
ideas.what_user_gets: Faster, more truthful 'which session needs me' with the reason (auth / question / permission) and message text on the card, plus coverage for cases hooks miss (auth expiry, hooks disabled or silent), with no scraping.
ideas.mechanisms: [Documented in Claude Code terminal-config docs, 2.1.295+, nothing to enable] In the vendored SwiftTerm answer the `ESC ] 7501 ; ?` probe so Claude starts reporting, parse state/kind/msg/progress/id per PTY, feed as a cross-check next to hooks and the registry. Hooks stay authoritative for identity and transitions (7501 has no session id, no /clear or /resume continuity); disagreement is drift evidence, a missing report after an answered probe is one more drift signal. Mitchell Hashimoto's spec (2026-10-06), at revision 0.4 (a draft).
ideas.debates: tmux, background sessions (even attached) and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 send nothing; the probe order and the 'programStatus=no' debug line are user-reported (#101114), not documented; the lifetime rule 'new prompt' means a new SHELL prompt (OSC 133 A), irrelevant to a PTY running claude directly; whether Claude emits ids for subagents is unverified. Receivers disagree on precedence (some let live 7501 override hooks, tuios ranks hooks higher), which supports 'hooks authoritative, 7501 cross-check'. `done` must be mapped carefully to Finished unviewed.

ideas.title: Richer card content: what it is asking / last said, peek, agent note, title precedence, notification text
ideas.what_user_gets: The sidebar and notifications answer 'does this need me, and for what' without opening the session: a one-line 'asking / last said' under the title, a peek popover (last message, question or final summary), an optional agent-reported note ('reproduced bug; testing fix'), a stable human title, and notifications whose body is the outcome or approval summary plus branch.
ideas.mechanisms: (a) 'Last said' from the Stop hook's last_assistant_message and the Notification message (both documented; Supacode caps about 1000 bytes, Warp about 200 chars), no transcript read; truncate hard, treat as untrusted text, respect a title-only privacy toggle for the lock screen; delete/update the notification when the session resumes, cap simultaneous toasts. (b) Peek = same text in a popover, read-only. (c) Agent-set note: the session updates one line through Loom's authenticated socket and loom skill (Orca `worktree set --comment`), shown with 'agent-reported' styling, capped, rate-limited, cleared on a new prompt, never used as status truth; ship the skill as a thin stub that asks the app for version-matched instructions. (d) Title precedence: user rename in Loom > Claude's own name (/rename or --name) > first/latest prompt; never let a hook or approval summary overwrite a user name (Warp's most repeated complaints); where Claude stores /rename is unknown (read incrementally, treat as drift). (e) One-sentence reason on each approval box (tool + path), from hook payload.
ideas.debates: cmux also runs an async auto-name hook on Stop (timeout 120, may run a summarizer): a model-call cost Loom would not want by default. Privacy: prompt/approval text on a locked screen. Prompt injection via agent-written notes is not a new vector but should be bounded.

ideas.title: Answer approvals from Loom's own surfaces via the documented hook decision
ideas.what_user_gets: Allow / Deny (and later pick-an-option) directly from the approval box, the menu-bar popover, the notification buttons or a hotkey, without switching to the session: one fewer context switch per approval with 3-6 parallel sessions. Verified outcome = the CLI continues.
ideas.mechanisms: [Documented] A per-session PermissionRequest hook injected with `claude --settings <inline JSON>` (or the existing Loom plugin), never the user's global settings.json, blocking on Loom's authenticated socket; the approval box, popover and notification resolve the same (session id, request id, kind); stale actions are discarded and logged; fail open if Loom is gone; advisory soft-wait (cmux 120 s) then hand back to the CLI prompt with a visible 'handed back' state; cancel the card on PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd/PID exit (kernel process-exit events, no polling). Keep 'Always' and 'Bypass' out of banners; notification actions = UNNotificationAction (banner must be expanded; Focus modes delay) and an optional Carbon global hotkey bound to the single visible request. Enter/Esc keyboard approve/decline on a focused box plus a per-turn approvals counter (Codex) to hint when to change permission mode. Do not answer by injecting keystrokes (fragile, layout-dependent).
ideas.debates: Unverified for interactive sessions: whether the TUI dialog and the hook race or the hook runs first, and whether answering in the terminal cancels the pending hook (one Vibe Island report says it does not, but the reporter also blamed the app's own self-healing; chat-ui-paths lists it as open question #3, decisive for safety). Hook timeouts differ (command/http/mcp_tool default 600 s, UserPromptSubmit 30 s, SessionEnd 1.5 s). Auto mode is now the starting permission mode for interactive sessions (2.1.283+), so approvals are rarer than the '93% rubber-stamped' framing suggests: re-weigh the value. CodeIsland idled about 5.3% CPU even after gating its animations, and Open Island #377 (kernel exit) and #517 are unmerged proposals. Channels (research preview) permission relay is the cleanest future input path to watch.

ideas.title: Rich approval content: real preview, question card, plan review panel
ideas.what_user_gets: Approve confidently without opening files or scrolling: the full Bash command, Edit/MultiEdit as a unified diff from old/new strings, Write as head + size, MCP as server + args; a card for AskUserQuestion (1-4 questions, single/multi-select, free text); and a rendered plan with Approve / Revise-with-feedback for ExitPlanMode. Always with 'answer in the terminal' as fallback.
ideas.mechanisms: (a) Preview purely from the hook payload already in memory, size-capped with 'show more', rendered only when visible; a lazy file read for true line numbers later. (b) AskUserQuestion: PreToolUse allow + updatedInput {questions echoed, answers keyed by exact question text} (documented, but framed for -p/permission-host flows; the interactive case is an inference). CC 2.1.300 validates updatedInput: unknown keys are dropped and input the tool rejects denies the call, so a schema slip denies instead of crashing. Pick one hook form (PreToolUse vs PermissionRequest; CodeIsland uses the undocumented PermissionRequest form, Notchi implements both) and pin it with a live-captured contract test. Documented headless alternative: `defer`. (c) ExitPlanMode is a tool name matched under PreToolUse/PostToolUse (not a separate event); plan and planFilePath are injected into tool_input; Revise = deny + message is unverified (does deny keep the CLI in plan mode?).
ideas.debates: Only one commercial product (Vibe Island, closed) ships plan review, so reception is unproven. Duplicating Claude's permission policy is a drift trap (Happy lesson): relay the CLI's own prompt. Diff without file context shows only the replaced fragment. Depends on I-15's request/response channel.

ideas.title: Attention-routing polish (ordering, roll-up, read/unread, Dock/menu bar, quit dialog, presence policy)
ideas.what_user_gets: Triage rather than hunting: a severity-ordered Active section, a roll-up on collapsed projects, a trustworthy unread model, a Dock menu and menu-bar list of what needs you, a Quit dialog that lists Working sessions (Quit stops all of them), and notifications that stay quiet when you are already looking.
ideas.mechanisms: All derived from state Loom has, one reducer for sidebar, badge, Dock and menu bar so counts cannot disagree (Cursor's badge bugs 3.22/3.23). (a) Order Active by severity (error > needs approval > finished unviewed > working) then waiting-since, keep a hovered/selected row stable and re-sort on the next state change; collapsed project row shows roll-up priority needs-you > failed > working > finished-unviewed and a muted '+2 need you' line. (b) 'Viewed' clears only when the pane is visible AND focused; Mark unread (Cmd+Shift+U), Clear all unread (Shift+Esc), Cmd+J also cycling Finished-unviewed, per-turn unviewed list; compare-before-write read marks. (c) Dock icon menu built on demand listing needs-approval and unread sessions; menu-bar list blocked-first with 'N more', badge counting only what the list shows; Quit dialog that lists Working sessions and lets you jump instead of quitting, no delay when nothing runs. (d) Presence-aware policy: suppress sound/notification when the session is selected, the window is key and the screen unlocked; mute on lock/screensaver (distributed notifications); optional quiet hours and focus mode; a reminder ladder (approvals up to 3 nudges, finishes once) via one-shot timers that exist only while something is pending; approvals exempt from throttling.
ideas.debates: Cursor's Dock/menu-bar lists show UNREAD (finished) agents only, not needs-approval; the yellow dot is for cloud subagents, so Cursor is a weaker precedent than the report claimed; Loom can do better. Notifications: Hashimoto turns them off, Cherny relies on them (fact-check: single-agent vs multi-agent regimes, not a doctrine conflict). Supacode counts idle agents in its hoist (over-broad membership) and orders alphabetically (its visible weakness). Rows jumping under the cursor; each suppression rule can hide a real alert. Much of this may already exist in Loom (check first); a separate mailbox probably duplicates the Active section.

ideas.title: Park / snooze / In-work: user-owned lifecycle flags for sessions
ideas.what_user_gets: A cheap, reversible 'I am done with this for now' (Park, optionally snooze until a time or until the plan limit resets) and an explicit 'In work' list of sessions you are still responsible for, so the Active list equals 'things that need or may need me'. 5-second Undo toast; 'park and go to the next session needing me'.
ideas.mechanisms: Loom-owned metadata only (pinned, parked, snoozed-until, work=open|done), a Parked shelf in the activity view; snooze-until-limit reuses the reset time from get_usage; auto-settle by age evaluated lazily when the sidebar is shown or by one one-shot timer to the next due time, never for a session with a pending approval, running subagent or live process (T3 isAutoSettlementCandidate checklist). OpenChamber 'In work': a sent message only opens, only the user closes (Done is one click/key), a message newer than doneAt reopens, a section above Active; define precedence so a session is listed once; no classifier ('looks done' hint costs a model call per turn).
ideas.debates: T3's docs say pinning does not prevent automatic settlement while the code excludes pinned threads (docs and code disagree). OpenChamber had to fix a pinned session appearing twice (v2.4.0). Two overlapping lists (Active vs In work) can confuse; skip PR-merge auto-settle until Loom knows PR state (I-31). Useful for the user's two work projects with many half-finished tickets.

ideas.title: Idle auto-park (hibernate): stop the process, keep the card, resume on open
ideas.what_user_gets: Directly serves the wish 'sessions that cost nothing when idle': after N minutes of true idleness a session's process is verifiably stopped while the card, ended-screen snapshot and resume handle stay; opening it resumes the same conversation. Ten open sessions stop being ten live Claude processes.
ideas.mechanisms: Manual 'Sleep' action first (cmux request #9873), then opt-in auto-park. Eligibility checklist (Orca/cmux/Conductor): Finished/Idle, not visible, untouched, no unsent input, no running subagents, no unfinished background tasks/monitors/wakeups, no pending approval, no unsettled orchestration. Trigger from state-change events plus ONE one-shot timer per idle session (no repeating ticker); mark 'Parked' only after the run scope's process group is verifiably gone; resume with `--resume <id>` and the ended screen shown meanwhile; make the window cache-aware (about one prompt-cache TTL, 5 min / 1 h) and show 'cache cold' as information. Variant B (Supacode): free only the RENDERER/scrollback of hidden-but-working sessions under memory pressure (DispatchSource), recency-exempt the last 3; needs a retained screen model and Supacode needed a per-dormant reader thread (about 5 wakeups/s).
ideas.debates: Convergent: Orca hibernation is experimental/off by default, 30 min default (1 min-24 h), eligibility includes no live subagent roster; Claude's own supervisor stops idle unattached sessions after about an hour; Supacode's is Beta but ON by default (5 min grace, keep 3). Corrections: cmux hibernation is NOT an idle timer, it evicts the oldest idle background agents only when live restorable terminals exceed maxLiveTerminals (12), off by default, so 'idle N minutes then park' is Loom's own design; Orca's resume is 'the same resume flags' (inference: --resume). Risks: Conductor shipped bugs where background tasks and long workflows were killed on idle; cold resume (cache loss, plus 200K+ conversations get idle-compacted at about 54 min since 2.1.299, idleCompaction setting 2.1.290+) can cost more than the RAM saved for short gaps; resume can fail after CLI updates; users surprised by a parked working-looking card.

ideas.title: Keep the Mac awake while a session is Working
ideas.what_user_gets: Long runs (tests, multi-agent workflows) survive idle sleep and screen lock without a side-terminal `caffeinate`; Off / While working / Always, with a small indicator and release on the last Finished.
ideas.mechanisms: One IOKit PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertion taken on the first Working transition and released when none remain (not during Needs approval, matching Zed), tied to the hook-silence watchdog so a stale Working expires the lease (Orca uses a stale-timeout lease); indicator in footer/menu bar; display sleep still allowed; release on Quit/crash is automatic; default off or only on power.
ideas.debates: Easiest high-convergence win; Conductor's setting went from experimental (0.50) to General (0.51). Risks: battery drain if status is falsely Working, clamshell/closed-lid limits, managed Macs. Relevant documented signals: quota_auto_resume_fired/stale/disabled Notification types (v2.1.234+) mean a 'Working' state may really be a quota wait, and after sleeping >30 min across the reset Claude waits for Enter; Desktop sessions survive sleep only while the process survives.

ideas.title: Crash-safe state and 'Resume interrupted' after Quit or crash
ideas.what_user_gets: A reboot, crash or update never loses the layout or the resume handles; after a Quit or crash a one-click 'Resume interrupted' (or resume-all) reopens the sessions that were mid-work.
ideas.mechanisms: Atomic state writes, a few rolling snapshots (about 15-minute throttle), back up an unreadable state file before overwriting, persist on NSWorkspace will-power-off; mark sessions 'interrupted' (not Failed) when the previous run ended by Quit/crash; validate saved resume references against Claude's own registry on restore instead of trusting them (herdr bugs #5261, #5348 show stale/missing references). Keep any pane screen history opt-in and out of scope (secrets).
ideas.debates: Honours the contract (Quit stops everything, verified) while softening its cost; persistence-remote-orchestration ranks it option A of 'keep the contract, add cheap resilience'. Low risk; part may already exist in Loom.

ideas.title: Claude supervisor integration: 'Background' visibility lane, then optional 'Run detached'
ideas.what_user_gets: Sessions started elsewhere (terminal, Desktop, agent view) become visible in Loom's list and openable; later, an explicit per-session 'Run detached' so a long turn survives a Loom Quit and costs nothing when idle, using Anthropic's supervisor instead of a Loom daemon.
ideas.mechanisms: 1) [Documented 'supported way to read session state'] Visibility only: `claude agents --json --all` on window focus, after a hook event or manual refresh (never on a timer; the doc itself says poll, there is no push); fields state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, status busy|waiting|idle, waitingFor enum, kind interactive|background; open with `claude attach <id>` inside a Loom PTY; Loom stops only what Loom launched; dedupe Loom's own interactive rows by sessionId/pid. 2) Later `claude --bg --name ...` as a third, explicitly labelled process class hosted by the supervisor (PPID 1; idle unattached sessions stopped after about an hour; `claude daemon status|logs|stop`; isolated worktree under .claude/worktrees when dispatched from agent view or --bg, which changes cwd/branch; a machine restart stops background sessions). 3) If ever built, Supacode's two-button Quit dialog (Quit / Quit and Terminate Sessions) with an orphan sweep.
ideas.debates: The biggest philosophical decision in the research. Conflicts with 'Quit stops all sessions', process ownership and 'no polling'. Loom currently disables the supervisor with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1 (Sources/LoomCore/ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:147), and the env-vars page says that variable disables the on-demand supervisor itself; supervisor state is per CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Anthropic's own daemon bugs are open: #87891 (64 leaked processes, 7.1 GB after six weeks), #65051, #88307 (symlinked settings.json deleted), #98208 (TCC re-prompts), #66402. persistence-remote-orchestration: run Option B only as a clearly labelled spike (hooks, env identity via --settings env, session ids, run-scope capture must all behave) and keep a Loom-owned PTY host (Option C) skipped. Agent view's Delete discards the worktree including uncommitted changes (second delete drops commits). agent_needs_input/agent_completed hooks fire only while agent view is open in a terminal. Haiku-class row summaries are extra billed requests. Agent view criticisms 'no project filter / no branch status' are stale (--cwd, PR/CI labels exist).

ideas.title: Per-session context meter on cards and header
ideas.what_user_gets: See which of five sessions is near its context limit (and about to compact) without switching to it and typing /context; a thin bar or number that only appears from about 50% and turns amber at 70, red at 85; optional 'compact' or 'new session from summary' hint (user-triggered, never automatic).
ideas.mechanisms: Transcript-derived, from the incremental reader Loom already has: tokens = input + cache_creation + cache_read of the last main-chain assistant record (max per message id; sidechain/subagents separate), reset from compact_boundary.postTokens, labelled 'approx'. Window size (200k vs 1M) is not reliably in the transcript: show tokens only when unsure (heuristic: assume 1M once any record exceeds 200k, or parse the model suffix; unverified). Exact variant via the I-24 statusLine bridge.
ideas.debates: Mismatch with /context is the top complaint of the tools doing this (ccstatusline #109, #233); advisor/multi-iteration turns double count (claude-hud #666, and the stdin field itself had bugs: 'stdin is trustworthy' should read 'documented and mostly correct'). Window size must come from a documented source, not a hardcoded table (drift). Demand evidence: Oct 2026 outcry when Desktop moved its context ring; Anthropic's mods docs use a context-fill chart as the example. Idle compaction (2.1.299) changes the picture while idle.

ideas.title: statusLine bridge for 'official numbers' (context %, cache, cost, effort, PR state)
ideas.what_user_gets: Exact per-session figures the CLI itself shows: context percentage, prompt-cache warm-until, per-session cost, effort/fast mode, worktree and branch, and pr.number / pr.review_state for a PR chip, plus rate_limits and per-subagent stats, without heuristics or extra git/gh calls.
ideas.mechanisms: [Documented statusline JSON] A tiny per-session statusLine command injected via inline `--settings` that copies stdin JSON to Loom's authenticated socket, then runs the user's own statusLine command and returns its output (chaining). CLI-driven events (new assistant message, compaction, permission-mode change, rate-limit reset, cache expiry; 300 ms debounce). Field availability is version-gated (prompt_cache 2.1.251+, last_miss_cause 2.1.260+, subagent agentType 2.1.293+; rate_limits only for Pro/Max after the first response) and degrades to absent.
ideas.debates: Weakest resource/principle fit in usage-tools: a process spawn per assistant message conflicts with D-32 (no process per update) and D-20 (CLI behaviour changes are a user decision); a custom statusLine hides most CLI footer hints (such as 'esc to interrupt'), overrides the user's own status line (Vibe Island #137 / Open Island takeover class) and double-wraps with claude-hud/ccstatusline; npx/bunx cold start per update is costly (the ccstatusline #22 'per subagent' claim was a 1.0.88 CLI bug). claude-official rates it M/good, usage-tools L/defer until I-23 is measured. Orca respects an existing user statusLine and does not reinstall after deletion (marker file). Decision belongs to the user.

ideas.title: Usage honesty: plan pace, provenance, cache-cold hint, limit-hit actions
ideas.what_user_gets: Turn the raw plan-window percentage into a decision and make every number trustworthy: 'at this pace the 5-hour window runs out in 1h 40m, reset in 2h 10m' (only when it matters), a tag on each figure (official / estimate / stale), a 'cache likely cold, next message re-reads about 143k tokens' hint before you resume an idle session, and 'Continue at reset' for a session stopped on the limit. (Remaining usage for ChatGPT is a later wish; Codex is frozen.)
ideas.mechanisms: Pure functions of data Loom already has: (a) pace from get_usage utilization + resets_at, shown at >=10% used and projected >=90% (amber chip, one-shot notification per window re-armed after reset; weekly bar only at >=80% or bad pace); recompute on get_usage refresh or turn end, never poll; state freshness ('as of 3 min ago'). (b) provenance enum on view models; limit % drops to 'unknown' after now passes resets_at; guard NaN/negative/epoch values. (c) cache-cold: computed at render from the last-assistant timestamp; TTL tier (5 min vs 1 h) is only documented in statusline JSON (prompt_cache.ttl), so say 'probably cold' unless I-24 exists; keep the TTL in one constant. (d) Limit actions: documented Notification types quota_auto_resume_fired/stale/disabled (setting autoContinueAtUsageLimit, v2.1.234+) mean the CLI can continue at reset by itself; otherwise a one-shot timer to the reset time then resume + explicit continue prompt verified by the hook, per-session opt-in, Loom must be running (say so), plus 'Snooze until reset' (I-18). Compact chip is information, never changes Enter.
ideas.debates: Linear projection is rough (burst from parallel subagents, early-window false alarms; hence the 10% floor and 'at this pace' wording); the Oct 2026 outcry about hidden indicators shows demand. Cache TTL tier unverified for transcripts. Orca ships a CacheTimer; T3 a Compact chip (but with compact-on-Enter default, which to avoid). Plan limits via get_usage are flagged experimental (shape may change). Do not read the Keychain OAuth token or call /api/oauth/usage (see skips).

ideas.title: Usage rollups per project, per ticket and by source
ideas.what_user_gets: Answers 'what did EDDP-1234 cost across five sessions and two subagent workflows' and 'which project eats my quota', plus attribution of tokens to main thread vs subagents vs side chats (and later scheduled runs), per session and per day, with an 'unusually large share' hint.
ideas.mechanisms: Group the existing incremental usage reader's data by project colour, ticket key and sidechain marker; demand-driven per-row detail for the selected/expanded card (Codex discipline); label estimates as API-equivalent as today; dedupe by message id + request id with fixtures for resume/fork replay; optional numbers-only daily rollup file (day, project, model, tokens, estimated cost) that survives transcript cleanup.
ideas.debates: Open user decision: Loom's permanent delete removes a session's Claude data, so a rollup that outlives it needs a rule (content-free totals may stay, or deletion also subtracts). cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) is documented and configurable, so do not assume 30 days. Over-counting on resume/fork replay is the classic bug (Usage Monitor #158, CodexBar #2037). If the transcript drops its subagent marker, show 'unattributed' rather than guess. Becomes essential once side chats exist.

ideas.title: Multiple Claude accounts via user-managed config dirs
ideas.what_user_gets: A label and a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account: new sessions (and 'restart on account B when idle') launch with that env, and the new-session picker/footer shows each account's limit headroom, so two-plan users stop logging out and in and can start the long run on the account with room.
ideas.mechanisms: Env-at-launch (already a Loom strength) with per-profile meters from the CLI's own get_usage control request (documented-ish; shape flagged experimental); profile switch applies to new launches only; show 'unknown' for plans that do not expose limits. Cross-account resume by symlinking history dirs (projects, session-env, todos...) depends on internal CLI layout and breaks 'never pin the CLI', so keep v1 to new sessions/restarts. Each config dir is a separate plugin/skill/settings set and a separate supervisor instance.
ideas.debates: Orca reads the Keychain OAuth token and calls undocumented /api/oauth/usage (skip: legal page says third parties may not collect/store/intermediate Claude.ai credentials). Superset notes one conversation history is shared across accounts. Recurring support surface (two settings/plugin sets); ToS sensitivity. T3 supports multiple Claude provider instances through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as a design reference. Real demand: a Reddit user alternates two Max 20 plans.

ideas.title: Read-only diff / Changes pane per session
ideas.what_user_gets: See what the agent changed without leaving Loom: a Changes pane for the session's cwd/branch (Unstaged, Staged, Branch vs base, Last turn), '+N -M in K files' on the card so you triage which finished session to open first, and 'Open in editor' / 'Copy patch'. No accept/reject, no editing.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest: diff-stat chip + open-in-editor/GitLab, a files-changed list (from PostToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit payloads per turn and `git diff --stat`). Pane: git CLI plumbing only (`git --no-optional-locks diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color -z`, against HEAD or merge-base; never -uall, Superset #6004), run on demand when the pane opens and once after Stop/UserPromptSubmit, FSEvents only on the visible worktree with a debounce (Claude's own /diff mod: 150 ms debounce, 2 s HEAD poll only while seen, 5 s git timeout, 10 redraws/s; Emdash moved to 1 s; Orca 125 ms), hard caps on files/lines, cancel on leave, virtualized native text rendering, skip binary/generated, renames/quoting handled (Paseo's long diff-fix list shows parsing is hard). Syntax highlighting adds a dependency. Claude's built-in terminal /diff panel (2.1.287+, fullscreen, 110+ columns) already has per-turn source picker T1/T2 and an 'ask' button that attaches a file diff to the next prompt, so overlap is real.
ideas.debates: Most-proposed capability and the user's largest gap, but power-user-workflows argues AGAINST a diff viewer (Anthropic Desktop already ships diff, preview, PR monitor; generation is no longer the constraint, human review is, so build light aids only: diff-stat chip, tests-changed flag, open in IDE/GitLab, user-started fresh reviewer session). Competitors converge on 'git CLI, on demand, bounded'; their CPU pain came from watchers and polling (Superset per-workspace watchers/git fan-out and -uall; Emdash 250 ms full scan; Orca). Scope creep toward commit/PR/CI is the named risk; Zed/Cursor/Paseo keep it read-only. Hardest parts: large repos, submodules, line drift after agent edits.

ideas.title: Review comments batched back into the session
ideas.what_user_gets: Select lines in the Changes pane, write comments, and send them as ONE structured prompt to the right session (or keep them pending until the turn ends). Review feedback is the step done most after an agent finishes; one batched message with file, line and quoted code cuts round trips.
ideas.mechanisms: Comments live in Loom's store as the system of record with sent/unsent state and staleness anchors (store diffIdentity and mark 'outdated' rather than moving them); a batch is always one message, plain text 'File / Lines / User comment' (Orca) or Warp's build_review_prompt style ('run git diff yourself'). Delivery order from review-git-loop: (A) status-gated, hook-verified PTY paste with a 'draft only' default and explicit 'send now' via I-01; (B) pull-at-skill (`/loom:review` constant command + !`cmd` export; export call is Loom's proof of handover); (C) mods $.prompt.submit later; (D) hold pending and deliver at Stop for busy sessions. States: queued / handed over / delivered / outcome unknown; hash mismatch shows truncated/modified. 'Ask about this file' attaches a diff.
ideas.debates: Where the research most disagrees is the transport. review-git-loop prefers B over A; its own fact-check weakens B (injected !`cmd` needs pre-approved commands or the skill aborts; slash commands are exactly what autocomplete swallowed in #15553) and A (Claude needs a typed lead line, pasted text may get <pasted_content> wrapping, invisible-char stripping leaves a draft, long input bursts truncate). Orca's evidence and re-send behaviour are inconsistent (code removes delivered notes, docs say unresolved return). Emdash notes with a real PTY Loom cannot verify acceptance of a paste, but Loom's UserPromptSubmit hook can (with normalization). Mods path may be blocked on managed machines (sec-default mod, allowManagedModsOnly).

ideas.title: Per-turn checkpoints and last-turn change chip
ideas.what_user_gets: 'What did this turn change' per prompt, correct regardless of which tool the agent used: a chip on the card, a per-turn file list/diff in the detail pane, and a trustworthy 'since I last looked' marker. Restore is deferred.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest: record HEAD and `git diff --stat` at UserPromptSubmit and Stop (hook events, no polling). Fuller: a hidden snapshot ref per turn built with a temporary index (write-tree / commit-tree / update-ref into refs/loom/checkpoints/<session>/<n>) so the user's index and worktree are untouched, then diff consecutive refs (T3 CheckpointStore handles sparse checkout, racy index timestamps and fsync of refs; budget for them or limit to simple repos). `git stash create` skips untracked files (needs testing). Fall back to 'since session start' and say so when the baseline hook is missing. Restore/rewind stays with Claude's own /rewind; no auto-commit per turn.
ideas.debates: Claude's /rewind restores only edits made through Claude's file tools (misses Bash, subagent and outside changes) and cannot be driven in a TUI session, which is the case for snapshot refs; Vibe Kanban's auto-commit rewrites branch history and its reset engine depends on drifting flags (--resume-session-at), so skip both. Concurrent sessions in one checkout make 'last turn' include other edits: label scope honestly ('changes since the prompt was sent'). Hidden refs in the user's repo need a cleanup policy; size/time caps, skip non-git and giant repos, run off the main thread. review-git-loop: do after the diff view, or skip if 'commit first' plus /rewind is enough.

ideas.title: PR / CI chip and canned git actions
ideas.what_user_gets: PR number, merge state and check state on the card ('CI failing' next to the branch, surfacing in the Active list), and one-keystroke Create PR / Fix CI / Resolve conflicts as short prompts to the session; fits the ticket-key workflow.
ideas.mechanisms: Event-driven only: refresh on Stop hook, app activation, a visible card's push and a manual refresh; while checks are pending and the card is visible back off (30 s, 60 s, 2 min) and stop when settled; `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup,mergeStateStatus` through the installed gh (no tokens stored), ETag/conditional requests, label 'checked at <time>', never a false green when gh is missing/logged out; a failed check can move the session to needs-you. Alternative: pr.number / pr.review_state from the I-24 statusLine JSON (no gh), GitHub only. Canned actions are constant slash commands or editable templates sent through I-01 (review-git-loop 'lightest git write path'); merge-tree conflict preview cached by OID pair is optional (OIDs come from PR data and the base ref is fetched, so it is not network-free).
ideas.debates: Competitors poll: Superset PR status every 10 s and comments every 30 s, Orca 120 s stale, Emdash per-repo each minute, Supacode GraphQL storms and rate limits (#830, #844); the research insists on event-driven only. The user's work repos may be GitLab (power-user-workflows), where gh gives nothing. Skip merge buttons, stacks, auto-merge, auto-fix loops unless asked (agent can run gh itself).

ideas.title: Worktree-backed sessions (parallel agents on one repo)
ideas.what_user_gets: 'New session in worktree' for a project or ticket: branch named from the ticket key, the session opens there with worktree provenance on the card, environment files copied, and cleanup is a verified action, so two agents on the same repo stop colliding.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest, documented: delegate to Claude's own `claude --worktree <name>` and .worktreeinclude (plus WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks, keep/remove prompt, cleanup sweep); Loom launches, labels and reaps; add env LOOM_SESSION_ID and a reserved port range (Conductor: 10 ports) for the user's own scripts. Heavier: a small Loom module around plain `git worktree add --no-track -b <ticket-branch>` (Emdash final design: inspect, resolve base, add, verify; never fetch if the base resolves locally; APFS-clone preserved ignored files in a background step), a registry of what Loom created, removal only through a verified dry-run delete that refuses dirty or unpushed work (or snapshots to a branch/patch), a storage list with keep-N cleanup that never touches a running or pinned session, linked worktrees treated as one project by reading .git (no exec), per-project setup commands from a committed file with per-project approval showing the command. No pre-warmed pool.
ideas.debates: Polarising: power-user-workflows says skip a worktree manager (Desktop and `claude --worktree` already ship it; realistic parallelism is 2-3 sessions) while ten reports ask for it; HN: worktrees do not isolate ports, DBs, .env and add a layer, review is the bottleneck. Deletion is the data-loss risk (Cursor forum data-loss report; Supacode data-loss bugs on creation failure; Agent View deletes uncommitted changes and a second delete drops commits); dependency installs per worktree are slow/large (about 200 MB+); detached-HEAD default (Codex) to avoid; claude --worktree cleanup semantics must be re-verified against the installed CLI; refuse two sessions on the same branch; setup scripts execute arbitrary commands. Scope creep into a git client (Supacode: process storms, rate limits).

ideas.title: Fast launch surface: new-session sheet, presets, loom:// URLs, recipes, skills launcher
ideas.what_user_gets: Starting the third parallel task takes seconds: a palette-style sheet (project, branch or worktree, plan/permission mode, effort, first message) with an empty state listing the two work projects and recent ticket keys; saved presets (and 'Save this session as preset') reachable from a '+' menu, from Raycast or scripts via loom://preset/<name>; reusable prompt recipes; a launcher for the user's skills and commands.
ideas.mechanisms: Launch-time only, no live process: documented CLI flags with drift detection (show plan mode/effort only when detected), permission mode shown on the card afterwards; presets as TOML/JSON (project, branch/worktree template, Claude options, first message, colour) built on the existing 'a session opens a session' flow; URL scheme behind the same user-authority gate; worktree presets use verified git calls (I-32); recipes = project + prompt + worktree choice from the palette; skills/commands browser as launcher, not manager; global quick-capture hotkey (Codex).
ideas.debates: Skip Cursor's plan tab / Build in Parallel (Claude's plan lives in its terminal). Branch/worktree choice must not silently switch the user's working tree. URL schemes widen the attack surface. Plan-mode flag availability varies by CLI version.

ideas.title: Ticket-centred sessions (new session from ticket, ticket chip/grouping, derived work ledger)
ideas.what_user_gets: Group sessions, branches and PRs by ticket key (EDDP-123); 'New session from ticket' with the ticket context in a delimited block the user can edit before sending; a computed Work list (Needs you / Working / In review / Merged) answering 'where was I'; optional, user-confirmed suggestions to move the ticket or archive the session when the PR merges.
ideas.mechanisms: Variant (b) no tracker code: first message tells Claude to fetch the ticket with the user's own MCP/CLI, shown for editing before send; variant (a) Loom-side fetch from Linear/Jira with a Keychain token, on demand only, refreshed at send. De-duplicate by ticket key (already shipped). Ticket chip and project-view grouping are modest UI; state is derived from session status, branch and PR (I-31), never a manually maintained board. Write-back (Linear/Jira transition) only as a visible suggestion.
ideas.debates: Do not rebuild issue tracking or a kanban (Vibe Kanban's cloud-dependent board died with the company; users in #3424 said keep the ledger, drop the runner); no webhook auto-triggered sessions (needs a daemon). Ticket text is a prompt-injection vector: always show and delimit it. Emdash's ticket write-back is contested (#1930 unconfirmed). The Atlassian Claude Agent for Jira runs on Managed Agents (API-key, GitHub only), not Claude Code, so it is no evidence for the user's GitLab workflow. The ledger duplicates the activity view unless it adds the ticket dimension.

ideas.title: Extend 'a session opens a session' (parent/child, batch fan-out, narrow always-allow, ceilings)
ideas.what_user_gets: The shipped open-session flow becomes legible and quicker: the opened session nests under its parent with one 'child finished / needs you' signal on the parent card; an agent can propose several sessions and the user approves them in one sheet; trusted cases ask once per project; results return to the asking agent as session id + verified outcome.
ideas.mechanisms: Parent link + nesting; a single UI event on the parent card (never a prompt injected into the parent's PTY); detach and cascade-stop only as explicit gestures (Paseo cascades archive by default; do not copy); batch sheet with a cap and cost note; literal-action confirmation and a revocable per-project + action-type 'always allow' (never for delete or send-to-session unless opted in); a child may not get a broader permission mode than its caller (T3 ceiling); optional worktree field; rate-limited prompts and de-duplication by ticket key.
ideas.debates: Supacode's 'Always allow' flips a GLOBAL automatedActionPolicy to .always (all CLI/deeplink actions incl. destructive), so Loom's narrow scope is a deliberate improvement, not a Supacode feature; its socket auth is only 0700 permissions (Loom's authenticated socket is stronger). OpenChamber's agent tool is on by default with no per-action approval (do not copy); Vibe Kanban's MCP has no approval step. Stale parent links after deletion; orphan handling.

ideas.title: `loom` CLI + read-only verbs + wait + event hooks (the read side of multi-agent work)
ideas.what_user_gets: Agents and the user's own shell/Raycast scripts can address 'this session' and query siblings without polling: `loom sessions --json`, `loom status <id> [--explain]`, `loom wait <id> --until needs-you|finished|failed --timeout`, `loom read <id> --last-turn`; plus a small personal hooks file that runs commands on Loom events (session finished, needs approval, ticket opened, worktree created).
ideas.mechanisms: Export LOOM_SESSION_ID/LOOM_PROJECT into every hosted session (Supacode's SUPACODE_* ids are deprecated and its commands default to the FOCUSED target, which must not be copied); read verbs answered from Loom's in-memory hook-derived state over the existing authenticated socket via an event subscription (herdr's 100 ms sleep loop is what not to copy), pinned to session id + run identity so a resumed/replaced process cannot satisfy a wait; reads need no approval, mutating verbs (open, send, stop) keep the approval card; per-session short-lived credentials revoked on stop (T3 McpSessionRegistry); scope to the same project unless the user allows more; skill pattern from herdr (gate on LOOM_SESSION=1, the binary is the syntax authority, never predict ids, trigger only on explicit mention, safety rules). Scripting catalog (list, rename, focus, status, set_title) behind a Settings > Scripting switch (off by default) with an owner-only discovery record and short-lived action-scoped grants (Warp local_control). Event hooks: plain processes with LOOM_* env and bounded timeout/output, failures reported, no marketplace, no sandbox.
ideas.debates: Scope creep into a full orchestration API and a second configuration language; version the API and detect mismatch rather than pin. T3's outside-agent grants last 30 days across all projects (no per-ticket scoping precedent); Warp's warpctrl is dogfood-only at the cloned commit; herdr's marketplace is unreviewed arbitrary code (explicitly not the model). Exposes more session data to agents, so keep it read-only and scoped.

ideas.title: Cross-session message channel as a user-authority broker (the wanted D-43/D-46 channel)
ideas.what_user_gets: One session can hand a short result or question to another (planner to implementer, reviewer back to author) under the user's control and with verified outcomes, instead of copy-paste between cards; or the user can send between sessions themselves.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest, no new agent-originated channel: user-initiated send/queue (I-02 + I-01) plus session reference (I-38). Next: an authority broker over Loom's authenticated socket (loom:read-session / loom:send-to-session skills): approval card showing the exact text and source session, scoped per source/target/action pair (persisting until Stop or Quit), refuse delivery into Needs approval, explicit states queued -> delivered (prompt observed) -> read | failed (plus 'stalled'), idempotency keys instead of blind retry, text-only with a size cap (cmux 32 KiB) and control characters rejected, provenance label 'not an instruction from your operator', hold while the recipient waits on a human, per-session/project opt-out, iteration cap for reviewer loops, delegation only while the parent is working (T3). Govern the CLI's own messaging instead of duplicating it [documented since 2.1.224]: per-session inbox socket (CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET), Loom sets crossSessionInbound accept|hold|refuse via --settings, shows peers and 'message held from X' as a needs-you reason, surfaces notify_when_idle.
ideas.debates: Debate: build Loom's own broker (herdr/cmux/Superset/OpenChamber/T3 style) vs 'do not build a second transport, govern Claude's native one' (claude-official; persistence-remote-orchestration G with H as later adapter). Corrections: explicit crossSessionInbound=hold shows a notice per message and delivers NOTHING, with no dialog and no expiry; the approve/deny dialog (default 5 min) belongs to the unset default rule and only in interactive terminal sessions (Desktop/VS Code cannot show it); the unset default auto-delivers when the receiver prompts for permissions and the sender is not bypassing, so 'user-authorized only' requires explicit hold/refuse; Loom's explicit refuse also blocks the own-child posting path; the message wire format is only reverse-engineered (documented: path, optional auth line, 30 s incomplete-line close); #78706, #65972, #52084 are not precedents (Desktop MCP tool, closed not_planned/duplicate); send cap of 10 per human input is request #94000; Claude agent teams are experimental and token-heavy (do not adopt). Channels (research preview, dev flag) with permission relay is a documented future transport. Herdr: refusal only works when its detector knows the pane is blocked; its failure #5263 shows keystrokes into the wrong state. Prompt-injection chains between sessions and approval fatigue are the main risks. Standing decisions D-43/D-46 (wanted, undated).

ideas.title: Handoff and session reference (bounded digest, fresh session, fresh reviewer)
ideas.what_user_gets: Feed one session's work into another without a messaging channel: drag a card into another session or use 'Reference session' to paste a small bounded reference (transcript path plus a generated markdown digest of title, last N turns, truncated tool bodies, files touched); a 'start fresh session with a handoff note' action when context is heavy (via the user's own skill / Obsidian); a user-initiated fresh reviewer (second-opinion) session. Costs no tokens until the agent reads it.
ideas.mechanisms: Digest written under a Loom-owned cache from the incremental transcript reader; only an id/path goes in the prompt and the agent reads on demand (T3 @thread chips + t3_thread_read); preview what will be referenced (secret-leak risk across projects); handoff brief template with zero-context assumptions (Paseo); handoff delivery via the open-session flow with verified delivery; Zed 'New From Summary' as the UX precedent; the compact/new-session hint tied to I-23.
ideas.debates: Handoff vs /compact: the compaction-threshold advice in the research varies (35-40%, 50%, 100-120k, 500k, 700k clusters; the cited 40-50% is one of several). User-initiated, read-only and bounded keeps cross-session authority clean. Skip T3's cross-environment export complexity.

ideas.title: User-armed Goal mode driven by the Stop hook
ideas.what_user_gets: Arm a goal (objective, token budget, turn cap default 20) and walk away: Loom answers each Stop with a block+reason that continues the work until an independent check says done / needs-you / budget / cap. The blue 'finished unviewed' then fires once at the end. Stop always wins and pauses the goal.
ideas.mechanisms: [Documented] Stop hook decision (block + reason); no 15 s quiet-window timer needed because the hook IS the turn-end signal; the check sees only the objective and the last assistant message with three yes/no questions decided in code (OpenChamber audit.js). Arming is an explicit per-session user act, visible on the card; suppress intermediate notifications; metered.
ideas.debates: Single source; Codex ships thread/goal/* in its documented app-server (precedent). Risks: runaway spend, loop fighting the user's own hooks, behaviour of Stop blocks across CLI versions, whether Stop fires separately for subagents (unverified), checker misjudgment (their self-measured lab: about 98%). OpenChamber's public docs are stale (blocked settles on the first auditor answer, now verified in code). HN: walk-away works 'most of the time, not always'. power-user-workflows warns against orchestration/swarm complexity.

ideas.title: Scheduled runs with a triage inbox (later)
ideas.what_user_gets: A Scheduled section whose runs (daily repo brief, CI-failure triage, stale-docs sweep) arrive as ordinary sessions in the existing Active/Finished-unviewed machinery, with 'nothing to report' runs auto-marked viewed.
ideas.mechanisms: One armed timer for the next due run; works only while Loom runs and says missed runs were skipped (Codex needs the app running too); each run in an isolated worktree; standalone vs 'return to this session'; per-task budget; scheduled prompts authored by the user, agents cannot create schedules without approval; build only after worktrees and usage-by-source exist. Recipe-only variant (no scheduler) from Emdash; if true background runs are wanted, delegate to Claude's own Routines (research preview, min 1 h) / Desktop scheduled tasks or launchd rather than keeping Loom alive.
ideas.debates: Superset and Emdash both advise against a Loom-style cron daemon (contradicts Quit stops everything / no daemon); the real-value version is unattended runs, which needs a different ownership model and a tight permission mode. Anthropic already ships Routines and Desktop scheduled tasks (min 1 min, while the app is open, one catch-up within 7 days).

ideas.title: Cross-session transcript search
ideas.what_user_gets: 'Which session did I solve X in / which touched EDDP-123' becomes a keystroke: content hits in the existing sidebar search (and a Cmd-K palette), ranked above loose title matches, showing the matching line and opening at the right place; Cmd+F inside a session's transcript panel.
ideas.mechanisms: Lightest, no index: search the most recent N sessions' JSONL on demand with a time and byte budget and a streaming matcher, cancel on typing (Cursor-style bounded variant). Heavier: incremental SQLite FTS5 index fed by the same FSEvents transcript reader as Usage, user and assistant text only (not tool output or scrollback), size-capped, rebuildable from transcripts so CLI format drift degrades coverage not correctness, operators agent:/repo:/before:, nothing running when the search UI is closed. Deletion: the permanent-delete flow must purge that session's index rows in the same transaction and report it.
ideas.debates: Index growth (Orca had unbounded-growth complaints) vs an on-demand scan; an index is a second copy of sensitive conversation text (needs an off switch and per-project exclusion). Transcript format is internal and unversioned; transcripts are subject to cleanupPeriodDays (default 30, configurable). power-user-workflows places it in the 'after measuring' tier.

ideas.title: Away from the Mac: Remote Control toggle, presence file, optional content-free push
ideas.what_user_gets: For sessions that already run in Loom PTYs, a 'Reachable from phone' toggle (and a Settings default) so approvals, answers and nudges can be done from the phone, with an RC badge on the card; Claude's own phone pushes are suppressed while you are at the Mac; optionally a content-free 'session X needs you' push. No Loom server, relay or app.
ideas.mechanisms: 1) [Documented, `--remote-control [name]` present in `claude --help` 2.1.300] Launch with `--remote-control "<title>"` (or send /remote-control later); badge from CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID in hook payloads (v2.1.199) once connected; preflight with `claude auth status` and explain why unavailable (API-key auth, Bedrock/Vertex, custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN/setup-token, ZDR/HIPAA, Team/Enterprise owner toggle, disableRemoteControl, Trusted Devices). 2) [documented on the RC page] write/delete the CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE on screen lock/unlock (NSDistributedNotificationCenter) so CLI pushes happen only when away; env is read at CLI start, so it only affects sessions started afterwards. 3) Optional webhook/ntfy/Shortcuts push, off by default, fixed string + session title only, no approve-from-phone; likely redundant because RC already sends documented mobile pushes for finished and needs-permission.
ideas.debates: Corrections: DISABLE_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK no longer block RC since 2.1.283 (unless Trusted Devices required); the 'Mac must stay awake' claim is overstated (a sleeping laptop reconnects; server mode gives up after about 10 min); Remote Control sessions can pick Auto mode; truncated-approval-card evidence is a ~5-month-old comment. Privacy: transcript is stored on Anthropic servers while connected, so default off with plain wording; Quit still stops the session, so the phone loses it (say so). Unresolved tests needed with a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: does --remote-control start a long-lived daemon outliving Loom's scope on macOS, and does RC work with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1 (Loom sets it). Loom can claim only 'requested' unless RC state is visible to hooks/registry (unverified; /rc active indicator exists in the TUI). Mobile reality: value is attention (push, approve/deny, short result, one follow-up), not deep review. Paseo's loopback web page over Tailscale/SSH is the heaviest acceptable variant and persistence-remote-orchestration ranks any Loom-owned relay/web/app as skip.

ideas.title: Process-tree view: listening ports / dev-server pill and on-demand resource inspector
ideas.what_user_gets: An 'Open localhost:PORT' pill on a card when its own process tree is listening (default browser; an embedded WKWebView only on request), and an on-demand popover with per-session process-tree memory/CPU and the top 3 child processes, so a leaked dev server or runaway test run is visible and feeds the park decision.
ideas.mechanisms: Enumerate sockets and resource totals of the run scope's pids via libproc only when the card is visible, on the Stop hook, on click or while the popover is open (never a scanner: Superset's lsof scan every 2.5 s / 30 s idle was a CPU/lag source); name only what Loom started; show 'sampled at'; optional LOOM_PORT range env for per-worktree ports (Conductor gives 10 ports per workspace). Nothing drawn when hidden.
ideas.debates: Per-process attribution on macOS (shared coalitions, helpers) is easy to overstate; Conductor fixed wrong memory totals twice. An embedded browser is the heaviest component Loom would own and contradicts 'idle costs nothing' if left open (cmux and Superset pay in memory). Backend-focused user: low payoff for annotated-browser/design-mode work (see skips).

ideas.title: Engineering guardrails: performance budgets, reader regression, contract fixtures, compat advisories
ideas.what_user_gets: Protects the properties that make Loom usable all day (CPU gate, no beachballs with 30+ sessions, accurate status) as v2 adds per-card data, and turns CLI-update surprises into actionable messages.
ideas.mechanisms: (a) Sidebar budget as a test: immutable value snapshots plus action closures, Equatable rows with .equatable(), no state writes from body or the ForEach projection, per-card extras via one coalesced equality-guarded projection, hidden means no work, 1/10/100-session synthetic harness without real CLIs, run only when the user says the computer is idle. (b) Transcript reader regression: incremental by byte offset + inode, idle sessions cause zero reads (Happy's 3 s full re-read took 20-40% CPU). (c) No animation or render for hidden panes (herdr: removing the sidebar spinner and skipping hidden-pane renders cut CPU 89-95%). (d) Captured-payload contract tests for hooks and approvals, agent-tracking fixtures. (e) Compatibility advisories: a small JSON of known-bad CLI versions and feature thresholds bundled with each release, optionally one conditional fetch at launch, shown as a non-blocking banner and as the explanation when drift detection fires; never block by version. (f) Hook hygiene: tiny, fast, no-op outside Loom, scoped via --settings, fail-open, short timeouts.
ideas.debates: T3 treats 2.1.111..2.1.280 as 'graceful' and only <2.1.111 as unsupported, and only emits an advisory (the '2.1.280+ hard minimum' is from release notes, not code), so version advisories are compatible with 'never pin' only if advisory. Several resource data points are single-user reports (cmux #2487 not #2586 for the 8.5 h figure; herdr #5289 is a non-default mode; Superset's 12.8 s hook and 50x git status are single measurements); the stable-vs-nightly difference matters (cmux freezes were seen on nightlies). Whether Loom already covers each item is unknown.

skips.what: A Loom-owned PTY daemon or multiplexer that keeps sessions alive after Quit (zmx/tmux style)
