skips.why: Daemon-owned PTYs are the biggest pain source in the field: Superset pty-master fd leak exhausting kern.tty.ptmx_max and CPU/lsof issues, Orca daemon generations (#9138: 8 sessions shown vs about 46 live Claude processes, filed on v1.4.143, still open), Anthropic's own supervisor leaks (#87891, #65051), Happy's relay stack. Breaks 'Quit stops all', process ownership, verified stop and idle cost. Ended screen + --resume + idle-park (I-19) already give most of the value. If ever wanted: per-session user-chosen 'detach on Quit' hosted via Claude's supervisor (I-22) with a spike first. A user may still miss survive-Quit (Supacode's most praised feature).

skips.what: Driving Claude through the Agent SDK, ACP (claude-agent-acp) or an embedded Node/Bun helper for the main session
skips.why: Replaces the real CLI interface, adds Node 22+ and a several-hundred-MB adapter tree, feature lag (hidden slash commands, #3126), pinned or bundled CLI versions against 'never pin', and exposure to Anthropic's SDK billing policy that changed four times in ten months. If a structured engine is ever wanted, I-07 reaches the same protocol without a runtime; revisit ACP only if multi-provider (Codex/Gemini/OpenCode) returns. Swift ACP SDKs are thin and low-activity (32/7/11 stars).

skips.what: Screen-scraping the TUI for dialogs, input state or status (Ghostex-style) and herdr-style regex detectors
skips.why: About 5.2k lines of Rust for Claude alone, comments pinned to CLI versions, violates update resilience and 'never report false success' because a paste cannot be verified. Hooks, registry and OSC 7501 are the stable base.

skips.what: Notch overlay, mascots, sentiment analysis, haptics, AppleScript/Accessibility terminal-jumping, SSH hook bridging, Watch relay, and managing hooks in the user's global settings.json
skips.why: The category's own authors spent releases fixing idle CPU and jump bugs these create (CodeIsland idled about 5.3% CPU even after gating mascot animation); jumping is moot because Loom owns the tabs; global hook management causes duplicate/stale hooks. Use menu bar, notifications and per-session --settings instead.

skips.what: A Loom-owned remote surface: relay, E2E crypto, push service, native phone app, web terminal, voice agent
skips.why: Needs a process surviving Quit and constant connections, huge support surface (Happy's relay audit and outage; Paseo spends most effort on phone UX), conflicts with local-only data and low resource use; Claude's Remote Control (I-42) already does outbound-only mobile access. The only acceptable heavier variants are a loopback read-and-approve page over the user's own Tailscale/SSH while Loom runs, or a content-free push; cloud-style Remote Control and Warp-style shared sessions are out.

skips.what: Reading the CLI's Keychain OAuth token or calling the undocumented /api/oauth/usage endpoint for plan limits (Orca, CodeIsland, Notchi, OpenChamber do this)
skips.why: Reverse-engineered interface using the user's subscription token; Anthropic's legal page says third parties may not collect, store or intermediate Claude.ai credentials. Keep the documented get_usage control request and statusLine rate_limits.

skips.what: Embedded browser panel, script-injecting preview proxy, element/region annotation, agent-driven browsing (design mode)
skips.why: A browser engine is the heaviest component Loom could own and costs memory while open (cmux and Superset pay); a CSP-stripping proxy with injected framework adapters is a permanent surface; the user is backend-focused. Lighter: open the dev-server URL in the default browser (I-43) or a lazily created WKWebView destroyed when hidden, and a screenshot-region-to-prompt capture if ever wanted.

skips.what: An automatic reviewer/guardian agent or a classifier that decides a session 'looks done'
skips.why: Hidden model spend (Codex Guardian helper agent about 35% of tokens in one report; OpenChamber's classifier is a model call per turn) conflicts with low resource use and cost transparency. A per-turn approvals counter (I-15) is the cheap substitute.

skips.what: Kanban board / task runner / ticket auto-trigger from webhooks
skips.why: Vibe Kanban's board died with its cloud; users said keep the ledger, drop the runner; webhook-triggered sessions need a daemon and break 'Quit stops all'. Keep derived ticket grouping (I-34) instead.

skips.what: Plugin marketplace or Electron-style plugin host; a worktree pre-warm pool
skips.why: Marketplace/hosts conflict with Loom's size and trust principles (herdr's is unreviewed arbitrary code); Emdash itself removed its worktree pool (commit 4193beb) because spare worktrees are state nobody asked for. A personal hooks file (I-36) covers the long tail.

skips.what: Auto-commit per turn, Loom's own rewind/reset engine, in-app accept/reject hunks or editor, stage/revert UI
skips.why: Auto-commit rewrites the user's branch history; reset depends on drifting CLI flags (--resume-session-at); accept/reject needs an editor holding buffers and duplicates the user's IDE. Link out to Claude's /rewind and keep the diff read-only (I-28/I-30).

skips.what: Per-repo or per-workspace polling and watchers (PR dashboards, git status timers, lsof port scanners, 15-45 s session-list reloads)
skips.why: The loudest CPU/rate-limit failures in the field: Superset (10 s/30 s PR polling, per-workspace GitWatcher, git fan-out), Emdash (250 ms scan, per-repo polling), Supacode (GraphQL storms #830/#844), OpenChamber #5023, Happy's 3 s transcript re-read. Event-driven and visible-only (I-28, I-31, I-43, I-44).

skips.what: Orchestrator/swarm UI, a custom composer that replaces the CLI prompt, a full diff/PR/CI stack and a worktree manager as the v2 headline
skips.why: Position of power-user-workflows: they duplicate what Anthropic Desktop/agent view ships, scale the part users cannot absorb (realistic ceiling 2-3 sessions, plan quota the second ceiling), and trigger wrapper failure modes. Note this DISAGREES with the 10-14 product reports that propose diff and worktrees, so treat I-28/I-32 as a user decision, not a given.

skips.what: Making Claude's mods the base transport (watch-list only), plus Channels, asyncRewake waiters and the CLI's inbox socket as the review transport
skips.why: Mods are two weeks old with API churn nearly every release 2.1.295-2.1.301 (the exact count is unverified), run unsandboxed with full user permissions, are blockable by managed policy (sec-default mod, allowManagedModsOnly) and the sec-default mod shows Anthropic treats them as a security surface. Keep hooks + statusline + OSC 7501 as the stable base; revisit after a few release cycles (I-01 option 3).

skips.what: Orca-style blind write after a delivery timeout, hidden --prefill dependence, and pasting without readiness gating (Superset)
skips.why: Reports 'delivered' without proof; --prefill is undocumented. Use I-01's gated, verified, 'outcome unknown' semantics.

skips.what: Compact-on-Enter defaults, countdown tickers, always-on animation or live timers in the sidebar
skips.why: Changes what Enter means (predictability) and costs idle CPU; schedule one wake at the deadline instead.

skips.what: Adopting Claude agent teams as a Loom concept; copying Paseo's cascade-archive default; copying OpenChamber's on-by-default agent tool
skips.why: Agent teams are experimental and token-heavy; cascade and no-approval tools break cross-session actions under the user's authority.

skips.what: Changes Walkthrough (one-shot claude -p over the diff, cached) for now
skips.why: Needs the large prerequisite diff view (I-28) and a model call with usage accounting; presents confident output that can be wrong if anchoring fails. Revisit only after the plain diff view proves use.

cross_cutting_lessons: Resource failures are the loudest competitor complaint, and native does not guarantee lightness: cmux (native Swift) had a 100% CPU SwiftUI sidebar layout loop, leaked openThread loops and a large memory report; Electron peers (Superset git subprocess fan-out and lsof scanner, Orca daemon generations, Paseo resident daemon, OpenChamber 45 s list polling and unvirtualized rows, Emdash 250 ms scans) are worse. Common causes: watchers/polling per workspace, whole-file transcript re-reads (Happy 3 s rescan 20-40% CPU), animated overlays (CodeIsland 5.3% idle even after gating), mounting all history. Cure that worked: herdr cut 89-95% CPU by dropping the sidebar spinner and skipping hidden-pane renders. Many figures are single-user anecdotes or on nightlies; treat them as failure classes, not baselines.

CLI-update fragility is the second theme: T3 treats Claude 2.1.111-2.1.280 as graceful and warns by advisory; herdr abandoned hook-driven state for Claude then removed its hooks from users' settings after stale-state bugs; Orca's docs disagree with its code (uses a keychain token, OSC titles); Vibe Kanban pins a default CLI; Conductor bundles the CLI (about 1 day behind) and lags at SDK/feature level; mods API churn nearly every release; JSONL is declared CLI-internal in the SDK typings; updatedInput is validated from 2.1.300 (unknown keys dropped); statusline and OSC fields are version-gated; hook timeouts differ per event. Design rule: documented interfaces first (hooks, --settings, statusline, OSC 7501, claude agents --json, get_usage), capability detection and drift evidence for everything else, unknown renders as 'unknown' or raw, never pin.

Delivery verification is Loom's real edge and every competitor lacks it: Warp, Superset, Orca (on the diff-note path), Emdash and Vibe Kanban write to the PTY without proof; Loom's UserPromptSubmit hook sees the submitted prompt. Caveats from fact-checks: the hook prompt has pastes expanded or wrapped in <pasted_content>, invisible Unicode is stripped on Enter, Claude wants a typed lead before a paste, slash commands get swallowed by autocomplete, long bursts truncate, so 'exact hash match' is overstated (normalize or use a marker), a single writer per session is needed, and the honest outcome vocabulary is queued / delivered / outcome unknown with no auto-retry. Refuse to write in Needs approval or any modal.

Status truth rests on documented-but-subtle hook semantics: Stop carries background_tasks and session_crons and last_assistant_message; Stop does NOT fire on interrupt and there is no interrupt event; permission_prompt Notification waits about 6 s while PermissionRequest is immediate; idle_prompt (about 60 s after finishing) is not 'needs you'; SubagentStop also fires for internal agents (prompt suggestions, /btw); transcript_path writes lag; agent_needs_input/agent_completed fire only while agent view is open. Emdash's regex-on-message-text workaround is obsolete (notification_type is documented). Competitor bug classes to turn into tests: finished-with-background-work, foreign sessions inheriting env, Failed downgraded by a later Notification, resume/compact counted as completion.

Billing/policy: the real CLI in a PTY is on the safe side. Anthropic's support article (updated 2026-10-07) says Agent SDK, claude -p and third-party apps still draw from subscription limits, the May 13 metering change was paused June 15 'for now', the April 4 policy hit third-party harnesses, the legal page says SDK-based products should use API keys and allows the unmodified binary with the user's own login, forbids collecting or intermediating Claude.ai credentials, and the Oct 7 monthly credits are API credits that do not cover interactive Claude Code. Conductor/T3/Paseo/Zed users were hit by the uncertainty. Any headless/stream-json feature (I-07, headless side chat) should be an isolated, killable opt-in, and the support article re-read before each release.

Anthropic absorbs breadth: Desktop ships diff view with batched comments, side chat (Cmd+;), preview, PR/CI monitor, scheduled tasks and Routines; the CLI ships agent view, Remote Control, /btw, /diff (a mod), cross-session messaging, --worktree, idle compaction. Loom should compete on what a light native host does better: attention routing, status accuracy, multi-project/multi-session workspace, usage/context health, subagent tree, ticket-centred organisation, user-authorized cross-session actions, and cheap lifecycle (park, keep-awake). Warp and Zed 'Terminal Threads' show that keeping the real CLI is a shipped, viable design; chat-first re-renderings are criticised for hiding what the CLI does while terminal tools are criticised as tab managers, which is why a lens over the real session (I-05/I-06) is the favoured middle.

The bottleneck is the human, not generation: review, attention and plan quota. Practitioner ceiling is about 2-3 interactive sessions (3-5 with strong separation); Hashimoto vs Cherny on notifications is single-agent vs multi-agent regimes, not doctrine; Auto mode (2.1.283+) makes approvals rarer than older statistics suggest. So v2 value is triage (what needs me and why), review aids and context/quota health rather than more agents; features that raise parallelism (worktrees, orchestration UI) are contested (power-user-workflows skips them, ten product reports want worktrees).

Persistence converges on hibernate-and-resume, not daemons: Orca hibernation (30 min default, experimental), Claude's supervisor (idle unattached stop after about an hour), Supacode (on by default, Beta), cmux (only above 12 live terminals), Conductor (idle shutdown + --resume). Loom already has the hard parts (run scope, verified Stop, resume, ended screen). Hazards: killing background tasks/monitors/wakeups, cold-resume cache cost and idle compaction, resume failing after CLI updates, stale resume references (herdr), and the supervisor's own open leak bugs.

Fork-style features share costs and cleanup duties: a fork re-reads the whole context (tokens, cache), shares the working tree (read-only is guidance or tool limits, Codex enforces only at prompt level), pollutes the registry and `claude --resume` lists, double-counts usage, and only sees flushed turns (fork from the last completed turn). Verified deletion must cover forks and any search index rows, and transcript cleanup (cleanupPeriodDays, default 30, configurable) must be considered for rollups.

Cross-session authority: competitors differ mainly in approvals. Safe patterns: scoped, short-lived per-session credentials revoked on stop; delegation only while the parent works; privilege ceilings; refusal into blocked sessions; explicit delivery states; text-only size-capped messages with provenance labels; idempotency keys; narrow revocable always-allow. Anti-patterns: OpenChamber's on-by-default tool, Vibe Kanban's MCP with no approval, Supacode's global always-allow flip, T3's 30-day all-project grants, herdr's blocked check that only works when its scraper is right. Claude's native cross-session messaging exists (2.1.224+) but its default is not user-authorized-only and its wire format is undocumented.

Hook hygiene: scope hooks per Loom-started session with `claude --settings` (never the user's global settings.json), keep them tiny and a no-op outside Loom, fail open, bind decisions to (session id, request id, kind), cancel pending cards on PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd/PID exit, hand back rather than decide on timeout, and avoid statusLine takeover (Vibe Island #137 / Open Island class, hides CLI footer hints) unless chaining the user's own. Orca's managed statusLine install respects an existing user statusLine.

Evidence discipline: fact-checks repeatedly corrected citations (open_issues_count includes PRs; many cited issues are closed/fixed or single-reporter; star counts are inflated; competitor comparison pages and some reports are interested parties; Steinberger is a Codex user; Warp's Ctrl-C synthesis is only the viewer path; cmux hibernation is not an idle timer; DISABLE_TELEMETRY no longer blocks Remote Control; crossSessionInbound hold has no dialog). The product-note fact-check section wins over report text, and several mechanisms remain explicitly unverified (PermissionRequest hook vs TUI dialog race, fork behaviour mid-turn, side_question shape, RC daemon behaviour on macOS, window-size/TTL tier in transcripts, agent ids in hooks).

The user's own long-standing wishes map to: side chat -> I-08 (free shortcut) then I-09 (forked PTY child), with I-05/I-07 only if a chat look is wanted; right panel -> I-10 (needs D-34 revisited; subagent tree already opens in place of the terminal); remaining usage -> shipped plus I-25/I-26/I-27 (ChatGPT later, Codex frozen); reliable deletion -> already shipped, extended to forks, search index and rollups; idle sessions cost nothing -> I-19 plus I-05 ended-session view; a user-authorized cross-session channel -> I-02/I-38 then I-37.

Suggested sequencing signals from the evidence (not a decision): cheap, high-convergence, low-risk first (I-20 keep-awake, I-12 status hardening, I-23 context meter, I-17 attention polish, I-08 /btw shortcut, I-14 card content), then the shared foundations (I-01 send primitive, I-05 read-only conversation view), then the features that depend on them (I-02 queue, I-09 side chat, I-28/I-29 review loop, I-15/I-16 approvals), and last the contested or large decisions that need the user (I-32 worktrees, I-07 Chat mode, I-22 supervisor, I-24 statusLine bridge, I-37 channel, D-34 right panel).

feasibility.one_line: Worth building as a small LoomCore primitive (hook-gated, draft-only by default, hook-confirmed 'delivered', never retried), but the safety claim 'never press Enter into a dialog' is not documented anywhere, so a one-day real-Claude spike (send matrix + modal visibility) must decide the constants and whether 'submit' ships at all.
feasibility.loom_design:
WHERE IT PLUGS IN (all verified in the tree)
- Core: new `Sources/LoomCore/SessionInputSender.swift` (actor, owned by `SessionRuntime` beside `claudeAdapter`/`inputGate`; ~300 lines) plus a pure `SendReadiness` gate and `PromptText` (sanitize + normalize), ~120 lines. LoomCore stays UI-free: it decides and sequences; it writes through a small `TerminalInputPort` protocol that `TerminalSurface` implements and registers by runID. `TerminalInputGate` (LoomCore, already the runID registry the surface fills in `TerminalSurface.attach`) is the natural place to hold the port next to the `TerminalInputQueue`.
- Write path: reuse the run's existing `TerminalInputQueue` (one ordered, bounded 4 MiB writer per run; user keys and paste already share it, `TerminalSurface.send`). The sender enqueues `ESC[200~ text ESC[201~` as one chunk, waits one delay, then enqueues `\r` as a separate write. Loom already writes a draft without Enter today (`LoomTerminalView.insertDroppedFiles` -> `pasteText`, UI-MAP line 77), so draft-only is an existing behaviour made gated, not a new class of risk.
- One writer per session: at most one in-flight send per run inside the actor; a second request gets `refused(.busy)` (or joins the Loom-side queue). A delayed Enter therefore cannot submit another send's text. The user is a second writer Loom cannot lock out, so the Enter step re-checks (below).
- State source: `ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift) already sees every hook event in order after `ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive`. Add one call there: after a non-synthetic `.userPromptSubmit` is applied, `sender.promptObserved(runID, promptID, digest)`; after `.stop` applied, `sender.turnEnded(runID)` (fires an armed 'after this turn' send). `ClaudeHookEvent.init` (ClaudeHook.swift ~l.448) already reads `prompt` only for `promptIsSynthetic`; add a content-free `promptDigest` computed from the normalized prompt (SHA-256, not the text), so Loom still retains no prompt text.
- GATE (`SendReadiness`, pure, table-tested), evaluated before the paste and again right before Enter. Inputs: `ProviderWorkState.activity`, `identity`, `issue`, `stopFailure`, `userRequests` / awaiting-open-approval, deletion fence (`TerminalInputQueue.close`), queue open and not draining, subagent-approval state, user-input proof. Rules: submit allowed only for `.atPrompt` and `.turnComplete` with a clean prompt proof; `.waitingForInput` is draft-only (SessionIndicator and the tracker map idle_prompt, elicitation_dialog and agent_needs_input to the same case, so a question dialog is indistinguishable from an idle prompt until E2 shows otherwise); `.working` -> refuse or Loom-side 'after this turn'; `.waitingForApproval`, `.unknown`, `.failed`, problem/identity-unclear/stop-unverified, no live run -> refuse with a reason string. Never auto-resume a stopped session (resume-and-send is a consumer decision).
- Clean-prompt proof (the hard part, honestly): Loom sees every user byte, which competitors do not, but `TerminalSurface.send` also carries terminal replies, so the counter must sit in `LoomTerminalView` (keyDown, paste, insertText, dropped files; already overridden/owned) as `userInputEpoch`. Core marks the prompt 'touched' on the first user input after a baseline (SessionStart or a non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit), ignoring input that arrives while the state is Needs approval (permission answers are not drafts); event-driven (one callback per baseline), no polling. Touched or input in the last ~2 s -> draft-only or refuse. Residual blind spots that no Loom-side signal closes: client-side pickers (/model, /resume, rewind menu) and text typed during a turn then Stop. Hence 'submit' is an opt-in, per-send button, 'draft' is the default.
- Sequence for submit: gate -> sanitize -> (optional typed lead line, raw, single line, constant from the consumer; only if E1 shows Claude needs it) -> bracketed paste -> sleep(delay) -> gate again + `userInputEpoch` unchanged + queue drained -> write `\r` -> arm one confirm timer (5-8 s) -> `promptObserved` resolves it. Delay constants, lead-line rule and size cap live in one `ClaudeInputProfile` value, not scattered.
- Sanitize (your own, because Claude strips invisible characters on Enter and then submits nothing, leaving a draft): drop ESC and C0/C1 controls except LF/TAB, DEL, bidi/zero-width/other Cf characters, any literal `ESC[201~`; normalize line endings; cap at 32 KiB (larger payloads are a consumer problem: write a file and send a short pointer). Reject a body that starts with `/`, `!`, `&`, `@`, `#` unless the consumer declares `kind: .slashCommand` from a constant allowlist (autocomplete swallows programmatic Enter on slash commands, issue #15553 comments; slash commands are out of scope for v1).
- Outcomes (value type returned to the caller as an AsyncStream of at most 3 updates): `refused(reason)`, `queued` (Loom-side, waiting for Stop), `pasted` (written to the terminal, not submitted; label it 'placed in the prompt, not confirmed': drained bytes are not bytes Claude read, see `closeIfIdle` doc comment), `delivered(matched)` (UserPromptSubmit digest equals), `delivered(unmatched)` (a non-synthetic prompt arrived right after our Enter but the text differs: edited or truncated), `outcomeUnknown` (no prompt in the window; late arrival upgrades it while the tombstone lives; no automatic retry, ever). Matching is two-level because 'exact hash' is overstated: normalize pasted_content wrappers, invisible characters and trailing whitespace on both sides, compare digest of the normalized text; fall back to 'a user prompt arrived'. Only the hook can say delivered.
- Drift handling: journal rare events via `DiagnosticJournal` (`send_unconfirmed`, with CLI version, no content), reuse `ProviderToolchain` executable stamp; two consecutive `outcomeUnknown` with a clean prompt degrade the primitive to draft-only for the rest of the app run and show one line saying so (same spirit as `ClaudeSessionAdapter.hookSilenceIssue`). Nothing pins a CLI version; `--prefill` is never used (hidden, absent from `claude --help` 2.1.300, same deeplink path had an RCE fixed in 2.1.118).
- Bounds: one in-flight send per run, optional queue of at most 5 entries per session, memory only (lost on Quit, contract §7 requires queue persistence/cancellation to be defined: say so explicitly in the UI), 32 KiB per item, two one-shot timers only while a send is in flight, all cancelled on run end, Stop, deletion (`TerminalInputQueue.close`) and Quit (`SessionRuntime.shutdown`).
- Authority: `send(origin:)` takes a required origin; only `.user` (an explicit click or shortcut in Loom) is implemented. The D-43 cross-session sender is a later consumer that adds per-target approval; PTY paste does not satisfy contract §11 CP3's 'using only documented interfaces' gate, so I-01 does not close CP3.

OTHER MECHANISMS FROM THE IDEA
- (2) hook additionalContext: separate feature ('attach to the next turn'), not part of this primitive. Loom's helpers are synchronous 1 s `loom-hook` processes that return no provider decision (ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings), so adding stdout JSON means making the hook wait for Loom's reply on the hot path. Later, optional.
- (3) Loom mod (`$.prompt.read/fill/submit({asUser:true})`): the only mechanism that can read the draft and refuse under a dialog, i.e. it closes exactly the two blind spots above. Loom already passes `--plugin-dir` (ClaudeLoomPlugin), so a mod file could ship there, but it is unsandboxed, 15 days old, API-churning, blockable by org policy and unverified end to end (asUser is missing from the repo's d.ts). Treat as a runtime-detected upgrade after the PTY path, behind its own spike (E4).
- (4) pull-at-skill (`/loom:review` + !`$LOOM_CLI ...`): not the default. The pasted payload is a slash command, which is the failing class in #15553; the injected command needs an `allowed-tools`/allow rule in every Loom session's `--settings`, which is a D-20-class change to CLI behaviour (user decision) and fails under disableSkillShellExecution or org policy. Keep as a later option for payloads over 32 KiB.
- (5) `--prefill`: reject.

FIRST CONSUMER (so it is testable and useful): one 'Send to Session...' popover from the header actions menu (see ui_sketch). Queued prompts, composer, review comments and hand-back are later consumers of the same call.

TESTS: `SendReadiness` as a pure table test; sender state machine with an injected fake port and fake clock (refusal matrix, user typed between paste and Enter, run ends mid-send, late hook after timeout, duplicate/synthetic prompts, single-writer); `ClaudeHookTests` for the digest; the fake provider (`loom-fake-provider`, reads lines with readLine) cannot reproduce bracketed paste or Ink behaviour, so real-Claude evidence comes from the spike, not from the suite.
feasibility.ui_sketch: v1 has no new chrome and nothing in the sidebar. In the detail header's actions menu (the three-dot group, DESIGN §3 item 6) add 'Send Text to Session...' which opens a small popover over the terminal: multi-line text field, a primary button 'Place in Prompt' (draft-only, default), a secondary 'Send' (enabled only when the gate proves a clean prompt; disabled with a one-line reason otherwise) and, while the session is Working, 'Send After This Turn' (Loom-side, shows '1 queued', cancel, and a note that queued text is dropped on Quit). The popover closes on send and the header shows one transient status line near the state pill: 'Placed in the prompt. Press Return in the terminal.' / 'Delivered' / 'Not confirmed. Check the terminal; Loom did not retry.' / 'Not sent: Needs approval'. Nothing is drawn or watched when the popover is closed; the card and menu bar are untouched (no new redraw source in the sidebar hot path). Stopped sessions: the action is disabled with 'Resume to send'.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: PASS if built as designed (no polling; two one-shot timers only during a send; memory-only bounded queue; digest not text; nothing drawn when hidden). RISK: any 'wait until idle' loop, screen scraping for the prompt state, or a persisted queue would violate it; avoided. Predictability: RISK, the central one. Enter into a permission dialog is the herdr #5263 failure; mitigation is double gating (before paste and before Enter), draft-only default, user-input proof, no blind Enter after a timeout. Residual blind spots (client-side pickers, drafts typed during a turn) are only closed by the optional mod path, so 'Send' must stay an explicit, opt-in button. Accurate status: PASS, only a UserPromptSubmit hook upgrades to 'delivered'; 'pasted' is labelled unconfirmed; 'outcome unknown' is never retried or shown as success (do not copy Orca's blind write after timeout, nor herdr's post-write 5 s effect gate). Fluency: PASS with care; refusals must carry a reason and a one-click alternative (draft, queue), otherwise the primitive becomes a nag. CLI-update resilience: PASS/RISK; only documented hooks (UserPromptSubmit prompt/prompt_id) plus terminal-standard bracketed paste, but the Claude TUI's input handling is undocumented, so delay/lead-line/size constants live in one profile, drift is journaled and the primitive self-degrades to draft-only; never pins a version. Modularity: PASS (LoomCore decides behind a port; TerminalSurface only moves bytes; consumers separate; one hook call site in the adapter). Process ownership: PASS, it only writes to a PTY Loom owns, by runID, and refuses for ended or deleting runs. User authority: PASS for `.user` origin; cross-session origin deliberately not implemented (D-43 needs per-target approval and a documented-interface path). Contract: the terminal stays the real CLI (input aid only); contract §7 'Text transfer' says bracketed paste does not prove acceptance, which this design honours by defining delivered as hook-confirmed only.
feasibility.value_reason: For a heavy multi-session, multi-agent user it removes the manual switch-paste-hope step and is the common substrate for a queued-prompt list, a composer, review-comment hand-back and side-answer hand-back, and its hook-verified outcomes are something competitors (Superset #6243, Warp, Orca's note path) do not have. Standalone it is nearly invisible (value ~2) until a consumer exists, and the 'submit' half carries real risk, so I rate the foundation 4, not 5. Honest cost: M covers primitive + draft tracker + one popover consumer + tests; the queue/composer/review features built on it are separate (L together).

feasibility.one_line: Worth building as a small Loom-held "after this turn" queue (a different semantic from the CLI's mid-turn queue), but only after a one-day spike proves that pasting and submitting into the real CLI and matching the UserPromptSubmit prompt really works, since "verified delivery" is the whole premise and the shared I-01 primitive carries all the risk.
feasibility.loom_design:
FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE DESIGN (facts, with sources)
- The CLI's own queue is NOT an "after the turn" queue. Documented (code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode, "Queue messages while Claude works"): a message typed while tool calls run is passed to Claude "as soon as those tool calls finish, within the same turn"; only commands and `!` shell lines wait for the turn end. Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+X Ctrl+S (chat:sendNow, v2.1.275+) sends now; Up takes queued messages back for editing. So Loom's real differentiators are (a) composing for a session you are not looking at, (b) true next-turn semantics ("when this finishes, do X"), (c) edit/remove before delivery with a Loom-side verified outcome. Persistence is a weaker differentiator: Quit stops every session, so a persisted item for a stopped session can only go out after an explicit Resume.
- Pieces Loom already has: (1) an ordered, bounded write path per live run: TerminalInputQueue (4 MiB, ordered, closes atomically), registered by run id in TerminalInputGate (Sources/LoomCore/TerminalInputGate.swift, TerminalInputQueue.swift). Every live run keeps its TerminalSurface and queue even when not selected (ConversationController.entries); ended runs keep only a snapshot. (2) Turn boundaries from hooks: ClaudeHookStateTracker (ClaudeHook.swift ~L540-790) yields atPrompt (SessionStart), working (UserPromptSubmit), turnComplete (Stop, with background_tasks counts), waitingForApproval, waitingForInput (registry "idle", Notification idle_prompt/agent_needs_input/elicitation_dialog), failed. The registry watch (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift receiveRegistry) covers the Esc-interrupt case where Claude fires no Stop. (3) Precedent for programmatic input: ConversationController.typeForEvidence (evidence only) and LoomTerminalView.insertDroppedFiles -> pasteText (bracketed-paste aware). The D-40 start path passes a first message as the documented positional prompt after `--` (ProviderLaunchProfile.ClaudeOpening). (4) Deletion hooks: ConversationForgetters (ConversationDeletion.swift) and TerminalInputGate.close(runID:) at deletion step 1.
- Gaps found in code: (a) ClaudeHookEvent parses `prompt` only to set promptIsSynthetic and keeps nothing, so "delivered when UserPromptSubmit shows the text" needs a small addition: a digest of the normalised prompt (never the text) in the event. (b) The hub stream is bufferingNewest(1) (SessionEventHub.subscribe), so a quick Stop -> UserPromptSubmit pair can be collapsed; the delivery trigger must not ride the UI frame stream. (c) AgentActivity.waitingForInput conflates "idle for a minute" with "Claude asked a question" (notificationActivity maps idle_prompt, agent_needs_input and elicitation_dialog to one case), so it is not a safe delivery signal on its own. (d) The fake provider's UserPromptSubmit hook carries only prompt_id (loom-fake-provider/main.swift ~L221); tests need a `prompt` field. (e) TerminalSurface.send cannot tell keyboard bytes from programmatic ones, and TerminalInputQueue.lastAcceptedInput counts both.

LIGHTEST VERSION THAT FITS (the "adopt-light" shape once the spike passes)
1. Data (LoomCore). A `prompt_queue` table in the catalog, added on open like ensureActivityColumn/ensureOriginColumns (no schema-version bump, so older builds still open the file): (id, session_id, position, text, state, created_at, attempt_at). `secure_delete = ON` is already set per connection, so a deleted session leaves no prompt bytes. Register a ConversationForgetters entry that deletes its rows, and cancel items at deletion step "stopping" (contract section 8, point 2). Bounds: at most 8 items per session, 16 KiB per item, 64 overall; beyond that the add is refused visibly. A memory-only queue is the fallback if the user does not want prompt text in the catalog.
2. Delivery coordinator: a new LoomCore actor `PromptDeliveryCoordinator`, one file, owned by SessionRuntime. It is fed directly from ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive after tracker.receive applied the event (ordered, inside the run's transition, after updateProviderWorkState), NOT from the hub. It reacts to three inputs only: Stop/atPrompt (candidate boundary), UserPromptSubmit (verification), SessionEnd/run end/delete (cancel). No timers except two one-shot tasks per delivering run: a ~400 ms settle after Stop (a CLI-queued message or a background-subagent hand-back may start another turn at once; if a UserPromptSubmit arrives in the window, wait for the next Stop) and an ~8 s verification deadline after the write.
3. State machine per item: queued -> sending (bytes accepted by the run's input queue) -> delivered (a non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit of this run whose prompt digest equals the item's) | not confirmed (deadline passed, no match; NEVER auto-retried; the strip says "Check the terminal" and offers Retry or Discard) | failed (input queue refused: closed/overflow/writeFailed; text kept) | held, with a reason shown ("needs approval", "you are typing here", "session is working", "last turn failed", "session not running"). Only the head item is in flight, and the next goes after the previous is verified, so ordering is Loom's, not the TUI's.
4. Deliverable gate, checked at the Stop event and never by polling: run live and the card's active conversation; provider state reliable; activity is turnComplete with pendingProviderWorkCount == 0 (or atPrompt; waitingForInput only when the tracker records that it came from the registry "idle" or an idle_prompt after a turn, which needs one small field, lastNotificationType, on ClaudeSessionStatus); never waitingForApproval, failed, unknown, or an open-session approval pending; the user has not typed into this terminal since the last turn boundary. In user words: deliver when the card reads Ready/Finished.
5. Typing guard (LoomTerminal). TerminalSurface already sees every user byte in send(source:data:). Add a flag "user bytes other than a bare Return since the last UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart", and make programmatic submission a separate entry point (`TerminalSurface.submitQueuedPrompt(_:)`, using view.pasteText so bracketed paste is honoured, then Return) that does not set it. If the flag is set the item is held with "you are typing here" and the strip offers Send now. It is a heuristic (history recall, Ctrl+U and menus are invisible to it), which is why the hold and the visible not-confirmed outcome both exist.
6. Stopped sessions. A queued item on a session with no live run shows "waits for Resume". "Resume and send" uses the documented positional prompt (the D-40 mechanism), so no paste is involved and the UserPromptSubmit digest still verifies it. It is an explicit user click, never automatic after Quit or relaunch (no daemon, user authority).
7. Send now on a Working session (not approval) pastes and submits at once, which makes it an ordinary CLI type-ahead message (mid-turn delivery, documented). Do not synthesise Ctrl+X Ctrl+S in v1 (it can move work to the background since 2.1.281).
8. Not in v1: the global quick-capture hotkey (Loom has no global hotkey today; it needs Carbon RegisterEventHotKey plus a floating window; a menu bar item entry or Cmd+Shift+Q on the selected card is cheaper), drag reorder (Move up/down in the row menu instead), slash and bang items (UserPromptSubmit may not fire for local commands such as /model, /status, /clear, so "delivered" cannot be proven; refuse them or label them "sent, cannot be confirmed" until measured), attachments and images, per-item model overrides.
9. Where the code goes: LoomCore (SessionCatalog+PromptQueue.swift, PromptDeliveryCoordinator.swift, digest field in ClaudeHookEvent, lastNotificationType); LoomTerminal (TerminalSurface entry point and typing flag, a controller-level submit intent); LoomCatalogUI (PromptQueueStrip.swift, CatalogModel+PromptQueue.swift, a ConversationIntents method, a queue/draft mark on SessionListEntry). Dependencies still point down and LoomCore stays UI-free.

WHAT WOULD BREAK A PRINCIPLE, AND THE GUARD
- Polling: a "retry until Ready" loop or a periodic queue scan. Guard: only hook-path callbacks plus two one-shot tasks; nothing runs while the table is empty.
- Resources: an unbounded queue, or prompt bodies held in memory for every session. Guard: the caps above; bodies are read from SQLite only for the head item at delivery and for a visible strip.
- Accurate status: calling a PTY write "delivered". Guard: delivered only on a matching UserPromptSubmit digest, otherwise "not confirmed"; no blind retry (contract section 7: "on ambiguous delivery, no blind automatic retry").
- Predictability: answering a dialog by accident (plan approval, AskUserQuestion, folder trust, /resume picker, half-typed input). Guard: Stop-edge delivery only, approval/unknown/failed refused, the typing guard, and the not-confirmed outcome that leaves the text visible in the terminal.
- Authority: any agent writing to the queue. Guard: items come only from the user's own composer; this is the safe first half of D-43's channel, but agent-originated items (loom:open-session style) would need a per-send approval and are out of scope.
- CLI-update resilience: depends on bracketed paste and Return semantics of the TUI and on UserPromptSubmit carrying `prompt` (documented in the hooks reference). Guard: verification fails closed to "not confirmed"; a cli_compat_warning-style journal entry when digests never match across several sends; no CLI pinning.
- Ownership: nothing new is spawned and there is no daemon. Quit keeps items as drafts and says so in the existing QuitConfirmation text ("3 queued prompts are kept; sessions stop").

REVISED COST (for this codebase)
Spike: S (about 1 day). Phase 1: M-L, dominated by UI and tests, not core logic. Rough scope: store + migration + forget hook (~250 lines), coordinator + event plumbing + tracker fields (~400), surface entry point and typing flag (~120), strip UI + composer + row menus + card mark + quit text (~500), tests (digest and ordering on the fake provider with scripted hooks, deletion, input-queue refusal, quit/restore, one captured real-CLI transcript for paste/submit) (~500), docs (ARCHITECTURE section 3 flow, contract section 7 note, DECISIONS entry, DESIGN element). If I-01 is not built first, the paste/submit/verify primitive belongs to I-02, so I-01 + I-02 are one L effort. The global hotkey would add another S-M.

It shows only when the session has items. Collapsed: one line, "2 queued · next sends when this finishes", with a chevron. Expanded: up to 8 compact rows, each with a one-line preview, a state tag (Queued / Sending / Delivered / Not confirmed / Held: needs approval, or you are typing here), and a row menu (Edit, Move up, Move down, Send now, Remove, Retry on a not-confirmed item). Delivered rows fade out after a few seconds; not-confirmed and failed rows stay until dismissed. Adding: Cmd+Shift+Q (or "Queue Prompt…" in the card's context menu and the header action menu) opens a small multi-line sheet or popover for the selected or chosen session; Return queues, Shift+Return is a newline, Esc cancels. feasibility.title: Per-session prompt queue with verified delivery

feasibility.one_line: Worth building only as a small, optional helper on a verified send path (paste with a bracketed-paste gate, separate Enter, a UserPromptSubmit receipt), and two real-CLI spikes must first decide the shape: Claude's documented Ctrl+G external-editor hook that nobody in the research saw, versus direct PTY injection. feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS FROM THE CODE AND DOCS (observed)
- Loom has no way yet to put app-originated text into a session. The only app-side write is the evidence hook `ConversationController.typeForEvidence`, which calls `TerminalSurface.send` (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/ConversationController.swift). Every write goes through one ordered `TerminalInputQueue` (4 MiB cap, visible rejection, no silent drops; Sources/LoomCore/TerminalInputQueue.swift). `TerminalInputGate` closes it for a deleting or stopping run, so a late composer send is refused visibly.
- Image paste is already handled. `LoomTerminalView.paste` forwards an image-only clipboard as Ctrl+V, and dropped files insert quoted paths (Sources/LoomTerminal/TerminalSurface.swift ~l.362-452). Claude documents Ctrl+V as inserting an `[Image #N]` chip. The overlay's "image becomes a file path" feature adds almost nothing on top of that.
- Receipt plumbing half exists. `ClaudeHookEvent` parses UserPromptSubmit, `prompt_id` and a `promptIsSynthetic` flag, but it throws the prompt text away (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeHook.swift). `ClaudeSessionAdapter` handles `.userPromptSubmit` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~l.268). `ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive` sets Working. `SessionViewState` and `SessionEventChange` (SessionEventHub.swift) carry no "a prompt was accepted" signal.
- The hook helper runs with `timeout: 1` and is synchronous (ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings), not the 30 s default in the debate note. UserPromptSubmit fires before Claude processes the prompt, so on an idle session the latency is tens of ms. The risk is not a slow hook but the session state at send time.
- "Waiting for you" cannot tell a prompt apart from a dialog. `ClaudeHookStateTracker.notificationActivity` maps idle_prompt, agent_needs_input and elicitation_dialog all to `.waitingForInput`. Only `.atPrompt` (SessionStart) and `.turnComplete` (Stop) reliably mean the input box is up. A paste plus Enter into an AskUserQuestion or plan dialog could answer it wrongly. That is worse than an unsent draft.
- SwiftTerm `pasteText` only wraps the text in 200~/201~ when the program has enabled mode 2004 (`Terminal.bracketedPasteMode`). Without it, newlines go out as `\r`, which submits every line. The composer must refuse to send unless `bracketedPasteMode` is true, and must sanitise its own text rather than rely on `pasteText`'s `allowUnsafe` fallback (AppleKittyClipboard.swift l.136-144).
- Claude 2.1.300 docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode, fetched via tinyfish): Ctrl+G or Ctrl+X Ctrl+E "opens in default text editor"; the `v` key in the transcript viewer opens `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR`. Messages typed while Claude works are queued and shown grey until sent; Ctrl+Enter sends them at once. Multi-line paste is a documented input method. Issue #18990 (closed) showed Ctrl+G once auto-detected IDEs and ignored `$EDITOR`; current behaviour is unverified.
- Slash commands that Claude runs locally (/clear, /model, ...) fire no UserPromptSubmit. A receipt timer on such a draft would false-alarm.

DESIGN (lightest version)
1. Draft store. `ComposerDrafts` in LoomCatalogUI, in memory only: `[sessionID: String]`, each draft capped at about 100 KB, at most 32 drafts, least recently used evicted. Plain text. Dropped by the existing `ConversationForgetting` hook on deletion (ConversationDeletion.swift) and on Quit. Keep it memory-only because a persisted draft is conversation content that contract §8 deletion would then have to purge and verify. Extend `QuitConfirmation` (SessionNavigation.swift) with "N unsent drafts" so a quit cannot silently lose text.
2. Overlay. A ZStack child in `DetailContent`, floating over the bottom of `TerminalHost`, with opacity-only appearance (DESIGN.md Motion row: a height change would resize the PTY). It is an `NSTextView` wrapper that exists only while open: no timers, nothing drawn when closed or hidden. State is `CatalogModel.composer: ComposerState?` plus a menu item in the Edit or Session menu (a free key such as Cmd+E; check the menu table in UI-MAP.md l.85). Esc closes and keeps the draft. It can open at any state, because writing a draft during Needs approval is useful. Only Send and Insert are gated.
3. Two actions, to keep the zero-risk mode first-class:
   - Insert: bracketed paste only, no Enter; the user reads it in the TUI and presses Enter. Allowed whenever a live run owns the terminal and `bracketedPasteMode` is true.
   - Send: paste, then a single-shot `Task.sleep` (about 150-300 ms, to be set by the spike), then one `\r`, all through the run's `TerminalInputQueue` so order against keystrokes is preserved. Allowed only when activity is `.atPrompt` or `.turnComplete`, hooks are reliable (`providerWorkStateIsReliable`), no approval is pending and `bracketedPasteMode` is true. A draft starting with `!`, `&` or `/` is Insert-only: `!` and `&` switch Claude's input mode, and `/` commands may produce no hook. While the session is Working, Send is disabled; do not claim a receipt for Claude's own queue, whose UserPromptSubmit timing is unknown. This is where I-01 (the shared send primitive) and the Loom-side queue idea connect.
   - Sanitiser: strip ESC and all C0 controls except LF and TAB, normalise CR to LF, remove any 201~ sequence.
4. Receipt, event-driven. Extend `ClaudeHookEvent` to keep a bounded digest of the prompt (SHA-256 of the first and last 256 characters plus the length), never the text. Publish a new `SessionEventChange.promptSubmitted(PromptReceipt)` from `ClaudeSessionAdapter` next to `markProviderUsed`. The change is state-light: `SessionViewState` gets only `lastPrompt: (sequence, digest, at)`. Mind the hub's equal-frame suppression and the SidebarRenderTests hot path: do not feed this into card rows. The composer arms a single 5 s timer at the Enter write. Digest match gives "Submitted". Timer expiry gives "Not confirmed yet - your text may be in the prompt; press Enter in the terminal", with the draft kept. A late match upgrades that to Submitted, so slow hooks never leave a permanent false alarm. Never auto-retry the Enter. A second Enter on an already-submitted, now-empty prompt is harmless. No polling anywhere.
5. Where the receipt shows. Inside the overlay and as transient header text in the existing fixed-height row (like `PreparingNotice` in DetailView.swift), so no layout shift. Not on sidebar cards.

PREFERRED SHAPE IF SPIKE 1 PASSES: a "compose bridge" through the documented Ctrl+G
Set `VISUAL` and `EDITOR` in the run's env (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift ~l.145-153 already sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, LOOM_HOOK_*, LOOM_CLI) to a small subcommand of loom-hook: `$LOOM_CLI compose <file>`. This follows the existing split in Sources/loom-hook/main.swift, where arguments mean the agent-facing command. The helper connects to the authenticated control socket (the `loom-hook open` pattern, OpenSessionControlServer) and blocks. Loom shows the overlay bound to that file with the CLI's current prompt prefilled. Done writes the file and exits 0, and Claude loads it back into its own input. There is no PTY injection, no readiness guess, and the CLI itself decides whether it is at a prompt. Vim mode, slash completion and queueing stay in the CLI. The helper is a child of claude inside the run scope, so Stop and Quit already own and kill it. Guard against the helper capturing unrelated `$EDITOR` calls (an agent's `git commit` in a Bash tool inherits the env): recognise Claude's prompt temp file, else exec the user's original editor, passed as `LOOM_ORIGINAL_EDITOR`. Make this an opt-in Setting because it changes what Ctrl+G does.

BOUNDS: draft 100 KB x 32, one overlay at a time, one 5 s single-shot timer per send, digest not text, hook payload already capped at 1 MiB (ClaudeHookClient.maximumPayloadByteCount). Idle or stopped records have no terminal, so the composer is unavailable there; a later "Resume with this prompt" can reuse the documented launch path that takes the prompt after the options (open-session flow in ARCHITECTURE.md ~l.168).

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A PRINCIPLE VIOLATION, AND THE AVOIDANCE
- False success: reporting "submitted" on a PTY write. Avoided by the digest receipt and a neutral "not confirmed" wording.
- Predictability: Enter landing in a dialog. Avoided by the Insert/Send split, the `.atPrompt`/`.turnComplete`-only gate and the bracketed-paste check.
- Resources: a resident editor, a file index or a draft timer. Avoided: the editor exists only while open, no index, no timers beyond the single shot.
- Fluency: auto-opening on Stop would steal focus, and keystrokes meant for another terminal would land in the overlay. Recommend never auto-focusing. At most offer a passive affordance.
- CLI resilience: per-version delay tables as Warp has. Avoided: one delay, plus the receipt as the drift signal (receipts that stop arriving surface as a diagnostics note, like the existing hook-silence watchdog).
- Contract: the terminal stays the real CLI and the overlay is optional. This is the "light helper" variant, not the do-not-build replacement composer in power-user-workflows.md. It needs the user's explicit acknowledgement, because the contract text says the terminal is never replaced.
- Deletion: persisted drafts or saved images would add a deletion obligation. Avoided by memory-only drafts and no image files.

COST (honest for this codebase)
- Light version (overlay, Insert/Send, sanitiser, draft store, receipt, tests, doc updates): M (about 1 slice). Pieces: TerminalSurface paste/send API plus sanitiser, S. Hook digest, hub change and adapter publish, S-M. Overlay, model state, menu item, header text, M. The repo's tests, evidence run and doc requirements (ARCHITECTURE, UI-MAP, DESIGN) add a meaningful share.
- Compose bridge on top of the light version: +M (helper subcommand, control-socket request type, env wiring, setting, EDITOR fallback).
- Full original idea (@file completion, image files, persisted drafts, auto-open): L, and several of those parts break the principles above.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Shortcut (for example Cmd+E) opens a bottom-anchored panel over the selected session's terminal. It is a rounded Surface.panel card, about 30-40 % of the terminal height, 12 pt inset, fade-in only, no resize of the PTY. Contents: a plain multi-line mono NSTextView, a footer with a character count, an Insert button, a primary Send button, and a one-line state text.

State text, in order of precedence:
- "Waiting for approval - Insert or Send is off"
- "Working - Insert only"
- "Sent - waiting for Claude" (neutral, no spinner)
- "Submitted" (fades after a few seconds)
- "Not confirmed yet - press Enter in the terminal; your text is kept"

Esc closes the panel and keeps the draft. A small "Draft" dot sits in the header chip row of that session only, not on sidebar cards. Return does nothing special: Cmd+Return sends and Return inserts a newline. A `!`, `&` or `/` first character shows "Insert only" with a one-clause reason.

If the compose bridge passes the spike, Ctrl+G in the terminal (or a Loom menu item that sends ^G) opens the same panel prefilled from the CLI's prompt file, with a single Done button in place of Insert and Send.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources (pass): memory-only drafts, NSTextView only while open, a single-shot timer, no index, no polling. The hook already arrives, so the digest costs one hash per prompt.
Predictability (risk, mitigated): the TUI input state is not directly observable. Gate on `.atPrompt`/`.turnComplete`, hooks reliable and `bracketedPasteMode`; Insert is the zero-risk default; Needs approval and Working disable Send.
Accurate status (pass, if the digest receipt is implemented): "submitted" only on a matching UserPromptSubmit; the neutral "not confirmed" and the late upgrade avoid false alarms. A digest mismatch or a hook-silence state is shown as unconfirmed, never as failure.
Fluency (risk): no auto-open and no confirmations; the optional overlay adds one shortcut. Auto-open on Stop is a focus-steal hazard.
Modularity (pass): the send/receipt primitive is shared with I-01 and the queue and diff-comment ideas; the overlay is a thin UI on it; the helper subcommand follows the existing loom-hook split.
CLI-update resilience (risk, bounded): bracketed paste, mode 2004 and `!`/`&`/`/` input behaviour are TUI behaviours, not a contract. The receipt turns breakage into a visible signal. The Ctrl+G route uses a documented key and `$VISUAL`, but its IDE auto-detection history needs verification.
Process ownership (pass): writes go to the Loom-owned PTY only; the compose helper lives in the run scope.
User authority (pass): every send is the user's own action in the focused app; nothing crosses sessions.
Contract: the "terminal never replaced" rule is only touched by an optional helper; keep it opt-in and say so.
Deletion contract: pass only with memory-only drafts and no saved images.
feasibility.value_reason: Real but modest for this user. They write long ticket prompts across several sessions, and a multi-line editor with per-session drafts is a comfort gain. But the CLI already offers Ctrl+G, multi-line paste, Ctrl+V images and message queueing, so the new value is mostly Loom-side (a draft that survives a session switch, and a verified receipt). The receipt matters more as foundation for non-focused sends (queue, cross-session, side-chat or diff comments) than for a focused overlay where the user sees the TUI react. If v2 becomes chat-centred, the composer is rebuilt as the main input, so the reusable asset is the send primitive plus receipt, not the overlay. Not on the user's stated wish list; the research's "wish list" claim in warp.md is the researcher's inference.
depends_on: I-01: the shared send primitive (bracketed paste, separate Enter, readiness gate); this idea should not carry its own copy
UserPromptSubmit digest receipt (small hook and hub change owned by this idea or I-01)
optional: the compose-bridge helper subcommand if spike 1 passes
experiments: SPIKE 1, Ctrl+G bridge (decides Variant A). In an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with a throwaway project, run Claude 2.1.300 in a PTY (loom-probe pattern: Sources/loom-probe/ClaudeQ1Experiment.swift) with VISUAL and EDITOR pointing at a script that logs argv, cwd and the file contents, then rewrites the file. Questions: (a) does Ctrl+G honour VISUAL/EDITOR or pick an IDE; (b) what is in the temp file; (c) is the edited text loaded into the input box or auto-submitted; (d) does the TUI use the alternate screen, and does Loom's screen capture and resize cope; (e) does the editor child land in the run scope; (f) do Bash-tool subprocesses inherit the env and call the editor (git commit without -m). Decides: if (a) and (c) pass, build Variant A and make direct injection optional; if Ctrl+G ignores the env, fall back to Variant B.

SPIKE 2, direct paste plus delayed Enter with receipt (decides the Send delay and gates). Same isolated setup with real Claude, driving `TerminalInputQueue` bytes. Matrix: idle at prompt and just after Stop; a 100 KB multi-line text; text beginning with `!`, `&` and `/`; while Working (what does Claude's own queue do, and when does UserPromptSubmit fire for a queued message); with a permission dialog; with an AskUserQuestion or plan dialog (does `.waitingForInput` plus bracketed paste plus Enter answer it); right after SessionStart before mode 2004 is on (does `bracketedPasteMode` flip as the gate expects). Measure the minimum safe gap between the paste and Enter and the hook latency distribution. Decides: the delay constant, whether `.waitingForInput` is Insert-only, and whether Working may Send at all. feasibility.one_line: Most of this is already built (Ctrl+V on an image-only clipboard, quoted-path drops via bracketed paste, a text-input client for dictation), so adopt only a one-time hands-on checklist plus the small fixes it finds, and treat /voice microphone attribution as the one real unknown.
feasibility.loom_design:
OBSERVED STATE (code, not inference). The audit is not a blank slate; Loom already has the three mechanisms, in LoomTerminalView (Sources/LoomTerminal/TerminalSurface.swift, ~L362-452):
1) Image paste: `paste(_:)` checks `NSPasteboard.general`; if there is no `.string` and `canReadObject(forClasses:[NSImage.self])`, it does `send(data:[0x16])` (Ctrl+V), else falls to SwiftTerm `super.paste`. Claude Code's documented image-paste binding is Ctrl+V on macOS (Cmd+V only in iTerm2), so Loom matches the docs. Menu path: Edit > Paste uses `NSText.paste(_:)` (AppDelegate.swift:702), which reaches the first responder.
2) Drag-drop: `registerForDraggedTypes([.fileURL])` (TerminalSurface.init, L168), `draggingEntered` accepts only when file URLs exist, `performDragOperation` -> `insertDroppedFiles` -> `quotedPaths` (POSIX single-quote quoting, control bytes escaped) -> `pasteText` (bracketed paste when the app enabled ?2004h, no Enter). Pinned by `Tests/LoomTerminalTests/TerminalSurfaceTests.swift` `finderDropUsesBracketedPasteQueueWithoutEnter` and `TerminalProductTests.multipleDroppedPathsAreShellQuotedWithoutEnter`. Documented in design/UI-MAP.md:77 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:39.
3) Dictation: the vendored SwiftTerm TerminalView conforms to NSTextInputClient (Vendor/SwiftTerm/Sources/SwiftTerm/Mac/MacTerminalView.swift: insertText L2447, setMarkedText L2557 with a marked-text overlay whose comment names "dictation hypotheses", hasMarkedText/selectedRange/firstRect L3128-3200, `extension TerminalView: NSTextInputClient`). So system dictation (Fn-Fn) and third-party dictation that inserts through the input system should land as committed text via the same path as typing. Not yet confirmed on screen in Loom.
4) Large paste: `pasteText` goes through the single ordered TerminalInputQueue (LoomCore/TerminalInputQueue.swift) capped at `TerminalSurfaceLimits.pendingInputBytes` = 4 MiB, with visible `onInputError` on overflow (never silent loss).
WHAT IS GENUINELY UNVERIFIED (this is the audit's real content):
a) Mixed clipboards: a Finder-copied image file or a browser/Preview "Copy Image" carries a string flavour (filename or URL) next to the image, so `pasteboard.string(forType:.string) == nil` is false and Loom pastes text, not Ctrl+V. Whether Claude Code would have accepted the image in that case is the test. If yes and it matters, widen the rule to "has image data and the string is only a filename or URL" (a few lines in `paste`).
b) Image-file paths: Claude Code recognises a pasted image path as an attachment; whether it does so for Loom's single-quoted form (vs backslash-escaped, Terminal.app style) is untested. If not, change `quotedPaths` to the CLI's preferred escaping for Claude sessions only (a one-function change, existing test updated).
c) Non-file drags (browser image drag, Mail attachment promises) are refused (`draggingEntered` returns []), so the drop bounces. Fixing this means writing temp files, which is a new feature with cleanup and ownership cost; recommend NOT doing it, only documenting it.
d) /voice (documented: hold/tap Space after enabling; native mic capture by the claude process). Neither Info.plist from scripts/package-dev-app.sh (app L107-126, LoomRunHost.app L86-100, LSBackgroundOnly) has NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, and a grep finds no microphone or entitlement strings anywhere in Sources/scripts. The claude process runs as a descendant of the bundled LoomRunHost.app inside Loom's run scope, so which bundle TCC treats as responsible for the microphone request, and whether the missing usage string makes the prompt fail silently, is unknown. This is the only item that could need a packaging change (add NSMicrophoneUsageDescription to one or both plists; maybe the audio-input entitlement under hardened runtime, `--options runtime` is used at package-dev-app.sh:130-143).
DESIGN: no new runtime component. Deliverable = (i) a short manual checklist (screenshot Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4 then Cmd+V; Finder copy of a PNG then Cmd+V; drag a file with spaces/apostrophes/Turkish characters; drag a screenshot thumbnail; 200 KB and 3 MB text paste; Fn-Fn dictation including a Turkish phrase; /voice) recorded as an evidence note, run once per Claude Code minor release only if drift is suspected; (ii) only the fixes (a), (b), (d) the checklist proves necessary; (iii) one regression test per fix in the existing LoomTerminalTests suites (the test harness already injects bytes and hashes the child's input, so fidelity is checkable without UI). Triggers: user events only (paste, drop, key); no polling, no new watchers, nothing drawn or kept when hidden. Bounds: unchanged 4 MiB input queue, visible error on overflow. 'Verified' status: do not add 'image attached' indicators; Claude Code's own [Image #N] chip is the receipt, Loom claims nothing.
PRINCIPLE VIOLATIONS TO AVOID: a Loom-side image/clipboard watcher or thumbnail strip (resource use, duplicate of the CLI chip); temp-file creation for non-file drags (ownership, cleanup, deletion dry-run scope); an embedded voice/ASR stack or hosted dependency (Happy's voice agent at ~$0.01/min via ElevenLabs is exactly what to avoid); pinning behaviour to one CLI version (keep keystroke Ctrl+V, which is the documented binding, and verify by hands-on check instead of a version table).
feasibility.ui_sketch: None. No new UI. At most, if /voice needs a plist change, one line in docs/Help or Settings notes that microphone access is granted to Loom (macOS shows its own system prompt). Dictation and paste keep looking like typing in the terminal; Claude Code's own [Image #N] chip is the only feedback.
feasibility.principle_check: resources: pass (zero new runtime cost, event-driven only). predictability: pass, the rules are already deterministic and pinned by tests; risk only if the mixed-clipboard rule gets clever. accurate status: pass, Loom claims nothing about attachment; the CLI chip is the receipt. fluency: pass, this removes friction (silent text paste instead of image). modularity: pass, all changes stay inside LoomTerminalView/quotedPaths and, if needed, two plist templates in package-dev-app.sh. CLI-update resilience: pass with care; relies on the documented Ctrl+V binding, no version pins; risk that Claude Code changes the image-paste key or path-detection, so the checklist (not a table) is the guard. ownership: pass; no new processes or files; temp-file drag support would break this, so excluded. user authority: pass; nothing cross-session. Contract: terminal remains the real CLI; no custom composer.
feasibility.value_reason: Screenshots into Claude are a daily habit for a heavy agentic developer (UI bugs, error dialogs, ticket screenshots), so a silent text-instead-of-image failure would be costly, but the common case (image-only screenshot clipboard, Finder drag) is already handled and tested; the remaining payoff is edge cases plus a possible /voice unlock, and the user's notes mention neither voice nor image paste as a wish. Value is correctness insurance, not a new capability.

(2) Finder Cmd+C on a PNG, and Safari/Preview 'Copy Image', then Cmd+V; decides whether the string-nil condition in LoomTerminalView.paste must be widened.

Drag a PNG, a file with spaces/apostrophes/Turkish characters, and a screenshot thumbnail into the terminal; check whether Claude Code attaches the image from the single-quoted bracketed paste; decides whether quotedPaths needs the backslash-escaped form for Claude sessions.

Fn-Fn system dictation in an idle Claude prompt (English and Turkish), watching the marked-text overlay then commit; decides whether SwiftTerm's NSTextInputClient is enough (expected yes) or needs a patch under patches/.

Also confirm /voice exists and is enabled on the installed CLI (claude 2.1.300 here; --help does not list it).

If a browser-image or Mail-attachment drag is refused today, do you accept 'documented, not supported' rather than Loom writing temp files for it?
