feasibility.one_line: Build it as a read-only transcript view that reuses the subagent panel's tail/feed/model machinery, shipped first for sessions with no terminal (stopped, stale, after relaunch) and then live, with no composer, no cross-session search and no hook-text dependency. The plumbing is mostly there; the real cost is a faithful main-session decoder, markdown/diff rendering and backward paging, so L stays honest.
feasibility.loom_design:
FIT: the subagent panel (FB4-5) already is the pattern. SubagentTranscriptLocation (realpath inside projects, O_NOFOLLOW, regular file of this user), SubagentTranscriptTail (offset+inode, whole lines only, partial line held back, shrink/replace restarts, cold window), SubagentTranscriptFeed (one vnode source, 200 ms coalescing = at most 5 reads/s, utility queue, AsyncStream, stop() returns at once), SubagentTranscriptModel (feed exists only while onScreen && windowVisible, generation counters, ring), and DetailContent swapping the terminal for the transcript in place. I-05 generalises these to the main session. CORRECTION to the idea text: Usage uses one directory-level FSEvents stream (UsageTranscriptWatcher); for one visible file the per-file vnode feed is lighter than a second FSEvents stream, so reuse the feed, add no stream.

NEW OR CHANGED PIECES (no new target, no schema change, no new dependency):
1. LoomCore, locate: generalise SubagentTranscriptLocation to also accept projects/<folder>/<uuid>.jsonl. The main session's path is not stored anywhere today (ClaudeHookEvent.transcriptPath is parsed at ClaudeHook.swift:442 but only used for subagent meta). Resolve on open, off the main actor: prefer the hook path while a run is live, else ClaudeTranscriptEffort.transcript(conversationID:projectsDirectory:) (folder scan by name, newest mtime wins), with SessionRuntime.claudeProjectsDirectory() as the root. The path is derived, never persisted, so there is nothing to purge on permanent deletion.
2. LoomCore, reader: generalise SubagentTranscriptTail into a TranscriptTail (keep the subagent API as a thin wrapper so its 27 tests stay). Add readBackward(maxBytes) (chunked reverse newline scan from a known offset) for "Earlier turns". Raise the main-session line cap (128 KiB is too small for tool results and Writes), and replace today's silent skip with a counted placeholder (skipped record, N KiB, offset), because a faithful view must not drop turns silently. Cold open reads about 1 MiB from the end (T3's bounded cold open is about 75 rows / 1 MiB), never the whole file.
3. LoomCore, decoder: ConversationParser beside SubagentTranscriptParser. Same technique: memmem gate (attachments and other bulky record types never decoded), a narrow lenient Decodable that never names toolUseResult, and per-block Lossy decoding. Emits records with timestamp, uuid/parentUuid, message.id, stop_reason and a source locator (offset, length). Kinds: userPrompt (+ image count, no base64), assistantText (full text, larger clip than 4 KiB, with a "show more" fetched on demand), toolUse (name, main argument; inline payload kept only for Edit/MultiEdit/Write diffs, AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode), toolResult (first lines, line count, byte count, isError), thought(ms) (the existing parser already relies on the CLI writing only a duration), system notes (compact boundary, API error, local command) and subagent calls (Agent/Task). Anything unrecognised becomes .unknown(type, bytes): a collapsed raw row whose bytes are fetched on expand. First sighting of an unknown type or shape is reported once through the existing ClaudeRegistryDiagnostics-style path (log notice + cli_compat_warning journal event), and a count shows in the view the way the Usage page shows "N usage records could not be understood".
4. LoomCore, turn builder (pure, fixture-tested per CLI version): folds records into turns (user prompt, steps, final text), pairs tool_use with tool_result by tool_use_id, groups runs of tool rows ("Ran 4 commands, read 3 files", "Worked for 22s" from first/last timestamps). Order is file order plus parentUuid/timestamps, never insertion time (Orca's #23851 "prompt after response" came from optimistic inserts; a read-only view has none). Whether abandoned rewind branches need a parentUuid leaf-chain walk is decided by the spike.
5. LoomCore, raw bodies: ConversationBodyReader preads one line by (offset, length), re-parses only the wanted block, clips at 256 KiB and marks truncation. Expand = one bounded read; the ring holds only clipped summaries. Never expand-all by default (OpenChamber #2267/#4607).
6. LoomCatalogUI: ConversationViewModel copies SubagentTranscriptModel's gating exactly (feed only while onScreen && windowVisible, stop on selection change/hide/deletion, drop batches from a stale generation). Memory bound: last ~60 turns plus a byte cap per view, one view live at a time, older turns prepended via readBackward. CatalogModel gets a memory-only per-session mode (.terminal/.conversation), like viewedSubagent. DetailContent gets a branch beside the subagent-panel and ended-screen branches, and ConversationDetail (the facts-only record view) is replaced by the transcript with the facts demoted. The live terminal stays with its controller, running, only not shown, so nothing above it resizes.
7. Rendering: LazyVStack of turn rows (or an NSTableView host if the prototype shows SwiftUI cannot prepend rows without a scroll jump; the app already hosts AppKit views, EndedScreenView is an NSTextView). Markdown: Claude answers are lists, fences and tables, which Text(AttributedString(markdown:)) does not render as blocks, so write a small block parser (paragraph, list, heading, quote, fence, table) with inline spans through AttributedString, cached per record and built only for visible rows. Do not add swift-markdown/cmark-gfm for v1. Edit/Write diffs are computed from the tool_use input (old_string/new_string), not from toolUseResult.structuredPatch, which the lean decoder deliberately never reads. Links are never opened and images never loaded (the subagent panel's rule). Selection is per row only, as in the subagent panel; add a Copy turn action.

TRIGGERS (events only): user switches the mode, selects an ended or stale session in conversation mode, a run starts/ends (liveStates), the vnode event on the open file, window visibility. One cold read, then the feed runs only while the view is on screen and the file can still grow. A stopped session's file is read once and its feed stopped; a Resume that appends to the file restarts the feed from the run-start edge. No timer, no poll.

STATUS AUTHORITY: the header pill and cards stay hook/registry driven (D-45). The view never infers Working or Finished from the file. "Working…" renders only when row.indicator says so, and the running turn collapses to the latest ~5 steps plus "+N more" (OpenChamber). JSONL is written per content block or message rather than per token (granularity still to confirm), so there is no partial streaming text; say so in the UI.

HOOK TEXT: Stop.last_assistant_message is parsed (ClaudeHook.swift:445) and kept in ClaudeSessionStatus.lastAssistantMessage (:768), but it is not on the SessionViewState/hub path. With a continuous tail, the vnode event delivers the final text a few ms after Stop, so it is NOT needed for v1. It is useful only as a bounded fallback ("transcript is behind", shown marked after ~2 s) and as the sidebar-subtitle source, which is a different idea. The idea's rule "final text from the hook" fits a poll-at-Stop design, not a tail.

SLICES: A) locate + backward-capable tail + parser + turn builder + read-only view for sessions with no terminal, with fixtures (this is where the value is highest: today the ended screen is memory-only, 16 screens and 4 MiB, and after a relaunch a stopped session shows only the facts grid). B) live tail + the Terminal/Chat toggle for running sessions + diffs/questions + Earlier turns. C) later and out of the light scope: ended-record composer (Resume with the message as the first prompt via the existing startConversation(opening:)/ProviderResume path, confirmed by the first UserPromptSubmit hook), in-view find, FTS cross-session search, unify the subagent panel onto the new engine.

COST RE-ESTIMATE: L, not M. Reuse removes most plumbing (location, tail core, feed, model gating, panel swap, tests' patterns), but still new: a main-session decoder with fixtures (M), turn model (S-M), backward paging (S-M), markdown block renderer plus diff rows (M), list scroll/prepend behaviour (M with risk), mode/header/deletion/resume wiring (S-M), and acceptance scripts (S). Ghostex spends about 5.2k Rust lines on Claude chat, but that includes TUI scraping, which this design omits; Orca and Conductor show that ordering and scroll polish dominate the issues.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Where: the detail panel, in place of the terminal (the P1 pattern from D-54), using the existing panel chrome and LoomTheme.Typography.transcript tokens, with no new colour classes.

Switch: a two-state control "Terminal | Chat" (label is a user decision; see below) in the session header's control area as a new fixed slot, shown only when a transcript resolves, plus a keyboard toggle. Sessions with no live terminal (stopped, stale, after relaunch) open in the chat view by default. The "This session is not running" notice with Resume stays above it. The memory-only last-screen snapshot stays one click away as "Last screen" for the moment of stopping, or is dropped later (user decision).

Layout: a readable column (about 720-780 pt max) scrolling to the bottom and following the tail only while the reader is at the bottom (same rule as SubagentTranscriptView). Top: an "Earlier turns" row that loads another ~1 MiB backward.

Per turn:
- the user prompt as a quiet block;
- assistant text as rendered markdown;
- a single folded step row between them: "Worked for 22s · 3 commands · 2 edits" with a chevron. Expanded, it lists the Claude-style rows already used in the subagent panel (⏺ Bash(first line), ⎿ first line and "+N lines"). An Edit row shows "file +12 -3" and expands to a bounded diff, and a result row expands to the bounded raw body via one pread.
- AskUserQuestion shows as a read-only card (question and chosen answer); the actual answering stays in the terminal or the existing approval boxes.
- Unknown or skipped records are dim one-line rows ("1 record not shown, 212 KiB") with a raw expand.

Running turn: the current turn shows only the latest ~5 steps ("+14 earlier") and "Working…" only while the hook state is Working. A "Jump to latest" pill appears when scrolled up. Esc and Cmd+F are not needed in v1; find over the loaded turns can come later, stating its scope.

States: "Reading the transcript…", "The transcript is not available" (file gone or drift), and always a fallback hint to switch to the terminal.
feasibility.principle_check:
RESOURCES: pass if the bounds hold. The feed exists only while the view is on screen and the window visible (copied gating); a stopped file is read once; cold open about 1 MiB; at most 5 reads/s while a turn runs; the ring is capped by turns and bytes; markdown is built for visible rows only and cached; one live view at a time; raw bodies load on expand only. It becomes a violation if history is all mounted, expand-all is the default, the whole file is parsed on open, the feed runs for a hidden or stopped view, or a second always-on watcher is added. The terminal underneath keeps parsing PTY output while hidden (same as the subagent panel today); that cost is already accepted and measured under CPU40, but re-measure it with a visible chat view during a 1 MiB/s run.

PREDICTABLE: pass with a label. It is the same session read two ways. Mode is explicit and per session, read-only is stated, and nothing in it sends input.

ACCURATE STATUS: the main risk. The view must never be the source of Working/Finished/Needs approval (hooks and registry stay authoritative), and it must never drop content silently: oversize, unknown and unreadable records show as rows and counts, and the end of file is shown honestly ("transcript is behind" instead of a guessed final message). It would violate the principle if it showed "Finished" from file contents, or hid skipped records so a turn looks complete.

FLUENCY: pass. Switching is local; cold open is one bounded read; no confirmations. Watch the first-paint time of markdown for long answers.

MODULARITY: pass. The decoder, turn builder and reader live in LoomCore (UI-free, testable with recorded fixtures); the model/view in LoomCatalogUI mirror the subagent files; no new target. It also gives one transcript engine that the future side-chat panel (forked session file) and the subagent panel can share.

CLI-UPDATE RESILIENCE: moderate risk, designed for. The JSONL is declared CLI-internal in the SDK typings and the CLI shipped 26 releases in 30 days. Mitigations: a lenient narrow decoder; unknown records shown as collapsed raw rows; recorded golden fixtures per CLI version (run through loom-fake-provider and an isolated profile); drift reported once through the existing cli_compat_warning journal path; never pin; a graceful fallback to the terminal. Hook payload fields (transcript_path, last_assistant_message) are documented; the file contents are not.

OWNERSHIP: pass. No process is started; read-only O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, closed on hide/stop. Teardown on deletion is required: an fd left open on a deleted file keeps the content readable until it closes, so the view must close on the deletion request and on the .conversationDeleted frame, and write nothing to disk (no cache, no index in the light version), so verified deletion stays true.

USER AUTHORITY: pass. Read-only, with no cross-session reads (it shows only this session's own file); a future composer would be an explicit user action confirmed by the first UserPromptSubmit hook, and the contract's "terminal is the real CLI and is never replaced" holds for live sessions, since this is an extra view.

PRIVACY: transcript text is untrusted; render only, open no links, load no remote images.
feasibility.value_reason: The user runs several sessions and many subagents, and the real gaps are catching up on what a long run did ("Finished while away"), reading long markdown answers, and reading any stopped session. Today, after a relaunch, a stopped session shows only a facts grid. The ended screen is a memory-only screenshot of at most 16 sessions and 4 MiB, and the terminal scrollback is 2,000 lines. A transcript view fixes that at zero idle cost, fits the stated openness to a chat-centred UI without breaking the contract (it is a view), and is the shared base for side chat (render a forked session's file), the right panel and a later FTS search. feasibility.title: Read-only conversation view of the SAME session (chat-looking transcript, no new engine)

feasibility.one_line: The read-only half (a Chat lens over the main session's transcript) fits Loom and is adopt-light via I-05, but the composer-over-PTY and hook-approval half rests on unverified TUI behaviour (a stray Enter can approve a dialog; Loom's "Waiting for you" cannot tell a prompt from a question dialog), so prove the write path in three isolated spikes before committing to the XL whole.
feasibility.loom_design:
SHAPE: a second VIEW of the one PTY process Loom already owns. No new process, no stream-json, no SDK, no Node. Billing/ToS posture stays "hosts the unmodified interactive CLI". Staged so each stage is shippable and the next is gated by evidence.

STAGE 0 - spikes (see experiments). Nothing is built until S1-S3 answer.

STAGE 1 - Chat lens, read-only (this is I-05 for the main session; cost L). 
Plug-in points:
- Transcript identity. `ClaudeHookEvent.transcriptPath` (ClaudeHook.swift:383/442, documented `transcript_path` on every hook) is parsed but only used for the subagent ledger (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:328). Keep the main conversation's path on the live state (new field beside `SessionViewState.subagents`, SessionEventHub.swift:46) from SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop. For records with no live run (idle, stopped, after relaunch) resolve it by id with the existing `ClaudeTranscriptEffort.transcript(conversationID:projectsDirectory:)` and the same realpath-inside-projects, O_NOFOLLOW, regular-file, own-uid rules as `SubagentTranscriptLocation`.
- Reader (LoomCore, new `ConversationTranscript*`): generalise the proven trio instead of inventing one. `SubagentTranscriptTail` (whole lines only, partial last line held back, cold window = last 512 KiB from a line start, shrink/replaced-inode restart), `SubagentTranscriptFeed` (one vnode source, 200 ms coalescing so at most 5 reads/s, started only while on screen and window visible, `stop()` returns at once). Required changes: (a) the 128 KiB line cap must stop silently dropping lines - a big tool-result line must surface as a "Large record, N KB" placeholder with its byte offset; (b) page backwards on demand in 512 KiB windows ("Earlier" row) - never read a whole file (Paseo #6669 OOM is the cautionary tale); (c) no watcher at all for a record with no live writer - one bounded cold read, then zero cost.
- Parser (new, richer than `SubagentTranscriptParser`, which is a deliberate lossy digest: 4 KiB string clip, first line of tool results, no markdown, `toolUseResult` never decoded): keeps assistant text up to a per-block cap (~64 KiB) for markdown, tool_use name plus input summary, tool_result head plus size, thinking duration, compaction/summary boundary, image placeholders, unknown record types as a collapsed "Unrecognized record (type)" row. Same defensive rules: memmem byte gates before decode, lenient `Lossy<>` blocks, never decode bulky duplicates; heavy bodies (Edit diffs in `toolUseResult`, long tool output) are NOT held - each row keeps its file offset and re-reads that single record when the user expands it. Group by `message.id` (Claude writes one assistant line per content block - ClaudeUsageIndex.swift:16 - so text arrives per completed block, not per token). Order by transcript sequence plus hook timestamps, never insertion time (Orca #23851 showed prompts rendered after responses). Follow the `parentUuid` chain to the active leaf so rewound/abandoned branches are not shown (hypothesis, verify in S3).
- Model/UI (LoomCatalogUI): `ChatLensModel` modelled on `SubagentTranscriptModel` (ring, one observable update per batch, feed alive only while the view is on screen and `windowIsVisible`), `ChatLensView` as a third content branch in `DetailContent` next to the subagent panel and the terminal (DetailView.swift:225 area). The terminal stays with `ConversationController`, running and drained; it is only not in the view hierarchy, exactly the P1 mechanism (D-54) the subagent panel already uses. Per-session mode lives in `CatalogModel` like `viewedSubagent`; last-used mode may go into `UIPreferences`. Markdown without a new dependency: `AttributedString(markdown:, interpretedSyntax: .full)` presentation intents mapped to SwiftUI blocks (paragraph, heading, list, quote, fenced code, table), built on the utility queue and stored immutable on the item; no syntax highlighting in v1. For an ended/idle record the lens replaces `EndedScreenView` as the real history (it survives relaunch, which the memory-only ended screen does not), with the existing Resume notice slot.
- Hard bounds: ring ~400-1000 items, <= ~8 MiB per open lens, released when the session is deselected; only the selected session has a lens; nothing reads when hidden; no timers except the existing 200 ms coalesce.

STAGE 2 - Composer over the PTY (cost M, only if S1 passes). 
- Pure LoomCore function `PromptSubmission` (testable without UI): validates length (<= 64 KiB like OpenSessionInput), refuses leading `/ ! & #` (a leading `!` can run a shell command in the TUI; built-ins like /model open dialogs and fire no UserPromptSubmit so they cannot be verified), wraps in ESC[200~ ... ESC[201~. Single choke point `ConversationController` intent `sendPrompt(text, sessionID)` -> `TerminalSurface.submit` -> the run's existing `TerminalInputQueue.enqueue` (ordered with the user's own keystrokes, 4 MiB bound, closed by `TerminalInputGate` on stop/delete). No second write path.
- Preconditions evaluated at the choke point, from Loom-owned facts only: run live; no `SessionViewState.issue` (hook-silence watchdog quiet); no pending userRequests or open-session wait; activity is atPrompt/turnComplete, or waitingForInput only when the retained Notification type is `idle_prompt` or the registry says idle (today `ClaudeHookStateTracker.notificationActivity` folds idle_prompt, agent_needs_input and elicitation_dialog into one `.waitingForInput`, so the tracker must keep the notification type); the emulator reports bracketed paste on (`Terminal.bracketedPasteMode`, Vendor SwiftTerm Terminal.swift:681 - a standard terminal mode of Loom's own engine, not scraping; if off, refuse, otherwise embedded newlines would submit line by line); and a new "terminal dirty" flag is clear: `TerminalInputQueue` counts non-Enter bytes the user typed since the last UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionStart, so a half-typed line or an open slash dialog in the TUI makes the composer say "The terminal has unsent input" instead of pasting into it (the Ghostex "your draft comes with you" case, solved with bytes Loom itself wrote).
- Enter is a separate write after a short gap (Loom's own CP2 experiment plans/experiments/claude-approval.json writes text, waits 0.3 s, then \r), and state is re-checked immediately before the \r: if the session left the promptable state during the gap, the Enter is NOT sent and the UI says so.
- Verified delivery: add a digest (length + hash, not the text) of the documented `prompt` field of UserPromptSubmit to the hook event/tracker (`promptIsSynthetic` already reads that field). Optimistic bubble is styled "Sending" until a UserPromptSubmit whose prompt matches (pasted placeholders arrive expanded, possibly wrapped in <pasted_content> marker lines, and /loop, background-subagent hand-backs and cross-session messages also fire the hook, so match content, never the mere event) or the transcript echoes the user record; one single-shot 3 s timeout (no polling) then "Sent to the terminal, not confirmed" - never a retry, never "Sent". 
- Interrupt: a single ESC byte, only while activity == working, at most once per working period and never twice within 2 s (the 800 ms double-Escape rewind window Ghostex pins to 2.1.280). Stop hook does not fire on a user interrupt (hooks doc), so confirmation is the registry's idle sample (already watched by a vnode source).
- Drafts per session in memory; Up-arrow history from the lens's own user entries. Explicitly out of v1: slash menu, @ mentions, attachments (terminal drop/paste stays), model/effort/plan pills, type-ahead while Working (the CLI has a native queue; could be added later as "queued, unconfirmed" until its UserPromptSubmit arrives).
- Fallback if S1 fails the delivery or stray-Enter bar: "Send as draft" - paste without Enter, switch to Terminal, user presses Enter. Zero approval risk, still removes the multi-line/IME editing pain.

STAGE 3 - Approvals and questions as cards (cost M-L, only if S2 passes). Extend `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings` (today every hook is `timeout: 1`, advisory, returns no decision): for PermissionRequest, and PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode` (matcher keeps it off the per-tool spawn path the code deliberately avoids), run `loom-hook` in a blocking mode that follows the existing `OpenSessionControlServer` request/response pattern (held connection, token, 90 s precedent). The helper first reports the event as today (status unchanged), then asks Loom "is a Chat lens showing this session?" - if not, or Loom is unreachable, it returns nothing at once and the TUI dialog appears as today; if yes it waits up to a bounded time for the user's click and returns the documented decision JSON (allow/deny; updatedInput for questions). Timeout falls through to the TUI (cmux "soft wait"), never auto-denies. Only allow-once/deny and plain AskUserQuestion options; "always allow", plan-mode choices and everything else stay "Answer in Terminal". Card style = existing orange `RequestList` callout; Return never approves (DESIGN rule kept). "Approved" is shown only after the tool_use's tool_result appears in the transcript.

DATA FLOW / TRIGGERS (all event-driven): hook event -> tracker/registry vnode sample -> SessionEventHub frame -> CatalogModel -> lens state line; transcript vnode write -> 200 ms coalesce -> utility-queue parse -> one batch -> ring; user action -> choke point -> input queue; one single-shot timer per send for the delivery timeout. No polling anywhere.

COST RE-ESTIMATE for this codebase: whole idea stays XL (rough order 6-9k lines with tests). Stage 1 L (scaffolding reuse saves a lot, but markdown blocks, expand-on-demand, backwards paging and scroll-position stability with variable-height rows are the real work; the existing subagent panel is ~1k lines with tests and is plain text). Stage 2 M (extra work is the fake provider: `loom-fake-provider` must emulate bracketed paste, UserPromptSubmit with prompt, dialogs). Stage 3 M-L. Not counting spikes.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Header control group (DESIGN section 6, D-53): add a Terminal | Chat segment beside Stop and the three-dot menu; keyboard toggle (shortcut to be chosen in the design round, must not steal Return from the terminal). State is per session and remembered; default for live sessions is a user decision.

Chat view in the detail panel, same panel colour and 6 pt inset rules, a readable centred column (not edge to edge like the terminal). Rows reuse the subagent panel's glyph language so the look is continuous: user prompts as plain blocks, assistant markdown rendered, tool calls collapsed to one line "Bash(npm test)  24 lines" and grouped per turn ("Ran 5 commands, edited 2 files"), thinking as "Thought for 12s", unknown records as one muted row. Tap a tool row to expand the single record on demand. Earlier history behind an "Earlier" row (backwards page read). Follows the tail only while the reader is at the bottom (existing logic).

Bottom composer (Stage 2): 1-8 line auto-growing NSTextView, Return = newline or send per a setting (Cmd+Return the other), a one-line state chip above it: "Ready", "Claude is working - Esc to interrupt", "Needs approval - answer below or in Terminal", "The terminal has unsent input - open Terminal", "Not confirmed - check Terminal". Disabled with the reason spelled out, never silently. Sent messages show "Sending" until verified. Approval/question cards (Stage 3) sit above the composer in the existing orange callout; Allow/Deny are buttons, neither is the default action.

Ended or idle record: the same view without composer, with the existing Resume notice on top, replacing the static ended screen as the readable history; no process, no watcher.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources - pass if disciplined: lens exists only for the selected, visible session; feed and vnode source only while on screen and window visible (SubagentTranscriptModel pattern), at most 5 reads/s, cold open = last 512 KiB, ring and per-item caps, heavy bodies re-read on expand, no watcher for records without a writer, no new process. Terminal parsing cost is unchanged (the PTY keeps draining; it is just not drawn). Risk: markdown/AttributedString on very long messages and variable-height SwiftUI rows - must be built off-main, cached immutable, and measured against the 40% CPU gate.
Predictability - pass: one toggle, one send path, one meaning for Return; composer disabled with an explicit reason. Risk: two input surfaces, resolved by visibility (only one is in the hierarchy) plus the dirty-terminal rule.
Accurate status - the central risk, passable only with proof: "Sending" becomes "Delivered" only on a matching UserPromptSubmit prompt (documented field) or a transcript echo; otherwise "not confirmed", never retried. Interrupt is confirmed by the registry idle sample, approval by the tool_result. Risk: the status model cannot yet tell a prompt from a question dialog (waitingForInput merges idle_prompt, agent_needs_input, elicitation_dialog), and a composer Enter that lands in a permission dialog can approve it (Herdr #5263 is the real incident). Mitigated by gating, dirty-terminal accounting and re-check before Enter, not eliminated - that residual risk needs the user's explicit acceptance, or the Send-as-draft fallback.
Fluency - pass: toggle is instant (cold tail read on a utility queue); composer adds one short gap before Enter; no confirmations. Cost: text shows per completed content block, not per token, so live token streaming stays a Terminal-view benefit.
Modularity - pass: reader and parser in LoomCore with no UI import, `PromptSubmission` pure and testable, UI in new ChatLens files, small touches to `DetailContent`, `ConversationIntents`, `ClaudeHookEvent`, `TerminalInputQueue`; dependency direction preserved. Risk: scope creep toward Orca's ~120 native-chat component files; the bounded-subset list is the guard.
CLI-update resilience - risk, contained: the JSONL schema is declared CLI-internal, so lenient decode, unknown records shown (never dropped or faked), recorded-fixture tests per CLI version, drift journaling reusing the `cli_compat_warning` mechanism, and the terminal always one click away. Write-path coupling points are named and each fails closed: bracketed-paste mode, Enter timing, leading-character modes, Esc semantics. No screen scraping (Ghostex needed ~5.2k lines pinned to 2.1.268/2.1.280/2.1.284). `--prefill` is hidden/undocumented and is not used.
Ownership - pass: no new process; input goes through the run's own PTY and queue, closed by `TerminalInputGate` on stop/delete; Quit and verified Stop unchanged. (Alternatives B/C/D in chat-ui-paths would add a second owner.)
User authority - pass with care: every send, interrupt and approval is an explicit user click or keystroke; nothing auto-approves; Return never approves; the hook wait times out into the TUI dialog, not into a denial; the lens only holds a hook when it is actually showing that session.
feasibility.value_reason: High for the reading half: a heavy multi-session, multi-subagent user gets rendered markdown, folded tool noise, catch-up on finished sessions and, for idle/ended records, real history that costs no process and survives relaunch (the static ended screen does not). It is also the foundation the user's side chat and right panel need, with no SDK or billing exposure. The composer adds less (multi-line editing, native IME/Turkish-layout input that the terminal handled badly in D-36) while carrying the only real hazards, so the value drops to about 3 if the user is happy typing in the terminal; the approval cards overlap what I-15/I-16 notifications already give.

feasibility.one_line: Technically the right engine for a chat-centred Loom and it fits the run-scope and ownership model better than the research assumes, but it is an unbounded XL build with a headless-billing exposure and an unanswered replace-vs-convenience question, so run a recorded capture spike and gate the build on I-05 proving use.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS FROM THE CODE (what makes it cheaper or dearer than the idea text says)
- Run-scope pipes already exist. RunScope.Stdio has `.descriptors(input:output:error:)` (Sources/LoomCore/RunScope.swift ~l.355-437) and loom-run-host supports SPAWN_STDIO (Sources/loom-run-host/main.c l.31, 81). It is used by LaunchEnvironment.swift:397 (the environment-capture helper) and tested in Tests/LoomCoreTests/RunScopeTests.swift. So a pipe child can live in the same fresh coalition and be stopped and verified like a PTY child. The research note's "no session-lifecycle code exists" is true for the stream-json client but not for the process-ownership half.
- But ProcessSupervisor.launch (Sources/LoomCore/ProcessSupervisor.swift l.282-450) is PTY-shaped end to end: rows/columns, spawnInScope returns a PTYProcess, Runtime.terminal is a TerminalEndpoint, ManagedSessionLaunch carries a TerminalEndpoint, and SessionRuntime.register (l.687-692) wraps it. The only stop-path use of the endpoint is `runtime.terminal.finish()` (ProcessSupervisor+Stop.swift:223). A small transport protocol (pid, finish(), exitStatus) over {PTY endpoint, pipe endpoint} is the minimum supervisor change; everything else (ledger, scope release, stop report, catalog finishRun, Quit) is already transport-agnostic.
- "Exactly one process owns a session id" is already enforced: launch refuses `conversationAlreadyRunning(provider:conversationID:)` for a second live run on the same provider conversation id (ProcessSupervisor.swift ~l.292-300). Mode switch = ProcessSupervisor.stop (verified) then resume in the other transport; ProviderResume/`--resume` already exists. The resume path also restores effort from the transcript (ClaudeTranscriptEffort).
- Status can stay hook-driven. ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings (l.~170-200) injects per-session --settings hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, Notification, PermissionRequest, SessionEnd, SubagentStart/Stop) and the loom-hook env (LOOM_HOOK_SOCKET/TOKEN, LOOM_MANAGED_RUN_ID). If hooks fire in `-p` (documented: plain -p runs settings hooks), ClaudeSessionAdapter and ClaudeHookStateTracker work unchanged, Needs approval/Waiting/Finished/Failed and the subagent ledger stay one code path, and session_state_changed (opt-in via CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1) is only a cross-check, not the authority. That is the biggest design simplification and it removes the "status from an opt-in event" fragility. Unknown to verify: ClaudeRegistryReader reads <config>/sessions/<pid>.json (ClaudeRegistry.swift l.66); whether a -p process writes it is unverified, and the hook-silence watchdog (ClaudeSessionAdapter.armSilenceWatchdog) keys off the registry saying busy, so an absent file must read as "unavailable", not as a fault.
- Existing wire code is a probe only: ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher (ClaudePlanLimits.swift) uses Foundation Process, not the run scope, one request, 4 MiB output cap, 1 MiB line cap, blocking poll() loop on a detached task. It deliberately passes --settings {"disableAllHooks":true} --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence, i.e. it already learned that plain -p runs user hooks and MCP (seen on 2.1.293). It is a framing/parsing precedent (PlanLimitsWire) but its blocking poll loop must NOT be copied; a resident child needs a DispatchSourceRead like EventDrivenPTYProcess. Note the same plain-`-p` exposure applies to it: if -p ever defaults to --bare (headless.md), both the usage chip's plan windows and any chat child lose OAuth.

LIGHTEST VERSION THAT STILL IS "CHAT MODE" (v1 scope)
1. New LoomCore group `ClaudeChat` (no UI imports, off MainActor): `StreamJSONFraming` (NDJSON, 1 MiB line cap, tolerant: unknown `type`/`subtype` becomes `.unknown(raw prefix)` and is counted, never fatal), `ChatEvent` (assistant text blocks, tool_use, tool_result, can_use_tool request, control_response, system/init with capabilities + claude_code_version, result with error category), `ChatSessionProcess` (spawn through RunScope `.descriptors`, pipe read via DispatchSourceRead, bounded write queue like TerminalInputQueue, SIGINT/`interrupt` for stop-turn, close stdin then verified stop for exit).
2. Supervisor: add the transport protocol above and a `launchPiped` that shares the pre-spawn checks (markers, deletion fence, one-owner check, ledger/scope registration) by extracting them from `launch`. Do not copy 170 lines; factor.
3. Catalog: `sessions.mode` ('terminal' default | 'chat') added on open without a version bump, exactly as ensureActivityColumn/ensureOriginColumns do, so 0.4.x can still open the catalog. Mode only changes on a verified stop.
4. Render model: reuse the shape of SubagentTranscriptEntry/Model (last 400 entries, strings clipped at 4 KiB, one batch = one update, coalesced to at most 5 updates/s, same Feed pattern). Start WITHOUT --include-partial-messages: message-level rendering, no per-token deltas. This removes the biggest CPU/redraw risk and a large share of the parser; token streaming is a later opt-in that is coalesced and dropped while hidden.
5. Approvals: PermissionRequest hook already reaches Loom (status). The decision itself needs `--permission-prompts host` plus the can_use_tool control_request answered by a user click on an approval card; the SDK-internal `--permission-prompt-tool stdio` value is the fragile part and is exactly what the spike must pin down (documented fallbacks: MCP permission tool in Loom's plugin dir, or `defer`). Never auto-allow; deny on timeout/disconnect.
6. Triggers (all event-driven): pipe readability, process exit via the run host's EXITED frame, user send, hook frames, FSEvents already watching projects/ for usage. No timers, nothing drawn when the chat view or window is hidden (keep the parsed entries, drop deltas).
7. Idle: a chat child is a full claude process exactly like the TUI process Loom already keeps resident under D-38 (no idle stop). So the idle-memory story is the same as today; the PTY terminal buffer is the only thing saved. Optional stop-after-result and `--resume` on next send is a user decision (it conflicts with D-38 and costs a cold start per message); default off.
8. Deletion and usage need nothing new for a plain chat session (same JSONL under projects/, ClaudeDataInventory plans it; UsageTranscriptWatcher sees the writes). A fork-based side chat (separate idea) would need its copies added to the inventory and the Loom-owned cleanup.
9. Safety: flags come from `claude --help` detection (ProviderCapabilities pattern) and missing ones are reported through reportCompatibility/journal `cli_compat_warning` instead of pinning; init `capabilities` is stored in the journal summary (version + capability names, no content); chat sessions refuse to open for a folder the user has not added as a project, because plain -p skips the workspace-trust dialog (headless.md).

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A PRINCIPLE VIOLATION AND THE AVOIDANCE
- Resource: per-token stream_event churn redrawing a SwiftUI list; avoid by message-level v1 and coalescing. Unbounded transcript in memory; avoid by the 400-entry/4 KiB model. A second resident process per mode switch; avoid by one-owner rule plus verified stop.
- Accurate status: deriving Working/Needs approval from the new stream would fork the state machine; avoid by keeping hooks as authority. A write that is not verified delivered (user message sent while the child is dead) must not show as sent; use --replay-user-messages as the delivery receipt (a message is "sent" only when echoed back), otherwise show failed.
- CLI resilience: a hand-rolled client over a protocol typed only in the SDK .d.ts is exactly where drift bites (about 26 CLI releases a month). Avoid by: unknown-passthrough decoding, init capability detection, a recorded-fixture suite per CLI version in loom-fake-provider, and a kill switch that falls back to the terminal for the same session.
- Billing/policy: headless is the surface policy moved on four times; keep PTY default, per-session explicit mode, no --bare, no token handling, surface billing_error/oauth/authentication categories as a visible notice, one Settings switch that disables Chat mode globally.
- Contract: "the real CLI/terminal experience is preserved" (LOOM-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md §3 Core experience) and the user's "no custom chat UI replacing the terminal" rule are changed only for sessions that explicitly choose Chat mode. That is a user-authority decision, not mine.
- Ownership: do not spawn through Foundation Process like the plan-limits probe; chat children must be run-scope members.

COST (honest, for this codebase)
- Wire client + process + fake-provider fixtures + tests: M (about 1.5-2k lines).
- Supervisor transport factoring, catalog mode column, SessionRuntime/ConversationController wiring for a non-terminal run (ConversationController is built around TerminalSurface creation/reconcile, 474 lines), mode-switch flow with verified stop and failure states: M-L.
- Chat UI: transcript with markdown, code and diffs, tool cards, approval and AskUserQuestion cards, composer with multi-line, image paste, @-file and slash-command completion, model/effort/permission-mode controls, stop-turn, ended-state: L, and the long tail is open-ended because TUI dialog commands (/permissions, /config, /mcp, /agents) and agent teams do not exist in headless.
- Total XL confirmed. A "convenience view" scope (text, tools, approve/deny, stop, switch) is L; "daily driver with parity" is XL and not boundable.

Header is unchanged (state pill, project+branch chip, Stop); add a small segmented 'Terminal | Chat' control or a header action 'Switch to Terminal' that runs the verified stop-and-resume with a short 'Switching…' busy state (ConversationBusy-style) and keeps the draft. New-session menu gets 'New Claude Session' (terminal, default) and 'New Chat Session' (explicit, labelled as experimental until the spike passes). Sidebar cards are unchanged apart from a tiny mode glyph beside the provider icon. Chat view: bubble-free column in the terminal's background, assistant text, collapsed tool cards (name + main argument, same fields SubagentTranscriptParser already extracts), an inline approval card with Allow/Deny that also drives the existing needs-approval indicator, a composer pinned at the bottom (Return sends, Shift+Return newline, Esc stops the turn). The subagent panel and its click-through keep working (hooks-fed ledger). No right panel in v1; a side-chat panel is the separate idea that would plug in later.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: RISK, bounded by design. A chat child is the same claude process the PTY mode keeps resident under D-38, so memory is roughly equal (the 230-260 MB figure is a parked spare's floor, unmeasured for a live session either way); the saving is the terminal buffer, the cost is a Swift render model. Pass if v1 is message-level, coalesced to 5 updates/s, entries capped, nothing drawn when hidden, no polling (pipe readability, exit frame, hooks, FSEvents). Not measured: stream-json child CPU while a turn runs with partial messages; must clear the 40%-of-a-core gate in the spike.
Predictability: PASS if the mode is explicit per session, PTY is default and fallback, and a switch is a visible verified stop plus resume.
Accurate status: PASS only if hooks stay the authority and a message is 'sent' only on --replay-user-messages echo; RISK if status is derived from the opt-in session_state_changed.
Fluency: RISK. Cold resume per switch and per optional stop-after-result costs seconds; headless has no TUI dialogs or agent teams, which this user uses heavily (multi-agent workflows), so chat mode would be a worse tool for those sessions.
Modularity: PASS with care. New ClaudeChat group in LoomCore with no UI imports; the supervisor needs a transport abstraction, which touches the central, well-tested ProcessSupervisor and is the main regression surface.
CLI-update resilience: RISK, the central risk. The protocol is typed only in SDK typings and moves with about 26 CLI releases a month; --permission-prompt-tool stdio is SDK-internal; -p may become --bare by default; session_state_changed is opt-in. Mitigated by capability detection, passthrough decoding, recorded fixtures and the terminal fallback, never by pinning.
Ownership: PASS. Pipes through the existing run host and coalition, one-owner check already in launch, verified stop; plain Foundation Process (as the plan-limits probe does) would NOT pass and must not be used.
User authority: PASS if every approval is a user click on a card, no auto-allow, deny on disconnect, and no cross-session action is introduced. New risk: plain -p skips the trust dialog and runs project hooks and .mcp.json, so restrict to folders the user added as projects.
Billing/policy (outside the list but decisive): RISK. Support article 15036540 still allows subscription use, but the May 13 metering of claude -p was only paused and the Apr 4 policy covered all third-party harnesses; unmodified binary with the user's own login is permitted. Needs a kill switch and a re-read before releases.
feasibility.value_reason: It is the only path to the chat-centred, typed, tool-card and side-question UI the user asked about, and Loom's ownership layer makes it safer here than in Conductor/T3/Zed. But the user's real workflow (many sessions, subagents and multi-agent workflows, skills, MCP, TUI dialogs) is best served today by the PTY, most of the near-term wins (readable ended sessions, side chat, approvals in the panel) can come from lighter ideas, and the value jumps to 4-5 only if the user decides Chat mode replaces the terminal, which also makes the unbounded parity work and the billing exposure the price.

feasibility.one_line: Adopt a menu item plus one key that types '/btw ' into the live terminal (real CLI, nothing new owned), guarded by a short isolated hook/registry observation; it is cheap and fits every principle, but it only saves about five keystrokes and does not deliver the persistent side chat the user wants.
feasibility.loom_design:
PLUG-IN POINTS (all follow existing patterns, no new subsystem):
1. Intent: add `askSideQuestion(sessionID:)` to `ConversationIntents` (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/CatalogModel.swift:31) with a default no-op (like approveOpen/closeEndedScreen), implemented in `ConversationController` (ConversationController.swift:177 area). It finds the entry whose `owner == id` (same lookup as `typeForEvidence`, line ~146 and `terminalView(sessionID:)`, line 346), calls `container.focusTerminal()` (line 27) and writes the 5 bytes "/btw " through `surface.send(source:data:)` (TerminalSurface.swift:274) so they take the normal ordered path `TerminalInputQueue` (4 MiB, bounded) -> `TerminalEndpoint.write`. Do not press Enter: the user types the question. Prefer raw keystrokes over `pasteText` (the path `insertDroppedFiles` uses, TerminalSurface.swift:436) so the CLI shows its normal slash-command menu and treats '/' at prompt start like real typing; spike item below decides.
2. Model: `CatalogModel.canAskSideQuestion` (like `canStop`, CatalogModel.swift:1506): selected row has a live terminal owned by a run, activity is not Needs approval (typed letters would hit a dialog), no ended-screen, no open subagent panel (if `viewedSubagent` is set, call `closeSubagent()` first, CatalogModel+Subagents.swift:41, then focus the terminal; or disable). Statuses Working, Waiting for you, Ready, Finished unviewed are all allowed: /btw is documented to work mid-turn.
3. Menu/key: one `NSMenuItem` "Ask a Side Question (/btw)" in `installMenus` (AppDelegate.swift:~735, next to the SessionShortcut items) plus a `SessionShortcut` entry (SessionNavigation.swift:85) so title/key live in one tested place, and a `validateMenuItem` case (AppDelegate.swift:537). Key equivalents reach the menu before the focused terminal (comment at AppDelegate.swift:745), so no change to `LoomTerminalView.keyDown`. Key choice matters: Claude Desktop uses Cmd+; but the user has a Turkish Q layout (the code already special-cases it, TerminalSurface.swift:362) where ';' is not a free key; pick a letter chord (for example Cmd+Shift+B) or let the user choose.
4. Trigger = one user key press, event-driven. No timer, no polling, no new file watcher, no process, no state; nothing is drawn or watched when hidden. The overlay is the CLI's own TUI inside the existing terminal pane, so Loom has nothing to render or keep readable beyond not stealing its keys (Esc/Space/Enter dismiss; Shift+Left/Right, [ ], Tab step older answers; c copy; f fork; x clear). Check that none of these chords is bound in Loom's menus (Cmd+Option arrows and Cmd+Shift+[ ] are, but those carry Cmd).
5. Hardening that the shortcut makes more frequent (internal agents already exist today via prompt suggestions): hooks doc says SubagentStop fires for /btw side questions with `agent_type` = the agent name the session runs as, empty when no --agent/`agent` setting. `SubagentLedger.apply` (SubagentLedger.swift ~lines 150-165) drops an unknown stop only when `type.isEmpty` (comment line 187). If the user runs with an `agent` setting, each /btw would add a finished phantom row to the subagent tree (ClaudeHook.disposition lets agent_id lifecycle events through, ClaudeHook.swift:662). Fix only if the spike shows it: ignore a stop with no earlier start AND no meta.json (internal agents have none, real ones get `agent-<id>.meta.json` ~25 ms after start) or a stop whose agent_transcript_path is absent.
6. Status accuracy: Claude may write the registry `status` busy/idle around a side question. Loom reads the registry (ClaudeRegistryWatch vnode, ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:60) and `receiveRegistry` (ClaudeHook.swift:574) accepts any sample newer than the last hook, so a mid-turn /btw that flips the registry to idle on completion could show 'Waiting for you' while the main turn still works until the next hook, and a /btw at an idle prompt could show 'Working' briefly. This already happens if the user types /btw by hand; the shortcut only makes it more frequent. Observe first, fix in the tracker only if it happens (for example do not trust an 'idle' sample newer than the last hook while a turn is known active, which needs a design check against D-45).
7. Usage: ClaudeUsageIndex already attributes `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` to the parent session (ClaudeUsageIndex.swift:635-665), so if /btw writes a subagent transcript its tokens are counted for free; if it writes nothing, the chip undercounts slightly. Note, do not build.
8. Tests: a controller/model test that the intent writes exactly "/btw " in order through the queue and is refused for Needs approval / ended / no run (mirror TerminalSurfaceTests.swift:125 style); validateMenuItem rules; SessionShortcut table. No e2e needed beyond one fake-provider check that the bytes arrive.

feasibility.ui_sketch: No new surface. Window menu (or a Session menu) gets 'Ask a Side Question (/btw)' with a key chord, enabled when the selected session has a live terminal and is not waiting on an approval. Press: focus goes to the terminal and '/btw ' appears at the CLI's prompt; the user types the question and presses Enter; the CLI draws its own dismissible overlay over the prompt area (Space/Enter/Esc dismiss, Shift+Left/Right older answers, c copy, f fork to a background subagent, which then shows in Loom's subagent tree as a real subagent). Optional tiny polish: the menu item's help text or the Help menu says 'Answers are not saved; closing the overlay forgets them' so nobody expects history. If a draft is already in the prompt the text lands at the cursor exactly like typing; Ctrl+U clears it (a documented limit, not detected).
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass (event-driven, 5 bytes, zero idle cost, no watcher). Predictability: pass with one risk; the CLI cannot report prompt contents, so with an existing draft or vim NORMAL mode the inserted text may land wrongly; mitigated by doing exactly what typing does and by not auto-submitting. Accurate status: RISK until observed; /btw may move the registry status or fire SubagentStop with a non-empty agent_type (phantom subagent row); both are tracker issues that already exist for by-hand /btw and prompt suggestions, so run the spike and harden the ledger/registry rule if needed. Fluency: pass (no confirmations, works mid-turn, saves about five keystrokes plus the need to remember the command). Modularity: pass (one intent, one model predicate, one shortcut entry; LoomCore untouched unless the ledger fix is needed). CLI-update resilience: pass; relies on a documented slash command, no flags, no file format, nothing pinned; if a future CLI renames or removes /btw the user sees the CLI's own 'unknown command' and nothing in Loom breaks. Ownership: pass (no new process; the side question is a model call inside the existing Claude run, covered by Stop and Quit). User authority: pass (no cross-session action; the user types and submits). Contract/decisions: pass; the terminal stays the real CLI (DESIGN.md line 20), D-34 is not touched (no right sidebar); section 13 side-chat item remains open. Would become a violation if: Loom auto-submitted or auto-typed without a key press, scraped the screen for the answer, polled for the overlay, or stored the answer (new durable data, deletion scope, and a CLI-internal rendering dependency).
feasibility.value_reason: Real for this user: long multi-agent turns are exactly where a no-tools, cache-cheap question while the main turn runs helps, it needs no new process, and it ships the first slice of a long-standing wish for almost nothing. But the keystroke saving is tiny (typing '/btw ' is five keys), the answer is single-response, in-memory, tool-less and unreachable by Loom, so the wished-for persistent ChatGPT-style side thread in a right panel is not served. The real value is discoverability and a consistent menu entry; it should not be mistaken for, or delay, a Loom-owned side thread decision.

feasibility.one_line: Build it as a hidden child card whose run is `claude --resume <parent> --fork-session` in a plan-mode PTY (the only mechanism that keeps the real CLI, has no billing exposure and reuses Loom's start, stop and verified-delete machinery), but run a one-day isolated-profile spike first, because the card-identity, cache and mid-turn-fork behaviour of the flag are unverified and decide the design.
feasibility.loom_design:
PLAN: a side chat is a NORMAL Loom Claude session (own card, own run scope, own hooks) with one extra catalog link, `side_of = parent card id`. Almost nothing new at runtime. Mechanism 1 only; mechanisms 2 and 3 wait for the I-05/I-07 renderer; mechanism 4 stays rejected.

CORE (LoomCore, no UI):
1. Launch profile. `ProviderLaunchProfile.swift`: add `ClaudeRoute.fork(parent:String, child:UUID)` -> `--resume <parent> --fork-session --session-id <child> --permission-mode plan -n <title>` plus the boundary and question as the trailing positional prompt (the same trailing-prompt slot D-40's `ClaudeOpening` uses; today it is refused for non-`.new` routes, so that guard is relaxed for `.fork`). Add `ProviderCapabilities.supportsForkSession = help.contains("--fork-session")` next to the other substring checks and include it in `detectedClaudeOptions`. Unlike `--settings`/`--session-id` (which the code deliberately passes anyway, ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:111 comment), a missing `--fork-session` REFUSES the side start with a drift notice (`reportCompatibility` + `cli_compat_warning` journal): a launch that silently lacks the flag would be `--resume <parent>`, i.e. a second process writing into the main conversation, the exact pollution the feature exists to avoid. Effort is carried from the parent id through `ClaudeTranscriptEffort.last` as `.resume` does (SessionRuntime+Claude.swift `claudeProfile`).
2. Runtime entry. New `SessionRuntime+SideSession.swift`: `startSideSession(parent:, question:, rows:, columns:, outputSink:)` modelled on `startConversation(opening:)` (SessionRuntime.swift:371-410): refuse unless the parent is Claude, has a `providerConversationID`, is not pending deletion, and its folder exists; same working directory, project and toolchain as the parent (resume looks the transcript up by folder); `supervisor.createSession(...)` with an automatic title (`Aside: <question head>`), `side_of`, and, critically, `providerConversationID = child` PRESET. Reason (read in code): `ProcessSupervisor.adoptConversation` (ProcessSupervisor.swift ~454-585) returns the same card only when `current.providerConversationID == conversationID`; with a nil id and `SessionStart.source == "resume"` (mapped to `.resume` in ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:241-243) it mints a SECOND card and leaves the launch card as an empty orphan. Then `launchClaude(...)` unchanged. Bounds: at most 1 live side run per parent and 2 live overall (refusal text like the tab-strip's "Close one to open another").
3. Verified outcome. `ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~204-255) gets a per-run expectation for side runs: the first SessionStart must report `child`; anything else (equal to parent, or different) stops that run at once and publishes `.issue("Side chat did not fork; stopped")`. 'Started' is therefore never reported for a fork that did not fork. The existing `conversationAlreadyRunning` guard in `adoptConversation` is a second net if the CLI ever reported the parent's id.
4. Catalog. `sessions.side_of TEXT` added by an ensure-on-open step beside `ensureOriginColumns` (CatalogDatabase.swift:247-260), no schema bump, so 0.4.x still opens the catalog. Add to `SessionCatalog.sessionColumns` / `CatalogSession` (SessionCatalog.swift:194-196, 352). Add `s.side_of IS NULL` to the shared `conditions(for:)` in SessionCatalog+Paging.swift (pages, search, counts) and to stale/cleanup classification; new `sideSessions(of: [UUID])` read (one query per visible parents, like `ensureOrigins`, CatalogModel.swift:735) and `promoteSide(id)` (sets NULL, publishes a frame; the transcript keeps the boundary text, so promotion also changes nothing in Claude).
5. Close = Stop. Closing a side chat is the existing verified `stopConversation`; the ended-screen snapshot (EndedScreens, 16 screens / 4 MiB LRU) then shows it, and reopening is a normal `resumeConversation` (cold-cache re-read, see cost). No new lifecycle, no idle timer (D-38), and no auto-stop when the parent ends (a surprise stop; Quit already stops everything).
6. Discard = existing permanent delete. `SessionRuntime.deleteConversation` already does stop -> files -> catalog -> verify (ConversationDeletion.swift; ClaudeDataInventory plans by session id, so the fork's own `<child>.jsonl` and companions are found like any session). Two additions: (a) deleting a PARENT must cascade to its side chats, because each child transcript holds a verbatim copy of the parent's history; otherwise 'permanently deleted' is false (contract §8). The dry-run preview lists '+N side chats' (ClaudeDataInventory.plan takes multiple ids). (b) no confirm dialog on Discard of an unpromoted side chat is the proposal; user decision.
7. Bring the answer back. On click only: read the last assistant text of the CHILD transcript with the existing bounded tail reader (SubagentTranscriptTail 512 KiB cold open + SubagentTranscriptParser narrow decode, no feed, no watcher), then write it as a bracketed paste (NOT Enter) into the PARENT's terminal through `TerminalInputQueue`, only when the parent shows Ready or Waiting for you (never Working / Needs approval, where the paste would land in a permission prompt). Status text is honest: 'Inserted in the prompt, not sent'. If the transcript cannot be parsed (format drift) say so and offer Copy from the side terminal. This is the only place a side chat touches the parent, and it is a user click (D-43/D-46 authority rule).
8. Read-only guard. `--permission-mode plan` is CLI-enforced (stronger than Codex's prompt-only boundary), plus the boundary text as the FIRST user message (inherited history is reference only; do not continue its plans or tool calls; no subagents; no file changes). Do not pin tool names (`--disallowedTools Agent` would be a drift hazard: the tool was renamed Task -> Agent over time). `--system-prompt-snapshot on` is the default in 2.1.300 and, per `claude --help`, resumes send the recorded system prompt 'as-is' even if a later launch passes different text: so `--append-system-prompt` for the boundary would likely be ignored, and also should not be used because it would be a cache-prefix change if honoured; the boundary goes in the message (matches chat-ui-paths SC2).
9. Fork point. The CLI has no documented `--up-to-message`; only the SDK `forkSession` has one. The fork sees whatever the parent has flushed to its transcript, so a mid-turn fork may contain an assistant tool_use without its tool_result. Loom cannot fork 'before the last completed turn' (OpenChamber's rule) with documented options; the boundary message says the last step may be incomplete, and the UI says 'sees up to the last saved message'. Do not fall back to copying the JSONL (Happy).
10. Hook/usage/other fan-out: hooks are keyed by run id, so side status is isolated from the parent. `AttentionOrder`, Dock badge, menu bar and Quit confirmation iterate `liveStates` + `liveRecords` (CatalogModel+Navigation.swift:13-22) and `liveRecords` lazy-loads unknown live ids (CatalogModel.swift:539), so a side chat that needs approval counts without extra code; titles prefixed 'Aside:' keep it readable. Usage: `ClaudeUsageIndex` keys by `message.id` (ClaudeUsageIndex.swift:269), so copied parent lines should dedupe and only the fork's new turns add; verify in the spike. All event-driven (hook frames, vnode watchers already present); no polling, nothing runs when closed.

SMALLEST SHIPPABLE SLICE (the 'M' core): items 1-5 + sidebar child row + header Close/Discard/Promote. Bring-back (7), cascade preview (6a) and the parent-state pill can follow as an S+S.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
ENTRY: header Session menu item 'Ask Aside' and Cmd+; (parity with Claude Desktop) on a live Claude session that has a conversation id. A small popover (one text field, Enter) takes the first question; empty Enter opens the side session with only the boundary. The popover is the only new composer; every later turn is typed in the side terminal itself (the real CLI), so there is no custom chat UI and D-34/contract 'terminal is the CLI' stay intact.
SIDEBAR: under the parent card, in the same guide-line tree as the subagents (SubagentTree.swift, SidebarView.swift SessionListEntry), a row 'Aside · <question head>' with the chase when Working, dot when Needs approval/Waiting, check when stopped. Hidden from the activity list, project list, Active section and search; one click selects it. Up to a few shown, rest folded like 'N finished'.
DETAIL: selecting it swaps it in place of the parent in the detail pane (same mechanism as any session; the parent terminal keeps running and is never resized). Header variant like SubagentHeaderRow: crumb 'Parent title › Aside', its own state pill, a small 'Main: Working / Needs approval / Waiting for you' pill (Codex's SideParentStatus idea, so a blocked parent is never forgotten), then Bring Back, Promote, and a group with Close (Stop) and Discard. Cmd+; or a 'Main' control goes back to the parent. Not Esc: Esc belongs to the Claude TUI here (the subagent panel could use Esc because it has no terminal).
PROMOTE: drops `side_of`; the card joins the normal lists and loses the 'Aside' prefix; a note that the boundary text stays in its transcript.
CLOSED: ended-screen snapshot in memory, record view after relaunch; nothing running. An optional later v2 is a right-hand split (resizes the parent's TUI, see decisions).
feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS. Closed = no process, no terminal, no watcher; open = exactly one more Claude + one LoomRunHost, bounded 1 per parent / 2 live. The ended-screen cache is already bounded (16 / 4 MiB). No polling. Honest cost is TOKENS, not CPU: a fork re-reads the whole parent context (warm cache cheap, cold cache = full cache write), every reopen of a stopped side chat likewise. RISK: plan-window burn on 150k+ token contexts; mitigated by the unmeasured cache behaviour in E4.
- Predictability: PASS if behaviour is fixed: Close stops, Discard deletes, Promote unhides, nothing stops on a timer, nothing flows back without a click. RISK: users expecting the answer to flow back (labelled 'Inserted in prompt, not sent'); the fork being a snapshot (does not see later main work).
- Accurate status: PASS with the added first-SessionStart check (item 3) so 'started' means a different conversation id actually started; delete reports only after ClaudeDataDeleter.verify; Bring Back reports 'inserted' not 'delivered'. RISK: a mid-turn fork carrying a dangling tool_use (spike E3); any state shown for the side chat is its own hooks, never inferred from the parent.
- Fluency: PASS. One shortcut and one field; no confirmation on ask; Discard of an unpromoted side chat proposed without a dialog. RISK: the fork's first turn on a cold cache can take seconds; the prompt is accepted before that.
- Modularity: PASS. One new Core file, one profile route, one nullable column, one hidden-filter condition, one child-row view next to SubagentTree; no new protocol or daemon. RISK: `side_of IS NULL` must be added everywhere lists/counts/cleanup read sessions (tests: CatalogHotPathTests, SessionCatalogSearchTests).
- CLI-update resilience: PASS. Only documented flags (`--resume`, `--fork-session`, `--session-id`, `--permission-mode plan`, `-n`), detected from `claude --help` through the existing capabilities struct, no version pin, refusal with drift notice if the flag is gone. RISK: help text shape change causes a false refusal (feature off until fixed; acceptable); `--session-id` combined with `--fork-session` is unverified (E1). The Happy approach (copy the JSONL) is rejected, as is any undocumented `side_question` use in v1.
- Ownership: PASS. Own run scope through the normal launch path; Stop/Quit verified; Discard stops before deleting. No second ownership model.
- User authority: PASS. Everything is user-initiated; the side session cannot write to the main thread; Bring Back is a click that only pastes into an idle prompt; boundary text forbids subagents; `$LOOM_CLI open` from the side session still needs the existing approval box.
- Contract/decisions: D-34 (no right sidebar now) is respected by the in-place v1; contract §13 lists this as an unscoped user wish, so it needs the user's go; contract 'terminal is the real CLI' holds. No billing exposure (interactive PTY, not `-p`/SDK, unlike mechanism 2).
feasibility.value_reason: It is the user's longest-standing wish and the top-converging idea (14 sources); a heavy agentic user running multi-hour agents on EDDP-style tickets repeatedly needs 'why did you do that?' / 'what does this file do?' without derailing or blocking the main run, and today's alternatives (type /btw, which is single-answer, tool-less and ephemeral, or open a new session and re-explain) are worse. A PTY fork is not the ChatGPT-style chat look, which costs it a little, but it is multi-turn, can read files, persists, and arrives with no renderer work.
depends_on: None hard for the PTY child (mechanism 1). Reuses: D-40 trailing-prompt launch slot, D-39 subagent tree row, FB4-3 ended screens, CP4-C verified deletion.
I-05/I-07 (structured renderer) only for the later headless variant (mechanism 2) or a chat-style view of the side transcript.
Mechanism 3 (undocumented side_question) needs a Chat-mode process, not this design; skip until then.
experiments: E1 flag combination (decides the card-identity design): in an ISOLATED CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (the repo's existing isolated real-Claude method; never ~/.claude), run `claude --resume P --fork-session --session-id C --permission-mode plan -n x -- '<boundary> hi'` against a seeded 2-turn parent. Decide: does it accept `--session-id` with `--fork-session`, honour C, and take a positional prompt together with --resume? If it refuses, fall back to a per-run 'expects fork' flag in the adapter that binds the first reported id (still verify id != parent).

E2 hook payload: with a logging SessionStart hook, record `source` and `session_id` of the fork. Decides whether `ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:241` (clear/fork -> .new, resume -> .resume) needs a side-run special case, and whether presetting `providerConversationID` fully prevents the duplicate-card path in ProcessSupervisor.adoptConversation.

E3 mid-turn fork: fork while the parent PTY is mid-turn and while it waits on a permission prompt. Look at the child's transcript for a dangling tool_use, whether the child tries to continue the parent's plan despite the boundary, and whether plan mode really blocks edits. Decides whether Ask Aside is allowed during Working / Needs approval or only at the prompt.

E4 cache and cost: read `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` of the fork's first assistant usage line (it is in the child's own JSONL, no API instrumentation) warm (<5 min after parent's turn) and cold, with default `--system-prompt-snapshot`. Decides the cost hint, whether to warn on large contexts, and whether the same-prefix claim in claude-official holds.

E5 residue: diff the isolated config tree before/after a fork and after a Loom-style delete by child id; check `ClaudeDataInventory.plan([child])` leaves `residual` empty and that the parent's data is untouched. Also check the child JSONL keeps the parent's `message.id`s so ClaudeUsageIndex dedupe (key 'm|'+id) does not double count: run the usage scan on the temp profile before and after.

E6 listing pollution: does the interactive fork show in `claude --resume` and `claude agents`? (chat-ui-paths says only headless forks are tagged programmatic.) Decides whether 'Aside:' naming is enough or the picker pollution is a reason to default to auto-discard of empty side chats.

Pass/stop criteria: build if E1+E2 give a verifiable child id without duplicate cards, E3 shows plan mode holds, and E5 residue is covered by the existing deleter; accept a weaker cost story if E4 is poor, but then show the context size before the first ask.
user_decisions: Layout: v1 swaps the side chat into the detail pane in place (parent never resized, but you cannot watch the main run at the same time), or a right-hand split now? A split narrows the parent's Claude TUI (SIGWINCH reflow, 480 pt detail minimum, D-34 says no right sidebar yet).

Read-only strictness: `--permission-mode plan` (CLI-enforced; some read-only Bash will prompt) vs prompt-only boundary like Codex vs an 'Allow edits' toggle like T3. Recommendation: plan by default, promote to edit.

Persistence: persistent child with explicit Discard (recommended, matches the Codex #26227/#40854 demand) vs ephemeral auto-delete on close like Claude Desktop and Codex /side. And: may Discard of an unpromoted side chat skip the confirmation dialog?
Cascade: deleting a parent also deletes its side chats (they hold a copy of its history). Confirm.
Do you accept that a fork is a snapshot of what Claude has saved (a running step is not included), and that Bring Back only pastes into the main prompt and you press Enter?
Cost: a fork and every reopen re-read the whole context; is spending plan window on that acceptable by default, and do you want a context-size hint before the first ask?
Should side runs ever stop on their own (idle, or when the parent ends)? D-38 says no idle stops; the recommendation is no timers at all.
Entry: a one-field question popover plus Cmd+; (recommended), or open an empty side terminal only?

Scope: contract §13 lists the side chat as an idea without a scope decision, so it needs your explicit go before it enters a plan. Also confirm that the PTY child (not a chat-style renderer) is acceptable for the first version.

feasibility.one_line: Build only a one-tenant right pane for a real forked side session (not a generic tabbed panel), but first run a CLI fork/hook/cache/resize spike, because the pane is the cheap part and the child-session plumbing is the risk.
feasibility.loom_design:
SCOPE CUT. Subagents are already solved: the sidebar tree plus the in-place read-only transcript (CatalogModel+Subagents.swift, SubagentTranscriptView/Model, D-54 P1, chosen days ago, "terminal is not resized"). Changes and note tabs are separate ideas (checkpoint diff L, vault notes). So I-10 reduces to: a collapsible right pane whose first and only tenant is a side chat. Add a tab or enum host only when a second tenant exists (YAGNI). Possible second tenant later: "show this subagent beside" reusing SubagentTranscriptView unchanged.

1) SHELL (S-M). MainSplitViewController.swift already is an NSSplitViewController with sidebarItem + contentItem (detail min 480). Add a third NSSplitViewItem(inspectorWithViewController:), collapsed by default. Mirror SidebarCollapseSync/SplitViewItemCollapse for collapse truth and persist width/open flag in UIPreferences (sidebarWidth/sidebarCollapsed pattern, new optional keys decoded with decodeIfPresent so old files load). Mount its SwiftUI content lazily: the hosting controller's rootView is an empty placeholder while collapsed, real content only while open, so a collapsed pane observes nothing and draws nothing (NSSplitViewItem collapse only hides the view; it does not stop SwiftUI observation). New view files only: LoomCatalogUI/SidePanelView.swift, SidePanelHeader (parent state pill reused from StatePill, child state, Stop, Promote, Discard, Close), CatalogModel+SidePanel.swift (keep out of the 1,612-line CatalogModel.swift). Pane chrome follows DetailView panel rules (10 pt radius, hairline, panel fill); all values via LoomTheme (scripts/check-theme-literals.sh).

2) SIDE SESSION = a normal Loom session, not a new runtime. Path already exists: approveOpen / startConversation(opening:) start a session without moving selection, in its own run scope (RunScopeLauncher), with openedBy. Add: ClaudeRoute.fork(parentProviderID, newID) in ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(route:...) producing `--resume <parent> --fork-session --session-id <newID>` (verify combination in the spike), keep `--settings`/hooks/--plugin-dir exactly as for any run; `ProviderCapabilities.supportsForkSession = help.contains("--fork-session")` and add it to detectedClaudeOptions/missingRequiredClaudeOptions like the other options (drift is journaled once, the start still proceeds, per the existing rule). New SessionRuntime+SideSessions.swift: startSideSession(of:question:mode:) -> reuses createSession/launch; a new nullable catalog column sessions.side_of added by the same ensureOriginColumns/ensureActivityColumn pattern (no schema bump, 0.2.1/0.3.0 still open the catalog). No JSONL copying (reject Happy's copyFile approach; it breaks on format drift).

3) ASK-FIRST LAUNCH, zero idle cost. Opening the pane shows a SwiftUI composer only (no process). On Enter, Loom starts the fork with the boundary text and the question as the Claude positional prompt (the existing `trailingArguments` after `--`, as ClaudeOpening does): "Everything above is reference only; do not continue its plans or tool calls; no subagents; no edits unless asked here. Question: ...". Boundary goes in the message, not the system prompt, to keep the cached prefix. After that the pane swaps to the child's live TerminalContainerView (model.terminalView(for:) already returns it; TerminalContainerView.viewDidMoveToWindow steals first responder, so focus must be made explicit for the pane). Read-only default via --permission-mode plan (cache-friendly: mode text lives in messages) with an "Allow edits" toggle (T3 PR #18243); do NOT use --tools to restrict (changes tool definitions, would miss the cache) unless the spike shows otherwise.

4) LISTS AND ATTENTION. Child is hidden from lists by `AND s.side_of IS NULL` in SessionCatalog+Paging.swift (sessionPage, searchSessions window query), SessionCatalog+Projects.swift sessionCounts, classifyStale/oldestStaleCandidate, and the CatalogModel+Patching listedSession path; it is NOT hidden from attention: its hook state still feeds SessionEventHub, so approvals/notifications/menu bar/Dock badge/Cmd+J (AttentionOrder) work unchanged and the pane toggle shows an attention dot when the child needs approval or finished. The parent's approval is already always visible because the parent terminal and RequestList stay on screen beside the pane (this is the OpenChamber v2.4.0 failure the split layout avoids by construction; with a slide-over it would have to be re-solved). Under the parent card show a one-line child row like SubagentTree, or only a small glyph.

5) LIFECYCLE (all event-driven, no polling). Open pane: nothing runs. Send: start child (state Starting until SessionStart/registry confirms; failure shown, never reported as started). Close pane while child Working: keep running, pane toggle shows Working; when child is idle/finished and the pane is closed, optional one-shot timer armed from the Stop hook stops it (SessionLifecycleController idle machinery exists; stopsIdleRuns is false in the app, D-38, so this needs the user's OK). Stop = existing verified ProcessSupervisor.stop; Quit already stops all runs. The record survives (hidden, reachable from the parent's menu "Side chats"); Promote = clear side_of (one UPDATE + hub frame); Discard = existing ConversationDeletion flow (dry run, verified). Usage is already deduped by message.id (ClaudeUsageIndex), so the fork's copied history is not double-counted.

6) BOUNDS. At most one live side child per parent and (say) 2 live globally; no auto-open ever; a context-size hint before the first send ("re-reads ~N tokens; cache may be cold"). Fork sees only what the parent has flushed to its transcript (say so in the UI).

HONEST COST. Shell alone S-M. The real work is the child-session plumbing (fork route, side_of column and 4-5 query filters, lifecycle/Promote/Discard, focus, tests with loom-fake-provider, ARCHITECTURE/UI-MAP/DECISIONS updates): whole thing L (the research's M is right for the pane, not for the feature). No new polling, no new process type, no new socket.
