Open: the detail panel narrows and a second rounded panel appears on the right (default 420 pt, draggable 340-640, remembered). Top of the pane: "Side chat" title, parent's state pill ("main: needs approval / working / finished", the Codex SideParentStatus idea, from liveStates), child's state pill, Allow-edits toggle, Stop, and a menu (Promote to session, Copy last answer to main prompt, Discard, Close). Body: before the first send a text box "Ask something about this session" with the context-size hint; after it, the live terminal of the forked Claude. Esc in the box or a click on the main terminal returns focus to main. Width warning: at the default 1220 pt window, sidebar 300 plus a 420 pt pane leaves roughly 55 columns for main and 44 for the pane, so opening the pane should offer to collapse the sidebar (or stay a slide-over), and it is comfortable only from about 1450 pt (full screen on a 14-inch laptop).
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: PASS if the pane mounts content lazily and the child exists only after Send (collapsed pane = no SwiftUI observation, no process, no vnode source; hidden terminals already suspend rendering via suspendsRenderingWhenNotVisible); RISK: a second live Claude is a few hundred MB RSS and a fork re-reads the whole context (cache reuse across sessions unverified), so show the hint and cap live children. A violation would be a persistent hidden child, a poll of the parent's transcript, or an always-mounted SwiftUI pane. Predictable: PASS (user-initiated only, never auto-open). Accurate status: PASS with care (started only after SessionStart/registry confirmation, stop and delete use the existing verified paths, "sees only flushed transcript" disclosed); RISK: PTY resize mid-turn of the main Claude (Ink reflow artifacts) has not been measured. Fluency: PASS (ask-first launch, no confirms except Discard). Modularity: PASS if kept in new files and a CatalogModel extension; RISK: the side_of filter must be applied in every list query or hidden children leak into counts and search. CLI-update resilience: PASS (documented flags --resume/--fork-session/--session-id/--permission-mode, feature-detected from help, drift journaled, no private-file copying); RISK: --fork-session with --session-id and the hook's SessionStart source are inferred, not verified here (`claude --help` 2.1.300 confirms --fork-session and --session-id exist separately). Ownership: PASS (child in its own run scope, Stop/Quit verified, deletion via ConversationDeletion). User authority: PASS (user opens it; the child inherits LOOM_CLI so it could still raise an open-session request, which keeps its approval card). Contract: the child IS the real CLI in a PTY, so the "terminal is never replaced by a custom chat UI" rule is not touched; D-34 ("no right sidebar now, side chat later") is what must be lifted; contract section 13 already lists "side chat and right panel" as an unscoped wish.
feasibility.value_reason: The side chat is the user's oldest wish and fits a heavy multi-agent workflow (ask "why did you do that" without derailing a long turn, with tools and a persistent thread, which native /btw lacks), but the generic panel with subagents, changes and notes tabs adds little: subagents are already served by the sidebar tree and transcript panel, and the others are separate ideas, so the whole of I-10 as written is about a 3 and the side-chat core is a 4.

feasibility.one_line: Adopt the verified half now (name the subagent that asked, using the agent_id Loom already receives, plus deterministic closure rules so no record stays 'running'); defer live per-subagent cost/context, which needs the subagentStatusLine bridge (I-24) and a tick-rate spike.
feasibility.loom_design:
KEY CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH: the 'agent id on permission events is unverified' debate is already settled in Loom. Hooks docs list agent_id/agent_type as common input fields on every hook fired inside a subagent, and FB2-6 (plans/FEEDBACK-2.md, real Claude, 12 Oct) observed PermissionRequest and permission_prompt Notification events carrying agent_id, which ClaudeHookEvent.isSubagentPermissionPrompt already uses. Loom just throws the identity away: ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive only sets .waitingForApproval plus subagentApprovalReturn, and ClaudeHookEvent.permissionRequest keeps toolName only. No new hook event is needed. Do NOT add PreToolUse/PostToolUse: ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings deliberately registers no per-tool hooks because each fires a loom-hook process; that would break the resource principle.

TIER 1 (adopt): attribution.
- SubagentRecord (SubagentLedger.swift) gains `approval: SubagentApproval?` (toolName, since). SubagentLedger gets noteApproval(agentID:toolName:at:) and clearApprovals(). If the prompt arrives before its SubagentStart (hooks are separate processes), keep a small bounded pending-ask map keyed by agent id and attach it when the record appears.
- ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive, in the existing isSubagentPermissionPrompt branch, calls noteApproval. It clears on exactly the existing clear points: the registry's next accepted idle/busy sample (receiveRegistry, where subagentApprovalReturn is cleared), any main-thread event (where subagentApprovalReturn = nil), that agent's SubagentStop, beginRun, and a new SessionStart. ProviderSessionAdapters.receive must also call publishSubagents for permission events that carry an agent_id, and after a registry sample that clears an ask. Today it publishes only on lifecycle, sessionStart, userPromptSubmit and stop. The existing .subagents hub change carries the data, so there is no new channel or watcher.
- Only the tool NAME is kept, never tool_input (a command line can hold secrets).

TIER 1b (adopt, after a small spike): never stuck 'running'. Loom's tree is hook-fed (SubagentStart/Stop plus Stop.background_tasks), not transcript-fed, so claude-hud's queue-operation / queued_command / task-id-only fixtures map only loosely. The real stuck cases here are:
 (1) a background subagent whose SubagentStop is lost. The helper has a 1 s timeout, and the ledger keeps an unlisted known-background record running because 'what an unlisted background subagent means is not verified' (SubagentLedger.turnEnded).
 (2) a foreground subagent when the user interrupts the turn. Docs: Stop does not run on a user interrupt, so turnEnded never fires, and the row reads 'Running 40m' until the next Stop.
 (3) kill or failure of a background task, which the hooks do not report.
 Event-driven closure rules, each added only after the spike confirms it:
 - An accepted registry sample 'idle' (receiveRegistry already reads it by vnode, no polling) ends all running records, because the code comments say Claude reports 'busy' while a background subagent runs.
 - A Stop whose background_tasks key is PRESENT ends known-background records it does not list. This needs ClaudeHookEvent to tell an absent key from an empty list, since BackgroundSubagentTask.parse(nil) and [] look the same today. Docs: the arrays are present when the task registry is reachable.
 - The synthetic UserPromptSubmit that ClaudeHookEvent already detects (promptIsSynthetic, '<\task-notification') may carry <task-id> and a status. If a spike shows it does, parse it to end that record and show 'Failed' or 'Stopped' as a verified outcome. Otherwise keep 'Finished' only.
 Never add a time-based guess: a long-running subagent is legitimate. The honest fallback is the elapsed time that the row already shows.
 Fixtures (Tests/LoomCoreTests/SubagentTests.swift style, plus the loom-fake-provider scripted subagents): lost background stop, interrupted turn, kill, prompt-before-start race, two simultaneous askers, /clear and fork and resume mid-run, a duplicated Start after Stop, and Claude's internal agents (SubagentStop with empty agent_type from prompt suggestions and /btw, which the ledger already ignores via !type.isEmpty).

TIER 2 (later, light): per-subagent tokens without any new I/O. ClaudeUsageIndex already indexes subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl (UsageTranscriptWalker.session maps subagent files to their owning session), keyed per file (msg.file_id) with dedupe by message id (which covers 'usage logged several times per response'). Add one query, tokens (and the last request's input as context fill) for a path. Call it only when a subagent panel is open (shown in the SubagentHeaderRow pill, e.g. 'Running 4m · 38k') and once when a record finishes (shown in the row's .help tooltip). Do not live-publish counts to every card: the card re-render and CatalogHotPathTests budgets would pay for it. Tool counts have no cheap live source. PostToolUse(Agent) only reports totalToolUseCount for foreground agents and gives no usage for background ones, which are the default. The alternative is one bounded SubagentTranscriptParser pass at SubagentStop, counting .toolCall entries with a size cap. Context PERCENT needs contextWindowSize, which is not in the transcript (200k vs 1M variants), so show absolute tokens only until the bridge exists.

TIER 3 (later, behind I-24, needs spike E2): subagentStatusLine via the per-session --settings JSON. Documented fields per task: status (running/completed/failed/killed, ground truth including failures and kills), tokenCount, contextWindowSize, model, effort, label, agentType (2.1.293+). It runs a command 'once per refresh tick' with all visible rows, so the process-spawn rate is the risk. Emit nothing to keep Claude's default row. A loom-hook sub-mode would forward the JSON over the existing authenticated hook socket as a new envelope kind.

Per-subagent Stop is not promised: no confirmed safe TUI equivalent of the SDK's Query.stopTask.

Resources: PASS for Tier 1 and 2. No new hook events, watchers, timers or processes. It rides the registry vnode and hook events already received, plus the existing FSEvents usage watcher. RISK for the idea as written: PreToolUse for agent_id would spawn a helper per tool call (refused in ProviderLaunchProfile). subagentStatusLine spawns a process per tick, so it needs the E2 measurement before any adoption.
Predictability: PASS. Fixed rules and bounded state: asks bounded by the ledger caps (50 running, 20 finished) and by the 200-id ended list.
Accurate status: PASS only with discipline. Attribution is verified (hook payload). Do not infer 'failed' or 'killed' without a verified source, since the contract requires started/stopped/delivered/deleted to be verified outcomes. Do not close records on a timeout. Each closure rule must be proven by the spike. Today's unlisted-background rule is explicitly marked unverified in the code, so this idea reduces the false-status risk.
Fluency: PASS. Faster triage of which subagent is blocking. No new prompts or waits.
Modularity: PASS. The change lives in LoomCore (ledger, tracker, adapter publish) plus pure value types in LoomCatalogUI (SubagentTreeContent is already unit-tested as a plain value). No new layer.
CLI-update resilience: PASS. agent_id and agent_type are documented common hook fields. If absent, the row degrades to today's session-level state (no ask is noted, nothing breaks). Registry statuses are already handled with unknown-value diagnostics. Transcript fields are not a contract, so Tier 2 must show 'unknown' on drift. Never pin the CLI.
Ownership: PASS. Read-only; nothing started or stopped.
User authority: PASS. No cross-session actions, and no per-subagent Stop is promised (no confirmed safe equivalent).
Contract/decisions: consistent with D-39 (the tree) and FB4-5 (the read-only panel). It touches no D-34 or terminal-is-real-CLI rule.

feasibility.loom_design:
AUDIT RESULT (code read, not run). Already covered: (a) `ClaudeHookEvent` parses `Stop.background_tasks` and `session_crons` into `ClaudeSessionStatus.backgroundTaskCount/scheduledTaskCount`; `ClaudeSessionAdapter` publishes `ProviderWorkState.pendingProviderWorkCount`; `SessionIndicator.init` shows `.working` for `.turnComplete` with pending>0; `SessionEventHub.activePhase` keeps it `.underWay`; synthetic hand-back prompts (`promptIsSynthetic`) do not start a user turn; `SubagentLedger` reconciles background subagents. (b) Hooks are injected only through the per-session `--settings` JSON in `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings` (nothing written to ~/.claude/settings.json, so no-op outside Loom by construction); `loom-hook` exits unless LOOM_SESSION_ID/LOOM_MANAGED_RUN_ID/token env are present; `ClaudeHookStateTracker.disposition` rejects wrongSession/staleRun/wrongConversation/retiredConversation/duplicateSessionStart and drops `agent_id` payloads as `.childAgent` (test `childAgentPayloadCannotMutateParentStatus`). (c-part) Informational notification types keep the state (`informationalNotificationsKeepTheState`); `idle_prompt` is not treated as a new completion (maps to waitingForInput, acknowledged via `waitingAcknowledged`). (d) Esc interrupt: the registry watch (`ClaudeRegistryWatch`, vnode-driven, no timer) turns Claude's own busy->idle into 'Waiting for you' (test `interruptedWorkingReturnsToInputWhileRealStopRemainsAuthoritative`; FEEDBACK-4 line 101 records the real behaviour). A Loom-side Esc/Ctrl-C timer would need raw key interception in LoomTerminal, add a heuristic, and duplicate a verified signal: skip. (e) `SessionViewState` is in-memory only and `runStarted` resets `unviewedCompletion/activePhase/status`, so no Working survives a launch and resume/clear never set unviewedCompletion (it needs a Stop transition to `.turnComplete`); `PreviousRunRecovery`/`closeAbandonedRuns` handle catalog rows.
REAL GAPS (to build): (1) Sticky Failed. In `ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive`, `.notification` of idle_prompt/agent_needs_input/elicitation_dialog assigns `currentStatus.activity = .waitingForInput` unconditionally, so a `.failed` set by StopFailure is downgraded to 'Waiting for you' when the idle notice arrives (about 60 s later, if Claude sends it after a failed turn: unverified). Fix: a notification with activity .waitingForInput may not replace `.failed`; only UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart (new conversation) or SessionEnd leave it. Registry samples already cannot override it (generation is nil after Stop). Mirror the guard in `receiveRegistry`. (2) Pinned sequences in `ClaudeHookTests`/`SessionEventHubTests`: StopFailure -> idle_prompt; Stop(bg>0) -> idle_prompt -> synthetic UserPromptSubmit -> Stop(bg=0) (one real completion, unviewed set once); SessionStart(compact/resume/clear) after a viewed turn leaves unviewedCompletion false; PreCompact is not registered, so test that SessionStart(source=compact) of the same conversation is a duplicate that keeps Working. Use exact payloads from existing recordings (Claude 2.1.287 sequences in ClaudeRegistryTests). (3) Drift evidence: today only unknown registry statuses are journaled (`noteUnknownRegistryStatus`); add the same once-per-token `cli_compat_warning` for an unknown `notification_type`, an unknown `hook_event_name` (`ClaudeHookEvent.Kind.unknown`) and unexpected Stop field shapes (background_tasks neither array nor dict), through `supervisor.journal` with the existing `ClaudeRegistryDiagnostics.token` sanitising. Note `.unknown` event currently sets activity .unknown; it is unreachable for unregistered events, so leave it. (4) 'Why' readout, pull not push: add to `ClaudeHookStateTracker` a bounded ring (last 8 entries) of {signal name (hook event / notification_type / registry status / watchdog), receivedAt, from, to} recorded only when `activity` actually changes; expose `ClaudeSessionAdapter.explain(sessionID:)` -> `SessionRuntime` -> a `ConversationIntents` closure (same pattern as `subagentTranscript`) -> a pure `StatusExplanation.make(record:live:transitions:)` in LoomCatalogUI that also names the UI-layer cause the tracker cannot know (stopFailure, issue, identityUnclear, open-request approval, waitingAcknowledged, unviewedCompletion, pending work count). Do NOT put the reason into `ProviderWorkState` or `SessionViewState` (extra fields or timestamps would break frame de-duplication in `SessionEventHub.publish` and re-trigger `SessionLifecycleController` evaluations). Also append the last transitions and the existing `HookDiagnostics` drop counts to Collect Diagnostics (`SessionRuntime+Diagnostics`), which is the copy-paste evidence path. (5) Optional later, after the spike: a distinct pill label for 'Background work' (StatePillStyle already accepts a label override, as the subagent panel's 'Running 4m' does).
TRIGGERS/BOUNDS: all event-driven (hook arrival, registry vnode, user click); no timers, no polling, no new hooks (PreCompact/PostToolUse stay unregistered: each hook spawns a helper); memory 8 small entries per live run, freed with the tracker on run end; popover costs one actor call on click.
`loom status --explain` is out of scope: `loom-hook` only has the `open` command and the cross-session channel (D-43/D-46) is undated; revisit when that channel exists, reusing the same explain function.

feasibility.one_line: Receiving OSC 7501 fits Loom's principles as a passive, hooks-subordinate cross-check, but most of the promised user gain (reason and message text) is already available from hook fields Loom drops, so run a half-day wire-capture spike first and adopt only a light version if Claude emits 7501 in states hooks miss.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS (read in the tree): (1) Each live run has its own TerminalSurface for the whole run, selected or not (ConversationController.adopt/entries/keepEndedScreen); ended runs keep only a snapshot. So a per-surface receiver exists exactly when a PTY exists, with no cost for idle records. (2) SwiftTerm already has a public OSC override, Terminal.registerOscHandler(code:handler:), which runs synchronously inside parser dispatch under the terminal lock, in stream order with the later CSI c reply, and a public observeOscEvents on TerminalView. But TerminalView.terminal is internal, so a surface cannot reach registerOscHandler today. observeOscEvents is asynchronous (private queue) and copies every OSC including the frequent title updates, and its reply would arrive after the DA reply, so Claude would count the terminal as unsupported (spec: if the CSI c reply comes first, unsupported). (3) Claude 2.1.300 is installed here; its bundle contains the probe strings 'probe: no reply to OSC 7501 ; ?' and 'probe: OSC 7501 reply', plus probes for XTVERSION, CSI ? u, DECRPM 2026/1016 and the graphics query. The exact emitted kinds and msg texts cannot be read from the bundle. (4) The spec (revision 0.4, read from superlogical.com) fixes: whole sequence <= 4096 bytes, msg <= 2048 decoded bytes, reply to the probe is `OSC 7501 ; ? ST`, optionally with states= and kinds= lists (omitting them means the five fixed states and three kinds), terminals must refuse a report whose decoded msg or title contains control characters, and 'MUST NOT read meaning into msg'. working and blocked records drop at process exit, done and error persist, no heartbeat.

DESIGN (lightest version, three small pieces):
A. Vendor patch 15 in Vendor/SwiftTerm (same shape as patch 14, about 10 lines): a nonisolated TerminalView.setOscOverride(code:handler:) that forwards through renderOwner to Terminal.registerOscHandler. Document it in LOOM-VENDOR.md and the Updating list. No other engine change.
B. LoomTerminal: TerminalSurface installs a handler for code 7501 in init. Handler (feed thread, under the lock) does only: if payload == '?', terminal.sendResponse(ESC ] 7501 ; ? ESC \) (bare '?', the lowest commitment; the reply goes through the existing TerminalSurface.send -> TerminalInputQueue path, and before attach it is held in the bounded .launching buffer, so it is ordered ahead of the DA reply that the same parse pass produces). Otherwise call a pure parser (new file, e.g. LoomCore/ProgramStatus.swift: ProgramStatusReport, ProgramStatusParser) that enforces the spec limits, drops a whole report on any bad pair or control character, decodes base64, strips bidi and format characters, truncates msg to about 160 characters for display, and keeps at most about 8 records per run (root plus children by id, least recently updated evicted). It yields the changed root/summary into a bufferingNewest(1) AsyncStream, so a burst costs one wake-up. The surface exposes onProgramStatus like onTitle; ConversationController.adopt wires it by runID, resolving the owner when it fires (the existing pattern).
C. LoomCore: SessionRuntime gets deliverProgramStatus(runID:report:) -> ClaudeSessionAdapter -> ClaudeHookStateTracker as an evidence field only (never writes currentStatus.activity). A small ProgramStatusComparer maps hook activity to the expected 7501 state (working<->working, waitingForApproval<->blocked/permission, waitingForInput<->blocked/question or idle, turnComplete/atPrompt<->done or idle) and, only when they differ, arms ONE one-shot timer per run (about 2 s settle, cancelled on agreement or any hook) because hooks arrive through a spawned loom-hook process after the in-band report. A disagreement that outlives the window is journaled once per kind as cli_compat_warning (same dedupe as ClaudeSessionAdapter.noteUnknownRegistryStatus); nothing is shown. 'Probe answered but no report by the first Stop' is journaled once per app run, with the CLI version from ProviderCapabilities.version and the user's CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE excluded, as a drift signal.
D. Optional display step, only after the spike: publish a short SessionViewState.statusDetail (kind plus sanitized msg) through SessionEventHub and show it where the label already lives (detail header state pill or its tooltip, and the menu-bar row), never as new card text and never in notification bodies.

TRIGGERS AND BOUNDS: every step is driven by bytes already arriving on the PTY or by a hook; no polling, no timer except the one-shot above. No work when nothing is reported (Claude sends no heartbeat). Parse is bounded by 4096 bytes per report and 8 records per run, memory is a few KiB per run, the handler never blocks (no actor hop, no allocation beyond the report). Hidden window: PTY feed and parse continue as today, the handler adds no draw. Nothing persists; records vanish with the surface when the run ends.

AUTHORITY RULE (matches contract section on hybrid sources: 'which state comes from which source, and the conflict rule, must be explicit'): hooks own identity, transitions, notifications, Dock badge, Cmd+J order and Finished unviewed. 7501 may only add evidence and a sanitized reason string. 7501 `done` must never create Finished unviewed (that comes from Stop plus Loom's own viewed tracking). The 7501 stream is unauthenticated terminal output (anything printed into the PTY can forge it), unlike the token-checked hook socket, so it must not drive attention state, notifications or any cross-session action.

CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE THAT COVERS MOST OF THE STATED GAIN: Loom already parses PermissionRequest.tool_name (ClaudeHookEvent.Kind.permissionRequest(toolName:)) but drops Notification.message and tool_input. Reading `message` from the Notification hook and showing tool_name in the header gives the 'reason with text' on the authenticated channel with no vendor patch. Do this regardless of the 7501 decision.

RESILIENCE UPSIDE (not a promise): Loom's second status source today is ClaudeRegistry, an undocumented ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json file read behind vnode watches and strict identity checks (ClaudeRegistry.swift, ClaudeRegistryReader.decode). 7501 is a documented, generic protocol that gives the same busy/waiting/idle information in-band. If the spike shows it reliable across a few Claude releases, it could later replace or back up the registry watch, which would remove a private-format dependency.

The sidebar card stays as is: UI-MAP says the label text is shown in the header and the accessibility label, not on the card, and the card is a deliberate dot-only design, so a message line on the card would reverse a design decision and needs the user's say. feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass. Event-driven, bounded (4096 B per report, 8 records per run), one-shot timer only on disagreement, nothing when the window is hidden or the run is idle or ended. Risk: a tool-heavy turn could emit many reports; mitigate with a bufferingNewest(1) stream and measure in the spike against the 40% of a core at 1 MiB/s gate. Predictability: pass if 7501 never overrides hooks; risk if a later change lets it set state, because receivers disagree on precedence. Accurate status: pass as evidence-only; `done` mapped to Finished unviewed would be a violation, and so would trusting an unauthenticated PTY stream to raise Needs approval or a notification. Fluency: neutral to small gain; the probe is answered with no prompt or setting. Modularity: pass; parser in LoomCore (pure, testable), surface hook in LoomTerminal, comparer in the adapter; costs one more vendored patch (the 15th) that must be re-applied on every SwiftTerm update. CLI-update resilience: mostly pass (documented in Claude's terminal-config docs, generic protocol, feature-detected, unknown keys and states ignored, never pinned); risks are that the spec is revision 0.4 (a draft), the probe order is user-reported (issue 101114), and answering the probe could change other Claude behaviour, for example the terminal title that Loom stores as the session title (CatalogModel.terminalTitleChanged / recordTerminalTitle); the spike must check this. Ownership: no process or file is created. User authority: nothing cross-session; msg is untrusted text, rendered as plain text, never put in notification bodies, and not interpreted (the spec says terminals must not read meaning into msg). Settings and CLAUDE.md of the user are untouched.\nThings that would make it a violation: polling the registry or screen to compare, letting 7501 set currentStatus.activity, parsing msg for meaning, showing unsanitized msg, or a per-OSC observer that copies every title update (use the synchronous override for code 7501 only).
feasibility.value_reason: Hooks plus the registry already give this user Working, Needs approval, Waiting for you, Failed and Finished unviewed, and a hook fires at the same moment as the 7501 report (the spawn latency of loom-hook is tens of milliseconds, not perceptible). The reason text can come from hook fields at near-zero cost. What 7501 adds uniquely is coverage of states with no hook (startup folder-trust or login dialogs, hooks disabled or lost), drift evidence, and a documented replacement path for the private registry file. For a user with 5 to 10 parallel sessions in two projects these are rare edge cases, though they get more valuable if v2 moves toward a chat-centred UI that wants a precise 'needs you because' line, because 7501 is UI-agnostic. Honest re-estimate: cost S holds for the passive receiver (patch, parser, surface hook, journal), but the proposed card reason and disagreement logic make it M.

feasibility.one_line: Adopt a small version: show Stop's last_assistant_message and PermissionRequest's tool_name/tool_input (already in the hook payloads Loom receives) as a bounded, memory-only line that is shown only while the matching state holds, on attention cards (or as a tooltip first), plus a richer approval banner; defer the agent-set note, and treat title precedence as already satisfied.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS FROM THE CODE (what already exists)
- ClaudeHookEvent (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeHook.swift:364-478) already parses last_assistant_message. ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive copies it into ClaudeSessionStatus.lastAssistantMessage on Stop and StopFailure (lines ~766-776). Nothing outside tests and loom-probe reads it, so it never reaches SessionViewState or the UI. ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:~260-312) stores the status in lastStatuses and publishes only ProviderWorkState(activity, pendingProviderWorkCount).
- Not parsed today: Notification message/title (Kind is notification(type:)), PermissionRequest tool_input (Kind is permissionRequest(toolName:)), and SessionStart session_title.
- The generated hook settings (ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings, ~180-208) register SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, Notification, PermissionRequest, SessionEnd, SubagentStart and SubagentStop, with timeout 1. There is no PreToolUse or PostToolUse, on purpose ("each hook spawns a helper").
- Claude approvals happen in the terminal and the hook returns no decision. Loom has no in-app approval box for Claude. SessionViewState.userRequests is the Codex path (paused) and DetailView's RequestList. The only Claude-side boxes are the open-session request boxes. So part (e) cannot be "a sentence on the approval box"; it becomes the card line, the tooltip and the banner body.
- Approval banners: ApprovalNotificationPlanner posts on the transition into Needs approval while Loom is inactive and removes the banner when the session leaves it. ApprovalNotifier.approvalsChanged is fed by the menu bar summary (AppDelegate+System.swift:35-37). The body is the fixed text "<project> · Claude is waiting for your approval." There is no finished or needs-input banner (D-52 chose approvals only, no sound). Removal on resume and "cap simultaneous toasts" are therefore already covered: Loom has no in-app toasts and macOS does the stacking.
- Titles (part d): SessionCatalog+Titles.swift has title_is_custom. renameSession sets it; recordTerminalTitle (fed only by Claude's OSC title via ConversationController.titleChanged) writes only WHERE title_is_custom = 0. Hooks and approval text never touch the title. The user > Claude's own title ordering therefore already exists and Warp's overwrite bug class cannot happen here. The docs answer the "where is /rename stored" unknown: SessionStart carries a documented session_title (set via --name, /rename, a hook or the SDK; generated titles are excluded), and the statusLine JSON carries session_name. Loom must not use the statusLine (a helper spawn per refresh, and it collides with the user's own statusLine). Whether a mid-session /rename reaches the OSC title is unverified.
- The skill/plugin (part c): ClaudeLoomPlugin.install rewrites its files from the app's source into <data root>/claude-plugin whenever they differ, so the skill is already version-matched. A "thin stub that asks the app for instructions" adds nothing here.
- The control socket (OpenSessionProtocol.swift) is shaped only for `open`: OpenSessionWireRequest has title/ticket/project/message and protocolVersion 1. A note command would need a command discriminator, a new handler, a new CLI verb in OpenSessionCommand and a second skill.

DESIGN (smallest version that pays)
1. Core, pure and tested like ApprovalNotificationPlanner: new `AttentionText` type in LoomCore. It sanitizes (drops control, bidi and zero-width scalars, collapses whitespace, grapheme-safe cut), takes the LAST ~240 characters of last_assistant_message (a question sits at the end; a summary's tail is the outcome) and the first ~160 of a tool summary, and keeps a ~600-byte peek variant. `summary(tool:input:)` covers the documented tool_input shapes: Bash.command, Edit/Write/Read.file_path, WebFetch.url, Grep/Glob.pattern, an MCP tool shown as "server: tool". An unknown tool shows just the tool name.
2. Hook layer: ClaudeHookEvent also reads PermissionRequest tool_input (only the few fields above; Write content is skipped, but the payload is already JSON-decoded today), the Notification message/title (used only for elicitation_dialog; permission_prompt and idle_prompt texts are generic: "Claude needs your permission"), and truncates lastAssistantMessage at parse time. This also removes up to 1 MiB per live session now kept in tracker and lastStatuses.
3. State: add `attention: AttentionNote?` to SessionViewState plus a SessionEventChange case, published beside .status from ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive, in the same serialized transition and BEFORE the status change. That way the Needs-approval set change (which triggers the banner) already sees the text. The note holds (kind: approval | input | finished | failed, text). Memory only: nothing in the catalog and no second copy of the transcript (contract §8 "deleted is not an archive", the "no second copy" rule at contract line 209, schema untouched). SessionEventHub.publish dedupes equal states, the reducer clears the note on working, a new run, a detach and the run's end, and a relaunch shows nothing.
4. Accuracy by construction: the UI shows the note only while SessionIndicator maps to the same kind (waitingForApproval, waitingForInput or unviewedCompletion, failed). A stale note can never appear against a different status. It is never an input to the indicator, the Active section, Cmd+J or the badge counts.
5. Card: the existing two-row card (DESIGN §1 item 4) gains an optional third line only for the four attention kinds, 11 pt secondary (not tertiary), one line, tail-truncated, plain `Text(verbatim:)` (never Markdown or LocalizedStringKey, so agent text cannot render as formatting or links). The same text goes into `.help` (native tooltip, about 600 bytes) as the "peek". Start with the tooltip and decide on the third line with a preview HTML, as the repo does for design changes. Read the note inside the card body only. Do not add a new observed property per card beyond live.attention.
6. Banner: title stays the session title. Add a subtitle "Needs approval · <project>" and a body "Bash: git push origin feature/x" from the note, with an optional "· <branch>" from BranchCache. With no note (older CLI, missing field) the current generic body is used. The id-based remove-on-leave stays.
7. Menu bar rows: the same text as the NSMenuItem tooltip. MenuBarRowText stays unchanged.
8. Title (d): no code change. Add one invariant test (a hook, an approval or an agent note never changes the title or title_is_custom). Optionally read the documented SessionStart.session_title as a provider-title input to the existing recordTerminalTitle path, which keeps the custom-title guard. That is S and only worth doing if the spike below shows /rename does not reach the OSC title.
9. Agent note (c): do not build now. It needs a protocol bump, a handler, a CLI verb, a second skill and about 80 more tokens of skill description in every session. It also depends on the model choosing to call it, and every update is a tool call that costs latency and tokens. For this user, mid-turn Working sessions are the ones that do not need triage; Stop already delivers the agent's own words for free. If it is ever built, reuse the requester check in OpenSessionCoordinator.authorize (run live, launch card == LOOM_SESSION_ID), cap it at 140 characters and 1 write per 10 s, clear it on UserPromptSubmit, render it with an "agent-reported" glyph, and never let it touch status.

TRIGGERS AND BOUNDS: everything is driven by hook events Loom already receives (Stop, StopFailure, PermissionRequest, Notification). There is no timer, no polling and no transcript read. The cost is one capped string per live session. The card line costs nothing when the card is not drawn. The tooltip costs nothing until hover.

WHAT WOULD VIOLATE A PRINCIPLE: reading the transcript for "last said" (undocumented format, and the doc says the transcript lags the hook); adding PreToolUse or PostToolUse hooks for text (a helper spawn per tool); persisting the text; letting the text decide status; rendering it as Markdown; calling a model to summarize (cmux's auto-name hook); adding a card line to every card (density, layout jumps).
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Sidebar card, attention states only (and in practice only the cards in the Active section or "Waiting for you"): the usual two rows, then one 11 pt secondary line under the branch row. Examples:
- Needs approval: "Bash: git push origin feature/EDDP-412"
- Waiting for you / Finished: "...want me to keep the old endpoint, or remove it?" (the tail of the last message)
- Failed: "API error: rate_limit".
A Working, Ready, Idle or ended card is unchanged (exactly two rows). Hovering a card with a note shows a tooltip holding the longer text (~600 bytes) as a read-only peek; a real popover is a later option, only if the tooltip proves too small. Banner: title = session title; subtitle "Needs approval · <project>"; body = tool summary (+ branch). Menu bar rows: the same text as the item tooltip. The detail header and terminal are unchanged. feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS. Event-driven, one capped string per live session, nothing read or drawn when hidden. It reduces memory (truncating the retained 1 MiB message). The risk is a card re-evaluating on every live change, which is already true; SidebarRenderTests/CatalogHotPathTests should gain a case showing that a note change touches only that card.
- Predictability: PASS. The note appears only with its state and follows the same rule everywhere (card, tooltip, banner, menu).
- Accurate status: PASS if the note is gated by the indicator kind and never feeds it. RISK: "waiting for you" text is only the last message, not necessarily a question; label and tooltip must say "last message", not "asking". A second PermissionRequest during an unchanged Needs-approval period updates the card text but not the already-posted banner.
- Fluency: PASS. No confirmations or waits; it removes trips into sessions to find out what they want. RISK: card height changes when a state flips (the list shifts under the pointer). Limit the line to attention states and keep it fixed to one line.
- Modularity: PASS. `AttentionText` is pure in LoomCore; the UI only reads. The change touches ClaudeHook, ProviderSessionAdapters, SessionEventHub, SessionViewState, CatalogModel apply/patching, SidebarView, ApprovalNotifier and the planner.
- CLI-update resilience: PASS. Only documented fields (Stop.last_assistant_message, Notification.message/title, PermissionRequest.tool_name/tool_input). A missing field degrades to today's UI. Do not parse the transcript. The tool_input field names per tool are only partly specified, so fall back to the tool name.
- Ownership: not involved.
- User authority: PASS. Display only. The agent-set note (c) also only labels the caller's own session and needs no cross-session authority, but it is deferred.
- Privacy and security (not on the list but binding): the text is untrusted and is displayed verbatim only (no Markdown or links, bidi and control scalars stripped, hard caps). Commands and paths can contain secrets, and they would appear in banners. macOS already offers Notifications → Loom → Show previews (When Unlocked / Never) for the lock screen. A Loom switch "Show details in banners" is S and covers screen sharing; a user decision.
- Contract: "the terminal is the real CLI" is untouched. D-34 (no right rail) is untouched. "No second copy of transcripts": satisfied by memory-only storage. DESIGN §1 item 4 (two-row card, no status words) needs a design preview and a decision from the user for a third line.
feasibility.value_reason: With 3 or more sessions across two EDDP projects, the real cost is deciding which session to open and why. Today the card says only "Waiting for you" or "Needs approval", and the banner is the fixed text "Claude is waiting for your approval". The data is already in the hooks Loom receives and part of it is already parsed, so most of the benefit costs only plumbing. It scores 4 rather than 5 for two reasons. The fact-check says auto mode is now the default starting mode, so approvals are rarer (the banner part matters less than the last-message part). Selecting a live session in Loom is also cheap, since its terminal is already running. The agent note (c) alone would be about 2, so it is not worth its protocol and token cost.
experiments: Hook payload recording with an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, using the existing loom-probe HookRecorder (Sources/loom-probe/HookRecorder.swift) against a real current claude. Record Notification payloads for permission_prompt, idle_prompt and elicitation_dialog. What decides it: whether `message` carries anything beyond the generic text (if not, only PermissionRequest and Stop feed the line; if elicitation_dialog carries the MCP prompt, include it).

Same recording, PermissionRequest tool_input for Bash, Edit, Write, Read, WebFetch and an MCP tool. What decides it: the exact field names used by `AttentionText.summary`, and whether a large Write payload keeps the 1 MiB hook cap safe.

Same recording, does PermissionRequest fire in an interactive session for AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode? Loom has no PreToolUse hook, so if it does not fire, the most useful 'what is it asking' text (a multiple-choice question) is missing. What decides it: whether to leave that gap or register `PreToolUse` with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode` (matcher-filtered, so there is no helper spawn per ordinary tool; verify that on the real CLI) as a follow-up.

Stop.last_assistant_message shape: is it the whole final text or just the last text block, and is it empty when the turn ends in a tool call or after a background-task Stop? What decides it: tail-versus-head truncation and the empty-string handling.

Does a mid-session /rename or --name change reach Claude's OSC title that ConversationController.titleChanged already receives, and does SessionStart (startup, resume, compact) carry session_title? What decides it: whether the optional session_title read is needed or the current terminal-title path already satisfies the precedence rule.

feasibility.one_line: Loom is already 80% wired for it (per-session `--settings` PermissionRequest hook, authenticated sockets, a Codex-era approval box), but the one fact that decides safety (does the CLI dialog wait for or race the hook, and does a terminal answer cancel it) is unmeasured, so run a half-day hook-race spike, then build a small first slice (box + banner buttons + menu rows, no hotkey, no Always/Bypass).
feasibility.loom_design:
OBSERVED STARTING POINT. (1) ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings already injects a per-session inline `--settings` JSON whose hooks include PermissionRequest, but as a fire-and-forget `loom-hook` command with `timeout: 1` and the comment "helpers return no provider decision"; nothing goes to the user's settings.json (contract section 9 says the same). (2) ClaudeHookServer is one-shot: it reads one message under a 1 s deadline, closes, and never answers, so the decision channel cannot reuse it. (3) The control socket (OpenSessionControlServer, `c-<8>.sock`, same token, LocalSocket, up to 32 held connections, `Task.detached` handler, `finish()` replies on the held connection) is the existing request/response-with-hold pattern, built for D-40. (4) A provider-approval box already exists: `ProviderUserRequest` (id, kind, summary, failure, isAnswerable) published via `SessionEventHub.Change.userRequests`, reset on runStarted/runEnded, drawn by `RequestList` in DetailView (Approve/Deny, `returnApproves:false` over a live terminal so Return stays with the CLI), answered through `CatalogModel.answerRequest` to `intents.answer`. Today only the Codex path fills it (SessionRuntime+Codex.publishRequests); Claude's Needs approval is a state with no card, banner text "Claude is waiting for your approval." with click-to-jump only (ApprovalNotifier, UserNotificationService: no actions), and the subagent panel says "answer it in the session's terminal" (SubagentApprovalNotice). (5) Answered-in-terminal is already detectable without polling: ClaudeRegistryReader watches the registry file (status idle/busy/waiting) and ClaudeHookStateTracker returns from Needs approval on the next registry sample.

DESIGN (lightest). (a) Wire: add a `decide` mode to loom-hook, selected by the payload's hook_event_name == PermissionRequest (no new argument needed; the existing entry stays one entry, its `timeout` raised from 1 to about 125 s). The helper first sends the normal state envelope on the hook socket exactly as today (so status/identity ordering is unchanged), then opens a framed request on the control socket (length-prefixed or newline frame, NOT half-close, so EOF means the helper died) carrying token, session id, run id, the payload (tool_name, tool_input, permission_suggestions, agent_id, cwd) capped at 64 KiB, and waits. Every failure path (no socket, refused, token rejected, cap exceeded, timeout, Loom quit, unknown reply) exits 0 with empty stdout = CLI prompt untouched (fail open; never exit 2 and never allow by default). A reply `allow` prints `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PermissionRequest","decision":{"behavior":"allow"}}}` with no updatedInput and no updatedPermissions; `deny` prints behavior deny with message "Denied from Loom" and interrupt false; `pass` prints nothing. (b) Loom side: a `ClaudeApprovalCoordinator` actor beside OpenSessionCoordinator: authorize (live run, launch card == LOOM_SESSION_ID, as OpenSessionCoordinator does), assign a Loom request id per connection (PermissionRequest has no tool_use_id, so never hash input), keep an in-memory per-session queue (cap about 8; overflow answered `pass` at once), publish `.userRequests` with a richer summary (tool, full command or file path plus old/new text). Tool names AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode are answered `pass` immediately (an allow without answers would break them; they belong to separate ideas). A DispatchSourceRead on each held connection reports helper death. (c) Cancel/hand-back triggers, all event-driven: registry sample waiting->busy/idle, Stop, SessionEnd, StopFailure, runEnded/runDetached (leader exit is already tracked by ProcessSupervisor), Loom quit (reply `unavailable`), and one one-shot Task.sleep soft-wait (about 120 s, below the 600 s default) that exists only while a request is pending and hands back with a visible `handed back to the terminal` state. Timeouts hand back, never decide. (d) Surfaces all resolve the same (session id, request id, kind): RequestList box (extend `answerRequest` to route Claude vs Codex); ApprovalNotifier posts one banner per request (identifier = request id) with a UNNotificationCategory of Allow and Deny actions (no `.foreground`, no Always, no Bypass), the delegate calls the model with the ids; MenuBarController rows get an Allow/Deny submenu (the NSMenu is rebuilt on open, so it never shows stale rows). A stale or unknown id is discarded and logged once (LoomLog ClaudeHooks category), never applied to the head of a queue. (e) Verified outcome has two honest stages: `sent to the CLI` (helper reports it wrote the decision and exited) and `continued` (registry busy or a later hook event); if the second does not arrive the card says so rather than claiming success. (f) Smart hold policy chosen after the spike: if the dialog is NOT gated by the hook, always hold; if it is gated, hold only when the user is not looking at that session's live terminal (app inactive or another session selected) and release on focus, because a gated dialog would otherwise be delayed by the hold. (g) Safety: the preview is bounded plain text and never silently truncated; if the command or diff exceeds the cap, Allow is disabled (Deny and Open session remain). Hook allow cannot override deny rules and updatedInput is not used, so Loom cannot widen what the CLI would allow. Per-session scope also means subagent requests (agent_id present) become answerable from the same card, which today is impossible without leaving the transcript panel. (h) Skip in v1: Carbon hotkey, Enter/Esc beyond the focused box (keep `returnApproves:false` over a live terminal), the Codex per-turn approvals counter, Always-allow (later: only the CLI-suggested session-scoped entry), AskUserQuestion and plan cards. Tests: reuse loom-fake-provider/loom-test-child to emit PermissionRequest and hold; contract tests from payloads captured from a live CLI; coordinator tests for stale id, cancel races, overflow, quit.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Detail pane: above the live terminal (same slot as RequestList), a callout card "Bash wants to run" with the full command in a monospaced selectable block (or Edit as old/new lines), a source line (session, subagent name if any), and Deny / Allow buttons (neither is the Return default over a terminal). A "+2 more" line when several are queued. After a decision the card turns into a one-line status: "Sent, waiting for Claude to continue", then disappears on continue; or "Handed back to the terminal" when the soft-wait expired or the terminal answered first. Sidebar card keeps the existing Needs approval pill; its second line can show the tool name (shares work with the card-line idea). Notification banner: title = session, body = tool plus first line of the command, buttons Allow and Deny (visible on hover or expansion; with Alerts style always visible). Menu bar menu: a Needs you row with approval gets a submenu Allow / Deny / Show Session. No popover, no notch overlay, no always-on window; nothing is drawn when hidden.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass. Event-driven only (socket reads, registry vnode samples that already exist, kernel-tracked leader exit, one one-shot sleep per pending request); no polling, no new visible window, no animation; one helper process per pending request, and Loom already spawns one per PermissionRequest today, now held longer; held sockets cost a file descriptor, not a thread (hard cap 32 in flight, per-session cap about 8). Risk: CodeIsland still idles at about 5.3% CPU, but that is its notch overlay, which this design does not have. Predictability: risk until the spike, because raising the hook timeout from 1 s to about 125 s changes worst-case behaviour if the CLI gates its dialog on hooks; the spike and the smart-hold policy bound it. Accurate status: pass if two-stage outcome is kept (`sent` versus `continued`), cards removed on registry/Stop/SessionEnd/run end, `handed back` shown rather than silent loss, and stale ids discarded and logged; the failure to avoid is the CodeIsland 308 bug (answering the head of the queue) and reporting Allowed because a button was pressed. Fluency: pass, one fewer window switch per approval; Allow stays disabled on a truncated preview, a small intentional friction. Modularity: pass; one coordinator plus one protocol file, reuse of ProviderUserRequest/RequestList/answerRequest, no TerminalSurface or renderer change. CLI-update resilience: acceptable but is the biggest ongoing cost; PermissionRequest decision control is documented (hooks reference, v2.1.300 checked), `--settings` is already used and drift-checked, but the interactive ordering semantics are not documented, so ship a captured-payload contract test, a drift journal entry if the helper sees an unexpected payload shape, and fail open on anything unknown. Never pin. Ownership: pass, per-session scope, no global settings.json writes (counter-example: Vibe Island hook self-healing, #245), fully owned by the run scope; Quit answers every waiting helper and drops requests (memory only, like open requests). feasibility.loom_design:
## What Loom has today (observed in code)
- The PermissionRequest hook is registered per session in `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings` (Sources/LoomCore/ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:~185-200) as the same `bounded` fire-and-forget helper as the other events: `{type: command, command: helperPath, args: [], timeout: 1}`. The comment there says "helpers return no provider decision" and "No per-tool hooks: each hook spawns a helper".
- `loom-hook` (Sources/loom-hook/main.swift) sends one envelope over `ClaudeHookClient.send` and exits. `ClaudeHookServer` (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeHook.swift) is one-way: 1 s receive deadline, no reply, serial queue. `ClaudeHookEvent.init(payload:)` reads PermissionRequest only as `.permissionRequest(toolName:)`; `tool_input` and `permission_suggestions` are never parsed or kept (the full payload, up to 1 MiB, is in `ClaudeHookEnvelope.payload` in memory).
- The tracker turns PermissionRequest into `.waitingForApproval` (`ClaudeHookStateTracker.receive`, ClaudeHook.swift:~733/762) and then lets the registry's "idle/busy" samples move it on (`receiveRegistry`, ~l.590-620). Interrupting or denying in the terminal fires no Stop and no PermissionDenied (plans/experiments/cp5-claude-native-denial-research.json), so the registry sample is the only "card is stale" signal.
- A request/response channel already exists: `OpenSessionControlServer` (Sources/LoomCore/OpenSessionProtocol.swift) on `c-<8>.sock`, same token, holds a connection open per request (max 32 in flight, `Task.detached` so no thread is blocked while waiting), answered later by `OpenSessionCoordinator` (actor, in-memory entries, `updates()` AsyncStream, replyDelay 85 s, Quit answers everyone `unavailable`). `SessionRuntime+OpenRequests.swift` is the UI-facing approve/deny API and `OpenRequestBox` (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/OpenRequestViews.swift) is a ready template: bounded preview, "Show full message" scroll, no default action so Return stays with the terminal, `fadesIn()` opacity only.
- There is NO Claude-side approval box with content today. `RequestList` (DetailView.swift:443) renders `SessionViewState.userRequests`, which only the frozen Codex path fills. For Claude the user sees "Needs approval", a fixed banner "Claude is waiting for your approval." (`ApprovalNotificationPlanner.body`) and `SubagentApprovalNotice` ("answer it in the session's terminal"). So the brief's "approval box" for Claude does not exist yet.
- No Markdown renderer in the repo; `SubagentTranscriptView` is explicitly plain text.

## Proposed split (three separable stages, each shippable alone)

### Stage 0: content line from the payload already received (S, no new hook, no blocking)
- Extend `ClaudeHookEvent` (LoomCore) with a bounded `ToolPreview` parsed only for `.permissionRequest` and only fields it needs: tool name, Bash `command`+`description`, Edit/MultiEdit `file_path` and old/new strings, Write `file_path`+size+head, MCP `mcp_server`+top-level arg keys. Cap each string at parse time (for example 8 KiB, with "N more bytes"), so the 1 MiB payload never travels further.
- Keep it OUT of `SessionViewState` (that struct is diffed per frame in the sidebar hot path; see CatalogHotPathTests/SidebarRenderTests). Publish it on a separate small stream like `openRequestUpdates()`: a `PendingInteraction` store in the adapter keyed by session, set by the PermissionRequest event and cleared when the tracker leaves `.waitingForApproval` (registry sample, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, run end). Event-driven, no timers.
- Consumers: (1) `ApprovalNotificationPlanner.body` gets a second line "Bash: git push --force origin main" (setting-gated because banners show on a locked screen), (2) menu bar row subtitle (MenuBarRowText), (3) a content line/box in the detail pane. For a selected live terminal the box adds little (the CLI dialog shows the same and a better diff), so keep it one or two lines there; the real gain is triage across sessions you are not looking at, and the subagent panel and ended-screen views where the terminal is not showing.
- Edit preview is old_string/new_string only (fragment diff, no true line numbers). Lazy file read for line numbers is a later, optional step (bounded read, only when the box is visible).

### Stage 1: decision channel for AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode only (M)
- Do NOT start with Bash/Edit allow/deny. Answering a question is not a permission decision, so Loom duplicates no policy (the Happy drift lesson) and never sits in front of the CLI's own permission logic. Allow/Deny for ordinary tools can reuse the same channel later (PermissionRequest allow/deny; "always allow" only with `destination: session`, never echoing a `localSettings` suggestion) but is a separate decision.
- New blocking hook entry per session in `claudeSettings`, scoped by matcher so it spawns only for the rare tools: either `PermissionRequest` with `matcher: "AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode"` or `PreToolUse` with the same matcher (the spike picks; see experiments). Command: the same `loom-hook` with a new first argument (for example `decide`), timeout about 600 s. Needs a branch in `LoomHook.main` before the `OpenSessionCommand` dispatch, which today treats any argument as the open command.
- The helper sends one request (token, session id, run id, stdin payload) to the existing control socket and waits. Generalise `OpenSessionControlServer`'s wire request with a `kind` field (or add a sibling server on the same socket directory with the same `LocalSocket` rules) rather than a third IPC mechanism. A new actor `HookDecisionCoordinator` (LoomCore, sibling of `OpenSessionCoordinator`) keeps pending decisions in memory keyed by (sessionID, runID, tool_use_id or invocation id), exposes `updates()`, and offers `answer(id, ...)`, `handBack(id)`. Reply shapes: hand back = exit 0 with empty stdout (the CLI then shows its own dialog); answer = the documented JSON on stdout.
- AskUserQuestion answer: echo the ORIGINAL `questions` value verbatim from the payload (keep it as the parsed JSON object, never re-encode through a typed model) and add only `answers` keyed by the exact question text (multi-select labels joined with commas). Loom reads just `question`, `options[].label/description`, `multiSelect`; every other field passes through untouched, so new CLI fields cannot cause a schema slip. Hand back instead of rendering when: questions is not 1-4 dictionaries, a question text repeats, the payload has an `agent_id` (subagent), or parsing fails (journal a `cli_compat_warning`).
- ExitPlanMode: render `tool_input.plan` (injected, documented), show `planFilePath`; Approve = allow (+ `updatedInput` echo); Revise = deny with the user's feedback as `message`; "Use terminal" = hand back. If the PermissionRequest form is chosen, Approve can carry `updatedPermissions: [{type: setMode, mode, destination: "session"}]` to mirror the CLI's "approve and auto-accept edits" choice (documented), which the PreToolUse form cannot do.
- Hold rule, no polling: the helper and socket stay open while the card is pending. Loom hands back at its own deadline (stay under the helper's 600 s timeout; a timed-out hook does not block per docs, so the CLI falls back to its dialog either way), on Quit, on run end, when the tracker leaves the waiting state, and when the user clicks "Use terminal". A visible "Handed back to the terminal" state replaces silent loss. Timeouts hand back, never decide.
- State accuracy: while a decision is pending the tracker must keep the card in Needs approval / Waiting for you. Risk: a blocking hook may make the registry report "busy", and `receiveRegistry` would then flip the card to Working under the pending card. Add a tracker input "interaction pending" that the registry samples cannot override until the coordinator resolves it. This is the most invasive code change in the idea (ClaudeHook.swift, ~900 lines of watermark logic).
- Verified outcome: register `PostToolUse` with the same matcher (rare tools, so near-zero spawn cost) and show "Answered" only when it arrives for that tool_use_id; a write to a dead helper, or no PostToolUse and a state change, shows "Claude moved on; answer was not used". The 2.1.300 behaviour (invalid `updatedInput` denies the call) makes this check necessary, not decorative.
- Authority: every action is an explicit click bound to the card's request id, no default/Return action (same rule as `OpenRequestBox`); stale card actions are discarded and logged (CodeIsland #308 lesson). Never log question or plan text (LoomLog is content-free); evidence export honours `redactsContent`.

### Stage 2: plan panel and question card UI
- Panels replace the terminal view while pending, like the subagent panel (`DetailContent`, DetailView.swift:~236-247: terminal keeps running at the same size, only not shown; a card above the terminal would resize the PTY, which DESIGN.md forbids except opacity-only fades). Always a visible "Use terminal" button and Esc returns to the terminal.
- Plan rendering needs a small bounded Markdown renderer (headings, lists, fenced code, inline emphasis through `AttributedString(markdown:)`, lazy blocks), cached by request id, drawn only while visible, cap about 256 KiB with "Show more". This is new code (no renderer exists) and the main reason the cost is above M for plans.
- Cmd+J (next session that needs you) lands on the panel; the notification action can open it. Notification buttons that answer are a later add-on.

## Triggers and bounds (summary)
Triggers: hook events, the coordinator's AsyncStream, user clicks, registry change notifications. Nothing polls. Bounds: payload 1 MiB (existing), preview strings 8 KiB at parse, plan 256 KiB, at most 32 held connections (existing `maximumInFlight`) and a small per-session pending queue (parallel tool calls, subagents), everything in memory only and dropped at Quit.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
- Stage 0: a one- or two-line tool summary on the orange "Needs approval" surface: notification body "Project · Bash: git push --force origin main", menu bar row subtitle, and a slim tinted box above the terminal (opacity fade, bounded, "Show full command" scroll like `OpenRequestBox`). Edit shows "src/Foo.swift  -3 +5" with a small red/green fragment; Write shows path, size, first lines; MCP shows server plus argument keys.
- Question card (Stage 2): replaces the terminal in the detail pane while pending. One block per question (1-4): header chip, question text, option rows with label+description, radio for single-select, checkboxes for multi-select, a free-text "Other" field; a Send button enabled when every question has an answer; "Use terminal" secondary button; no default action. After sending: "Answered" appears only after the PostToolUse confirmation, otherwise "Claude moved on".
- Plan panel: header "Plan ready for review" with the plan file path (Reveal / Copy path), the rendered Markdown in a scroll area, footer with Approve (and a mode menu if the PermissionRequest form works), "Revise..." opening a feedback text field that sends deny + message, and "Use terminal".
- Sidebar and menu bar need no new shapes: the existing orange Needs approval / Waiting for you dot and Cmd+J keep working; the card subtitle can show "Question" or "Plan" instead of a generic state when the interaction is known.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: PASS if scoped. Stage 0 adds one bounded parse per PermissionRequest and no new process. Stage 1 spawns a helper only for the matcher-scoped rare tools (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode), holds a socket and a suspended Task while pending (no thread, no timer), renders only when visible, and keeps nothing for idle sessions. RISK if someone registers a blocking hook on every PreToolUse or every PermissionRequest (a spawn per tool call, which the existing comment in ProviderLaunchProfile.swift rules out) or puts the preview strings into the per-frame `SessionViewState`.
Predictability: RISK, the main one. A blocking hook means the CLI's own dialog is not on screen until the hook returns, so a user who types into the terminal while Loom holds the request sees only a spinner. Mitigations: a visible card/panel with "Use terminal", a hand-back deadline, a Settings choice (answer in Loom / in the terminal; read per request, default is the user's call), and consistent behaviour (always hold for these two tools when the setting says Loom).
Accurate status: RISK, manageable. A held hook may make the registry say busy and flip the card to Working; needs the tracker "interaction pending" input. Delivered/answered must be verified (PostToolUse for the same tool_use_id), never inferred from the write; hand-back, timeout and stale card are shown states. The interrupted-in-terminal case sends no Stop, so cancellation relies on the registry sample and the helper-connection failure.
Fluency: PASS, one click or a few keystrokes from the card or Cmd+J instead of find-pane, scroll, press 1/2; no new confirmation steps. Return is deliberately not a default action.
Modularity: PASS. New `ToolPreview` parse in LoomCore, a `HookDecisionCoordinator` beside `OpenSessionCoordinator`, one `loom-hook decide` subcommand, one detail-pane view and a Markdown renderer; hot paths (sidebar frames, tracker watermarks) are touched only by the one tracker input.
CLI-update resilience: PASS with discipline. Uses documented hook fields (tool_input, plan, planFilePath, decision JSON, matcher); echoes the original `questions` verbatim; any shape mismatch hands back to the terminal and journals `cli_compat_warning`; no pinned versions; pin the chosen hook form with a payload captured from a live session (not hand-written) and keep it as a contract test fixture. Not documented for the interactive case: AskUserQuestion answering via hook is documented and framed for `-p`/permission hosts (the permissions page does document that an ExitPlanMode `allow`+`updatedInput` runs without a prompt in plan mode), so treat the interactive AskUserQuestion path as inferred until the spike confirms it. `defer` is -p only and ignored in interactive sessions, so it is not an option for a PTY host.
Process ownership: PASS. The helper is a child of the CLI inside the run scope; Stop/Quit tear everything down; Quit answers waiting clients and drops the in-memory requests.
User authority: PASS only if every decision is an explicit click bound to the request id, nothing answers on timeout, nothing is stored, and the user can switch the feature off. Contract section 9 says provider permission checks must not be bypassed and "multiple approvals not explained to the user" are unacceptable: answering a question or plan on the user's click is not a bypass, but the first time Loom answers on the CLI's behalf deserves its own DECISIONS entry. Stage 1 also changes the invariant "helpers return no provider decision" (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift comment), which must be updated in the docs.
Contract/decisions: the contract keeps the terminal as the real CLI; panels that replace the terminal temporarily (subagent panel precedent, D-54) with an always-visible way back stay inside it, and the user has said they are open to a chat-centred direction. D-34 (no right sidebar) is not touched because the panel lives in the detail pane. D-43/D-46 (cross-session channel) is untouched: this is intra-session.
feasibility.value_reason: For this user (several sessions, spec/interview loops with ticket keys, plan-first habits) AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode are where unattended sessions stall and where a human decision matters most, and answering from a rendered card is a real fluency win plus the first reusable piece of a chat-centred UI. Discounts: auto mode is now the default starting mode (v2.1.283+, per the power-user fact-check), so ordinary Bash/Edit approvals are rarer and the plain diff preview is the weakest part (the CLI dialog already shows a better diff for the selected session); only one closed product ships plan review, so reception is unproven; and the hook-held dialog trade-off needs the user's buy-in.

feasibility.one_line: Most of I-17 already ships (severity Cmd+J, Dock badge, menu-bar Needs-you list, quit question, project roll-up dot, viewed-only-when-key); adopt only the real gaps (away-aware viewed and banners, opt-in finish/failure banner, quit sheet naming sessions, Dock menu, Mark Unread), and skip severity re-sorting of Active, quiet hours, per-turn lists and a mailbox.
feasibility.loom_design:
CHECKED FIRST - what Loom already has (so the idea is mostly a delta):
- One derivation already feeds the Dock badge, the menu-bar badge/summary and Cmd+J: CatalogModel.updateAttentionCount() (CatalogModel+Navigation.swift) builds attentionCandidates() from liveStates and calls AttentionOrder.count (Dock, via onAttentionCountChange) and MenuBarSummary.derive (menu bar + approval notifier, via onMenuBarChange). Fires on change only, no timer. The set is SessionIndicator.needsAttention for all three, so counts cannot disagree today. Dock count (all needing you) equals menu list (5 rows + 'and N more...').
- Severity order exists for navigation: AttentionOrder.rank = failure class(0) > needs approval(1) > waiting for you(2) > finished unviewed(3), then newest activity, then id (SessionNavigation.swift). Cmd+J / Shift+Cmd+J walk it; Finished-unviewed is already included.
- Menu bar menu already exceeds Cursor: 'Needs you' section (failure > attention > unviewed, newest first) and 'Working' section, 5 rows each + 'and N more...' (MenuBarState.derive, D-49/D-52).
- Quit question exists (D-45, QuitConfirmation.prompt/busyCount, AppDelegate.askBeforeQuitting): 'Quit Loom and stop N working sessions?', Cancel default, never for system-initiated quit, no question when nothing is busy. It does not name the sessions.
- Collapsed-project roll-up dot exists (CatalogModel.attention(forProject:), ProjectHeader: failure > attention > unviewed, 7 pt, visible when collapsed). It has no 'working' state and no count (DESIGN: 'Project rows show no session count').
- 'Viewed' is already strict: CatalogModel.updateViewing -> hub.setViewed only when windowIsActive (visible AND not occluded AND key AND NSApp.isActive, AppDelegate.updateWindowActivity) and not the dev terminal, and the selected session; list refreshes/frames never count. Mark as Read exists (card menu, waitingAcknowledged in SessionEventHub). Active section order is deliberately 'list activity order; a state change alone moves nothing; selected row held' (FB4-2, heldActiveID).
- Approval banner exists (ApprovalNotificationPlanner/ApprovalNotifier): only the transition into Needs approval, only while !NSApp.isActive, no sound, removed when answered/quit/launch, no timers. Single window, single process, in-memory read state.

REAL GAPS, in value order, each event-driven and bounded:
A. Away-aware 'viewed' and banners (spike first). Hole: Loom frontmost + selected session + user away (screen locked / screensaver / display asleep) means a finish is born 'viewed' (SessionEventHub.publish checks viewedSessionID) and the approval banner is suppressed (isAppActive = NSApp.isActive). Design: a tiny `PresenceState` in loom-app that flips on documented NSWorkspace.screensDidSleep/Wake and sessionDidResign/BecomeActive plus the (undocumented but long-stable) distributed notifications com.apple.screenIsLocked/Unlocked and com.apple.screensaver.didstart/didstop; while 'away' it feeds updateWindowActivity() as an extra false term (so setViewed(nil)), and ApprovalNotifier.isAppActive becomes 'model.windowIsActive' instead of NSApp.isActive. On return the existing edge re-asserts setViewed(selected). No polling, no idle-time query. If the spike shows occlusionState already flips on lock/screensaver, A shrinks to the one-line notifier change.
B. Opt-in 'Notify when a session finishes or fails' (default off, Settings -> General next to the approval switch). Generalise ApprovalNotificationPlanner into an AttentionNotificationPlanner over (previous, current) sets per class; post only on transition into Finished-unviewed/Failed, only when away or Loom not active, only for turns longer than a threshold (e.g. 60 s; hub knows working to turnComplete edge), identifier = session id so approval/finish replace each other, removed when viewed or marked read. Title = session title, body = 'project - Finished' (no assistant text on the lock screen). Fits the Hashimoto/Cherny split as a setting.
C. Quit sheet names what will stop: informativeText lists up to 5 titles (project - title) of Working/Needs-approval sessions; QuitConfirmation.prompt takes [MenuBarEntry]-like titles. Optional third button 'Show' selects the first and cancels the quit. Zero cost when nothing runs (prompt stays nil).
D. Dock menu: implement applicationDockMenu(_:) returning a menu built on demand from the same pure MenuBarMenu.items(for: model.menuBarState()) the status item uses (extract MenuBarController's menu building into a shared builder). Built only when the Dock menu opens.
E. Mark Unread (card menu + Window menu, Cmd+Shift+U) = hub change .unviewedCompletion(true) on a session at prompt; 'Mark All as Read' menu item (no Shift+Esc: Esc/Shift+Esc must reach the PTY, Claude uses Esc to interrupt). Hub already has both mutation paths.
F. Reminder ladder: later. If wanted, one Task.sleep per pending approval armed by the transition into Needs approval and cancelled on leaving it, nudges at ~5 and ~15 min only while Loom is not active/away; approvals never throttled. No timers exist otherwise.
G. Tidy: make AttentionOrder.rank and ProjectAttention one class enum (today the menu bar lumps approval and waiting-for-you as 'attention' and identityUnclear differs in rank), so order, dot and menu cannot drift (the Cursor 3.22/3.23 badge-bug lesson). XS.
H. Optional roll-up refinement: show the working chase/dot on a collapsed project when nothing needs you (Paseo rule). attention(forProject:) re-runs per ProjectHeader on every liveRevision change (O(live states) each) so implement as a cached per-project summary updated in updateAttentionCount. A '+2 need you' text line contradicts DESIGN 'no session count' and needs the user.

SKIP: severity re-sort of the Active section (contradicts the explicit 'a state change alone moves nothing' decision, creates the rows-jump-under-cursor/shortcut-target complaint Codex #36300 and cmux users report; with 2-6 rows the dots plus Cmd+J already triage); quiet hours/focus mode/mute-on-lock for sound (Loom posts no sound and macOS Focus already filters UNUserNotification banners); per-turn unviewed list (needs turn-boundary tracking, thin value at <=5 sessions); compare-before-write read marks (one window, in-memory state, Quit stops all runs); a separate mailbox (duplicates Active and the menu).

(B) one more switch in Settings -> General: 'Notify when a session finishes or fails' (off by default), banner 'Alpha - EDDP-123 fix' / 'alpha - Finished'. (C) the existing quit sheet gains a short list under the title: 'EDDP-1 auth fix (api) / spec review (docs) / +2 more'. (D) right-clicking the Dock icon shows the same Needs you / Working rows as the status item above the system items. (E) card context menu and Window menu: 'Mark as Unread' next to 'Mark as Read', plus 'Mark All as Read'. feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass - everything is derived from existing hub frames; presence uses a handful of OS notifications (no polling); reminder timers (F) exist only while an approval is pending; Dock menu and quit list are built on demand. Predictability: pass if the rules are written in UI-MAP (viewed = visible+key+unlocked+selected; banners = transition + away/inactive); risk: every suppression rule can hide a real alert, so keep approvals unthrottled, always visible in sidebar/Dock/menu bar, and make B opt-in. Accurate status: pass and improves it (A removes false 'viewed'); risk: the undocumented com.apple.screenIsLocked names could change with macOS, so degrade to today's behaviour and keep the documented NSWorkspace sleep/session signals as the base. Fluency: pass (no new confirmations; quit sheet only gets more informative). Modularity: pass - pure planner/state types in LoomCatalogUI with tests, system hooks only in loom-app (SystemServices pattern); hub gets at most one injected change. CLI-update resilience: pass - nothing new depends on Claude; B uses the existing Stop-derived turnComplete; do not read new hook payload fields for banner text. Ownership: n/a (no process work). User authority: pass - banners only inform; no cross-session action. Principle violations to avoid: a repeating timer or idle-time poll for 'user present' (use events only), a global-settings or hook change, putting assistant text in lock-screen banners, auto-clearing 'Waiting for you' without the user's say (see decisions).
feasibility.value_reason: The original S/high-value framing overstates it for Loom because the Dock badge, menu-bar Needs-you list, severity Cmd+J, quit question, project roll-up dot and strict viewed rule already exist; the remaining pieces are polish. For a multi-session, long-run user the genuinely useful parts are away-aware viewed/banners and an opt-in finish/failure banner (the 'slow part was me noticing which one stopped' problem); the Dock menu, quit list and Mark Unread are small conveniences. Cost: each piece is S, but with pure-type tests, evidence and UI-MAP/DECISIONS updates the useful set is about M.
