feasibility.one_line: Adopt only the "In work" half (one persisted per-session flag, opened by the user's own prompt, closed only by one-key Done, 15-day stale falloff, no model call), and drop the Park shelf, timed snooze and auto-settle timers, because Loom's Active section is live-only and forgets everything at Quit, while Mark as Read and the stale lifecycle already cover most of what Park would do.
feasibility.loom_design:
Finding that changes the idea: Loom's Active section is live-only. `CatalogModel+Active.updateActive` admits a session only when `live?.runID != nil` and `SessionViewState.activePhase != .inactive`, and that state is in-memory hub state (`SessionEventHub.publish`: cleared on runEnded/runDetached). Quit stops everything (contract), so after every restart Active is empty and the user falls back to day headings. A persisted In-work list therefore fills a real gap. Park fills a smaller one: viewing a session already ends "Finished unviewed" and `markRead` acknowledges "Waiting for you" (SessionEventHub.markRead), so Park only adds suppression for sessions that are still working or waiting on approval, and those should not be hidden anyway (accurate status).

Design (light):
1. State = ONE nullable column, not several flags. `sessions.work_state TEXT` (NULL | 'work'), plus `work_state_at REAL` if a "since" is wanted. Add it on open with the existing no-version-bump pattern (`CatalogDatabase.ensureOriginColumns` / `ensureProjectColors`: nullable ALTER under the write lock, older builds still open the file). One column means a session cannot be in two lists by construction, which removes the OpenChamber v2.4.0 "listed twice" bug class. Extend `SessionCatalog.sessionColumns` (SessionCatalog.swift ~L195), the row decoder (~L345) and `CatalogSession` (init has defaults, so call sites survive).
2. Triggers (all existing events, no new timer):
 - Open: the user's own prompt. `ProcessSupervisor.markProviderUsed` -> `SessionCatalog.markUsed(reactivate: true)` is already called on `UserPromptSubmit` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~L268). Set `work_state='work'` inside that same UPDATE (one SQL statement, no extra write) only when `movesActivity` is true, so a resume (`SessionLifecycleController.reactivate`, movesActivity false) does not open it. The sent-message-opens, only-user-closes invariant is thereby a SQL rule. A new session's first prompt opens it too.
 - Close: user command only, `SessionCatalog.setWorkState(nil, for:)` modelled on `setPinned` (SessionCatalog+Sessions.swift L242) and `CatalogModel.setPinned` (CatalogModel+Cleanup.swift L10: write, then `refreshRow`; a failed write reports an error, never a false success). Done on a live session also calls `markRead` (display-only acknowledgement), and never stops anything (Stop stays a separate verified action).
 - Reopen: the next prompt (same rule as Open). No `doneAt` comparison needed.
 - Falloff (auto-settle by age, for free): the shelf excludes `lifecycle = 'stale'`. Stale is already classified by `SessionLifecycleController.classifyStale` on its existing one-shot timer chain (15 days unused, contract section 5), which publishes `.catalogLifecycle`. No new timer or scheduler. A stale row keeps its flag; a new prompt reactivates it.
3. Sidebar: add `CatalogScope.inWork` (one more `conditions(for:)` branch in SessionCatalog+Paging.swift: `s.work_state = 'work' AND s.lifecycle != 'stale'`) and `CatalogListKey.inWork` (CatalogModel.swift L7), loaded with the first page, capped at one page (100, `CatalogQuery.maxPageSize`) so it is bounded. A dedicated query is needed because the activity list is keyset-paged: deriving the shelf from loaded rows (as `activeRows` does) would miss In-work sessions older than the loaded range. `ActivityLayout` gains `inWork`; `daySections`/`activeRows` already take an exclusion set keyed by `activeRevision`, so the same mechanism excludes In-work IDs (single partition function = single place that decides precedence).
4. Precedence (listed once): Active (live, needs or is doing work) > In work > day sections. An In-work session that is live and under way shows in Active only, with the In-work glyph on its card; when it is read it drops into In work, not into the day list. While searching, no sections (existing rule). Project view is untouched (creation order never moves, D-39); there In work is only a card glyph.
5. Row patching: the new list joins `CatalogModel+Patching` (which already decides per list whether a patched record belongs) so a flag flip is one row read, not a full refresh.
6. Keyboard/Undo: File or Window menu command "Mark Done" / "Put Back in Work" (toggle, one chord; pick a free one, none of Cmd+J, Cmd+1/2, Cmd+Delete, Cmd+. is used by it) next to the Cmd+J items in `AppDelegate.installMenus`; context-menu item beside Pin/Mark as Read (SidebarView.swift ~L506). Reversible by the same toggle; plus an "Undo Mark Done" menu title valid until the next flag action, which costs no timer and no surface. "Done and go to the next session that needs me" = `markDone` then `jumpToAttention(.next)`; since the current session leaves the set or never was in it, `AttentionOrder.neighbor` already starts the walk at the first entry.
7. Retention: In-work sessions should be exempt from cleanup like pinned ones (`CleanupPlanner.classify`, `CleanupCandidate.pinned` / `taskLink`): a one-line exclusion reason. Cleanup review is dev-only and automatic deletion is off, so this is low risk; it needs a DECISIONS entry because contract section 5 lists the exceptions.
8. Left out on purpose: Parked shelf, snooze-until-time, snooze-until-plan-reset, T3 PR-merge settle, pending-approval/subagent auto-settle checklist (not needed: nothing auto-settles except the existing stale rule, which already skips running sessions via `oldestStaleCandidate(excluding: running)`), the "looks done" classifier, agents setting the flag over the control socket (user authority). Snooze-until-limit-reset belongs with the separate usage-limit idea: `ClaudePlanLimits.PlanLimitWindow.resetsAt` exists, but Loom only knows a reset when the CLI answered `get_usage`, and `UsageModel` asks only on events (afterShown 300 s, afterTurn 120 s), and nothing today links a session stopping on `StopFailure` to a limit.

Check before building: `markProviderUsed` runs for every `UserPromptSubmit`, including synthetic ones (`promptIsSynthetic`, ClaudeHook.swift L395: subagent hand-backs and task notifications), because the adapter at ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~L268 does not test it. Opening In work from there would reopen a Done session when a background subagent reports back. Gate the open on `!promptIsSynthetic` (pass a flag into `markProviderUsed`), with a test.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Activity view, top to bottom: Active (n) as today, then a new heading "In work  n" in the day-heading style (`ActivityHeading`, 11 pt semibold secondary, same paddings; not drawn when empty or while searching), then the day sections without those rows. Cards in In work are the normal two-row cards; a small "work" glyph (same slot and size as the pin glyph, theme tokens only) marks In-work membership on cards that appear in Active or in the project view. Context menu: "Mark Done" (In-work card) / "Put in Work" (any other), next to Pin and Mark as Read. One menu command with a chord does the same for the selected row. Feedback for Done: the card simply leaves the section; an "Undo Mark Done" Edit-menu title carries the 5-second-Undo promise without a toast. If a toast is wanted later, draw it as an overlay: the existing `Banners` stack in DetailView changes layout and would resize the terminal (PTY resize), which its own comment forbids. No Parked shelf and no snooze picker in v1.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: pass. One nullable column; one bounded query (cap 100) at list load; no timer, no polling, no watcher; the falloff reuses the stale classifier's existing one-shot chain; nothing drawn when the section is empty. Risk if built the heavy way: a lazy-evaluated or timer-driven snooze/auto-settle scheduler, or a classifier per turn.
Predictability: pass if precedence is one partition function and the state is one column (a session is in exactly one of Active / In work / day). Risk: auto-open on every prompt makes the list long and the user must learn Done; the rule stays simple (prompt opens, user closes, 15 days unused falls off) but must be shown in a tooltip.
Accurate status: pass with care. In work is user intent, not a verified provider outcome, so it must not share the status indicator (contract section 4: agent states are a separate field from active/idle/stale; keep this a third, orthogonal field). Done must never read as stopped or deleted; no suppression of Needs approval, Failed or Cmd+J/Dock badge in v1 (that is why Park is dropped: hiding a working or approval-blocked session would make the badge lie).
Fluency: pass: one key, no confirmation, same toggle undoes it. No wait added.
Modularity: pass: column in LoomCore catalog, scope/query in the paging file, list/partition in CatalogModel+Active-style extension, view in SidebarView; LoomCore stays UI-free.
CLI-update resilience: pass: uses only the UserPromptSubmit event Loom already consumes; no new hook, flag or CLI parse.
Ownership: pass: no process is started, stopped or touched; Done does not stop a run.
User authority: pass: only the user closes; no agent, hook or socket path can set the flag (explicitly not added to the open-session control socket).
Older builds: pass: nullable column added on open without a version bump (three precedents), older builds ignore it.
feasibility.value_reason: For someone running several sessions over two work projects with ticket keys, a persisted "what am I in the middle of" list directly fixes the empty-Active-after-restart gap, and it costs no resources. The full Park/snooze half scores about 2: Mark as Read and viewing already clear the noisy states, and hiding approval or working sessions conflicts with accurate attention counts.

usage-limit actions idea (Continue/Snooze at reset) for snooze-until-limit, kept separate
experiments: No spike needed for feasibility. One cheap code check decides a detail: confirm in a fixture test that a synthetic UserPromptSubmit (subagent hand-back) reaches markProviderUsed today, then gate the open on !promptIsSynthetic; the test must fail without the gate.

Optional decision aid before building (one week, no code): the user lists by hand how many sessions they prompt in a typical week that they would want in an In-work list; if auto-open would put more than about 15 items there, switch to manual 'Put in Work' plus auto-open only for sessions with a ticket key or project.

feasibility.title: Park / snooze / In-work: user-owned lifecycle flags for sessions

feasibility.one_line: Most of the machinery already exists in Loom (SessionLifecycleController idle path, verified stopForIdle, ended screen, --resume), but the user switched exactly this off in D-38, so a half-day spike on resume fidelity and on whether the hook signals are trustworthy must precede a strictly opt-in, visible re-enable.
feasibility.loom_design:
KEY FINDING: this is not a new subsystem. Loom already has an idle auto-stop, switched off by D-38 (8 Oct 2026; FEEDBACK-1 item 1: the 60-minute stop surprised the user). Sources/LoomCore/SessionLifecycleController.swift has SessionIdlePolicy(idleAfter, stopsIdleRuns), ONE event subscription plus ONE timer for the earliest deadline across all sessions (already better than the idea's "one timer per idle session"; reschedule() runs on state-change frames only), evaluateIdle() with a blocker set (unknownAgentState, activeTurn, waitingForApproval, waitingForInput, pendingProviderWork = Stop.background_tasks + session_crons count, pendingPromptDelivery, recentTerminalInput via TerminalInputGate.lastInputDate, nonBaselineDescendants, ambiguousIdentity, deletionPending), then ProcessSupervisor.stopForIdle (endReason .idle, refuses if providerWorkStateIsReliable is false) and catalog lifecycle .idle (contract 4.3 already specifies the transition contract). AppDelegate.swift:493 passes SessionIdlePolicy(stopsIdleRuns: false); the only other reference is Tests/LoomCoreTests/SessionRuntimeTests.swift:620. The UI side also exists: ConversationController.reconcile -> keepEndedScreen captures the ended screen from the live (even hidden) TerminalSurface and releases the surface; EndedScreenNotice offers Resume; runtime.resumeConversation uses the stored provider id, passes --effort back, and never falls back to a new conversation (ProviderResumeDiagnostics).

WHAT TO ADD (smallest version, "adopt-light" shape once the spike passes):
1. Setting: UIPreferences (ui-preferences.json) "Put idle sessions to sleep", OFF by default, window picker (15 min / 30 min / 1 h / 2 h; recommend default 30 min when switched on). SessionRuntime gets a setter that updates the lifecycle controller's policy (today `policy` is a `let`) and calls reschedule(); turning it off cancels the timer. No new timer type.
2. New blockers in evaluateIdle: (a) viewed: SessionEventHub.viewedSessionID is private, so add a read accessor; the session the user is looking at in a visible, active window is never parked; (b) possible draft: TerminalInputGate.lastInputDate(runID) later than the last UserPromptSubmit/Stop means unsent composer text may exist (Loom cannot read the TUI composer, so be conservative: any keystroke after the last submit blocks until the next prompt); (c) a pending open-session request of that run (OpenSessionCoordinator); (d) deletionPending already exists.
3. Fix two signal problems that would make real Claude sessions never park or park wrongly: (i) the .waitingForInput blocker (SessionLifecycleController.swift:438) cannot tell Claude's idle_prompt reminder (about 60 s after every finished turn) or the registry "idle" sample from a real question, because ClaudeHook.swift:791 and :618 map all of them to .waitingForInput. This is cmux bug #14308 in Loom form. SessionEventHub already distinguishes them (activePhase == .underWay with .waitingForInput at lines 249-252 and 342 versus an at-prompt period), so use "waitingForInput while activePhase is not underWay" as parkable. (ii) ClaudeHook.swift collectionCount(object["background_tasks"]) returns 0 when the key is missing, so a future CLI that drops or renames the documented Stop fields (background_tasks, session_crons; documented in code.claude.com hooks reference, in the CLI since about 2.1.145) would read as "no pending work" and park a session with live background tasks. Require the keys to be present (a Stop that lacks them makes the work state unknown, so no park) and log a cli_compat_warning once, in the style of the existing CLI-drift handling.
4. Drop the DescendantRecheckSchedule backoff (5 s to 300 s repeating re-checks) for parking: treat any non-leader descendant as a hard block that is re-evaluated at the next state event. Cheaper, no timer chain, and the false negative (a silently exited helper delays parking) is harmless. This user's three live Claude processes had no child processes at all when checked, so MCP children are not a blocker for them, but a user with stdio MCP servers would simply never park (conservative and acceptable, maybe a one-line reason in the card tooltip).
5. Trigger set stays event-driven: frames (turn complete, prompt, view change) reschedule; one Task.sleep to the earliest deadline; on fire, evaluate only due sessions. Optional later trigger: DispatchSource memory-pressure event parks the oldest eligible sessions early (zero polling, cmux/Supacode precedent). Skip Supacode variant B (renderer-only freeing): Loom's whole process with 3 live terminals was 75 MB RSS while each Claude is 194-324 MB, so the renderer is not where the memory is.
6. Verified outcome and state: "Asleep" is shown only from the existing succeeded SessionStopReport plus companion teardown, as lifecycle .idle with end_reason idle (no schema change). A failed stop stays the existing "Stop not verified" state. Journal a `park` event (counts and blocker names only, no content) like the other rare events in DiagnosticJournal.
7. Manual "Sleep" is already Stop (Cmd+.): same verified stop, same ended screen, same Resume. The only difference worth adding is that Stop closes the tab (ConversationController.stop) while a sleeping session may keep its tab. Do not build a separate manual path first; ship opt-in auto with the manual menu item reusing evaluateIdle's checklist as an explanation ("Asleep when X finishes").
8. Cache awareness is simpler than the idea says: the server-side prompt cache expires with or without the process, so parking after at least one TTL costs no cache that was still warm; a window of 30 min or more means "cache cold" is true by the time a session is parked. Show it as static text on the ended notice (using last_activity_at, assume the 5 min tier; exact tier only exists in statusLine JSON, so word it "probably cold"). No countdown. Idle compaction (2.1.299, 200K+ conversations idle about 54 min) will not fire in a parked session; whether that is a saving or a loss is part of the spike.
9. Out of scope: Variant B, a daemon, per-session timers, transcript scanning for background work (cmux's 32 MiB tail scan), and anything that keeps a process alive after Quit.

BOUNDS: zero extra wakeups while idle (one sleeping Task for all sessions); evaluation reads the process table once per due session at the deadline; no file reads; ended screens stay capped at 16 / 4 MiB (EndedScreens.swift), memory-only, so more than 16 sleeping sessions or a Loom restart fall back to the record view (ConversationDetail) rather than a screen. Note for D-43/D-46: a future cross-session channel must treat an Asleep target as not deliverable (or ask the user to wake it), never wake it silently.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Settings (General): toggle "Put idle sessions to sleep" (off) with "after 30 min". Card: label "Asleep" (no dot, same quiet treatment as Idle/Ready/ended per DESIGN; the contract word is `idle` but "Idle" collides with Claude's own registry idle, so rename the label) plus the existing relative time; project stripe, branch, subagent tree unchanged. Context menu: "Sleep" (Stop that keeps the tab) next to Resume. Detail: the existing ended-screen view with the slim notice "Asleep since 14:02. The conversation cache is probably cold." and the filled Resume button (existing "Resuming…" state while it starts). Open behaviour is a user decision: either click Resume as today, or a click-selection (not arrow-key browsing) of an Asleep card resumes at once, which would amend D-45's "Return does nothing on an ended screen / opening launches nothing" for this one state. Menu bar and Dock badge need no change (Asleep is not an attention state). Quit confirmation still counts only Working/Needs-approval sessions.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: PASS and the point of the idea. Measured today on the user's daily Loom: three live Claude processes at 194, 262 and 324 MB phys_footprint (208/306/363 MB RSS) on a 16 GB Mac (about 690 MB swap used), the Loom app itself 75 MB; ten live sessions is roughly 2.5-3 GB. Cost of the feature: one sleeping Task, no polling (drop the 5-300 s descendant re-check). Predictability: RISK, the central one. D-38 exists because an automatic stop at 60 min surprised the user; mitigate with opt-in (off), a visible "Asleep" state, a journal line, never parking the viewed session, and by listing blocker reasons. Accurate status: PASS if "Asleep" is shown only from the verified stop report (existing); RISK from the signal gaps found: idle_prompt/registry-idle lumped into waitingForInput (never parks) and missing `background_tasks`/`session_crons` read as 0 (parks wrongly). Fluency: RISK, resume latency and the extra click, plus lost session-local state (see experiments). CLI-update resilience: PASS with the missing-key fix; relies only on documented hook fields and `--resume`, never pins, resume failure is surfaced and never starts a new conversation (ProviderResumeDiagnostics). Modularity: PASS, extends the LoomCore lifecycle controller; UI only gets a setting, a label and notice text. Ownership: PASS, stop goes through the run scope; nothing outlives Quit. User authority: PASS only while opt-in; the same D-38 reversal would be a violation if it came back on by default.
feasibility.value_reason: It serves a stated wish ("idle sessions cost nothing") and the memory is real (200-330 MB per live Claude on a 16 GB machine that also runs Claude Desktop, Xcode and builds), but today the user keeps about three sessions live, so the gain is moderate, Stop plus Resume already gives a manual version, and the user turned the automatic version off once after being surprised. Value rises if the user routinely keeps 8-15 sessions open or the Mac is under memory pressure.
depends_on: D-38 amendment (user decision; contract 4.3 says the idle transition is not automatic)
Hook signal fixes inside this idea: idle_prompt versus real question in the waitingForInput blocker; required presence of Stop.background_tasks and session_crons
Optional later: the cache-cold hint idea (usage-tools, cost S) can share the static 'probably cold' text
Optional later: statusLine bridge idea if the exact cache tier or session-local settings (model, permission mode) are wanted
experiments: Resume fidelity (half day, isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, base it on scripts/perf/claude_resume_real.py; never the real ~/.claude). Start a real Claude through Loom's launch profile, set non-default state (shift-tab permission mode such as acceptEdits/plan, /model, a 'don't ask again this session' tool grant, /add-dir, fast mode, output style, a background Bash, a Monitor, a ScheduleWakeup or /loop wakeup, a todo list, /rename), then Stop and --resume. Record what survives. Decision rule: whatever is lost becomes either a restore flag taken from the transcript (as --effort already is, FB1) or an eligibility blocker (do not park a session in a non-default permission mode or with session grants); if the loss is large and cannot be restored or blocked, the feature stays 'manual Stop only' and the verdict becomes later/skip.

Signal truth: with real hooks, check what Stop.background_tasks and session_crons list for a background Bash, a Monitor, a running workflow, a background subagent and a ScheduleWakeup wakeup, and what happens to the state after an Esc interrupt (Stop does not fire on user interrupt per the hooks doc). Confirm the idle_prompt arrives about 60 s after a finished turn and that the hub's activePhase separates it from an AskUserQuestion/elicitation. Decision: if wakeups are not in session_crons, they need their own blocker or the feature must refuse sessions that ever used /loop or ScheduleWakeup; if the fields are unreliable, do not enable auto-park.

Resume latency: time from Resume to the SessionStart hook (atPrompt) for conversations of about 20K, 100K and 250K tokens. Decision: under about 3 s allows click-selection resume; much longer keeps an explicit Resume click with the 'Resuming…' notice.

Benefit check (read-only, 10 minutes): with N sessions live, compare `footprint` per Claude process and system memory pressure/swap against a parked state. Decision: if the user's real working set is 3-4 sessions and memory pressure is low, defer the feature until it hurts and keep Stop as the manual tool.

Park-before-compaction side effect: confirm whether a 200K+ idle session that is parked before about 54 min avoids the CLI's idle compaction token spend, and whether the cold resume then costs more or less than the compacted one. Informs the default window (30 min versus 1 h).
user_decisions: Is re-enabling automatic stop acceptable at all after D-38, as a strictly opt-in setting that is off by default (recommended), or should only a manual Sleep exist?
Default window when switched on: 30 min (recommended, past the 5 min cache tier, before the 54 min idle compaction) or 1 h or longer?
Opening an Asleep session: keep the explicit Resume click, or resume at once on click-selection (amends D-45's 'Return does nothing / opening launches nothing' for this state only)?

If the fidelity spike shows session-local state is lost (permission mode, session tool grants, model): restore what can be restored and block parking for the rest, or accept the loss with a note on the card?
Name: 'Asleep' (recommended, avoids confusion with Claude's registry 'idle') or 'Parked' or the contract's 'Idle'?
Should a session that has an open tab but is not on screen, or the selected session while the window is hidden for hours, be eligible?
Interest in the later memory-pressure trigger (park the oldest eligible sessions early under pressure), accepting that a park the user did not time themselves is less predictable?

feasibility.title: Idle auto-park (hibernate): stop the process, keep the card, resume on open

feasibility.one_line: Adopt a trimmed version: one on/off setting "Keep the Mac awake while sessions work", one idle-system-sleep assertion driven by the existing live-state fan-out (the same path as the menu bar item), with background tasks counted, scheduled crons excluded, a one-shot cap and a visible indicator. Drop "Always" and the "tied to the watchdog" claim, because Loom's Working is already registry-corrected and the watchdog only covers a run with zero hooks.
feasibility.loom_design:
PLUG-IN POINT (verified). `CatalogModel.updateAttentionCount()` (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/CatalogModel+Navigation.swift:43) already runs on every live-state or record change and never on a timer. It derives `MenuBarSummary` and fires `onMenuBarChange`, which `AppDelegate.installSystemIntegration` (Sources/loom-app/AppDelegate+System.swift:35) wires to `MenuBarController` and `ApprovalNotifier`. The keep-awake feature is a third consumer of the same pass. The model keeps `liveStates` current whether or not the window is visible, so no new subscription, watcher or timer is needed. This is the ApprovalNotifier pattern, which only hears a changed set (ApprovalNotifier.swift).

PIECES.
(1) `KeepAwakeRule` (pure, LoomCatalogUI, next to MenuBarState/SessionNavigation). Input is `liveStates` (SessionViewState). A session counts when `runID != nil`, no `stopFailure`, no `issue`, identity is not ambiguous, and either `status.activity == .working` or (`.turnComplete` with background work > 0). It does NOT count `.waitingForApproval`, which matches Zed and what the user asked for. It does NOT count scheduled crons.
   - Why not reuse `MenuBarSummary.working` or `SessionIndicator.working`? `SessionIndicator.init` (SessionDisplay.swift:58-60) maps `.turnComplete` with `pendingProviderWorkCount > 0` to Working. That count is `backgroundTaskCount + scheduledTaskCount` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift:84 and :301). `scheduledTaskCount` is `Stop.session_crons`, so a session with a /loop or cron looks Working forever and would pin the Mac awake. This is the real false-Working source in Loom, and it is not the stale-hook case the research feared.
   - Fix: add an additive `scheduledWorkCount` (default 0) to `ProviderWorkState` (SessionLifecycleController.swift:3), set only by the Claude adapter's two construction sites. `pendingProviderWorkCount` stays the sum, so the idle blockers (SessionLifecycleController.swift:441) and the Active section (SessionEventHub.swift:338) do not change. The rule then uses `pending - scheduled`. The smaller fallback is `activity == .working` only, which misses the case where Claude ends its turn and waits for a background test run.
(2) `PowerAssertionService` protocol in Sources/loom-app/SystemServices.swift, beside NotificationService and LoginItemService, with the live implementation and a recording fake under `--evidence`. The live version calls `IOPMAssertionCreateWithName(kIOPMAssertionTypePreventUserIdleSystemSleep, level on, "Loom: a session is working")` and `IOPMAssertionRelease`. It reports the IOReturn so the indicator only shows when creation succeeded. `ProcessInfo.beginActivity(.idleSystemSleepDisabled)` is the Foundation alternative, but IOKit is more exact. Do not use `.userInitiated`, which also changes App Nap and sudden-termination behaviour. Display sleep is not asserted, so the screen still sleeps and locks.
(3) `KeepAwakeController` (loom-app, @MainActor, ~60 lines). It takes `count` from the model and `model.keepAwake` from preferences. Count goes from 0 to >0: take the assertion and arm a single one-shot cap (suggest 6-8 h of continuous hold, then release until the next fresh transition from zero). Count goes to 0: release after a short grace (suggest 30 s, one-shot) so turn handoffs and quick follow-up prompts do not flap the assertion. Setting off, `applicationWillTerminate` (AppDelegate.swift:374) and Low Power Mode on also release (`NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange`, event-driven). A crash or kill releases automatically, because the kernel drops assertions with the process, so nothing outlives Loom (process ownership and the Quit contract hold). Exposed `isHolding` goes to the model for the indicator.
(4) Preference: `UIPreferences.keepAwake: Bool` (UIPreferences.swift:48-112, absent in an old file decodes to the default), `CatalogModel.setKeepAwake` with an `onKeepAwakeChange` closure, copying `setNotifyApprovals` (CatalogModel.swift:1189). Settings row in `SystemSettingsCard` (SettingsView.swift:~150), same `SettingsRow` + switch as "Notify when a session needs approval".
(5) Trigger plumbing: `updateAttentionCount` computes the keep-awake count in the same pass and calls the closure only when the boolean-relevant value changes (count 0 vs >0), as it does for `menuBarSummary`.

BOUNDS. No polling. At most two one-shot timers (grace and cap), both armed only on state edges. One assertion, one tiny object. Nothing is drawn while hidden (the indicator is state-driven). No new file watchers, no reads.

VERIFIED OUTCOME. The indicator shows only when `IOPMAssertionCreate` returned success. Evidence check: `pmset -g assertions` lists a PreventUserIdleSystemSleep entry named for Loom while a fake-provider session (Sources/loom-fake-provider) is Working and none after it finishes. Run this in the dev flavor with an isolated data root and a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, never the real app.

CLI-UPDATE RESILIENCE. It reads only state Loom already derives. Hook and registry drift is already detected (D-45), and the feature degrades safely: unknown state means no hold.

TESTS. Pure `KeepAwakeRule` cases: working, approval, ready, cron-only, background-only, problem/issue, stopUnverified. `KeepAwakeController` with the fake service: edges, grace, cap, setting off, Low Power Mode, quit. Reuse the SystemServices fake seam. One integration check with the fake provider.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Settings > General > the system card (SystemSettingsCard), one new row: title "Keep the Mac awake while sessions work", detail "Stops idle sleep while a session is working or waiting on background tasks. The screen can still sleep and lock. Closing the lid still sleeps the Mac." Switch only, and a notice line when Low Power Mode pauses it.

Indicator, shown only while actually holding (state-driven, no animation, monochrome SF Symbol per DESIGN 'Iconography'):
- The menu bar menu gets a disabled info line "Keeping this Mac awake" above the separator (MenuBarMenu.items). It also goes in the status item's accessibility label ("Loom, 2 sessions working, keeping the Mac awake").
- The sidebar footer gets a small 13 pt glyph (e.g. a sun/moon-slash or bolt style symbol) left of the usage chip, with a tooltip "Keeping this Mac awake while sessions work. Click to change." The click opens Settings > General. No layout shift: it is drawn only while holding, and the chip is the one flexible element in the footer (SidebarFooter.swift:11), so it absorbs the 28 pt.

No Dock badge change. Off by default or on by default is the user's call (see decisions).
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: pass. It runs on edges of existing state, with no polling, no watcher and no draw while hidden. The IOKit assertion costs nothing while held. Risk: only battery drain from a false hold, mitigated below.

Predictable: pass if it is a visible setting plus a visible indicator, and a hold is only for 'turn under way or background tasks'. Risks: (a) cron-only sessions look Working in Loom today and would hold forever, so exclude them as designed. (b) A genuinely stuck Working. Loom's Working is registry-backed in both directions: `ClaudeRegistryWatch` (vnode, no timer) turns an 'idle' sample back into waitingForInput, so an Esc interrupt or a lost Stop hook corrects itself. Remaining stuck cases get the one-shot cap, a process-end release, and the visible indicator. Do NOT add an inactivity lease like Orca's stale timeout: a 40-minute test run emits no hooks and would be released wrongly.

Accurate status: pass. 'Holding' means creation succeeded, it is released on every exit path, and nothing is shown as success otherwise. Caveats to state plainly in the UI copy: lid-close on battery still sleeps, and a Working session that Loom flags as Problem (hook silence) does not hold even if Claude is really busy.

Fluency: pass. No prompts, and it removes the side-terminal caffeinate habit.

Modularity: pass. A pure rule in LoomCatalogUI, a service protocol and controller in loom-app (as for notifications and login item), one additive field in LoomCore, and no dependency pointing up.

CLI-update resilience: pass. Documented hook and registry state only, nothing pinned, and unknown state means no hold. Quota auto-resume Notification types are currently ignored by `notificationActivity` (ClaudeHook.swift:788). Whether a quota wait shows as Working is unverified (see experiments).

Ownership: pass. The assertion belongs to the Loom process, so Quit or a crash releases it. No daemon, no change to 'Quit stops everything'.

User authority: pass. It is an explicit setting touching only this Mac's idle sleep, with no cross-session action. 'Always' is not recommended because it contradicts 'idle sessions cost nothing'.

A run that sleeps silently mid-turn, or a background test that freezes after Claude ends its turn, costs real time and tokens. The feature is small, invisible when working and removes a manual caffeinate habit. The ceiling is limited: lid-close still sleeps, and it does not give 'sessions run while the Mac is closed', which is the cloud or Remote Control domain. A student laptop on battery makes the default and Low Power Mode behaviour matter. Docs note Desktop sessions survive sleep only while the process survives, and it helps quota auto-resume, which waits for Enter if the Mac slept more than about 30 minutes across the reset.

feasibility.one_line: Most of the 'crash-safe state' half already exists in Loom (SQLite catalog with WAL, daily backups, damaged-catalog prompt, atomic prefs, system-quit handling, abandoned-run closing), so adopt only the missing half: a launch-time, derived 'Reopen what was running' offer (with an optional 'was mid-turn' tag), no snapshots and no new write path.
feasibility.loom_design:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (observed in code/docs, so the stated mechanisms are mostly moot):
- Durable state is not a layout file. Loom has no pane layout; the only 'layout' is UIPreferences {selectedSessionID, openTabs (max 8), windowFrame, viewMode, sidebar width} in ui-preferences.json (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/UIPreferences.swift). UIPreferencesStore.flush already writes with .atomic, writes only on change, renames an unreadable file to ui-preferences.unreadable-<ts>.json, tabs are written immediately, selection/frame coalesce for 300 ms (CatalogModel.preferenceWriteDelay) and flush on Quit (AppDelegate.applicationWillTerminate -> flushPreferences). Resume handles (sessions.provider_conversation_id, working_directory, provider_identity_changes) live in catalog.sqlite3: WAL, quick_check, per-event transactions, daily VACUUM INTO backups (3 kept, CatalogBackupStore), launch prompt Restore Backup / Start Fresh for a damaged catalog (AppDelegate+Diagnostics.offerCatalogRecovery, CatalogRecoveryPrompt), migrations in one transaction (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5).
- Reboot/logout/update: macOS sends the quit Apple event; QuitConfirmation.isSystemInitiated reads keyAEQuitReason (logo/rlgo/rrst/rest/rsdn/shut), never asks, shuts down through AppShutdownCoordinator, and replies terminate even if the shutdown is unverified (AppDelegate.quitFinished). An NSWorkspace.willPowerOff observer would only duplicate this path.
- Crash/Force Quit: SessionCatalog.closeAbandonedRuns (SessionRuntime.start, line ~340) ends runs whose leader is dead with reason applicationQuit and no exit status; PreviousRunRecovery drains run scopes; StaleSocketSweep removes sockets; the run host stops forked work if Loom dies (contract section 6).
- 'Not Failed': after Quit/crash no live state exists, so a mid-work session already shows Ended/Idle/Stale (SessionIndicator.init in SessionDisplay.swift), never Failed. What is missing is only the knowledge 'this one was running'.
- Stale resume reference validation: Loom does not scrape references. It launches new chats with --session-id and resumes with --resume (contract line ~258); /clear, fork and resume are tracked by adoptConversation + provider_identity_changes. So herdr bugs #5261 (daemon session recorded as another pane's) and #5348 (hook silently inert without python3) have no direct analogue. SessionRuntime.resumeConversation already refuses cleanly (noProviderIdentity, requireDirectory, deletionPending, unverifiedStop) and ProviderResumeDiagnostics maps 'No conversation found' to providerHistoryUnavailable. Missing: a pre-check before offering resume.

WHAT TO BUILD (lightest version):
1. Derived set, no new schema, no hot-path write. 'Ended with the app' = sessions whose latest run (via run_sessions.unlinked_at IS NULL, so a /clear that moved the run counts the card the run ended on) has runs.end_reason = 'applicationQuit' AND runs.ended_at is newer than the previous launch (CleanupCoordinator already keeps last_launch_at, app_state key, and reads the previous value before overwriting; capture it once at start) AND no later run exists for that session. This covers clean Quit (supervisor stop paths use applicationQuit, ProcessSupervisor+CatalogCommits.swift:32, ProcessSupervisor.swift:437/445, +Shutdown.swift:197) and crash (closeAbandonedRuns). A user Stop (.requested) and a CLI that exited by itself (.processExited) are excluded automatically. The set lives for exactly one launch generation, so it is bounded and needs no cleanup job. Implement as one catalog read in a new small extension (SessionCatalog+Runs.swift neighbour), returning ids, evaluated once after closeAbandonedRuns at runtime start and again only on explicit refresh.
2. Filter: provider == claude (Codex frozen, startableProviders), providerConversationID non-empty, not isDeletionPending, working directory exists (requireDirectory), and the Claude transcript for that id still exists under the profile projects folder (one stat per candidate, off MainActor; helper next to SubagentTranscriptLocation / ClaudeDataInventory which already know the layout). A candidate that fails is dropped from the offer (and could show 'cannot resume: history missing' on its card). This is the 'validate against Claude's own data instead of trusting' part, at zero cost.
3. Optional mid-turn tag (second step, still no hot path): at the start of SessionRuntime.shutdown, before ProcessSupervisor.shutdown, write one app_state row (e.g. quit_busy_sessions, JSON of ids) from the same busy predicate QuitConfirmation.busyCount uses (Working or Needs approval). Hooks are already stopped before the supervisor stops (ARCHITECTURE Quit section), so no late Stop hook can disturb it. For a crash this is unknown, and the UI says only 'was running', never claims mid-turn. The heavier alternative (a sessions.busy_since column set on the busy edge in ProcessSupervisor.updateProviderWorkState and cleared when a non-quit run end is recorded) gives crash-accurate mid-turn tags, costs 2 UPDATEs per turn (same cadence as existing markProviderUsed/markProviderActivity in ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~273/287), needs the ensureOriginColumns-style add-on-open migration, and has an accuracy trap: Esc-interrupt does not fire Stop, so the flag must follow the effective status, not raw hooks. Not recommended for v2 first cut.
4. Action: CatalogModel gets 'reopenCandidates' (ids) and 'reopenAll()' which calls the existing intents.resume(sessionID:) for each, staggered (sequential with a small delay, concurrency capped at 2-3) so N Claude processes and N terminals do not start in the same instant; each failure surfaces through the existing per-card problem text. Dismiss stores nothing durable beyond an in-memory flag (the set expires at next launch anyway); optionally app_state key reopen_dismissed_at.
5. Never automatic (user authority, tokens, process count): offer, do not act. No auto-resume on launch. No screen history persistence (secrets; the in-memory ended-screen snapshot, max 16 / 4 MiB in ConversationController, stays memory-only).

PRINCIPLE VIOLATIONS TO AVOID: polling for 'what is running' (do it at launch and at shutdown only); writing per hook event; auto-launching Claude processes; claiming 'interrupted/mid-turn' when only 'was running' is known; resuming Codex; reading the user's transcripts beyond a stat; adding a periodic snapshot timer (the herdr 15-minute/48-snapshot machinery solves a problem Loom does not have because its state is a transactional DB plus an 8-field JSON).

Should the offer survive a second launch if you ignore it, or expire after one launch as proposed (bounded, predictable)?

feasibility.one_line: Do not build now: the read-only lane is low-value for someone whose sessions live in Loom and carries an unmeasured side effect (`claude agents --json` may start Anthropic's supervisor outside Loom's scope), and 'Run detached' breaks Loom's hook-status channel across a Quit and contradicts D-40, while a small resume-interrupted feature gives most of the benefit.
feasibility.loom_design:
SPLIT THE IDEA. The three mechanisms have very different costs.

PART 1, 'Elsewhere' lane (read-only visibility). Lightest version, if the user ever wants it:
- Source. Prefer the sessions folder Loom already reads over a CLI spawn. `ClaudeRegistryReader` (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeRegistry.swift) already opens `<config>/sessions/<pid>.json` with O_NOFOLLOW, uid/mode checks and a 16 KiB cap, and `ClaudeDataInventory.liveSession` (line ~376) already scans `sessions/*.json`. A new sibling reader, `ClaudeExternalSessions`, would list that folder (bounded count and bytes), keep only files whose pid is alive with matching `procStart`, and drop Loom's own rows by leader pid or `sessionId` against `ProcessSupervisor` runs and `ManagedSession.providerConversationID`. No process is started and the supervisor is never touched. Cost: it is the 'private CLI capability' the registry file already is, so it needs the same drift handling (unknown kind or status becomes a visible but inert row; `ClaudeRegistryDiagnostics.noteUnknownStatus` pattern). Note `decode` today demands `kind == "interactive"`, so background rows need a new decode path.
- Documented alternative: `claude agents --json --all` (docs call it 'the supported way to read session state'). Loom's `ProviderToolchain.capture` (Sources/LoomCore/ProviderToolchain.swift:175) already runs `claude --help` in a bounded way, so a bounded capture of `agents --json` has a pattern. But it is a Node CLI start (hundreds of ms and a CPU burst), and whether it starts the supervisor is unknown (docs: the supervisor starts 'the first time you background a session or open agent view'; env page says CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW also disables the 'on-demand supervisor'). Loom must keep passing DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1 for this call (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:147 sets it only for hosted sessions; the app-side capture would have to set it too) and the spike must show the call still works with it and spawns nothing.
- Trigger (events only): window activation (the hook `CatalogModel.setWindowActive`, CatalogModel.swift:1022, where branch refresh already runs), a manual Refresh button, and the lane being expanded. No timer. A view-model `ElsewhereModel` in LoomCatalogUI holds at most ~50 rows, nothing observed while the lane is collapsed or the window hidden.
- What it can honestly do: list `cwd` (mapped to a Loom project by path), name, state/status, `waitingFor`, age. Open: ONLY a `kind: background` row can be opened with `claude attach <id>`; a plain interactive session running in another terminal cannot be attached (it is tied to that terminal), and `claude --resume <id>` on a live conversation would create a second writer on one transcript, so interactive rows stay read-only ('Copy session id', 'Reveal cwd'). That removes most of the 'openable' promise.
- Never a Stop on these rows. Contract §6: 'user sessions outside Loom are not touched'.

PART 2, 'Run detached' (explicit per-session supervisor hosting). Requires all of:
- A third process class beside 'Loom run in a scope' and 'ended'. New `RunKind.detached` in the catalog `runs` table (schema bump; note v3 No-downgrade policy DP-CP4-4), `ProcessSupervisor` registry entry that is NOT a scope member, a `DetachedSessionController` in LoomCore that shells `claude --bg --name`, `claude attach|stop|logs <id>` and verifies by reading `agents --json` after each action.
- Env. Loom sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1 on every hosted Claude so that `<-` on an empty prompt cannot background a session out of the scope (agent-view doc: `leftArrowOpensAgents` is on by default). The detached class must be launched by Loom's own process (not from inside a hosted session) with the variable unset, and every normal session keeps it set.
- Status channel breaks. Hook sockets and tokens are per app run: `SessionRuntime.ensureHooks` (SessionRuntime+Claude.swift:9-49) names `h-<8 hex of ownershipRunID>.sock` and mints a fresh token per run. A detached session keeps the settings it was spawned with, so after Loom quits and relaunches its hooks point at a dead socket for good, and `claude attach` runs the client in Loom's PTY while the actual `claude` process is under the supervisor with the supervisor's environment (open issues #98872, #102949), not Loom's `LOOM_*` variables. `ClaudeRegistryReader` keys on the leader pid (`sessions/<leader.pid>.json`), and the leader would be the attach client, so the existing tracker identity (pid + procStart + startedAt + sessionId) does not apply. Status for the detached class would have to come from `agents --json`, which is a poll: the only documented source. That contradicts 'no polling' and 'accurate status' unless limited to focus/manual refresh (stale between), which is a visibly weaker Working indicator.
- Quit. Add Supacode's two-button dialog (Quit / Quit and Terminate Sessions) in `AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate` and `AppShutdownCoordinator`, amend contract §6 ('no running work started and owned by Loom remains') and D-40 ('Claude's own background sessions ... stay off'), and add an orphan sweep for detached sessions Loom launched.
- Deletion. `ClaudeDataInventory.liveSession` correctly sees a detached session as live, so the deletion flow's 'stopping' step (`stopConversation`, requires report.succeeded) needs a detached branch that calls `claude stop` and verifies; and the delete dry run must warn about worktrees (agent view Delete discards a worktree including uncommitted changes; second delete drops commits).
- cwd semantics. Dispatch through `--bg` moves the session into `.claude/worktrees/...`, changing the card's cwd and branch chip (`GitBranch`/`BranchCache` read by folder). `/bg` or `<-` skip isolation but are blocked by our env var and have the open new-session-id bug (#87984).
- Run-scope capture of the supervisor is unknown: started from a hosted session it may be killed by Stop (taking every detached session with it) or escape unowned.

CHEAPER SUBSTITUTE for the same user need (survive a Quit): 'N interrupted' marker plus one-click Resume interrupted on the existing resume path (`ProviderResumePlanner.claude`, ProviderResume.swift), power assertion while Working (persistence note option A, cost S). It does not keep an in-flight turn alive, which is the only thing Part 2 adds.

Bounds if ever built: row cap ~50, 16 KiB per file, one capture in flight with a 5 s timeout, no capture while the window is hidden, output parse that never decodes content fields, unknown values shown but inert.

Context menu: Copy session id, Reveal cwd; for kind background also 'Open in Loom' (claude attach in a PTY). No Stop, no Delete. A refresh affordance in the section header and activation-time refresh; a 'last checked 2 min ago' label because the data is not live.

feasibility.one_line: Build a tokens-first, live-sessions-only context figure that rides the existing transcript watcher and usage index and resets on a documented compaction hook; add percent and amber/red only where the window is known, because current models run 1M by default, so the transcript route cannot give a trustworthy percent for the common case.
feasibility.loom_design:
**Key facts I verified (they change the idea)**
- Anthropic's model-config doc (fetched today via tinyfish) says Opus 4.7+, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5 and the Fable models run a native 1M window with no `[1m]` suffix. They auto-compact at about 967K by default. The user can change this with `autoCompactWindow`, `/autocompact`, `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`, and Loom cannot see any of these. Opus/Sonnet 4.6 reach 1M only through `[1m]`.
- So for this user the common case is a 1M window. A "50/70/85 percent" scale against an assumed 200K would show false amber at 140-199K tokens. The idea's one-way heuristic ("assume 1M once any record exceeds 200K") is right in direction but fails in exactly that common case, because it only helps after the session has already passed 200K.
- The statusLine stdin JSON is the only documented source of `context_window_size`. The doc itself says it counts "from the last API response" while `/context` adds an estimate, so "approx" is honest.
- Compaction already reaches Loom: `SessionStart` is hooked and carries `source` ("startup", "resume", "clear", "compact", "fork"). `ClaudeHookEvent.Kind.sessionStart(source:)` exists and `ClaudeSessionAdapter` currently treats "compact" as `.automatic`. The hooks doc also lists `PostCompact`, which fires after manual, auto and idle compaction. Loom therefore does NOT need `compact_boundary.postTokens` from the transcript (an internal format). The hook is a documented interface.
- Subagent transcripts ARE indexed: `UsageTranscriptWalker.session(forRelativeComponents:)` maps `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` to the parent session id. The query must therefore exclude sidechain rows (`msg.flags & 1`). It should also exclude files whose path contains `/subagents/`, in case a subagent line lacks `isSidechain` (spike E3).

**Where it plugs in (no new watcher, timer or process)**
1. LoomCore `ClaudeUsageIndex`: add `latestContext(forSessions:) -> [String: ContextSample]`.
   - A `ContextSample` holds timestamp, model symbol text and `input + cw5 + cw1 + cr`.
   - It is one indexed read of the `msg` table (columns `input`, `cw5`, `cw1`, `cr`, `ts_ms`, `flags`, `model`; partial index `msg_session`). Per live session: `WHERE session=? AND flags&1=0` joined to `file` with a `NOT LIKE '%/subagents/%'` guard, `ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT 1`.
   - Output tokens are excluded, matching the documented `used_percentage` formula.
   - The index already dedupes by message id (it keeps the larger total) and records `sidechain`, `model` and `sessionID` per row (`ClaudeUsageParser.ClaudeUsageRecord`, `UsageDatabase.upsert`). No parser change is needed.
   - If a long session makes `ORDER BY` measurable, add `(session, ts_ms)`. The index file is disposable and rebuilt on a schema bump.
   - Window inference, no hardcoded table: `maxContextByModel()` is `SELECT model, MAX(input+cw5+cw1+cr)` over the 90-day history. A model whose maximum ever exceeded 200K is "extended window known". Otherwise the window is unknown and the UI shows tokens only. This is derived from the user's own data and cannot drift like a table.
2. LoomCore `SessionEventHub` / `SessionViewState`: add `compactedAt: Date?`.
   - It is set from `SessionStart(source: "compact")` in `ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive` (the same place `.subagents` is published), and cleared by a new run, as `subagents` is.
   - A sample is valid only if `sample.timestamp > compactedAt`. This fixes the one real accuracy hole: after a manual `/compact` from 90 percent the bar would stay red until the next API call.
   - If spike E2 shows idle compaction does not send `SessionStart(compact)`, add `PostCompact` to the event list in `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings`. It is a rare event, unlike per-tool hooks, so the one-helper-per-event cost is negligible. `ClaudeHookEvent.Kind` also needs a `.postCompact` case. Today an unknown name becomes `.unknown` and must not be allowed to change status.
3. LoomCatalogUI: a small `ContextReading` value type (pure, unit-tested like `UsageChipContent`) holding tokens, an optional percent and a level (hidden, neutral, amber, red).
   - `UsageModel.run()` ends in `loadAfterScan`. After a scan it asks the index once for the conversation ids of rows that have a live run (`SessionRowModel.live?.runID != nil`, `live.conversationID`). This is at most about 10 ids.
   - `CatalogModel` patches `SessionRowModel.apply(context:)` only when the value changed, using the existing `apply(live:)` pattern. It should round to whole percent or to 5K tokens, so a streaming turn does not redraw cards.
   - Trigger chain, all existing events: FSEvents `UsageTranscriptWatcher` -> `UsageModel.transcriptsChanged` -> 2 s debounce -> index refresh -> one context read. Gating is unchanged: when no window is active the changes are only collected, and coming back reads just those files. Nothing runs when hidden. On activation or a run start, a live row with no reading gets one read with no transcript scan, because the index persists across launches.
4. Not in v1: any statusLine bridge (I-24), any text typed into the PTY, any notification.

**What would violate the principles, and the avoidance**
- A per-session tail reader or timer: avoided, because it reuses the single FSEvents stream and the index.
- A statusLine bridge spawning a process per assistant message: it conflicts with D-32 and D-20, and it overrides the user's own status line. Keep it as the later exact variant, off by default.
- A hardcoded model-to-window table: replaced by history-derived learning.
- Percent shown with an unknown window: replaced by tokens only, in a neutral colour.
- A stale bar after compaction or a long idle: handled by `compactedAt` plus a "as of <time>" tooltip.
- Drawing for ended or idle records: live runs only. An ended card shows nothing, which matches "idle sessions cost nothing".

**Re-estimated cost:** M, not S. Core query plus window learning with fixtures (sidechain, duplicate ids, an advisor/multi-iteration case, compaction) is about 150 lines plus tests. The hub field and hook plumbing are about 60 lines plus `ClaudeHookTests`. The UI model and row patching are about 120 lines plus a render-count test in the style of `SidebarRenderTests` and `CatalogHotPathTests`. Views and docs (card, header slot, a11y, Increase Contrast, UI-MAP/DESIGN) add the rest. The tokens-only core with no colours is a size-S slice if the user wants it first.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
- **Session card, second row:** a small caption figure such as `412k` between the branch/pin group and the project name/provider icon. It appears only for live runs and above a visible threshold (default idea: 100K tokens, or 50 percent once the window is known). It is secondary-coloured while the window is unknown. It turns the attention orange (`LoomTheme.Status.attention`, the same colour the footer chip uses under 20 percent remaining) at roughly 70 percent and the failure tone at roughly 85 percent, only when the window is known. The card row is already tight (branch, pin, project, 14 pt icon), so the figure must be the first thing to drop on a narrow sidebar, like the footer chip's meter. No bar on the card in v1.
- **Detail header:** a `ContextChip` slot next to the project/branch chip in `SessionHeaderViews` (`HeaderFlowPlan` needs one more optional slot with the lowest priority after the branch). It shows the figure plus a 34x4 meter reusing `UsageChipMeter`, only when the window is known. The tooltip reads "About 412K tokens in context, as of the last reply (2m ago). Approximate: /context may differ." and, for a known window, "of 1M". Accessibility label: "Context about 412 thousand tokens, 41 percent, approximate".
- **Hint:** v1 has none beyond the tooltip. A later user-triggered "Compact..." or "New session from summary" must be a deliberate click, and it must go through the existing open-session approval flow rather than typing into the PTY.
- **Nothing moves:** no reordering, no animation, no badge, no notification, no Dock change.
feasibility.principle_check:
- **Resources: pass.** There is no new watcher, timer or process. It piggybacks on the existing FSEvents stream and the `UsageModel` observing gate. The extra work is one indexed SQL read of at most about 10 rows after a scan that was already happening. A row is redrawn only when its rounded value changes. Risk: the 2 s debounce means a streaming turn triggers a read every few seconds while the window is active, which is the same cadence as the usage chip today.
- **Predictability: pass.** The figure is hidden under a threshold, positions never move, and it appears only for live runs.
- **Accurate status: the main risk, handled by design.**
  - Percent is shown only with a window learned from the user's own history.
  - "Approx" appears in the tooltip, plus the age of the sample.
  - `compactedAt` removes the stale-after-compact case.
  - The residual risks are real: a user-set `autoCompactWindow` or `DISABLE_1M` is invisible to Loom, advisor turns may double-count `cache_read` (claude-hud #666, spike E1), and `/context` can read higher than the last API response.
  - None of these produce a "success" claim, but the tooltip must not read as exact.
- **Fluency: pass.** There are no clicks and no confirmations.
- **Modularity: pass.** A core query, a pure value type, a row patch and two views. `LoomCore` stays UI-free and dependencies point down.
- **CLI-update resilience: mostly pass.**
  - It depends on transcript `usage` fields, but the usage index already depends on them, parses them defensively and counts un-understood lines in `linesNotUnderstood`.
  - The compaction signal uses the documented `SessionStart.source` and `PostCompact`.
  - No version pinning. The window comes from observed history, not a table.
  - Risk: the `msg` row keeps the larger total per message id, which is fine for the input side. A transcript-format change that drops `cache_*` fields would read as small numbers. Fixture tests and the drift counter cover that.
- **Ownership: n/a**, read-only. **User authority: pass**, because nothing acts on a session. Any later compact or handoff is user-triggered, and typing into a PTY remains out of scope.
- **Standing decisions:** no conflict with D-32, D-34 or the contract. It adds no right rail and no chat UI, and it does not replace the terminal. D-20 is touched only if `PostCompact` is added to the hook list. That is an observer hook that returns nothing, like `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`, but it should be named to the user.
feasibility.value_reason: The user runs several sessions with subagents and hands off by hygiene, and the token figure also feeds the cache-cold and resume-cost decision. So a glanceable per-session size is useful and there is demand evidence (the Oct 2026 Desktop context-ring outcry; Anthropic's mods docs use a context-fill chart as the example). But current models run 1M natively, so "about to compact" at 967K is rare. The real value is a size/cost awareness figure, not a compaction alarm. That is why it is 3 and not 4-5, and why a percent scale would oversell it. The value rises if the same figure also drives a "cache cold, resume re-reads about 400K" hint on return to an idle card.

experiments: E1 (window and accuracy; decides whether percent and colours ship). Use an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with Loom's per-session --settings plus a throwaway statusLine that appends stdin JSON to a file. Run 3-4 short turns on the current default model. Then repeat with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1, and with `--model opus[1m]` if an Opus 4.6 variant is available. Compare, per turn, the transcript-derived `input+cache_creation+cache_read` of the last main-chain record against `context_window.used_percentage`, `context_window_size` and `current_usage`. Decides: (a) what `message.model` looks like for native-1M versus `[1m]` versus DISABLE_1M (if the transcript cannot tell them apart, percent stays learned-from-history only); (b) whether the figures match within about 1-2 percent. If they do, ship tokens and percent. If there is a constant offset, show tokens only. Include an advisor/multi-iteration turn if the feature is available, to see whether `cache_read` doubles.

E2 (compaction signals). Same isolated profile with a hook dumper for SessionStart, PreCompact and PostCompact. Use `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=100000` (documented minimum) for auto-compaction, a manual `/compact`, and for idle compaction `CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` set low (documented, needs 2.1.290+) and a wait of about 54 minutes. The check is whether the idle-compaction run emits `SessionStart(source=compact)`, `PostCompact`, both, or neither, and what the `compact_boundary` transcript line contains. Decides: SessionStart(compact) alone versus adding PostCompact to the launch hooks; and, if neither fires on idle compaction, a sample older than the cache TTL must be shown only as 'as of <time>'.

E3 (subagent attribution). In the E1 profile, run a turn that spawns a subagent. Check that its lines in `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` carry `isSidechain: true` and the parent's `sessionId`. Decides whether the `/subagents/` path guard in the SQL is needed or just belt-and-braces.

feasibility.one_line: The data is documented and event-driven and the spawn cost is small (about 4 ms CPU per loom-hook spawn, measured), so the real risk is the footer hints and the user's own status line; run a half-day spike on those before committing, and ship only an opt-in, no-chaining light version first.
feasibility.loom_design:
Facts first. Nothing in Sources/ mentions statusLine today. Loom already injects an inline `--settings` JSON per session (ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings: `crossSessionInbound: refuse` plus 9 hook events, each running the bundled loom-hook with timeout 1). Env carries LOOM_HOOK_SOCKET, LOOM_HOOK_TOKEN, LOOM_CLI (= helper path), LOOM_CONTROL_SOCKET. SessionRuntime+Claude.ensureHooks creates h-<8>.sock and c-<8>.sock. The contract (LOOM-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md line 258) says `--settings` "carries only this session's hooks and settings", so a statusLine entry is a small text amendment, not a new kind of change. PERF.md T3 measured a loom-hook spawn at about 3.8 ms CPU, 6 ms wall, 6.5 MiB transient (plans/experiments/cp5-perf-claude-hook.json), and the hook set deliberately has no per-tool hooks. A statusLine fires per assistant message (about one per tool step, debounced 300 ms, in-flight run cancelled), so it has per-tool-hook cardinality: roughly 0.1 s CPU for a 30-step turn. That is small in CPU terms. The real conflicts are D-20 (footer hints, an extra row, the user's own status line) and the literal wording of D-32, not CPU.

LIGHT VERSION (what I would build after the spike):
1. Launch. In `claudeSettings`, when the Settings toggle "Live session numbers" is on (default off, D-20 class, `UIPreferences`), add `"statusLine": {"type":"command","command":"\"$LOOM_CLI\" statusline"}`. The CLI runs the command through a shell, so $LOOM_CLI expands and survives the space in "Loom Dev.app" (the shell-expansion and env inheritance are to be verified in the spike). Gate it on `capabilities.supportsSettings` like the rest. No `refreshInterval` (that would be polling). No `subagentStatusLine` (a second spawn per tick and it changes the agent panel; separate idea).
2. Skip, don't chain. Before adding the key, check whether any settings layer already defines `statusLine`: the profile's settings.json, `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, and the managed file. This is a key-presence check, not a precedence reimplementation. If one has it, Loom leaves the session alone and the Settings page says "your own status line is kept". Chaining (running the user's command from the wrapper) is phase 2 and only if the user actually runs claude-hud or ccstatusline; it needs the user's command string resolved across layers, which is the drift-prone part.
3. Helper. A `statusline` verb in Sources/loom-hook/main.swift, handled before the OpenSessionCommand dispatch (today any argument means the open command). It reads stdin with a hard cap (16 KiB; the JSON is a few KB), wraps it in an envelope of a new kind with LOOM_SESSION_ID, LOOM_MANAGED_RUN_ID and the token, and sends it over a new third socket n-<8>.sock or a `kind` field on the hook socket. Exit 0 always. It prints nothing, or one fixed short line if the spike shows an empty row is a problem. Without the Loom env it exits silently, so a session started outside Loom is unaffected.
4. Ingest. Do NOT send it through ClaudeHookIngress or ClaudeHookStateTracker. Status must never depend on these numbers (accurate-status principle). Add a small `SessionNumbersStore` in LoomCore, latest-wins per run (no queue). It decodes with a narrow all-optional Decodable (context_window.used_percentage and context_window_size, prompt_cache.warm/expires_at/ttl, pr.number/url/review_state/kind, cost.total_cost_usd, session_id, version) and ignores the rest, the same discipline as SubagentTranscriptParser. It authorises exactly as the hook server does (token + live runContext) and checks that the payload session_id matches the run's conversation.
5. Publish. `SessionViewState` gets `numbers: SessionNumbers?`, cleared by a new run, a detach and the end of the run, exactly like `subagents` (SessionEventHub.swift). To avoid a sidebar redraw per message, the store publishes only when a displayed value changes: context percentage rounded to 5 percent steps, the warm/cold flip, the PR number or state. H1-D2 patching then covers it (one row patch). Rate-limit and cost values are not published per message.
6. Cache-expiry. The CLI itself re-runs the statusLine when prompt_cache.expires_at passes, so "warm until HH:MM" turns into "cold" with no Loom timer; the label reads expires_at at render time (the same minute-tick pattern as CardTimeLabel).
7. Drift. A required-field check (session_id and context_window absent while `version` is present) journals one `cli_compat_warning` per run of the app, in the same style as D-45's hook-silence and unknown-registry reporting. Version-gated fields degrade to absent. Nothing is pinned.
8. Optional resource win. When a fresh `rate_limits` figure has arrived from a live session in the last few minutes, the get_usage headless ask (D-37) can be skipped, which removes a CLI process. get_usage stays the source when no session is live.

Original full version, for comparison: chaining plus subagentStatusLine plus rate_limits plumbing. That is L to XL.

What would make it a principle violation, and how the design avoids it: (a) hiding the CLI's footer hints, or taking over the user's own status line, without a user decision (opt-in, off by default, skip when one exists); (b) a spawn per update becoming a CPU problem (measured about 4 ms, debounced by the CLI, no refreshInterval, and the spike must re-measure a real 30-step turn with 4 sessions); (c) numbers shown as live when stale (cleared at run end, shown only with their source, a 5 percent step, and an "as of" tooltip); (d) a statusline payload moving the Working/Waiting state (separate path, never touches the tracker); (e) a pr.url from CLI JSON opened blindly (open it only on a user click, https only).
feasibility.ui_sketch: No new panel and no change to the two-row card. Detail header: the existing project+branch chip (SessionHeaderChip / ProjectBranchChip, 22 pt, HeaderFlow) can gain a trailing "#142" PR token coloured by review state (approved / pending / changes requested / draft) when pr.number is present. A click opens pr.url in the browser. It is the first thing HeaderFlow drops when narrow, after the branch. Context: a thin ring or bar appears on the detail header (and on the card's second row) only from about 50 percent, amber at 70, red at 85; the tooltip says "Context 73 percent of 1M, from Claude Code; cache warm until 14:32" (or "cache cold: next message re-reads about N tokens" when recache_tokens_if_cold exists). Cards of sessions below 50 percent look exactly as today. Settings: one switch "Live session numbers" under General with a one-line explanation: "Claude Code reports exact context and PR figures to Loom. It hides Claude's own keyboard hints and cannot be used together with your own status line." Idle and stopped records show no numbers (they cost nothing, so nothing runs). A session whose own status line is kept shows no figures and the toggle's help says why.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass with a caveat. About 4 ms CPU per spawn, CLI-debounced, no polling, no work for idle or stopped sessions, one latest-wins record per live run, 16 KiB cap. Risk: it is a per-assistant-message spawn, the per-tool-hook cardinality the hook set deliberately avoided; D-32's wording ("no extra CLI processes") is amended in its spirit, as D-37 did for get_usage, so it needs a decision note. Predictable behaviour: risk until the spike. Footer hints vanish and a row may appear; opt-in with a clear explanation fixes this. Accurate status: pass. A separate path from the hook tracker, numbers labelled as the CLI's own, absent instead of guessed, cleared at run end. Statusline JSON can lag the in-flight response, so say "as of the last message". Fluency: pass. Nothing waits on it; the script never blocks the turn. Modularity: pass for the light version (one verb, one store, one optional field on SessionViewState, one chip). Chaining would not pass: it reimplements settings layering. CLI-update resilience: mostly pass. It is a documented interface with version-gated fields that degrade to absent, plus a drift check. But statusLine is gated by workspace trust, disableAllHooks and allowManagedHooksOnly, and managed settings beat --settings, so absence is normal and must be silent. Ownership: pass. The helper is a child of the CLI inside the Loom run scope; nothing outlives it; the socket is Loom's own. User authority: pass if opt-in; it overrides nothing without consent, and a user's own statusLine is skipped, not replaced (Orca's rule).
feasibility.value_reason: Per-session context % across several live sessions is genuinely valuable for this heavy multi-session, multi-agent user. But Loom can already get an approximate figure from transcripts (the context-meter idea, zero CLI change). Branch is already read from git, effort is already read from the transcript, cost is the same list-price estimate Loom computes, and plan limits already come from get_usage. The unique gains are exact context and window size, cache TTL, and the PR chip. The PR chip only helps if the work repos are on GitHub or GitLab, which I could not confirm from the notes. Against that sit a visible CLI change (hints) and a possible conflict with the user's own status line.

In an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (never the real ~/.claude), start the real claude 2.1.300 with `--settings` carrying a statusLine whose command prints nothing, then one that prints a short line. Check by screenshot whether `esc to interrupt` and `? for shortcuts` still appear, and whether a blank status row takes a line. S2 override and env. With a second statusLine in the isolated user settings, confirm the inline `--settings` one wins (the notes mark this 'not tested in Loom'). Confirm `"$LOOM_CLI" statusline` expands from the hook env (needs LOOM_CLI and the socket variables in the statusLine process) and that a path with a space works. Confirm the trust-dialog gate (blank until accepted) and that `disableAllHooks` silences it. Decides: whether the quoted-env command is viable or the absolute path must be baked in.

S3 cost. Count real statusLine invocations per turn on a 30-step agentic turn with 4 concurrent sessions, and measure CPU of the helper with the same method as cp5-perf-claude-hook.json. Decides: if it is under about 0.2 s CPU per turn, the spawn concern is closed; if the CLI re-runs it far more often than once per assistant message, drop the idea.

S4 payload. Capture one real payload (from the S1 run, into a file in the isolated dir) and diff it against the documented fields: used_percentage, context_window_size, prompt_cache.ttl, pr.* on a repo with an open PR. Also compare used_percentage to /context to settle whether the transcript meter (I-23) is already close enough. Decides: whether this idea adds anything beyond PR state and cache TTL.

Are your work repos on GitHub or GitLab (so pr.* is ever present)? If they are on Bitbucket or something else, the PR chip has no value and the idea shrinks to context % plus cache, which the transcript meter mostly covers.
