feasibility.one_line: Adopt the pure-function core (plan pace on the existing chip, a stale/unknown marker, an honest "usage limit reached" state) as an S job; drop Loom's own "Continue at reset" because Claude Code 2.1.234+ already waits and continues by itself, and make the cache-cold hint a separate spike because the transcript can probably give the TTL tier but nobody has checked.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS READ
- Plan limits already exist end to end. `ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher` (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudePlanLimits.swift) runs a ~1 s headless `claude -p` with one `get_usage` control request and returns `PlanLimits{fiveHour, weekly: PlanLimitWindow{usedPercent:Int, resetsAt}, fetchedAt}`. `PlanLimitWindow.isCurrent(at:)` and `PlanLimits.current(at:)` already drop a window once `now` passes `resetsAt`. `interpret` already rejects non-finite values and clamps to 0...100. So half of the provenance idea (b) is already done.
- `UsageModel` (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/UsageModel.swift) is event-driven. `fetchLimitsIfDue` asks only while a Loom window or the Usage page is visible, never two at once, with a minimum age (`PlanLimitsCadence`: 300 s after the window is shown, 120 s after a turn ends, 10 s after the page opens). It has no timer. `minuteTick()` (called from CatalogModel.swift:1057 while the window is active) only calls `rebuildChip()`. `rebuildChip()` publishes a new `UsageChipContent` only when it differs, so the footer redraws only when the text changes.
- On a failed ask the chip keeps the last answer. `limitsFailure` only feeds the Usage page card ("not refreshed"). The footer percent therefore carries no age marker.
- The hook layer already receives what (d) needs. `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings` registers Notification and StopFailure. `ClaudeHookEvent.Kind` has `.notification(type:)` and `.stopFailure(error:details:)`. `notificationActivity` treats `quota_auto_resume_*` as informational, so the state is kept. A rate-limit turn end becomes `AgentActivity.failed("rate_limit")`, shown as red "Failed" (SessionIndicator.failed, ProjectAttention.failure, menu bar failure dot). ClaudeHookTests.swift:363 already has a `rate_limit` / 429 fixture.
- The transcript parser already reads the cache TTL tier. ClaudeUsageParser's `Usage.CacheCreation` decodes `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`, and the index `msg` table keeps `cw5`, `cw1`, `cr`, `input`, `ts_ms`, `session` and a sidechain flag. Indexes exist on `msg_session` and `msg_ts`. The research's "TTL tier unverified for transcripts" is probably answerable from data Loom already stores.

DOCS I FETCHED, which the research note does not cover
- Interactive-mode docs, "Wait for a usage limit to reset": from v2.1.234, in an interactive session signed in with a claude.ai subscription, automatic continue is ON BY DEFAULT. When a usage limit stops a turn, the open session shows "Continuing automatically at 3:45pm · esc to cancel" and continues at the reset by itself.
- The CLI does not start that wait for Remote Control / teammate sessions, or when the reset is more than 24 h away. For those, the user can pick "Wait here, then continue automatically" from `/rate-limit-options`.
- Exiting Claude, `/resume`, `/clear` or `/login` ends the wait, and it does not restart on resume.
- The continuation passes through `UserPromptSubmit` (a blocking hook ends the wait). Esc / Ctrl+C cancels it, and that cancel fires no hook (`quota_auto_resume_disabled` explicitly does not fire on Esc).
- Hooks docs: `idle_prompt` is not sent while the CLI waits for a limit reset. After a sleep of more than about 30 min across the reset, the CLI sends `quota_auto_resume_stale` and waits for Enter.
- Statusline and costs docs: `prompt_cache.ttl` ("5m" or "1h") is computed by the CLI "from the cache token counts in the API's responses". `/usage` already prints `warm (1h TTL, last activity 40s ago)`. A subscription session normally gets the 1 h tier, so a flat 5-minute "probably cold" would be wrong most of the time for this user.
- The v2.1.299 idle compaction (research note, confirmed by its fact-check): a conversation over about 200k tokens that has been idle about 54 min is compacted just before the 1 h cache expires, unless `idleCompaction` is false. A "re-reads ~N tokens" figure is therefore false for those sessions.

DESIGN, by part

(a) Pace. Add `PlanPace` in LoomCore next to ClaudePlanLimits.swift: a pure function `PlanPace.evaluate(window, kind, fetchedAt)` returning nil or `{projectedPercent, exhaustsAt}`.
- Compute it AT `fetchedAt`, not at `now`, because the utilization was only true then. elapsed = windowLength − (resetsAt − fetchedAt), with fixed lengths 5 h and 7 d.
- Unknown (nil) if resetsAt is missing, elapsed ≤ 0 or elapsed > windowLength.
- Show only when used ≥ 10 %, elapsed ≥ ~30 min for the 5 h window, projected ≥ 90 % and exhaustsAt < resetsAt. The research's 10 % floor alone gives false alarms at the start of a window, for example 10 % after 15 min.
- 5-hour only. A linear weekly projection will cry wolf for a user who does not work seven even days. The weekly bar needs no new rule: `bottleneck` already shows the lowest remaining percent, and the weekly window appears when it is the bottleneck.
- Plug into `UsageChipContent.make` by adding `Limit.pace`. It turns the percent and meter amber, the same attention tone as `isLow`, and the tooltip gets one line: "At this pace the 5-hour limit runs out about 14:20; it resets 15:45 (as of 14:02)".
- Use absolute clock times, not "in 1h 40m". A relative ETA would change the tooltip every minute and make `minuteTick` → `rebuildChip` redraw the footer every minute. The existing equality gating exists to avoid exactly that.
- Triggers are the ones that exist: a successful `fetchLimitsIfDue` and `minuteTick`. Add no fetch and no timer.
- Round-trip `utilization` as a Double inside PlanLimitWindow. The current Int rounding makes the early-window projection jumpy (12 % vs 13 % moves the projection by about 8 %).

(a2) Notification. The research proposes a one-shot macOS notification per window. Under the current cadence it is almost worthless: asks happen only while a Loom window is visible, which is when the user already sees the chip. Making it useful means an ask on turn end while hidden, which is a policy change to D-37 ("a few asks per hour while a window is visible").
- Defer it. If wanted, bound it: ask on turn end while hidden only when the last known utilization is ≥ 50 %, at most once per 120 s.
- `NotificationService.post(id: UUID, …)` and `onActivate: (UUID)` are session-keyed, so a usage notice needs a small protocol addition plus its own Settings switch (default off) beside the existing "Notify when a session needs approval".

(b) Provenance. Replace "nothing" with a three-case enum computed from existing data, shown as one dim glyph plus tooltip text, no extra chrome.
- limit % = official (CLI `get_usage`), with "as of HH:MM".
- Same % when `now − fetchedAt` > ~15 min, or `limitsFailure != nil` and the answer predates it = stale: the glyph "~" and "couldn't refresh since 14:02".
- Tokens today = estimate, from local transcripts. The tooltip already says "approximate" on the Usage page; say it on the chip too.
- The window past `resetsAt` already drops to nothing, so no new "unknown" case is needed there.
- Change the clamp for absurd values: today `utilization` > 100 or negative is clamped, so an epoch-sized garbage value shows "0 % remaining". Reject (treat the window as unavailable) beyond a sane bound such as > 150 or < 0, and keep clamping 100–150.
- Tests: extend ClaudePlanLimitsTests.swift and the UsageChipContent tests with an injected `now`.

(c) Cache-cold hint. This part needs a spike (see experiments).
- Add one method to `UsageIndexing`: `lastMainTurn(sessionID:) -> {timestamp, contextTokens = input+cw5+cw1+cr, lastWriteTier}?`.
  - It is one indexed query: `msg WHERE session=? AND sidechain=0 ORDER BY ts_ms DESC`, plus the latest row with cw5+cw1>0 to get the tier (cw1>0 means 1 h, cw5 only means 5 m).
  - It lives in ClaudeUsageIndex.swift. The fake in UsageModel's protocol extension needs a default (nil), like `diagnostics()`.
- Call it only when the user selects a session that is idle, stopped or Ready (CatalogModel selection event), once per selection. No scan and no background work. Nothing for sessions the user is not looking at.
- Pure `CacheHint.make(turn, now, idleCompactionPossible)` renders only when cold. It stays silent when the tier is unknown, when context > 200k and idle > 54 min (say "may have been compacted" or nothing), and when there is no usage row.
- The TTL constants live in one place. The 1 h / 5 m split comes from the data, not a constant.
- Where it shows:
  - The text of `EndedScreenNotice` (DetailView.swift:294) for a stopped session, the main "resume an idle session" case: "This session is not running. Resume re-reads about 143k tokens (cache expired 3 h ago)". Resume stays a plain button. Nothing changes what Enter or Return does.
  - A slim notice like `SessionIssueNotice` for a live session that sits at its prompt past the TTL.
- Wording "probably cold" only when the tier is unknown. Prefer saying nothing.

(d) Limit state and actions.
- Do NOT build Loom's own timer + resume + continue prompt.
  - The CLI already does it for the 5-hour window in every Loom PTY session, because Loom starts interactive subscription sessions and D-38 never stops them. A second continuation from Loom would be a double execution, which contract §7 forbids ("no blind retry, no double execution").
  - The weekly case (reset > 24 h) and stopped sessions are the only gaps. In both, Loom must be running at reset time anyway (Quit stops everything), so the user can pick "Wait here, then continue automatically" in the terminal themselves.
  - Loom's timer would also need `--resume <id> -- <prompt>`, which `ProviderLaunchProfile` currently refuses (opening only for `.new`), plus a hook-verified UserPromptSubmit. That is a real feature for a rare path.
- DO fix the status. Today a session waiting for a reset shows red "Failed" with the project dot and menu bar failure dot, and when the CLI continues it silently flips to Working.
  - Map `.failed("rate_limit")` in `SessionIndicator.init` (SessionDisplay.swift:56) to a distinct, non-failure indicator. Working name: `.limitReached`; label "Limit reached"; attention or neutral tone, not failure red.
  - The state pill tooltip shows the reset time from `UsageModel.limits` (five_hour `resetsAt`) with hedged wording: "Claude continues on its own after the reset unless it was cancelled". The wording must be hedged, because Esc-cancel fires no hook and Loom cannot know.
  - The informational `quota_auto_resume_fired/stale/disabled` Notification types can refine the tooltip: `stale` means "press Enter in the terminal", `disabled` means "will not continue".
  - Because `UserPromptSubmit` carries the continuation, the existing state tracker returns to Working correctly with no change.
  - This is a user-visible state change: needs the user's OK (see decisions). It also touches ProjectAttention and the menu bar, so it must stay within SessionIndicator's one derivation point so cards, dots and tabs agree.
- "Snooze until reset" stays with I-18.

BOUNDS AND TRIGGERS
- No new process, no timer, no polling, no new file format.
- (a) and (b) are O(1) per fetch result.
- (c) is one indexed SQLite read per selection.
- (d) is a switch on an existing string.
- CLI drift: all inputs are documented (`get_usage` is undocumented in public SDK docs but is already in use since D-37; hook types are documented). A missing field degrades to "no pace / no hint", never to a wrong claim.

COST (honest)
- (a) + (b) + (d) status-only: S, about 1 to 1.5 days including tests and the two real-session checks.
- (c): M. It needs the index method and the fake, selection plumbing, two views, the idle-compaction caveat and fixtures, and it should not start before the spike.
- The Loom-side Continue-at-reset in the original idea would be M to L and is not worth it.
- The bundle as written (S) is understated; the recommended light version is S.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
- Footer chip, same single-line 38 pt bar. It reads "1.2M today · 5h 38%" today. With a bad pace the "5h 38%" part and its meter turn attention-orange (the colour `isLow` already uses under 20 % remaining). Nothing else is added to the line.
- Tooltip, only when the pace is bad: "At this pace the 5-hour limit runs out about 14:20; it resets 15:45 (as of 14:02)."
- A stale answer gets a "~" before the percent and a tooltip line "couldn't refresh since 14:02".
- Weekly appears only as the bottleneck, as now.
- Session card and detail pill: a session whose last turn ended on a rate limit reads "Limit reached" (attention tone) instead of red "Failed". The pill tooltip says when the limit resets and that Claude continues by itself unless cancelled.
- Stopped session, `EndedScreenNotice`: one extra clause on the existing text line, "Resume re-reads about 143k tokens (cache expired 3 h ago)", shown only when cold and only when the tier is known. A live idle session past its TTL gets the same sentence in a slim notice styled like `SessionIssueNotice`. No new button; no change to Enter or Return; no compact action.
feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: pass. Pure functions of data already held. No new process, timer or poll. The hint costs one indexed read on selection. Risk: absolute clock times are needed so the tooltip does not change every minute and force a footer redraw on `minuteTick`.
- Predictability: pass. Thresholds are fixed constants. The pace is explicitly "at this pace". The hint never changes Enter and has no compact-on-Enter default (the T3 #17467 regression is avoided).
- Accurate status: the whole point of (b) and (d). The risk is claiming too much.
  - Esc-cancelled auto-continue is invisible to hooks, so "continues at X" must be hedged.
  - A cache hint with a guessed TTL or on a session that was idle-compacted is a false claim, so it stays silent when unsure.
  - Linear pace is a model, not a fact.
- Fluency: pass. No new confirmations or waits. Information appears only when it matters (pace ≥ threshold, cache cold).
- Modularity: pass. `PlanPace` and `CacheHint` are pure types in LoomCore with injected clocks. The UI reads view-model data only. The one cross-layer change is the `UsageIndexing` method.
- CLI-update resilience: mostly pass. Hook notification types and `/usage` fields are documented. `get_usage` is undocumented but already used. Transcript usage fields are not a contract: the cache hint must degrade to silence when `cache_creation` is missing. Never pin; nothing here needs a version gate beyond the existing capability probing.
- Ownership: pass. Loom's own timer is the thing that would have blurred ownership (two continuers on one session). Dropping it keeps the CLI as the sole actor on a Loom-owned PTY.
- User authority: pass for (a)–(c). (d) status mapping changes how a failure looks (a user decision). Any future automatic continue must be per-session opt-in and must not coexist with the CLI's own auto-continue.
- Constraints touched: D-32/D-37 (no polling beyond the visible-window cadence) is kept by adding no ask. The contract's "terminal is the real CLI" is untouched (no composer). D-20 (changing CLI behaviour is a user decision) is respected by not setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`. D-34 is unaffected.
- Violations to avoid:
  - a hidden-window fetch for notifications beyond the bounded rule above;
  - a ticking relative ETA in the chip text;
  - sending a prompt from Loom while the CLI's wait is still armed;
  - writing the user's settings.json to turn the CLI setting on or off.
feasibility.value_reason: This user runs several sessions plus subagent workflows and reaches the 5-hour window sooner than a single-session user, so "do I slow down?" is a daily decision and the chip already carries the data. The honest limit state also removes a misleading red "Failed" on a session that is just waiting for a reset. The cache-cold hint is a nice-to-have decision aid for resuming large sessions, not essential. The original Continue-at-reset adds little, because Claude Code does it by itself.
depends_on: I-24 (statusline bridge) is optional, only if exact TTL, context size or live rate_limits are wanted later; not needed for the light version

feasibility.loom_design:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (observed, not assumed): ClaudeUsageIndex (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeUsageIndex.swift) is already a durable, content-free, per-message SQLite ledger (usage-index.sqlite3 in the data root, table msg: key, file_id, ts_ms, session, model, input/output/cw5/cw1/cr/web, flags, total, cost; index msg_session). Its header says "Rows are history: a transcript Claude deletes later never lowers totals" and test aVanishedFileNeverReducesTotals pins it, so the idea's "numbers-only daily rollup file that survives transcript cleanup" already exists at message granularity and must NOT be built a second time. Dedupe is already by message.id alone (key "m|<id>", fallback request+session+timestamp), keeping the non-sidechain row, then the larger total; fixtures exist for cross-file duplicates, sidechain replays (sidechainFilesCountAndReplaysDoNotDoubleCount, sidechainReplayAfterTheParentIsDropped) and resume. flags bit 0 already stores isSidechain (ClaudeUsageParser reads it). Subagent file lines carry sessionId = parent (plans/experiments/run1-planning-scans/U-usage-data.md line 40), UsageTranscriptWalker.session() maps subagents/ files to the parent session, and resume appends to the same file. Delete rule is already decided in code: ConversationForgetters -> ClaudeUsageIndex.forget(sessionIDs:) keeps tokens in the totals and only nulls msg.session, removes file/symbol rows and keeps a SHA-256 digest (tests forgetKeepsTokensAndDropsTheSessionLink, aForgottenSessionLeavesNoIdBytesInTheIndexFiles). So the idea's open delete question is "extend the existing rule", not "invent one".

SMALLEST DESIGN (3 parts, no schema change, no new watcher, no new process):
1. LoomCore, ClaudeUsageIndex: one new read, e.g. sessionTotals(range:) = SELECT session, flags & 1, model, SUM(...) FROM msg WHERE ts_ms in range GROUP BY 1,2,3 (join symbol for the session text), plus a per-session variant using the existing msg_session index. Prices applied at query time exactly like snapshotOnce (UsagePricing, Self.cost) so cost stays an "API-equivalent estimate" and unknown models stay "-". Rows with session NULL (deleted via forget) or unmatched become explicit buckets. Add the method to the UsageIndexing protocol with a default for test fakes, as the file already does for summary/buckets.
2. LoomCatalogUI: a pure grouping function (new file, e.g. UsageRollup.swift) takes the index rows plus a snapshot of catalog facts [providerConversationID -> projectID, ticketKey/title] and returns buckets: by project (Loom CatalogProject id, name, tone), by source (main thread vs subagents, from the sidechain flag), by ticket (ticket_key, else the leading key of the title using the same fold/prefix rule as SessionCatalog.session(projectID:ticket:) in SessionCatalog+Sessions.swift; no new Jira concept). Buckets: "Outside Loom" (sessions the catalog does not know, e.g. plain CLI use) and "Deleted sessions" (session link cut by forget) and "Unattributed" (no sessionId or no sidechain marker); invariant tested: sum of buckets == snapshot total for the same range. The catalog facts come through an injected closure (SessionCatalog.sessions() is public) so UsageModel does not import the catalog.
3. Events: reuse UsageModel's existing gating. The rollup is computed only inside loadAfterScan/buildReport when usagePageVisible (UsageModel.swift), never for the footer chip, and recomputed only by the events that already rebuild the report (launch scan, watcher change, Settings opening, period switch, manual refresh). The record view (ConversationDetail in DetailView.swift, the Facts grid) gets one Fact "Usage" ("2.1M tokens, 31% in subagents, about $3.20 estimated"), fetched once when an idle/ended session record is selected (single indexed query on msg_session, same discipline as Codex's selected-row-only usage in agents_overview_usage.rs); live terminal sessions show nothing new.
Bounds: every query is limited to a UsageRange (24 h to 90 d, already offered), runs on the index's utility serial queue, returns at most (sessions x models x 2) rows, and nothing runs while the Settings window or main window is hidden.

WHAT TO CUT OR DEFER: (a) no separate daily rollup file (duplicates msg); (b) no "unusually large share" alert: thresholds are arbitrary and tokens overstate cost because cache reads dominate (the research fact-check on the Guardian numbers: 81-96% cached), so show plain shares ranked by estimated cost with tokens beside, like the existing By model card; (c) the side-chat and scheduled-run sources do not exist yet: add them later from Loom's own catalog relation (a child/parent link on the session row), not by guessing from transcript files; (d) per-subagent rows belong to the subagent tree idea, not here; (e) persisting a project key on each message (additive nullable column, version stays 2 so the index is not discarded; a schema bump would DELETE history that can no longer be rebuilt, see openDatabase -> removeDatabaseFiles on schema mismatch) only if the user wants deleted sessions to stay in project totals.

TICKET CAVEAT (observed): a ticket is known only for sessions opened through loom:open-session (sessions.ticket_key) or whose title starts with the key (Claude titles a session after its first prompt). Sessions the user types by hand without the key at the start of the title fall under "No ticket". The card must say "tickets found from titles" rather than imply completeness.

"By project": one row per Loom project with its colour stripe, plus "Outside Loom" and "Deleted sessions" rows; meta text "N sessions". "By source": two or three rows, "Main thread", "Subagents", "Unattributed" (hidden when 0). feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS FROM THE CODE. (1) The launch env is already per launch: ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(...) sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = config.path (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:146), and SessionRuntime.claudeProfile (SessionRuntime+Claude.swift:~90-115) pins it only when toolchain.profileDirectory != nil (acceptance runs); otherwise it passes the login shell's value and never pins ~/.claude. launchClaude builds the ClaudeRegistryReader from profile.environment, so the registry follows a per-launch dir for free. (2) Loom's hooks, socket env and skill reach the CLI by flags and env (--settings with hooks, --plugin-dir from ClaudeLoomPlugin, LOOM_HOOK_*/LOOM_CLI), written into Loom's data folder, so NOTHING Loom-owned has to be installed into a second config dir. This contradicts the idea's "separate plugin/skill set and separate supervisor instance": one ProcessSupervisor and one run scope can launch with any env. What does differ per dir is the USER's own CLAUDE.md, agents, skills, settings, MCP and plugins (this user's heavy setup lives in ~/.claude), so a fresh second dir starts bare; Loom must not manage that (user symlinks or copies it).
WHAT IS SINGLE-PROFILE TODAY AND MUST BECOME PER-SESSION (this is the real cost): (a) the catalog has no profile per session: sessions has no config column (only deletions.config_dir, CatalogDatabase.swift:190) and SessionCatalog.schemaVersion = 3; resume (resumeConversation, SessionRuntime.swift:446) must launch with the dir the conversation was created under or the CLI says "No conversation found". Needs schema 4: sessions.profile_id (nullable = default) and projects.profile_id, plus a small accounts list in app_state or a new table (label, absolute dir). (b) SystemProviderToolchains caches one ProviderToolchain per provider with one profileDirectory (ProviderToolchain.swift); key the cache by (provider, profile) or, lighter, keep the one toolchain and apply the profile at claudeProfile() time (capabilities come from --help, which does not depend on the dir). (c) claudeConfigDirectory() (SessionRuntime.swift:631) feeds deletion (ConversationDeletion.swift:199), claudeProjectsDirectory() for the subagent panel (ConversationController.swift:358) and ClaudeTranscriptEffort at resume; all must take the session's profile. Deletion is the accuracy trap: deleting a profile-B conversation by scanning the default dir would report success while the files remain. Rule: the deletion candidate resolves the dir from the stored session profile, and refuses (deletionRefused) if the profile is unknown or its folder missing. (d) The usage index and watcher are one-profile by construction (ClaudeUsageIndex(profile:), UsageTranscriptWatcher on one projects dir, AppDelegate+Usage.swift; STAGE-U already notes "index is not partitioned per profile"). Light version: leave tokens-today for the default profile only (label it), do not build a second index/FSEvents stream. (e) ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher is already parameterised by ClaudeProfileLayout (init takes profile; environment() pins non-default dirs), so a second fetcher per account is a few lines; its 2-minute / window-visible / never-two-at-once gating lives in UsageModel and would need to loop over accounts.
LIGHTEST VERSION (adopt-light shape, if/when wanted): 1. Accounts: label + absolute CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, stored in Loom's catalog app_state; added/removed in Settings (new "Accounts" block on General or a small section on Usage). Default = "the CLI's own default" (today's behaviour, no pinning). 2. Binding is per project, not a per-launch picker: projects.profile_id. A project (e.g. an EDDP work project) always starts on its account, so Cmd+N and the menu bar "New Claude Session" stay one action (fluency); sessions copy the project's profile into sessions.profile_id at creation and keep it forever (resume, delete, subagent reads, "a session opens a session" inherit the parent's profile via OpenSessionCoordinator). Projectless sessions use the default. A secondary "New Session on <account>" appears only in the right-click/context menu. 3. Switching an account on a project affects only new sessions; existing stopped sessions resume on their stored profile; no "restart on account B when idle" in v1 (cross-account resume needs Orca's symlinked history dirs, claude-profile-history.ts: internal layout, breaks "never pin the CLI"). 4. Meters: per account, get_usage via ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher(profile:), asked only on events already used: first window shows, Usage page opens, the new-session menu/popover opening, a window showing again after 5 min; at most one process at a time, ~1 s each, never with no window visible, result cached with fetchedAt. Plans without limits (API-key / Console login, `rate_limits_available == false`) render "limits unknown", never a number. 5. Login state: do not read credentials. The documented `claude auth status --json` (exists in 2.1.300) can say loggedIn once when an account is added or when a launch fails; an account that is not logged in just shows the CLI's own sign-in prompt in the terminal (a new dir also triggers onboarding screens). 6. Drift: nothing here reads the dir layout beyond what Loom already reads (projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl for usage/effort/subagents, which ClaudeProfileLayout already encodes); CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR itself is a documented env var (code.claude.com env-vars page). Bounds: accounts list capped (say 4), one fetch at a time, no timers, no extra watcher, no extra index.
WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO VIOLATE PRINCIPLES AND HOW THE DESIGN AVOIDS IT: polling quotas on a timer (Orca's 15-min OAuth poll that 429s) -> event-gated ask only; reading the Keychain OAuth token or calling /api/oauth/usage -> never, only the CLI's own get_usage (the legal page forbids third parties collecting/storing/intermediating claude.ai credentials); one usage index per profile with its own FSEvents stream -> not built; symlinking history dirs -> not done; false "deleted" or "resumed" on the wrong dir -> profile stored per session and verified before delete/resume; cross-session authority -> the open-session channel inherits the parent's account and still needs user approval, and an agent can never choose another account.
REESTIMATE: the idea says M. For this codebase the env-at-launch part is S; the correct per-session profile plumbing (schema 4 migration + backup/downgrade guard, resume, deletion, subagent panel, effort lookup, open-request inheritance, accounts model, Settings UI, card badge, header chip, per-account meters, failing-first tests with isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR fixtures; the fake provider already honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) is M-L. Light version above: M. Full version with a per-profile usage index and cross-account resume: XL and not recommended.

Project right-click (and the project colour menu neighbourhood) gets "Account: Default / Work" as a single choice. Cards and the detail header chip show the account label only when the user has more than one account (a quiet secondary-text suffix after the branch, so a single-account user sees no change). The footer chip stays as is (default account, bottleneck window); its popover or the Usage page's Plan limits card gains one extra row per account ("Work  5h 38% left, resets 16:40  Wk 71% left") using existing PlanLimitWindow formatting, and an account whose plan exposes no limits reads "limits unknown". feasibility.one_line: Build the cheap half now (an owned, bounded `git` read that gives a '+N -M, K files' chip on the card and header plus Copy patch / Open in editor), and keep the full in-app Changes pane behind an experiment, because Claude's own /diff already overlaps it and the chip is where Loom's unique triage value is.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACT BASE (read in the tree)
- Loom spawns no git per card today: `GitBranch.read` is pure file reads, run through `BranchCache` (actor, injectable `Reader`), refreshed on a `turnComplete` frame and on window activation (`CatalogModel.apply` ~l.1360, `setWindowActive` ~l.1026). Only the cleanup review runs git, through `CleanupWorktreeProtection.live` -> `ProcessSupervisor.captureHelper("/usr/bin/git", ..., GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0)`.
- `captureHelper` is the wrong runner for a per-turn read. `runOwnedJob(scope: .perCall)` opens a whole run scope (LaunchServices `open -n LoomRunHost.app`, coalition, handshake) for every call, polls every 20 ms, and throws (not truncates) over 4 MiB (`LaunchEnvironment.capture`). Right precedent: `ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher`'s `LimitsExchange` (plain `Process`, `CancelFlag`, 4 MiB cap, SIGTERM then SIGKILL by pid).
- `ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings` registers no per-tool hooks on purpose ('each hook spawns a helper'). The idea's 'files-changed from PostToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit' therefore contradicts a standing Loom choice. Do not add PostToolUse.
- The hook payload already carries `cwd` and `transcript_path` (`ClaudeHookEvent.workingDirectory/transcriptPath`, ClaudeHook.swift ~l.442). The detail pane already has an 'in place of the terminal' pattern (`viewedSubagent`, `SubagentTranscriptView`, `SessionBackControl`, D-54 P1) that leaves the PTY running and un-resized.

DESIGN (two phases)

Phase 1 (adopt, M): the chip and the exports.
1. New `LoomCore/GitChanges` (no UI): `GitRunner` (plain `Process`, absolute git path, env `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 LC_ALL=C`, args `--no-optional-locks -c core.quotepath=false -c core.fsmonitor=false`, 5 s timeout, 1 MiB stdout cap that truncates and flags, cancel flag checked in a poll(2) loop, killed on Quit via the runtime shutdown path). Probes, all `-z` plumbing, so no patch-header parsing (this avoids Paseo's quoting/rename bug class): `diff --numstat -z --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --ignore-submodules=all -M HEAD` (tracked, vs HEAD; unborn HEAD falls back to `--cached`), `status --porcelain=v2 -z -unormal --branch --ignore-submodules=all` (never -uall, Superset #6004). Untracked files are counted as 'new' entries without line counts in the chip (cheap, honest); line counts for untracked are read in-process only when the pane opens, capped (<=200 files, <=256 KiB each, NUL sniff = binary).
2. `ChangesStat { added, deleted, files, newFiles, truncated, computedAt, headShort }` or `.unknown` (timeout, not a repo, error). A timeout or failure is shown as no chip or a dim em dash, never as 0 (accurate-status rule).
3. `CatalogModel+Changes` (same shape as `BranchCache`/`refreshBranches`): a `ChangesCache` actor keyed by working directory with in-flight de-duplication and a 1 s minimum gap per folder; an injectable reader for tests. Triggers, all existing events: (a) `turnComplete` frame for that session, (b) selecting a session or opening the pane, (c) window activation for the selected session's folder only. No timer, no FSEvents in phase 1. While the window is hidden, events only mark folders dirty (same collect-while-hidden pattern as `UsageModel`); the next activation reads the selected/visible one. Launch runs no git. `retain()` drops folders no card shows.
4. UI hooks: a `changes` value on `SessionRowModel` (not a shared dict read by every card, which would re-evaluate all cards; the card hot path has render-probe tests, `SidebarRenderTests`). Card: a small secondary '+120 -8' after the branch label in the existing meta row (`SessionCardView`, SidebarView.swift ~l.462-480), shown only when a stat exists and the session is not Working. Header: a `changes` slot in `HeaderFlow` that drops before the branch (`HeaderFlowPlan`). Menu (`SessionLocationMenuItems`, SessionMenuItems.swift l.26): 'Copy Patch' (runs `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv HEAD`, capped, to the pasteboard) and 'Open Changed File...' / 'Open in Editor' (needs the editor decision below).
5. Attribution caveat is part of the design: the number is the FOLDER's uncommitted state, not 'what this session changed'. Two sessions in one folder show the same chip. The tooltip says 'Uncommitted changes in <folder>, as of 14:32', and it is shown for sessions with a live run (a stopped session's folder moves without it).

Phase 2 (spike-first, L): the Changes view.
- In-place swap like the subagent panel (`viewedChanges` next to `viewedSubagent` in `DetailContent`; Esc and the Session control go back). No split, so no PTY resize and no collision with D-34 (right sidebar deferred); the view model is placement-agnostic so it can become a tab of a later right panel.
- Scopes v1: Unstaged, Staged, Branch vs base (merge-base with `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, else hidden). Skip 'Last turn' in v1 (see below).
- File list from the -z plumbing above; per-file body fetched lazily on expand: `git --literal-pathspecs diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U3 <base> -- <path>` (for a rename pass both paths). The body is treated as opaque text and classified by first character, so no `diff --git` header parsing. Caps: 1,000 files listed, 5,000 lines and 256 KiB per file body, 5,000 chars per line (Warp's limits are 4.375 MB / 5,000 / 10,000); binary (`-\t-`) shown as one row; lockfiles, `*.min.*`, `vendor/` collapsed by default.
- Rendering: a read-only `NSTextView` with an attributed string like `EndedScreenView` (selection, copy and find free, no timer), one text view per expanded file section or one capped document. No syntax highlighting (a dependency); line washes only.
- Live while Working: no. The view says 'as of 14:32; refreshes when the turn ends' with a Refresh button. Optional later (separate spike): an FSEvents stream on `.git/{HEAD,index,refs}` only while the view is visible, 300 ms+ debounce, mirroring `UsageTranscriptWatcher`; a worktree-wide stream only if measured cheap on a node_modules/target-heavy repo.
- Snapshot lifetime: only the viewed session's snapshot is held; dropped on leave (cancel in-flight job, free text). Nothing cached for idle records.

'LAST TURN' WITHOUT POSTTOOLUSE (deferred, three options, none for v1)
(a) per-file numstat delta between a baseline taken at UserPromptSubmit and one at Stop (in memory, no repo writes, file-level only); (b) T3/Conductor private git refs via temp index + write-tree + commit-tree + update-ref (writes objects/refs into the user's repo, sparse-checkout and racy-index handling; reject for now); (c) the Edit/Write tool_use entries from the main transcript tail (Loom has `SubagentTranscriptTail`/`Parser`), but the research fact-check says `transcript_path` can lag the hook, and Bash edits are missed (same gap as Claude's own T1/T2, which come from Claude's file checkpoints, not git).

WHAT WOULD BE A PRINCIPLE VIOLATION, AND THE GUARD
- A watcher or timer per session/worktree (Superset #6729/#8108, Emdash 250 ms scan): none in phase 1; phase 2 watch only when visible.
- `git status -uall` or an unbounded diff: forbidden; `-unormal`, caps, 5 s timeout.
- A git process per card on a list reload: git runs only on a turn-complete event or on selection, for one folder, de-duplicated.
- Work while hidden: marked dirty only.
- A git call through `captureHelper` per refresh (a run scope each time): use the plain owned runner.
- Writing into the user's repo (index refresh, refs): `--no-optional-locks`, no snapshots, read-only.
- Scope creep to stage/revert/commit/PR/line-comments-to-PTY: out. Those are separate ideas and carry authority/delivery questions.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Card (activity and project view): meta row reads `branch-icon main  +120 -8` (secondary text, caption size, monochrome, no new colour), only for a live, not-Working session with a known stat; tooltip 'Uncommitted changes in <folder>, 5 files, 2 new, as of 14:32'. Detail header: a clickable chip `+120 -8 · 5` before the rule; it is the first thing to drop when the header is narrow. Header actions menu gains 'Show Changes', 'Copy Patch', 'Open in Editor'. Phase 2: choosing Show Changes replaces the terminal area (terminal keeps running underneath, no resize); header becomes `Session > Changes` with a segmented scope control (Unstaged | Staged | vs main), a file list on top or left with per-file `+a -d`, expandable unified diff below in the terminal font on the panel colour, add/remove lines marked by a sign column and a very light wash. Esc or the Session control returns. The wash tones are a new colour class and need the user's acceptance (DESIGN §6 allows only one accent, three status hues, one project class).
feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS for phase 1 (event-driven, one short git per finished turn or selection, de-duplicated, deferred while hidden, no timer, nothing held for idle records). RISK for phase 2 (rendering large diffs; must keep the caps and per-file lazy bodies; T3 shows the failure mode: 228% CPU / 10 GB GPU with a closed preview panel). Must pass the 'nothing drawn or watched when hidden' check and be measured on the user's two real work repos.
- Predictability: PASS if the chip always says 'folder, as of <time>'. RISK: a folder shared by two sessions shows the same number on both cards.
- Accurate status: RISK, handled by design: stale chip (no watcher), timeout or truncation must show unknown / '2,000+' and never 0; untracked files need an explicit 'new' count or the chip understates agent work; a stopped session's chip must not claim the session did it.
- Fluency: PASS. No confirmation, no waiting; the chip is the triage cue; Esc returns.
- Modularity: PASS. GitChanges in LoomCore (no UI, injectable runner like `BranchCache`/`CleanupWorktreeProtection.Capture`), CatalogModel+Changes, a view; dependency direction unchanged. Placement-agnostic so a later right panel can host it.
- CLI-update resilience: STRONG. Git plumbing does not depend on the Claude version. The in-terminal /diff mod, PostToolUse payloads and mods API all do; avoiding them is the resilient choice.
- Process ownership: PASS with one required item: the git child must be cancellable and killed on Quit (CancelFlag + shutdown hook, as the plan-limits fetch). Note `core.fsmonitor`, `diff.external`, textconv in a repo config can run programs; pass `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv -c core.fsmonitor=false`, and measure the fsmonitor trade-off on the big repos.
- User authority: PASS. Read-only; Copy Patch and Open in Editor are user clicks; nothing is sent to a session or the PTY. (Line comments back to the agent would be a different, authority-carrying feature.)
- Contract: no conflict. Terminal stays the real CLI; D-34 not touched (in-place view, not a right sidebar).
feasibility.value_reason: The research calls it the field's most-proposed capability, but this user's own long-standing wishes (side chat, right panel, usage, deletion, idle cost) do not include a diff viewer, they review in an IDE and GitLab MRs, and Anthropic ships a /diff pane plus a Desktop diff view; the power-user note argues review capacity, not tooling, is the bottleneck. The part with real, unique value for several concurrent sessions is the cross-session triage cue ('+N -M in K files' on the card of a finished session) and one-click Copy patch / open in editor, both cheap. The full pane is worth about 2, so the blend is 3. Honest cost: chip + exports M (runner, parsers with temp-repo tests for rename, quoting, binary, unborn HEAD, worktree, submodule; cache and triggers; card/header wiring with render-probe tests; DESIGN and UI-MAP updates); read-only pane L; adding a live watcher or per-turn snapshots makes it XL.
depends_on: No hard dependency. Soft: the user's answer on worktrees vs shared folders (decides whether a folder-level chip is misleading).
An owned plain-Process git runner is new shared plumbing; it could also replace the per-call run scope that the cleanup worktree check pays today.
If the user later wants line comments sent back to the agent: the 'send primitive' / verified prompt delivery ideas (a separate idea with its own authority questions).
If a right panel is built (D-34 later), Changes should become a tab of it; the view model is written placement-agnostic for that.
experiments: E1, zero code: in a Loom Dev session with an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, run Claude's built-in /diff (2.1.287+; installed CLI is 2.1.300) in Loom's terminal at the default window and at a widened one. Decides the pane: it needs the fullscreen renderer and 110+ columns, and at the default 1220 pt window with a 300 pt sidebar the terminal is probably near that limit (inference, not measured). If /diff works well inside Loom, the in-app pane becomes later/skip and only the chip and exports are built. If it opens only when widened, a one-line hint may be enough.

E2, git cost on real repos (read-only commands only): time `git --no-optional-locks diff --numstat -z HEAD` and `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 -z -unormal --ignore-submodules=all` cold and warm on the user's two work repos and the largest repo they use, with and without core.fsmonitor/untrackedCache. Decides the 5 s timeout, the caps, whether `-c core.fsmonitor=false` is acceptable, and whether the chip needs a per-folder size guard (skip the chip above a file-count threshold).

E3, runner latency: measure `captureHelper` per-call latency (scope open) against a plain Process runner on the same git command. Expected to confirm that the plain runner is needed; also settles the Quit-cancel wiring.

E4, only if phase 2 proceeds: an NSTextView diff of 5,000 lines and 256 KiB, expanded/collapsed, scrolled, while the window is visible vs hidden; check the CPU and memory against the 40%/1 MiB/s gate and the render-probe style counters. feasibility.loom_design:
PREREQUISITE (observed): Loom has no diff or git-status code. `GitBranch.swift` and `BranchCache.swift` only read `.git/HEAD` and never launch git. I-29 therefore needs a read-only Changes view first. The cheapest shape follows the precedent of `EndedScreenView` and the subagent transcript panel. It is shown in place of the terminal (same slot as `model.viewedSubagent` in `DetailView.swift`; Esc goes back). It is a selectable read-only NSTextView with the diff as attributed text, so line selection comes free and there is no custom Core Text renderer. The diff is per file and lazy, because only the selected file's diff is ever fetched. Short-lived git child processes (the `ClaudePlanLimits`/`DiagnosticsExport` `Process()` precedent) use `--no-optional-locks --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`, a 5 s timeout, and an output cap of about 1-2 MiB with the child killed at the cap. Triggers: pane opens, the Stop hook of this session while the pane is visible, window activation while visible, manual refresh. No FSEvents and no timers in v1.

1) STORE (LoomCore, SessionCatalog). New tables `review_comments` and `review_batches`, created on open like the other post-schema-3 additions (no `user_version` bump). Comment fields: session_id, path, new-side start/end line, quote (at most 6 lines, 200 characters per line, invisible Unicode removed), quote_hash, file diffIdentity (hash of that file's diff), head OID, body, state, batch_id.
 - Staleness: do not move comments. On each refresh, compare the quote hash at the stored range. A mismatch marks the comment `outdated`: shown dimmed, left out of the next batch unless the user ticks 'include anyway'. A sent and outdated comment reads as probably addressed.
 - `SessionCatalog+Deletions` must delete these rows, and the delete sheet's dry run should count them. The quotes are the user's work code and are personal data under contract section 8.
 - Quotes and comments are stored; diffs never are.

2) FORMAT (pure function in LoomCore, unit-testable). Merge Orca's File/Lines/Comment blocks, Vibe Kanban's quoted code and Warp's 'run git diff yourself' pointer.
 - First line: 'Review comments (N) on <branch> [loom-review <id4>]'.
 - Then numbered 'path Lstart-end' blocks with a '>' quote and 'Comment: ...'.
 - Then 'Full context: git diff HEAD.' and an end marker '[/loom-review <id4>]'.
 - Markers are ASCII only, because Claude strips invisible characters on Enter. The batch cap is about 12 KiB: beyond that, quotes drop and only the path and line range stay. Turkish characters and prompt-trigger characters (leading '!', '/', '@') must survive; E1 checks this.

3) STAGE (LoomTerminal + ConversationController). Add `TerminalSurface.stageDraft(_:)`, reached through a new `ConversationIntents.stageDraft(sessionID:text:)`, which returns an outcome enum (see 3a). It reuses SwiftTerm's `pasteText`, the same path `insertDroppedFiles` already uses, so it goes through TerminalInputQueue and its single ordered writer. It never sends Enter.
 3a) Refusals, checked against the run's state: no live run (the ended screen or record view keeps the comments pending and offers Resume); `waitingForApproval` or `waitingForInput` ('Needs approval: answer it first'); an `issue` on the session (hook silence); and the engine's `bracketedPasteMode == false`. The last one matters: without bracketed paste, embedded newlines would act as Enter. If E3 shows Claude drops DECSET 2004 in dialogs, this flag is also a free dialog detector. Pasting while Working is allowed, because typing ahead is documented to queue.
 3b) After a successful stage: focus the terminal and show 'Staged in prompt. Press Return to send.' No auto-send in v1: an auto Enter is I-01's job, and its failure modes (autocomplete swallowing Enter, #15553; a draft left behind) are what the draft-only default avoids.

4) VERIFY (LoomCore/ClaudeHook.swift + the Claude adapter). `ClaudeHookEvent` currently keeps only `promptIsSynthetic` and discards the prompt text. Extend it with a bounded scan for the `[loom-review <id>]` start and end markers, parsed at init like `promptIsSynthetic`, without retaining the prompt. The payload cap is 1 MiB, so a 12 KiB prompt is no problem. The adapter publishes a `reviewBatch(id, outcome)` event on the SessionEventHub, and the catalog updates the batch. States, all event-driven:
 - draft: in Loom only.
 - staged: bytes accepted by the input queue. This is not shown as delivered.
 - delivered: a non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit contains both markers. Comments become sent and are kept.
 - delivered, truncated: start marker only (#90910 truncates the start, so the end marker is the check).
 - not submitted: a later non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit has no marker, or the run ended. The comments return to draft. No automatic re-stage.
 Staged is a legitimate resting state while the user thinks. There is no timer.

5) SKIPPED (kept as notes). B (`/loom:review` skill with !`cmd`): its own fact-check says injected commands need a pre-approved allowed-tools rule or the skill aborts, and whether a rule can match `$LOOM_CLI` is unknown. Slash commands are the cases autocomplete swallowed in #15553. Its handover proof is the export call, not the user's prompt. It is only a fallback if E1 shows big pastes are unreliable. C (mods): young API, unsandboxed, blocked on managed machines, and a code-execution surface inside the CLI. D (additionalContext at Stop): it is a system reminder, not a user message, and it does not wake an idle session. E (cross-session inbox, channels): no user authority, contradicts `crossSessionInbound: refuse` in `ProviderLaunchProfile`, and belongs to D-43.

6) ROUTING. Target session = the session whose Changes pane it is. Per-session routing removes the Orca-style 'send to which agent' picker and keeps the action inside the user's own click: no cross-session authority question. The same worktree shared by two sessions is a known ambiguity; the comment belongs to the session where it was written.

COST RE-ESTIMATE
 - Store, deletion and format: S-M.
 - Stage and gating: S.
 - Hook marker, state machine and UI states: M.
 - The comment composer in the pane: M.
 - I-29 on top of an existing Changes pane: M.
 - Total from today including the pane: L. The pane (git runner, file list, diff text, caps, refresh policy) is most of it.
 - It should not ship as a standalone idea.

Whether it is a right panel instead (D-34) is the user's call.

Making a comment:

Sending:

State line:

feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS. Nothing runs while the pane is hidden. Git runs only on pane open, the Stop hook while visible, window activation while visible, or a manual refresh. It is one bounded read of a single file's diff, with a 5 s timeout and a size cap. No watchers and no polling in v1. Comments are small SQLite rows. RISK: `git status` on a huge work repo with ignored build output; mitigate with `--untracked-files=normal` and the timeout.
- Predictability: PASS. Nothing is sent without a click, and nothing is sent without the user pressing Return. Auto-send would break this, which is why it is out.
- Accurate status: PASS and an improvement. 'Delivered' means the hook saw the markers in a real UserPromptSubmit. 'Staged' is never shown as delivered. Truncation is detected through the end marker. A failed or unknown outcome is shown honestly, with no retry. RISK: the markers might not survive some future CLI prompt normalization; the failure mode is a visible 'not confirmed', not a false success.
- Fluency: RISK, accepted. The cost is one Return keypress and a terminal focus switch per batch. This is the trade for removing the Enter-swallow and draft-left-behind failure modes, and is still far fewer round trips than retyping paths and lines.
- Modularity: PASS. The format is a pure function. The store is one catalog extension. The stage API is a narrow intent. The marker is a hook-event field. The Changes pane is a separate component, and review never enters `ProcessSupervisor`.
- CLI-update resilience: PASS. It relies only on the documented `prompt` field of UserPromptSubmit (already registered in `ProviderLaunchProfile`) and on ordinary bracketed paste into the prompt, which a terminal user does constantly. It adds no CLI flag, no skill permission rule, no mods API, and does not pin a version. The stage refusal when 2004 is off is a safety check, not a version assumption.
- Process ownership: PASS. Git children are short-lived and bounded and have no run scope, like the plan-limits child. No daemon.
- User authority: PASS. The target is the pane's own session, chosen by the user, and the user presses Return. This is not the D-43 cross-session channel.
- Contract: the terminal stays the real CLI and no chat UI is introduced. The Changes view temporarily takes the terminal's slot, as the subagent transcript panel already does.
- Data: RISK. Code quotes from the work projects (EDDP) now live in the catalog. They need deletion coverage (`SessionCatalog+Deletions`, the dry run's counts) and should be excluded from the diagnostics export.
feasibility.value_reason:
The user runs several sessions and many subagents and reviews agent output constantly. Review is the step done most after a turn ends, and it is Loom's biggest gap relative to Claude Desktop, Conductor, Codex, Warp and Orca, all of which ship this loop.
 - Loom's catalog and hook knowledge give it a verified delivery state that none of the PTY-based competitors have.
 - The value is conditional. It only exists if the Changes pane is good enough that the user actually reviews in Loom instead of their IDE.
 - The pane has no syntax highlighting in v1 and is a bigger build than the comment layer.
 - Claude Code's own /diff panel (2.1.287+, with `ask`) already covers viewing diffs, so Loom's differentiator is the comment loop plus the cross-session overview.
 - The draft-only default costs one Return key, so it is slightly less automatic than Desktop's Cmd+Enter.
 - Score 4 only if the Changes pane is built; as a standalone idea it is worth 0.

feasibility.one_line: Worth building as a thin, view-only, event-driven layer (a chip plus a per-turn changed-file list, no restore, no diff renderer), but only after a spike settles four unknowns: where the snapshots live, git cost per hook on the user's real repos, the hook race at prompt time, and the cost of a run scope per git call.
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS FROM THE CODE (read)
- Both triggers already arrive. `ClaudeHookEvent` (Sources/LoomCore/ClaudeHook.swift) parses `userPromptSubmit`, `stop`, `stopFailure`, and also `cwd` (`workingDirectory`), `prompt_id` (`promptID`) and `promptIsSynthetic`. `ClaudeSessionAdapter.receive` (ProviderSessionAdapters.swift ~205-300) is the one place where a turn start (non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit) and a turn end (Stop/StopFailure) are known, ordered, after the tracker has accepted them.
- Loom registers no PostToolUse hook on purpose: ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings says "No per-tool hooks: each hook spawns a helper". So Loom cannot know which files the agent touched, and a git-level snapshot is the only way to be correct for Bash, subagent and outside edits.
- Loom has no git runner in the production path today. `GitBranch.read` / `BranchCache` only read files. The one git user is `CleanupWorktreeProtection.live` (CleanupCoordinator.swift), which calls `ProcessSupervisor.captureHelper("/usr/bin/git", ...)`, and the cleanup review is dev-build only (ARCHITECTURE section 2, Retention). The owned helper path exists, with a ledger entry, a deadline, a 4 MiB output cap and a cancel on Quit (ProcessSupervisor+EnvironmentJobs.swift, LaunchEnvironment.runHelper/capture).
- IMPORTANT cost fact: `captureHelper` uses `runOwnedJob(scope: .perCall)`, which opens a fresh LoomRunHost scope through LaunchServices (`open -n -g -j`) for EVERY call and releases it after. One call per git command would be heavy, so a snapshot must be ONE call (a `/bin/sh -c` script that runs the whole recipe), and probably should reuse a shared scope kind like `.environment` when snapshots overlap. The scope-launch latency is not measured anywhere in the repo that I could find (the cp5 runscope-latency file measures terminal echo, not scope open).

DESIGN (smallest version that is correct)
1. New LoomCore type `TurnSnapshotStore` (actor, same shape as `BranchCache`; no UI imports). Input: (loomSessionID, workingDirectory, kind: base|end, promptID). It runs one owned helper job per snapshot.
2. Where the snapshots live. Preferred: a Loom-owned shadow git dir under the data root (`<data root>/turn-snapshots/<hash of repo toplevel>.git`) used as `GIT_DIR=... GIT_WORK_TREE=<toplevel>`, with its own index. This is better than refs in the user's repo (T3's `refs/t3/...` and the idea's `refs/loom/checkpoints/...`) because: no ref or object is written into the user's repo; no exposure to `git push --mirror`; Loom's own index means no copy of the user's index and no racy-index trouble with the user's index; cleanup and size are one directory (rmdir plus verify), which fits the deletion contract and 'verified outcomes'; the user's `git gc` cannot race it. Cost: the first snapshot of a repo copies all non-ignored content (blobs) once, then it is incremental through the shadow index. Fallback within the spike: temp-index refs in the user's repo (the T3 recipe: copy index to a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, `git add -A`, `write-tree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref`). Honour `.gitignore`, pass `-c core.fsmonitor=false` (never start a git daemon in Loom's scope), `-c commit.gpgsign=false`, fixed GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER env, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (same env pattern as CleanupWorktreeProtection.live), and fsync the ref/loose objects (T3 saw 0-byte refs after unclean restarts).
3. Triggers (no polling, no watcher). (a) non-synthetic UserPromptSubmit: take 'base', detached from the hook path so it never blocks the adapter's `transitioningRuns` lock or Claude (the hook helper has timeout 1 and is synchronous). (b) Stop and StopFailure: take 'end', then `git diff --numstat -z base end` (object-only, no work-tree scan) in the same script; the result is path, +, -, status for at most 200 paths plus totals. A later Stop in the same turn (background subagents, synthetic hand-back prompts) overwrites 'end'. An interrupted turn has no Stop: the next real prompt's 'base' doubles as the previous turn's 'end', marked 'ended by interrupt'. Also record HEAD at both ends; if HEAD moved say 'commits/pull/checkout included' (the worktree diff itself is still right when the agent commits its own edits).
4. Bounds. One snapshot at a time per repo toplevel, at most 2 repos at once, a pending 'end' coalesces, 8 s deadline, outputs capped. A repo that blows the deadline is marked 'too slow' for this app run and shows 'tracking off for this repo', never retried in a loop. Skip non-git folders, bare/other-owner repos, folders where `git` is not usable. Per-session cap of 100 turns and 30 days (matches Claude's own /rewind retention), pruned in the same script at snapshot time (event-driven, no timer). Do nothing for idle/stopped sessions (no run, no hook, no git).
5. State. Memory only: `SessionViewState` gains `lastTurnChange: TurnChangeSummary?` (turn index, file count, +/-, state running/ended/interrupted/unavailable, scope text), carried by a new `SessionEventChange.turnChanges(...)` case, published by the adapter like `.subagents`. No catalog migration. The shadow repo is the durable truth: after a relaunch the detail pane re-derives a turn's list lazily from stored commit messages (prompt id, HEAD, timestamps) with one bounded `git diff`, only while that pane is open. 'Since you last looked': no extra snapshot; the unseen range is base(first turn after the last `setViewed`) to end(latest) and is one object-only `git diff`.
6. Deletion and honesty. Register a `ConversationForgetting` hook (as the usage index does in AppDelegate+Usage) that removes the session's snapshot refs from the shadow repo; the shadow repo itself is dropped when no session refers to it. Add one line to the deletion dry run ('N turn snapshots, X MB in Loom's data folder'). Restore stays out; the UI offers 'Copy patch' and 'Open in editor' only, and for a real revert points at /rewind or git.
7. Minimal UI hook: nothing runs in the view layer; `CatalogModel.apply` stores the summary on `SessionRowModel.live` like the other frame fields (statistics and render probes cover it).
feasibility.ui_sketch: Card (two-row card, design/DESIGN.md section 3 item 4): in the bottom row after the branch, a small tertiary-to-secondary 'Δ 4 files +120 -18' text only when the last turn ended with changes, only on live/Active sessions; blue/neutral, no new status hue, never colour-only (text carries it). Nothing is drawn for 0 changes or when tracking is unavailable. Header (SessionHeaderViews, next to the project/branch chip, D-53 fixed places): the same chip is a button that opens a popover (not a new pane) with: scope line ('Changes since the prompt was sent, 14:02 - 14:09; other edits in this folder are included' and, when it applies, 'HEAD moved: commits or a pull are included'), the turn picker (last turn, since you last looked, turn N), a file list with status and +/-, and Copy patch / Open in editor / Reveal. A Settings switch 'Track changes per turn' (Settings > General). Full diff rendering, line comments and restore are deliberately not part of this idea (they belong to the review-pane idea, which this feeds).
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: RISK, manageable. Event-driven, two git jobs per turn only for live sessions, nothing when idle or hidden. The risks are `git add -A` on a large tree and one run-scope launch per helper call (unmeasured); both are why this is spike-first. Predictability: PASS with a switch, and with a fixed scope label. Accurate status: PASS only with honest labels ('changes since the prompt was sent'; 'unavailable' when the base is missing, the repo is too slow or git is unusable; never an invented '0 changes'). The race at prompt time (the base snapshot runs after the hook returns; a first edit in the first few hundred ms would be missing) must be shown to be negligible or labelled. Concurrent sessions in one checkout: 'last turn' includes the others' edits, say so. Fluency: PASS if it never blocks the hook helper, the adapter lock or the UI. Modularity: PASS (LoomCore actor plus one hub case plus a chip; no new target). CLI-update resilience: PASS, it uses only documented hooks (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, cwd, prompt_id) and git; it does not depend on /rewind internals, `--resume-session-at` or the transcript format. Ownership: PASS only if every git process goes through the owned helper path (never `Process()` in the app), with fsmonitor disabled so no daemon outlives the scope. User authority: RISK for the refs-in-user-repo variant (Loom writes into the user's repository); the shadow store avoids it, and a switch gives the user control. New dependency: the production app would run /usr/bin/git for the first time; the Apple shim can pop an Xcode CLT installer dialog if the tools are missing, so check the toolchain before spawning (the cleanup review, dev-only today, already assumes it). Privacy: snapshots copy untracked, non-ignored files (for example an un-ignored .env) into Loom's data folder or the repo's objects.
feasibility.value_reason: The unique value is cross-session triage that Claude's own /diff (fullscreen TUI, per-turn T1/T2 from Claude's file-edit checkpoints, misses Bash) cannot give: with several sessions and subagent workflows, a card chip says which finished session actually changed code and how much, and 'since you last looked' makes the blue Finished dot more meaningful. The per-turn file list itself is a convenience, since the user can already press /diff or run git. Without a diff view (a separate idea) it is a data layer with a thin view, so the daily payoff is moderate; with that view it becomes the core of a review loop.
depends_on: a review/diff pane idea (the chip is useful alone, but 'Copy patch' and 'Open in editor' are the only drill-down without it)
Settings switch plumbing (UIPreferences) for 'Track changes per turn'
a shared-scope option in ProcessSupervisor+EnvironmentJobs if the per-call scope launch proves too slow
experiments: E1 snapshot cost and correctness (isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / fixture data root, loom-fake-provider, no real ~/.claude): on 3 repos (small, the user's two work-project sizes, one large/monorepo-like), time the one-script recipe through `captureHelper`: cold first snapshot, warm incremental, 1 changed file, 100 changed files, one large untracked file, a repo with a sparse checkout and a linked worktree, and a user with fsmonitor/untrackedCache on. Compare shadow-GIT_DIR vs temp-index-in-user-repo. Decide: warm p95 <= ~300 ms and cold <= ~3 s on the work repos; shadow disk growth small (a few percent of the repo for typical turns); CPU well inside the 40 % gate; user's `git status`/index untouched (index mtime and bytes unchanged, no index.lock). Anything above the thresholds means 'limit to simple/small repos' or skip.

E2 hook facts (fake provider plus a short real-Claude run in an isolated profile, D-04 allows it): (a) does UserPromptSubmit fire for a message queued mid-turn and for synthetic hand-back prompts (promptIsSynthetic), (b) is Stop skipped on Esc interrupt, (c) measure the gap between the UserPromptSubmit hook arriving and the first file change by the agent, versus the time to finish the base snapshot (the race window). Decide: if the base snapshot loses the race in more than a trivial share of turns, base on the previous turn's end snapshot instead and relabel the scope ('since the last turn ended').

E3 helper cost: measure `runOwnedJob(.perCall)` end to end (scope open, spawn, release) for a no-op `/bin/true` and for the snapshot script, 20 runs each, with 1 and 5 concurrent. Decide: per-call scope is acceptable only if its added median is small next to the git work; otherwise add a shared scope kind.

E4 'git stash create' claim from the idea: it takes no -u / --include-untracked option and works from the real index, so it misses untracked files and can contend with the user's index lock; confirm in one throw-away repo and drop it for good. Also confirm that `git add -A` against a copied or shadow index honours .gitignore, .git/info/exclude, nested repos and submodules as expected.

E5 safety and platform checks: with the Xcode CLT absent (or `xcode-select -p` failing) the /usr/bin/git shim must not open an installer dialog; and a project under ~/Documents must be readable by git inside the LoomRunHost scope (the host is its own TCC-responsible app, DEVELOPMENT.md section 2), as Claude's PTY child already is.

feasibility.one_line: Adopt a read-only, GitHub-only PR/checks chip fed by one bounded `gh pr list --json` call at the events Loom already has (turn end, window activation, manual refresh), and leave the canned Create PR / Fix CI / Resolve conflicts actions, ETag, merge-tree and "CI failure becomes needs-you" out, because the chip pays for itself only if the work repos are on GitHub and the actions only make sense once the I-01 send primitive exists.
feasibility.loom_design:
PLUG-IN POINTS (all verified in code). Loom already refreshes the card's Git branch at exactly the events the idea wants: `CatalogModel.apply(frame)` calls `refreshBranches([workingDirectory])` on a `.turnComplete` status frame, `setWindowActive(true)` calls `refreshBranches(Set(branches.keys))`, and `BranchCache` (actor, one read per folder, publishes only changed values, `retain()` prunes to shown folders, `pruneBranches()` ties lifetime to cards/selection/tabs). The PR status should be a sibling of that path, not a new scheduler: new `PullRequestCache` actor (LoomCatalogUI, same shape as `BranchCache`) keyed by (folder, branch), `CatalogModel.pullRequests: [PRKey: PullRequestStatus]` (in memory only, no catalog schema change, pruned with `pruneBranches`), `CatalogModel+PullRequests.swift` for triggers, same serialized-publish trick as `branchTask`.

NEW CORE PIECES (LoomCore, no UI imports, per ARCHITECTURE layer rule): (1) `PullRequestFetcher`, modelled on `LimitsExchange` in `ClaudePlanLimits.swift` (Foundation `Process`, poll with short steps so a cancel is noticed, 15 s timeout, 1 MiB output cap, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, stderr to null, cancelled on Quit). It runs `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --limit 1 --json number,url,state,isDraft,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,updatedAt` in the card's folder, with env from the resolved `ProviderToolchain.environment` (the user's login-shell PATH, because a LaunchServices-started Loom has no /opt/homebrew/bin) and `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 NO_COLOR=1`. Use `pr list --head` rather than `pr view`: it returns `[]` with exit 0 when the branch has no PR, so "no PR" is a verified outcome and no stderr text is ever parsed. Exit 4 (documented in `gh help exit-codes`) = not logged in; exit 1 / timeout / spawn failure = could not check. (2) `PullRequestStatus` pure value + parser/classifier (unit-testable with canned JSON): outcome is one of noPullRequest (verified), open/draft/merged/closed with `checks` in {none, pending, failing(n of m), passing} and `merge` in {clean, behind, blocked, conflicts, checking}, or `unavailable(reason: ghMissing | notLoggedIn | notGitHubRemote | failed | outputNotUnderstood)`. statusCheckRollup mixes CheckRun (status/conclusion) and StatusContext (state) entries; any unknown enum value is classified unknown, never passing; an EMPTY rollup is "no checks", never "passing"; `mergeStateStatus == UNKNOWN` (GitHub computes mergeability lazily after a push) is "checking", never "conflicts". (3) Forge gate without a process: read the remote URL from `.git/config` (same small bounded file reads as `GitBranch.read`, worktree `commondir` aware); if the host is not github.com or a host `gh` knows, show nothing and spawn nothing. This is also how a GitLab repo degrades quietly instead of showing a gh error on every card.

TRIGGERS (events only): (a) turn complete of a session, (b) window becomes active, (c) a card's first appearance when it has a live run and no cached value, (d) manual 'Refresh PR Status' in the session menu / chip context menu. NOT triggers: FSEvents on refs/remotes (the agent's push happens inside a turn so the Stop edge already catches it, and a push from another terminal is caught by activation; dropping the watcher removes a per-card file watcher), hooks per tool call (Loom registers no per-tool hooks on purpose, `claudeSettings` comment), any timer for settled PRs.

BOUNDS: refresh only for sessions that have a live run, plus the selected session and tab sessions (ended cards show their last cached value dimmed, or nothing); one gh child at a time (serial queue, like the ordered `branchTask`); at most one refresh per (folder, branch) per 30 s except manual; dedupe sessions sharing a folder; results below the 1 MiB cap only. The single deliberate exception to no-polling: while the last result is `checks: pending` (or just pushed and the rollup is still empty) AND the window is active AND the session is selected/tabbed/live, re-arm ONE cancellable one-shot task at 30 s, 60 s, 120 s, 120 s, ... capped at about 10 minutes total (7 calls), cancelled on window deactivate and on settle. After the cap the chip says 'pending, checked 14:41' and waits for the next event or a manual refresh. This is bounded and visible, and should be presented to the user as a decision, not hidden. GraphQL cost is about 1 point per call, so no ETag/`gh api -i` layer is needed at this call volume; the Supacode storms (#830, #844) came from timers over every worktree, which this design never does.

VERIFIED OUTCOMES: the chip carries `checkedAt` (shown in tooltip and header, 'checked 14:32') and, optionally, compares the PR's `headRefOid` with the local branch tip read from the ref file: if they differ the header says 'checks are for an older commit' (unpushed work), which stops a green PR from hiding local changes. 'merged' / 'closed' come only from gh's `state`, never from the agent saying so (contract: 'the agent saying done is not proof'). On failure the last known value stays but is dimmed with its time and the reason; it is never refreshed to green by a failed call.

DRIFT: gh's `--json` field list is documented (`gh pr list --help`). A removed field makes gh exit 1 with an unknown-field error; map that to `outputNotUnderstood` and journal one `cli_compat_warning` per app run, same pattern as `ClaudeRegistryDiagnostics` / `reportCompatibility` (D-45). No GitHub API versions, no tokens stored, no OAuth, uses the user's own gh login.

NOT IN THE LIGHT VERSION (and why): (1) 'failed check moves the session to needs-you': `SessionIndicator` derives from provider state (`SessionDisplay.swift`), `AttentionOrder.rank`, the Dock badge, the menu bar item, Cmd+J and the Active section's `activePhase` (set in `SessionEventHub.publish`) all share that one meaning ('Claude is waiting for you'); a red CI is a fact about a PR, not about the session, and mixing them breaks 'accurate status'. Show it as a chip tint only; revisit as a separate, opt-in 'CI failed' notification if the user asks. (2) Canned actions: Loom has no send-to-session path today (grep finds only the evidence-only `typeForEvidence`); they depend on the I-01 verified-send primitive. Until then the cheapest honest version is 'Copy Fix-CI Prompt' (with failing check names filled in) in the chip's context menu. Once I-01 exists, add constant or user-editable templates sent as a draft (not auto-submitted), refused while the session is Needs approval. (3) merge-tree conflict preview: not network-free (OIDs from PR data, base ref must be fetched, per the review-git-loop fact-check) and `mergeStateStatus` already says DIRTY/BEHIND/BLOCKED. (4) merge button, stacks, auto-merge, auto-fix loops: the agent can run gh itself, and auto loops spend tokens without the user.

GITLAB: Claude Code's statusLine JSON does carry `pr.number/url/review_state` and, for a GitLab remote, the merge request (`pr.kind: mr`, v2.1.234+), but only number and a coarse review state, no pipeline status, and getting it needs the I-24 statusLine bridge, which the usage-tools digest rates the weakest fit (per-update process spawn, an inline `--settings` statusLine replaces the user's own and hides CLI footer hints; D-32 forbids a process per update). So the I-24 route is not the cheap alternative the idea implies. If the work repos are GitLab, the honest options are a second forge adapter (`glab mr list --source-branch ... --output json`, +M, glab is not installed on this machine, gh is) or no chip for those projects.

COST (honest re-estimate): idea says M. Chip only: M at the low end (about 600-800 lines incl. tests): fetcher ~200, status parser/classifier ~150, cache + model ~200, card/header/menu views ~120, Settings switch + docs ~60; tests are cheap because a fake `gh` script on PATH and canned JSON cover parsing, tri-state, throttle, cancel-on-quit and prune. Full idea as written (ETag layer, FSEvents push watcher, merge-tree with fetch, canned actions with delivery verification, needs-you promotion) is L-XL and drags in I-01 and the Active/attention pipeline.

[pin] ... project  provider-icon` gets a compact PR token right after the branch: `⎇ EDDP-123-fix-x  #482 ✕`.
