feasibility.principle_check:
RESOURCES: pass with the light design (event-driven, serial, one short child per refresh for live/selected sessions only, 15 s timeout, 1 MiB cap, no watcher, nothing when the window is hidden, nothing when the setting is off). RISK: the pending back-off is a timer; keep it capped at about 10 min, window-active only, cancelled on hide and settle, and present it to the user as an explicit exception. Principle violations would be: a repeating interval over all cards (Superset 10 s, Emdash 1 min, Supacode #830/#844), a FSEvents watcher per card, fetching for every loaded or ended card, retry loops after errors, or `gh pr checks --watch` as a long-lived child.
PREDICTABILITY: pass if the trigger list is fixed and documented (turn end, activation, first appearance of a live card, manual); risk if the back-off feels like magic, so label it ('pending, will recheck') and show 'checked <time>'.
ACCURATE STATUS: pass only with the discipline above: tri-state results, no-PR distinguished from gh-missing/not-logged-in/failed, empty rollup is not green, unknown enum is not green, UNKNOWN mergeability is 'checking', failed refresh keeps a dimmed stale value, merged/closed only from gh. Hard risk: promoting CI failure into the session's own status (indicator, pill, Dock badge, Cmd+J, menu bar, Active) conflates two meanings; kept out. A false green is the worst failure of this feature.
FLUENCY: pass; read-only, no confirmation, click opens the PR. Canned actions are one keystroke only after I-01; they should draft, not submit.
MODULARITY: pass; core fetcher/parser in LoomCore with no UI imports, cache/model beside `BranchCache`, views in LoomCatalogUI, forge gate pure and testable; a GitLab adapter would slot behind the same `PullRequestStatus` type.
CLI-UPDATE RESILIENCE: pass; uses only the user's installed gh and its documented `--json` fields and exit codes (0/1/4), no stderr text parsing, no GitHub API versioning, no tokens; drift becomes a journaled `cli_compat_warning` plus an 'output not understood' chip state, never a crash or a pin. It does not touch the Claude CLI at all (the I-24 route would).
OWNERSHIP: pass with a caveat; gh (and the git it may call) are short-lived children of the Loom app, started by Loom and killed by it on timeout, cancel and Quit, the same precedent as `ClaudePlanLimitsFetcher` (D-37), not run-scope members. They must be cancelled in `SessionRuntime.shutdown` so Quit stays clean. Spike: confirm no leftover child after a forced cancel.
USER AUTHORITY: pass; read-only chip, user's own gh login, the network call is to the user's own forge. Any prompt sent to a session must be user-initiated (and via I-01's gating); no auto-fix, no auto-merge, no cross-session send. Privacy: repo and branch names go to GitHub exactly as `git push` already does; default-off setting makes the new network behaviour opt-in.
feasibility.value_reason: It removes a real context switch at the end of every agentic task (push, PR, wait for CI) for GitHub repos, and fits the ticket-key workflow because branch and PR title carry EDDP-*, but it is only informational: Claude Code already shows its own PR badge in the terminal footer, the user types prompts fluently so canned actions save little ('fix CI' is a few words and the agent runs `gh pr checks` itself), and the research notes say the user's backend work flows through GitLab/IntelliJ review, which a gh chip does not cover (glab is not even installed here). Value is 3 if the work repos are on GitHub, about 2 if they are GitLab.
depends_on: I-01 (verified send-to-session primitive): required only for the canned Create PR / Fix CI / Resolve conflicts actions, not for the chip
I-24 (statusLine bridge): only for the no-gh alternative; not recommended as the source (weakest-fit idea in the usage digest, gives number and review_state only, no CI)
Settings > General switch plumbing (UIPreferences) for the default-off opt-in
Existing BranchCache / refreshBranches triggers in CatalogModel (reuse, not a prerequisite to build)
experiments: gh contract spike (isolated scratch repo plus one read-only run by the user on a real repo, no Loom app needed): run the exact `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --limit 1 --json ...` from a Loom-like minimal environment (PATH from the resolved ProviderToolchain, no TTY, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1). Decide: (a) exit codes and output for no PR (expect exit 0 and `[]`), logged out (expect exit 4), non-GitHub remote and no remote (expect exit 1), offline; (b) p50/p95 latency (adopt if p95 is under about 2 s; if much slower, lengthen the throttle); (c) that statusCheckRollup shapes (CheckRun vs StatusContext) all map to the classifier, including a repo with no checks; (d) mergeStateStatus right after a push (UNKNOWN flapping) so 'checking' is correct and the pending back-off covers it.

Post-push timing spike: push a trivial commit to a scratch repo with a workflow and record what the rollup looks like at +0 s, +10 s, +30 s, +60 s (empty vs queued vs in_progress). Decides whether the 30/60/120 s back-off schedule and the 'waiting for checks to start' wording are right, or whether a different first delay is needed.

Ownership and environment spike (dev build, isolated data root): spawn the fetcher from a LaunchServices-started Loom Dev (not from a terminal) to confirm gh is found via the resolved toolchain PATH, that a repo under ~/Documents does not raise an extra TCC prompt for the child, and that cancelling mid-run and Quit leave no gh/git child behind.

Render-cost check using the existing counters: with 30 loaded cards, confirm the PR token adds no card body evaluations beyond the changed row (SidebarRenderProbe / CatalogHotPathTests pattern), i.e. PR updates patch one row via the same equality-guarded publish as `branches`.
user_decisions: Where do the EDDP-* work repos live: GitHub or GitLab? This decides everything: GitHub means the gh chip is worth building; GitLab means either a second adapter (glab, not installed here), a link-out only, or skipping the idea.

Should a failing CI ever alert you (a notification, or Needs-you), or is a red chip on the card enough? The recommendation is chip only, because session status means 'Claude is waiting for you'; a separate opt-in 'CI failed' notification could come later.

Accept the single bounded exception to no-polling (re-check at 30 s, 60 s, 2 min, capped at about 10 minutes, only while the window is active and the session is live, selected or in a tab), or insist on strictly event-only with a manual refresh?
Default off with a Settings switch (recommended, since it is Loom's first network-touching feature), or on whenever gh is found and logged in?

Do you want canned Create PR / Fix CI / Resolve conflicts prompts at all, given you can type them quickly and the agent can run gh itself? If yes: editable templates, drafted but not submitted, and only after the I-01 send primitive exists.
Should the chip show on every card or only on live, selected and Active cards (recommended, to keep gh calls proportional to the sessions you are actually working with)?

feasibility.one_line: Build a thin Loom-owned "New session in worktree" (one plain `git worktree add -b <ticket key>`, session opens with cwd = worktree, glyph on the card) plus a dry-run-guarded "Remove worktree", reusing the catalog's per-session working_directory and the existing CP4-G worktree check; do not delegate to `claude -w`, and skip the pool, registry, storage list, setup scripts and port ranges for now.
feasibility.loom_design:
**Why this is lighter than it looks.** `sessions.working_directory` is already per session and separate from `sessions.project_id` (CatalogDatabase schema; `SessionRuntime.workingDirectory(projectID:)` only supplies the default). A session with project_id = the main repo's project and working_directory = a worktree path therefore gets, with no change: grouping under the parent project, a correct branch chip (`GitBranch.read` already follows a `.git` pointer file to the worktree's own HEAD), Reveal in Finder and Copy Resume Command (`SessionMenuItems`), resume in the right folder (`resumeConversation`), ticket de-duplication (`SessionCatalog.session(projectID:ticket:)`), and usage/deletion (both walk the config dir by session id, not by cwd: `ClaudeDataInventory`, `ClaudeUsageIndex`). No schema change.

**Decision: Loom runs git itself, not `claude --worktree`.** Facts from `claude --help` (2.1.300) and code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees: `-w` makes `.claude/worktrees/<name>` on branch `worktree-<name>` (the branch cannot be named from the ticket key), branches from the remote default branch ("fresh"), may fetch for up to 5 s, shows its own keep/remove prompt on /exit, and moves the session's cwd itself. For Loom that means: the catalog still holds the project root, so the branch label and Reveal point at the wrong place until a new hook-cwd plumbing and a catalog write are added; two owners of the worktree lifecycle (Loom Stop kills the CLI so no exit prompt ever runs, orphans stay); and the semantics changed several times (v2.1.208 reuse, 2.1.212 resume), which is exactly the drift the principles warn about. A Loom-run `git worktree add` depends only on git, which does not drift. The cost is that Loom must copy `.worktreeinclude` files itself (below).

**Module and triggers (event-driven, no polling).**
1. New `Sources/LoomCore/WorktreeProvisioner.swift`: pure name/path planning plus an injected `Capture` (same shape as `CleanupWorktreeProtection.Capture`, production = `ProcessSupervisor.captureHelper("/usr/bin/git", ..., timeout 10-15 s)`, owned, bounded, cancelled at shutdown). Steps, only on an explicit user action: (a) inspect: project path is inside a git work tree (reuse the `.git` walk of `GitBranch`/`isLinkedWorktree`), branch name and path valid and not existing, branch not checked out elsewhere; (b) resolve base without network: `origin/HEAD` target if it resolves locally, else the main checkout's HEAD (never fetch; show the chosen base in the sheet); (c) `git worktree add --no-track -b <branch> <path> <base>` (named branch, never detached HEAD); (d) verify: `GitBranch.read(directory: path) == .named(branch)` and the path exists; (e) one-shot `.worktreeinclude` copy (below). Result is a typed outcome: created / created-with-warnings (n files not copied) / failed(stage, message). No rollback by deleting anything: on any failure after (c) Loom leaves the worktree and says so (Supacode #878 deleted a pre-existing folder when creation failed; never `rm -rf`, never `--force`).
2. `SessionRuntime.startConversation(provider:projectID:...)` gets an optional `directory:` override (validated: exists, is a linked worktree whose common git dir belongs to the project path). `ManagedSession.workingDirectory` = worktree, `projectID` = the main project. Launch profile, hooks, registry reader (`observeRegistry` takes the directory) and `--session-id` are unchanged: zero new Claude flags.
3. `.worktreeinclude` copy (Claude's documented file, same semantics: listed AND gitignored): `git ls-files -z -o --exclude-from=.worktreeinclude` then `git check-ignore -z --stdin` to keep only ignored files, copied with `copyfile(COPYFILE_CLONE)` (APFS clone) in one background step, caps on file count and bytes (for example 500 files / 50 MB), symlinks and paths escaping the repo skipped, existing targets never overwritten. This is a bounded one-shot, not a watcher. Fidelity with Claude's `**/` corner case is unverified (experiment 2).
4. Provenance: extend the branch read (`BranchCache`, already keyed per folder and refreshed at turn boundaries and activation) to also return "linked worktree" and the worktree name from the same `.git` file it already opens (no extra I/O, no exec). `SessionCardView` second row and the `SessionHeaderChip` show a small worktree glyph before the branch, tooltip with the path.
5. Removal ("Remove Worktree..." in the card context menu and the header ⋯ menu, a separate explicit action; contract §5 says worktrees are not an automatic side effect of chat deletion, and `CatalogModel+Deletion` already tells the user the worktree stays). Ownership rule without a registry: only a path that equals the working_directory of at least one catalog session, lies under the configured Loom worktree root, is a linked worktree, and has no live run in it (supervisor knows). Dry run reuses `CleanupWorktreeProtection.verdict` (uncommitted, unpushed, stash) but reports counts and file names instead of a bare "protected"; refuses on dirty or unpushed (no force in the UI; user uses git in the terminal, or commits/pushes first). Execution: `git worktree remove <path>` without `--force`, then verify the directory is gone and `<commondir>/worktrees/<name>` no longer exists (file reads). The branch is never deleted by Loom in v1 (herdr and Codex also keep it). The dialog lists the sessions that ran there and says they stay readable (ended screen, transcript) but cannot be resumed from Loom (`requireDirectory` refuses a missing folder); deleting them is the user's separate action. Note: the existing stash rule is repository-wide (stash refs are shared by all worktrees), so for removal it should be dropped or labelled, otherwise any stash blocks every removal.
6. Agent path (optional follow-up, S): `loom:open-session` (`OpenSessionInput`, `ClaudeLoomPlugin` skill text, `OpenRequestBoxContent`) gets `--worktree`; the approval box shows "in a new worktree EDDP-123 from main"; the ticket de-dup already runs first, so an agent cannot create two worktrees for one ticket; there is no agent command to remove a worktree (user authority).
7. Optional S add-on that is useful even without this idea: when Claude enters a worktree itself (EnterWorktree, doc says hook `cwd` follows it), the card keeps showing the main checkout's branch because the catalog holds the launch folder. `ClaudeHookEvent.workingDirectory` is parsed but unused; keep an in-memory observed cwd per run and feed it to `BranchCache.refresh` at turn boundaries. Not persisted.

**What is deliberately not built now:** the reserve pool (Emdash built it in Jan 2026 and removed it in Apr 2026 for stale bases and orphans), a registry table or a hard-coded directory scan (ownership comes from catalog rows plus path containment), a storage list with keep-N cleanup (Cursor's cleanup deletes worktrees it did not create; Vibe Kanban's GC removed active ones; revisit only if disk becomes a real problem at 2-3 parallel sessions), per-project setup/run/archive scripts (arbitrary command execution; Cursor gates it behind workspace trust; if wanted later it needs per-project approval showing the literal command, run in a visible Loom-owned session, never hidden), a reserved port range (`LOOM_PORT_BASE`-style env is a one-line addition to `ProviderLaunchProfile.claude` but only helps scripts the user parameterises; add when asked), grouping of manually made linked worktrees by reading `.git` (today's workaround: Add Project on the worktree folder), diff/PR/merge UI (git-client creep).

**Bounds.** Git execs: only on user action, one owned helper at a time, 10-15 s timeout, bounded output (`LaunchEnvironment.runHelper`). Copy: caps above. No git run on list load, selection or idle. Sidebar cost: none beyond the existing branch read.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Entry points: (1) project header "+" gets a context menu / long press with "New Session in Worktree..." (the plain click still starts a normal session at once, D-10 stays); the File menu and palette-less app get "New Session in Worktree..." (Shift+Cmd+N is taken by Codex, so a different key, decided later). (2) A small sheet (420 pt like RenameSheet): one field "Ticket or branch name" (prefilled from a ticket key if the sidebar search holds one), a read-only line "Branch EDDP-123 from origin/main (not fetched)", a line "Will copy N files from .worktreeinclude" when the file exists, Create (default action). Errors inline in the sheet; no second confirmation. While git runs the sheet shows a spinner (3-14 s possible on big repos, Emdash baseline) and the session opens in the project's group when done. (3) The card's second row shows a worktree glyph before the branch (same monochrome symbol class, no new colour); the header chip does the same, tooltip = path. (4) Remove: "Remove Worktree..." in the card and header menus opens a sheet in the style of `DeleteConversationSheet`: path, branch, which sessions ran there, "Clean: nothing uncommitted, all commits pushed" or the refusal with counts and the first file names, Remove (disabled when refused). Result banner states what is verified ("Worktree removed; branch EDDP-123 kept").
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass. Git only on explicit actions through the owned, timed `captureHelper`; no watchers, no polling, no pool; badge reads the file the branch read already opens. Risk: the copy step on a huge ignored tree, bounded by caps; dependency installs per worktree (~200 MB each in one Codex user's report, single post) are the user's, Loom adds none. Predictable: pass if the base is shown and never fetched, a name/path collision is refused (no silent reuse, unlike Claude's reopen-by-name), and creation never rolls back by deleting. Accurate status: pass only if 'created' means git exit 0 plus `GitBranch.read == named(branch)`, and 'removed' means exit 0 plus the directory and the admin folder gone; partial states (created with copy warnings, created but launch failed) are named, not hidden. Fluency: pass for create (one field, Enter), the only confirmation is the destructive removal. Modularity: pass; one new core file with an injected capture (testable on real temp repos like `CleanupCoordinatorTests`), one runtime parameter, two small UI files; no change to the hook state machine or schema. CLI-update resilience: pass, and the main reason not to use `claude -w`: no new Claude flag, nothing to pin; the only Claude coupling is `.worktreeinclude`, a documented file. Ownership: pass with the rule 'only a path a Loom session ran in, under Loom's root, with no live run'; weak point is a worktree whose last session was deleted (not removable from Loom). User authority: pass; agents can only ask (approval box) to open a session in a worktree and cannot remove anything. Violations to avoid: becoming a git client (no fetch, no status polling, no PR/merge), silent GC, `--force`, hidden setup commands, a second lifecycle owner next to Claude's sweep (worktrees Loom creates carry no Claude marker, so Claude's sweep keeps them). Standing decisions: D-34 and the 'terminal is the real CLI' contract rule are untouched; contract §5/§12 'worktrees are not a side effect of chat deletion' is respected by making removal separate; D-26 cleanup already protects dirty/unpushed worktrees.
feasibility.value_reason: It removes a real ritual for the EDDP ticket-per-session flow (git worktree add, copy .env, Add Project, later clean up) and keeps the user inside Loom, which a "main app" needs, and Loom's existing per-session cwd, ticket de-dup and worktree check make it cheap. But it is not daily: the field data says realistic interactive parallelism is 2-3 sessions across projects, review is the bottleneck, worktrees do not isolate ports/DBs/.env state, Claude Desktop and `claude -w` already cover the basic case, and the same-repo collision frequency for this user is unknown, so 3 rather than 4.
experiments: E1 trust dialog and prompt delivery (isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, temp repo, real Claude, a few short turns): start `claude --session-id <uuid> --settings <loom hooks> -- "msg"` with cwd = (a) sibling folder worktree, (b) <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<key>, (c) a folder under Loom's data root. Decides the default worktree root and whether the first message survives a workspace-trust dialog (if every new path shows the dialog, prefer (b) or tell the user once). Also record the hook `cwd` and the transcript's encoded folder.

E2 .worktreeinclude fidelity: on a fixture repo with .env, config/secrets.json, a gitignored build directory and a `**/` pattern, compare `git ls-files -z -o --exclude-from=.worktreeinclude` + `git check-ignore --stdin` against what `claude -w` copies; decides reimplement-as-is versus a documented deviation, and the file/byte caps.

E3 resume and removal edge cases: `claude --resume <id>` from the worktree folder (Loom's way), the same after `git worktree remove` (expected: Loom refuses via requireDirectory; check what Claude itself does and whether a transcript from a removed folder still reads in the ended screen and the usage index), and `git rev-list --count HEAD --branches --not --remotes` on a never-pushed zero-commit ticket branch (expected 0, so a clean new worktree is removable).

E4 creation time on the user's largest work repo (the user runs one `git worktree add --no-track -b` and reports seconds): decides whether the foreground spinner is enough or creation must become a visible background step like Emdash's Activity badge.

Branch convention: the bare ticket key (EDDP-123), or key plus slug, and which base (origin/main, develop, current HEAD)? Loom would show the base and never fetch.
Where may worktrees live: <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<key> (Claude's own layout, needs a gitignore entry, trust likely inherited), a sibling folder, or under Loom's data folder? E1 informs this.

Is guarded removal wanted in the first slice, or is `git worktree remove` in the terminal (git itself refuses dirty trees) enough at first? May Loom ever delete the branch (only when merged), or never?
Should an agent be able to ask for a worktree through `loom:open-session --worktree` (approval box as today), and should the stash rule block removal even though stashes are repo-wide?
Setup commands (npm/mvn install, docker) per worktree: skip and let the first prompt or Claude do it, or build a per-project approved command later?

feasibility.one_line: Build the new-session sheet, JSON presets/recipes and a prefill-only URL on Loom's existing launch path, show the permission mode from the documented hook field, and drop the skills browser, hotkey and Loom-side worktree creation (worktrees wait for I-32).
feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS CHECKED
- Starting a session today is one click and carries no options: CatalogModel.startConversation -> ConversationController.start -> SessionRuntime.startConversation(provider:projectID:opening:) -> claudeProfile -> ProviderLaunchProfile.claude. Only --session-id, --settings, --plugin-dir, resume-time --effort and the D-40 opening (-n title, then "-- message") are passed. Loom passes no permission-mode flag and no model flag.
- The installed CLI (2.1.300 --help) documents --permission-mode <mode> (choices acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk, plan), --effort, --model, -n/--name, and -w/--worktree [name]. ProviderCapabilities already parses --help for --effort and --name, and missingRequiredClaudeOptions/reportCompatibility already log drift without refusing a start. "Show plan mode only when detected" therefore needs one more parsed option plus a parsed choices list.
- Claude's docs list permission_mode as a common hook-input field ("manual" arrives as "default"; not every event carries it). Loom's ClaudeHookEvent does not parse it (grep finds no permission_mode in Sources). Showing the mode on the card can come from this documented field, so it stays right after the user presses Shift+Tab, instead of from launch intent.
- There is no URL scheme anywhere (no CFBundleURLTypes in scripts/package-dev-app.sh or scripts/release/build-loom.sh; no application(_:open:) in loom-app). The control socket used by "a session opens a session" is authenticated by a live session's LOOM_HOOK_TOKEN and always ends in the approval box. A URL has no token, so it cannot reuse that gate as it is.
- Catalog sessions already store workingDirectory per session, project, ticket_key (SessionCatalog.session(projectID:ticket:) is the de-dup lookup) and opened_by. SessionOpening.openedBy is a non-optional UUID today; createSession already takes it optional.
- Worktrees: documented claude --worktree creates .claude/worktrees/<name> on branch worktree-<name>, then the session's cwd and transcript move there. Loom's catalog working directory would stay the repo root, so GitBranch.read (card and header branch) would show the wrong branch. CleanupCoordinator's linked-worktree protection and Loom's resume assumptions would not see it. The CLI's own exit prompt (keep or remove) never appears because Stop kills the process. A worktree Loom creates itself (git worktree add, then start with workingDirectory = the worktree) keeps all of that consistent, but it is the worktree-lifecycle work of I-32 and must not be smuggled in here.

LIGHTEST DESIGN (four layers, each independently shippable)
1. Launch options in LoomCore (the base for everything else). New value type ClaudeStartOptions {permissionMode?, effort?, model?} passed into ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(route: .new) next to opening. ProviderCapabilities gains supportsPermissionMode and permissionModes (the choices parsed from the --permission-mode help block). The sheet offers only modes that are both detected and on Loom's allowlist (Manual, Plan, Accept Edits, Auto). bypassPermissions and dontAsk are not offered anywhere in v1 (user authority; the user can still Shift+Tab inside the TUI). Not detected means the control is hidden, and an undetected flag is not passed. SessionOpening becomes "SessionStart intent": title?, firstMessage?, ticketKey?, openedBy: UUID? (nil = the user started it), options. SessionRuntime.startConversation takes it; the D-40 path keeps passing no options, so an agent can never choose a mode (an agent-requested session cannot escalate).
2. New Session sheet (LoomCatalogUI, e.g. NewSessionSheet.swift + NewSessionModel, presented from CatalogModel). Fields: project (defaults to contextProjectID; the two work projects first, then others, plus "No project"), ticket key, title (auto), mode, effort, first message (multi-line; a leading "/skill args" works because that is how the CLI is typed, so no skills browser is needed). Empty state: the project list and "Recent tickets" from one bounded catalog query (DISTINCT sessions.ticket_key by last_activity_at, LIMIT 8) run when the sheet opens. While the user types a ticket key, the sheet does the same de-dup lookup as OpenSessionCoordinator and shows "EDDP-123 already has a session - Show" instead of starting a copy. Return/Cmd+Return starts; Esc closes. Start goes through the same ConversationController.start path, so busy/starting state, startingNew guard and error reporting are unchanged. Cmd+N keeps the instant one-click start; the sheet is a second entry (proposal: Option+Cmd+N, footer + menu "New Session...", project "+" menu).
3. Presets = recipes (one concept, not two). One JSON file per preset in <data root>/presets/<name>.json (Foundation Codable, no TOML dependency; Loom has no TOML parser and SwiftTerm is the only package). Fields: name, project (exact name or path, resolved at use like --project in OpenSessionInput, never created), ticketTemplate?, title template?, permissionMode?, effort?, model?, message template with {ticket}/{title} placeholders. No colour field (projects already carry D-48 colours). PresetStore is a small LoomCore type: read the folder when the + menu or sheet opens (on demand, at most 64 files of at most 64 KiB, lstat/regular-file checks, atomic 0600 write, unknown keys ignored so a newer file does not break an older Loom). No FSEvents watcher in v1. "Save this session as preset" (session context menu, SessionMenuItems) writes a preset from the card's project and the options Loom started it with. A preset chosen in the + menu with a clear, safe summary (e.g. "plan, high, project") starts at once or opens the sheet prefilled when the preset has a {ticket} placeholder.
4. loom:// as a PREFILL-ONLY entry. The handler (AppDelegate application(_:open:), URL parsed by a pure, tested function in LoomLaunchOptions or LoomCatalogUI) only opens the sheet with the preset (or explicit query items project/ticket/title/message) filled in. It never starts a session; the user presses Start in Loom with the full resolved message and options visible. That keeps the same user-authority rule as D-40, defends against any web page or local process firing a URL, and means no new socket or token. Dev builds register a different scheme (BuildIdentity owns production vs development names) so Loom Dev and Loom never fight for the handler. URLs received before the runtime is up are held until startupTask finishes. Raycast calls "open loom://preset/<name>".
Later and optional, on the user's word: a per-preset "start without asking" flag for trusted presets from the + menu only (never from URL).

NOT BUILT (and why)
- Skills/commands browser: the CLI's "/" menu already lists them, and a Loom-side lister must reproduce Claude's resolution rules (user, project, plugin, bundled, skillOverrides, user-invocable false, .claude/commands) and read the user's real ~/.claude. That is the drift and ownership risk the principles warn about. The free-text first message already takes "/skill args". Revisit only if the user later says discovery hurts.
- Global quick-capture hotkey: it is a different feature (queue a prompt to a session) and Raycast + the URL cover launching.
- Cursor plan tab / Build in Parallel: confirmed skip; plan mode is only the --permission-mode plan flag, and the plan stays in the terminal (contract: terminal is the real CLI).
- Loom-created worktrees or claude --worktree: belongs to I-32. Until it lands, a preset may carry an optional absolute directory (resolved and checked like a project) so a worktree the user made by hand can be started; nothing is created or removed here.

WHAT TO SHOW AFTER LAUNCH
Parse permission_mode (and optionally effort.level) from the documented hook JSON in ClaudeHookEvent, keep the latest value in the tracker's view state (only when the field is present; "default" displays as Manual), and show it as a small text chip in the detail header or tooltip, with no new status colour and no new animation. This is observation, not launch intent, so it is accurate after Shift+Tab. It is an independent slice (S) and would also serve other ideas, so it could ship first.

WHERE IT HURTS IF DONE WRONG
Polling/watchers for presets or skills, a permanent socket for URLs, a URL or agent that can start without a click, a bypass mode in one click, a Loom-side worktree that leaves the card showing the wrong branch, an options UI that goes stale when the CLI changes its choices. The design above avoids each by being launch-time only, on-demand reads, detection-gated, and approval-gated at the external boundary.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Entry points: footer "+" menu gets "New Session..." (Option+Cmd+N) and a "Presets" submenu listing each preset as "Name  -  project, plan, high" (a non-empty first line, since the user must see what a click will do); project header "+" menu gets the same project-scoped; File menu keeps Cmd+N as the instant start. Session context menu: "Save as Preset...".

The sheet is a compact palette-style panel (about 460 pt wide, 10 pt radius, theme tokens, appears with opacity only): row 1 project picker with the project colour stripe (work projects first); row 2 ticket field with a Recent chips line under it (EDDP-142, EDDP-139, ...) and an inline "already has a session - Show" notice when it matches; row 3 title (auto placeholder); row 4 two compact pop-ups, Mode (only detected ones) and Effort (only when --effort is detected); row 5 first message editor (3-8 lines); footer: Presets popup on the left, Cancel / Start (Cmd+Return) on the right. Empty state when no project is selected: the project rows themselves, so the first keystroke picks one. A preset or URL opens it prefilled and the Start button shows the resolved mode and effort in its label. After launch the card behaves as today; the header chip shows the live mode ("Plan") from the hook field. No new window chrome, no animation, no status words on cards (DESIGN section 2.4 holds).
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass. Everything is launch-time; presets and recent tickets are read on demand (bounded 64 files x 64 KiB; one LIMIT 8 query); no timer, watcher or process is added, and a closed sheet draws nothing. Risk only if someone adds a preset folder watcher or a skills scanner. Predictability: pass. Same start path, same startingNew guard; a preset's resolved options are shown before an external launch; project is resolved by exact name/path, never created. Accurate status: pass with one rule. 'Started' still means the verified scope launch. The permission mode on the card comes from the hook field and is hidden when absent; Loom must not claim a launch-time flag was applied, so a flag it did not detect is never shown or passed. Fluency: pass. One extra keystroke for URL starts is the deliberate cost; the + menu preset start can be one click. Modularity: pass. New code sits in three seams (ClaudeStartOptions/capabilities in LoomCore, PresetStore in LoomCore, sheet in LoomCatalogUI); nothing touches the terminal, supervisor or ledger. CatalogModel is already 1,600+ lines, so the sheet model must live in its own file and extension. CLI-update resilience: pass with a spike. Options are gated on parsed --help text like --effort/--name; the permission choices list is parsed, not hard-coded; unknown choices are ignored and the missing-option notice goes to the journal. The 'manual' versus 'default' naming already differs between flag and hook, which is exactly the drift the parse must tolerate. Process ownership: pass. No new process or socket; worktree creation (which would own files outside the run scope) is deliberately deferred to I-32. User authority: the key risk. The URL is prefill-only, agent-initiated opens (loom-hook open) get no mode or effort argument, bypassPermissions/dontAsk are not offered, and presets are user-authored files that an agent could in principle write, so any preset from outside the + menu goes through the sheet. D-20 (settings that change Claude behaviour are the user's decision) is satisfied because the user picks each option per launch. Contract: pass; the terminal remains the interface and no chat UI is added. D-34 is not touched.
feasibility.value_reason: The user already runs about three parallel sessions across two ticket-keyed work projects, and today each start is a bare click followed by retyping the same plan-mode preamble or ticket prompt. The sheet's ticket de-dup, plan mode, effort and first message remove that, and Raycast/URL starts help a backend dev who works across apps. The gain is real but bounded: the instant Cmd+N already exists, plan mode can be reached with Shift+Tab, and the heaviest pieces of the original idea (worktrees, skills browser) are deferred or dropped.

feasibility.one_line: Adopt only the cheap half (ticket chip, search by key, a user-side 'New session from ticket' sheet using variant (b), reusing the shipped de-dup); defer the Work ledger and tracker write-back, because Loom has no per-session branch or PR state to derive them from yet.
feasibility.loom_design:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (read): sessions.ticket_key and opened_by columns (CatalogDatabase.ensureOriginColumns, added on open without a version bump); CatalogSession.ticketKey/openedBy (SessionCatalog.swift:36-47); SessionCatalog.session(projectID:ticket:excluding:) does the de-dup by ticket_key, else a title that starts with the key (SessionCatalog+Sessions.swift:23); OpenSessionInput validates the key (1-40 of [A-Za-z0-9-_.], OpenSessionProtocol.swift:48-57); SessionRuntime.startConversation(opening:) launches Claude with `-n <title> ... -- <message>` through ProviderLaunchProfile.ClaudeOpening, so the first message is argv and needs no PTY injection or delivery verification. GAPS found: (1) ticket_key is only ever set on the agent-initiated path (loom:open-session, D-40); a session the user starts by hand never has one. (2) ticket_key is not shown anywhere in the UI (only OpenRequestDisplay) and search matches only provider, title and project name (SessionCatalog+Paging.swift:44-49). (3) SessionOpening.openedBy is a non-optional UUID (SessionRuntime.swift:160-167), so the user-initiated start needs it made optional (CatalogSession.openedBy is already optional and the sidebar origin line treats nil as 'user started'). (4) Branch is read per working directory (GitBranch.read, BranchCache keyed by path) and Loom sessions run in the project folder; Loom never creates worktrees. Every session of a project shares one branch, so 'ticket -> branch -> PR' per session is not derivable today.

DESIGN, three small slices, all event-driven:
A. Chip + find (no new state). Display key = ticket_key, else a leading key in the title that matches a user-set prefix list (e.g. EDDP); a bare `[A-Z]+-\d+` regex is wrong ('UTF-8', 'GPT-4', 'SHA-256'). A pure function next to SessionDisplay.swift, evaluated on the record already in memory: no IO, no timer. Draw it in card row 2 beside the branch (SidebarView ~l.460-480; collapse it into the branch slot when narrow, like the origin line) and in ProjectBranchChip (SessionHeaderViews.swift). Add `loom_fold(s.ticket_key) LIKE` to the search condition so typing EDDP-123 finds every session of the ticket across projects; this is the 'where was I' answer for the ticket dimension and reuses CatalogModel+Search.swift unchanged. Prefix list lives in UIPreferences (ui-preferences.json) or a nullable projects column added the ensureProjectColors way; the preference file is lighter.
B. New session from ticket (variant (b)). A sheet (no command palette exists in Loom; entry points: the project header '+' menu, File menu item, a shortcut): project, ticket key (validated by OpenSessionInput's rules), title prefilled '<KEY> - ', and a first-message TextEditor prefilled from a template with {key}. Default template tells Claude to fetch the ticket with the user's own Jira/Linear MCP or CLI and to wait for a go-ahead before changing code; the user can replace it with `/their-skill {key}`. The sheet shows exactly what will be sent, editable; nothing is sent until the button is pressed (user is the authority, so no approval box; the agent-opened path keeps its box). On key entry and again at submit, call the shipped catalog.session(projectID:ticket:); if a session exists, show 'EDDP-123 already has a session: Show Session' instead of Start. Start goes through ConversationIntents.start with an opening whose openedBy is nil. Extract the 'validate, re-check ticket, startConversation(opening:)' core now duplicated between OpenSessionCoordinator.approve (~l.330-348) and the new path into one function so there is one launcher.
C. Deferred: Work list and PR/merge suggestions. They need I-31 (PR/MR state: gh or glab on demand at Stop events or window activation, not polling) AND a per-session branch identity (worktrees, or the hook payload's cwd, which ClaudeHook parses at ClaudeHook.swift:444 but nothing stores). Without both, 'In review / Merged' would be a guess, which violates accurate status. 'Needs you / Working' columns are exactly the activity view's Active section, so the ledger adds value only through the ticket dimension, which slice A already gives. Revisit after I-31 and a worktree decision. Project-view grouping by ticket also fights keyset paging (lists page by creation order per project, CatalogModel+Search/Paging), so do not group rows in v1; use the chip and search.

BOUNDS: sheet is on demand; one folded LIKE inside the existing search query; message <= 64 KiB (OpenSessionLimits); template text capped; no network, no Keychain, no tracker SDK, no webhook, no daemon.

VARIANT (a) (Loom-side fetch): not recommended. It adds Keychain tokens, per-tracker REST shapes (Jira ADF descriptions, Linear GraphQL), rate limits, tracker drift (the exact CLI-update-resilience problem Loom avoids for Claude), network access in a 'very low resource' app, and a real prompt-injection channel inside Loom's own UI path. Variant (b) puts ticket text through Claude's normal tool-result path under the user's own MCP auth. If ever added, show and delimit the fetched text and refresh at send, as Emdash does (buildFinalPrompt / refreshLinkedIssueContext).

WRITE-BACK: only ever a visible suggestion after a verified merge; skip in this idea. Emdash #1930 is contested/unconfirmed (emdash.md fact-check) so it is no evidence it works.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Sidebar card row 2: `[EDDP-123] arrow.triangle.branch feature/x` (key in the secondary text style, same size as the branch; the key replaces nothing, it is dropped first when narrow, after the origin line). Detail header chip: project stripe | EDDP-123 | branch. Search field: typing a key shows all that ticket's sessions in either view. Project header '+' menu gets 'New Session from Ticket...' (and a File menu item): a sheet with Project popup, Ticket field (inline red text if invalid, orange 'already has a session - Show Session' if the key exists in that project), Title field, a monospaced multi-line 'First message' editor prefilled from the template, buttons Cancel / Start Session (Return does not submit from inside the editor). No new sidebar mode, no right rail (D-34 untouched), terminal stays the real CLI (contract untouched).
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass (chip is pure over in-memory records; one extra folded LIKE in an existing query; sheet on demand; no polling, no network). Predictability: pass, provided the prefix list is explicit; risk if keys were guessed with a loose regex (false chips on UTF-8/GPT-4). Accurate status: pass for slices A/B (start result is the existing verified start path; de-dup is a catalog fact); RISK for slice C: showing In review/Merged without verified per-session branch and PR state would be a false-status surface, hence deferred. Fluency: pass (removes copy-paste of ticket context; the editable-before-send step is one intentional pause the user asked for). Modularity: pass if the open-request launcher is extracted and shared; risk of a second copy of the start logic otherwise. CLI-update resilience: pass (argv `-n`/`--` already used, drift already reported; variant (b) has no tracker API; a skill-name template is user content Loom does not pin). Ownership: pass (session starts in a Loom run scope as usual). User authority: pass (user-initiated, visible message; no auto-triggered sessions, no tracker writes).
feasibility.value_reason: Fits the user's two ticketed work projects and the HN-style session-per-ticket workflow in power-user-workflows.md, and de-dup is already built. But the user can already type the prompt or use their own skill, ticket text fetching depends on their MCP, and the high-value half (PR/merge-derived Work list) is blocked on I-31 and worktree identity; the research itself says the ledger duplicates the activity view and that the ceiling is 2-3 parallel sessions, so a ticket board is low leverage for one person.
depends_on: I-31 (PR/MR state, glab for GitLab) for any In review / Merged column or merge suggestion
A per-session branch identity (worktree-per-ticket convention or storing the hook payload cwd) for ticket-to-branch derivation
Making SessionOpening.openedBy optional and extracting the shared validate/de-dup/start function from OpenSessionCoordinator

Spike 3 (read-only, on the user's catalog copy or by asking): how many existing sessions' titles start with an EDDP-style key versus have ticket_key set? Decides whether the title-prefix derivation in slice A is accurate enough or needs the user to start via the sheet to get real keys.

Does the user use one git worktree per ticket? If not, a per-ticket branch and PR cannot be derived and the Work list should stay skipped.
Is a modal sheet from the '+' menu acceptable, or is a keyboard-first quick entry (shortcut, key field only, default template) preferred?
Default first-message template: 'fetch the ticket and wait', or 'fetch and plan', or a user skill name?
Should the ledger wait for I-31, or is chip + search by key enough and the Work list dropped?

feasibility.one_line: Adopt a smaller version (a click-through roll-up row of opened sessions under the parent card, a capped batch open with one approval, and a deny cool-down); put per-project always-allow, the permission ceiling and the worktree field behind a spike or later, because they are the only parts that widen standing authority and need CLI facts Loom does not read today.
feasibility.loom_design:
WHAT ALREADY SHIPS (so I-35 is smaller than it reads): sessions.opened_by and ticket_key exist in the catalog (CatalogDatabase.ensureOriginColumns; SessionRuntime.startConversation(opening:) -> ProcessSupervisor.createSession(openedBy:)). The card shows 'from <requester>' (SessionOrigin in OpenRequestDisplay.swift; CatalogModel.origin(of:), ensureOrigins/pruneOrigins; stale or deleted parent reads 'another session' via missingOrigins) and the detail view has an 'Opened by' fact (DetailView.swift:403). The approval box is already literal (project, title, ticket, 4-line message preview plus full text; OpenRequestBoxContent) and neither button is the default so Return stays with the terminal. The requester's card already goes to 'Needs approval' through awaitingOpenApproval (CatalogModel.setOpenRequests -> SessionIndicator), so it feeds Active, Dock badge, menu bar and Cmd+J. Ticket de-duplication, one waiting request per requester, a 32 waiting cap, and a 64 entry cap are in OpenSessionCoordinator. The agent already gets 'started <id> "<title>"', 'exists', 'denied', 'pending' or 'error' (OpenSessionReply.line). Starting only reports started after launchClaude succeeds, so 'session id + verified outcome' is already true for one session.

PIECE 1 - PARENT ROLL-UP (the 'nesting' + 'one signal'). Do NOT re-parent cards in the list: the activity view is day-grouped with an Active section and paged, and a child may sit in another project (--project), so a real tree would break ordering and paging. Instead add a reference row under the parent card in the exact slot where SessionListEntry (SidebarView.swift ~line 375) already draws SubagentTreeView: a pure value 'OpenedSessionsContent' modelled on SubagentTreeContent (max 3 rows, '+N more', rows = child title + SessionIndicator label, click = select child). The child keeps its own normal card. The parent's own indicator is NOT changed by a child (accurate status: the parent is not 'Needs approval' because a child is). Data: one new catalog read 'children(of: [UUID])' (SELECT ... WHERE opened_by IN (...), chunked, bounded) run when a list reload loads rows, kept in a CatalogModel map next to origins (new file CatalogModel+OpenedSessions.swift, not CatalogModel.swift which is already 1612 lines), plus a partial index CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_opened_by ON sessions(opened_by) WHERE opened_by IS NOT NULL added the same additive way as the other columns (no user_version bump; older builds ignore it). Child state comes from liveStates/rowModels that the hub already delivers; no new hook, timer or event. The only live observation is up to 3 child row models per visible parent. Distinguish Finished (unviewedCompletion), Needs approval/Waiting, Failed, Stopped/Ended (Paseo's 0.12 changelog fixed 'parent told finished when child was merely stopped'; Loom's SessionIndicator already separates these, so reuse it). Deleted child: absent from the query. Deleted parent: children keep the existing 'another session' origin; the roll-up simply has no card to sit under. /clear: requesterID is the card the run is on at ask time, so the link follows that card (documented limitation). Optional explicit gestures only: context-menu 'Stop opened sessions (N)...' that loops the existing verified stop per child with a count confirmation; 'Remove link' sets opened_by NULL. No cascade by default, no cascade on Stop of the parent, no cascade on delete (contract §8/§234: deleting a chat is not a side effect on others).

PIECE 2 - BATCH OPEN. The single-request protocol cannot just be called N times: the agent's calls are sequential and each blocks up to 85 s, then gets 'pending - do not ask again' (OpenSessionLimits.serverReplyDelay), and the coordinator rejects a second undecided request from the same requester. So add one batch call: '"$LOOM_CLI" open-batch --file plan.json' where plan.json is a JSON array of {title, ticket?, message|messageFile} (OpenSessionCommand parse; OpenSessionInput.validated per item). Wire: optional 'items' array on OpenSessionWireRequest (decodeIfPresent; loom-hook and the app are one bundle, so there is no CLI-version skew on this socket; keep protocolVersion handling). Caps: at most 5 items (constant OpenSessionLimits.maximumBatch), per-item rules unchanged (64 KiB), wireByteLimit raised to ~1 MiB, duplicate ticket keys inside a batch rejected, items whose ticket already has a session answered 'exists' at submit and not shown for approval. Coordinator: a batch is one Entry holding N request items that share a batch id and one waiter; the UI shows one sheet/box in the requester's detail pane listing every item literally (project, title, ticket, message preview each expandable) with per-item Skip and two buttons 'Open N sessions' / 'Deny all', plus a cost note: 'N more live Claude sessions will start (M are running now)' - a count only, no invented RAM figure. Approval must start items strictly one after another (startConversation guards (provider, project) with startingNew -> alreadyStarting, and each start needs its own TerminalSurface from ConversationController.approveOpen), and each item reports its own outcome. Reply is one line per item in order ('started <id> "<title>"', 'exists ...', 'skipped', 'error: ...'); exit 0 only when every non-skipped item started or exists, 1 otherwise. Partial failure is reported per item and never retried (contract §7: no blind retry). If the 85 s wait lapses first the agent gets one 'pending' and learns no ids - state this plainly in the skill text; see experiment 2 for lifting the wait. Update ClaudeLoomPlugin.skill (it is written from source into <data root>/claude-plugin, so it follows the app version) and the OpenRequestEvidence rows.

PIECE 3 - RATE LIMIT. In-memory per requester: after a Deny (or 3 requests in 10 min), the coordinator answers 'denied: the user declined recently, do not ask again' without drawing a new box for a cool-down; the box count and 32-waiting cap stay as the hard bound. No persistence, no timer: the cool-down is a timestamp compared on the next submit.

DEFERRED PIECE 4 - ALWAYS-ALLOW + CEILING (spike-first, ship only together). A pure LoomCore struct OpenSessionPolicy (project id + action 'open') stored in Loom's own preferences/app_state (never in ~/.claude), evaluated event-driven in CatalogModel.setOpenRequests when a request arrives (the UI layer must call approveOpenRequest because the start needs a TerminalSurface), listed and revocable in Settings, with a per-start 'auto-approved' mark in the child's Opened-by fact. Hard limits if built: same project as the requester only (--project elsewhere always asks), only requests whose requester was not itself auto-opened (depth 1, because every session has $LOOM_CLI and a chain would otherwise self-propagate, contract §7 'a chain beyond the user's task is not authorized'), at most 3 auto-opens per requester per 10 min, a global live-session cap, never batches, never delete/send-to-session. Ceiling: Loom passes no --permission-mode today (ProviderLaunchProfile.claude builds only --session-id/--resume, effort, --settings with hooks and crossSessionInbound:refuse, --plugin-dir, -n and the prompt), so a child silently gets the user's settings default, which can be broader than a caller the user toggled to plan mode. To enforce 'child <= caller' Loom would parse the documented common hook field permission_mode (ClaudeHookEvent in ClaudeHook.swift currently ignores it), keep the latest value per run in ClaudeHookStateTracker, and launch the child with the documented --permission-mode <same>. If the value is unknown/unmappable or --permission-mode is missing from claude --help (same pattern as ProviderLaunchProfile.missingRequiredClaudeOptions), always-allow is simply unavailable and the box asks as today.

DEFERRED PIECE 5 - WORKTREE FIELD. Loom has no worktree code at all (grep: only cleanup-planner mentions); the field belongs to the separate 'new session in worktree' idea. Do not couple it here.

WHAT THE IDEA TEXT CLAIMS BUT ALREADY EXISTS OR BELONGS ELSEWHERE: 'results return as session id + verified outcome' exists for one session; 'child finished' as a return value to the agent (wait verb) is the separate read-only orchestration idea (T3) and must be event-driven from hook transitions, not polled.

feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: PASS for pieces 1-3 - no timer, no polling, no new hook events; one bounded catalog read per list reload and at most 3 child observations per visible parent; the batch cost is N real live CLIs, so it is capped (5) and the live count is shown; nothing is drawn when the window is hidden because the roll-up is ordinary sidebar content. The CPU gate is unaffected (no PTY output path touched), though a 5-session start burst should be measured once on an idle machine. RISK: unbounded child lookup (avoid by chunked IN with a cap) and reading child state for off-screen parents (avoid: only visible entries observe).
Predictability: PASS if the batch box shows every item literally and nothing starts without the press; RISK: a batch approved as a blob hides what each session will be told - hence per-item preview and Skip, cap 5, no always-allow on batches.
Accurate status: PASS - per-item verified outcomes (started only after launchClaude succeeds, 'exists' never counted as started), partial failure per item, no retry, parent never inherits a child's state, stopped is not finished. RISK: the 85 s reply window (an approval after it leaves the agent with only 'pending'); the skill must say so and experiment 2 may remove it. RISK: roll-up uses opened_by which is attribution not liveness - a child whose parent card was /cleared points at the old card.
Fluency: PASS - one approval instead of N, one-click jump to a child, no prompt injected into the parent's PTY. RISK: approval still lives in the requester's detail pane (the user must go there; Cmd+J and the Needs-approval indicator already lead there).
Modularity: PASS - batch grouping in the coordinator, roll-up as a pure content struct plus new extension file, policy as a pure LoomCore struct; LoomCore stays UI-free and nothing moves up the dependency graph.
CLI-update resilience: PASS for 1-3 (only Loom's own socket, command and skill; the plugin is a documented --plugin-dir mechanism written from app source). Piece 4 RISK: depends on the documented permission_mode hook field and --permission-mode choices (help lists acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk, plan, which are not guaranteed to equal the hook's strings, e.g. 'default' vs 'manual'); designed to disable itself on drift, never to pin.
Ownership: PASS - children are ordinary Loom-started runs in their own run scopes; cascade-stop is a loop of the existing verified stop per child and only as an explicit gesture; no process is ever started or stopped by the link itself.
User authority: PASS for 1-3 (approval per request or per batch, as D-40 and contract §7 require). Piece 4 is a standing authorization that amends D-40 ('starts only after the user approves') and §7, and a prompt-injected parent could use it to start an agent with an arbitrary first message with no human gate; Supacode's 'Always allow' is global and unscoped (fact-check), OpenChamber's tool is on by default with no per-action approval (partly: OpenCode's own tool permissions still apply), Vibe Kanban's MCP has no approval step - none of that may be copied. Paseo's default cascade-archive of children is likewise not copied.
feasibility.value_reason: The user runs several sessions and ticket-keyed multi-agent flows, which is exactly why D-40 was built, so a legible parent-to-children view and one approval for a multi-ticket plan are real wins. But the single-session flow already approves in one click with a literal box, the 'from <parent>' origin already exists, and the finish/needs-you of any child already reaches Active, the Dock badge, the menu bar and Cmd+J. The remaining gain is mostly the batch and the glanceable roll-up; the high-risk part (always-allow) buys one saved click on a rare action. Unknown: how often the user's agents actually call open-session today (no usage data in the repo).
depends_on: D-40/D-42 shipped open-session flow (no dependency on new work)
Piece 5 (worktree field) depends on the separate 'new session in worktree' idea; Loom has no worktree code
'child finished returned to the asking agent' (a wait verb) belongs to the separate read-only orchestration verbs idea (T3-style) and needs its own approval model
Piece 4 needs a user decision to amend D-40 and contract §7 before any build
experiments: E1 permission-ceiling spike (isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, no real ~/.claude): run claude 2.1.300 with a temp --settings hook that logs the raw payload, once per --permission-mode choice, plus a Shift+Tab toggle mid-turn. Decides: do the hook's permission_mode strings map 1:1 onto the --permission-mode choices (manual vs default naming), is the last event's value fresh enough when 'open' runs inside a turn, and is there a defensible ordering for 'not broader than' given auto and dontAsk. If any answer is no, piece 4 is dropped, not approximated.

E2 late-approval return: with the fake provider or an isolated Claude, test whether the open command can safely wait well beyond 85 s (Claude's Bash tool default timeout is about 2 min; background execution exists). Decides whether the 85 s pending-and-forget limit can be lifted so the agent always gets session ids after a slow approval, or whether the skill should instruct run-in-background. Pure protocol test, no real approvals needed.

E3 start-burst cost: start 5 sessions through the batch path against the fake provider first, then once with real Claude on an idle machine (only when the user says it is idle), reading Loom's existing process sampling. Decides the default cap (5 vs 3) and whether the cost note needs a measured memory figure.

feasibility.loom_design:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (observed in code; the idea is smaller than it reads)
- LOOM_SESSION_ID is already exported to every hosted session (LaunchEnvironment.make, Sources/LoomCore/LaunchEnvironment.swift:70). LOOM_MANAGED_RUN_ID is set in ProcessSupervisor.swift:325. LOOM_CLI (the bundled loom-hook binary), LOOM_CONTROL_SOCKET and LOOM_HOOK_TOKEN are set in ProviderLaunchProfile.swift:149-153. LOOM_PROJECT is not needed: the server derives the project from the caller's session, which is one fewer env var to drift. The herdr-style gate already exists as "Only inside Loom, where $LOOM_CLI is set" in ClaudeLoomPlugin.skill.
- The control socket (OpenSessionControlServer in OpenSessionProtocol.swift, c-<8>.sock, token compare, 32 in-flight cap, connection held per request, continuation-based so it holds no thread) and its authorize rule (SessionRuntime.swift:316: supervisor.runContext(runID) live AND launchSessionID == LOOM_SESSION_ID; returns the card the run is on now, so /clear is handled) already give "this session" plus run binding. A run ending makes authorize return nil, which is already the "revoked on stop" behaviour T3's per-session credentials buy, so do not add a second credential system. The token is shared by all sessions of one app run and readable by any same-uid process, so scoping is a guard against mistakes and prompt confusion, not a security boundary; say so in the docs.
- SessionEventHub (actor) already is the event source: subscribe() yields the current snapshot first and then frames, so "snapshot, then wait on events" is race-free by construction (herdr needed an explicit sequence snapshot because it polls at 100 ms). SessionViewState carries runID, status (ProviderWorkState incl. pendingProviderWorkCount), identity, issue, stopFailure, blockers, subagents.

DESIGN (slice 1)
1. Protocol: generalise the open-only wire shape (OpenSessionWireRequest v1) into a verb envelope {version, token, sessionID, managedRunID, verb, args}; keep `open` byte-compatible. Reply is JSON plus a one-line text form for agents. Server answers an explicit "unsupported version, update the Loom skill/app" instead of "malformed" (API versioned, mismatch detected, nothing pinned). Client side: extend OpenSessionCommand.run (191 lines) or add a sibling ControlCommand in LoomCore; loom-hook/main.swift already routes any argument to the agent command, so no new binary.
2. Verbs (4 at most): `sessions [--json] [--limit N]`, `status <id|self> [--json]`, `wait <id> --until needs-you|finished|failed [--timeout S]`, and nothing else. `open` stays as is and keeps its approval card. Ids are read from output, never predicted (`started <id>` from open already returns the child id, which is the main wait target).
3. Scope rule enforced server-side: the target must be in the caller's project, or be a session the caller opened (catalog `opened_by`). `sessions` lists live sessions (hub snapshot, bounded) plus at most N recent catalog rows (default 50, hard cap 200) with id, title, ticket, project, branch only if already cached, status, running. Cross-project only if the user turns it on (a Settings switch is the only UI this ever needs).
4. Status vocabulary lives in LoomCore. SessionIndicator (Sources/LoomCatalogUI/SessionDisplay.swift, 243 lines) is a pure function of CatalogSession and SessionViewState but sits in LoomCatalogUI, and LoomCore may not import UI. Move it (or its derivation core) into LoomCore so the card, the menu bar, Cmd+J and the CLI cannot disagree. That mechanical move is the largest hidden cost. Verb states: working | needs-approval | waiting-input | finished | failed | ready | ended | unknown, plus raw fields. `finished` must NOT depend on the user having viewed it (unviewedCompletion is a display concept).
5. Wait: a WaitRegistry actor in LoomCore. It subscribes to the hub only while at least one waiter exists (nothing watched otherwise), resolves waiters on frames, and cancels its subscription at zero. Pin each waiter to (sessionID, runID captured at start): a runEnded/runDetached/new runID resolves it as `ended` or `replaced`, never as success. Add a per-session `completionSeq` to SessionViewState (incremented on a turnComplete transition; the frame-level turnCompletions counter is global and the stream is bufferingNewest(1), so a fast working->complete->working could be missed). Subscribe with an unbounded or large buffer for the registry; frame rate is one per hook event. `finished` = a turn completion after the wait began, or the session is already turn-complete with pendingProviderWorkCount == 0; atPrompt/Ready (startup, resume, /clear) and unknown never count, and a Stop with background_tasks still pending stays working (the tracker already handles this, ClaudeHook.swift Stop parsing and SessionDisplay `.turnComplete where pending > 0 -> .working`). Distinct outcomes and exit codes: reached, timeout (4), ended/replaced (5), not-found/out-of-scope (2), unavailable at Quit (3, existing pattern). Caps: 16 waiters total, 4 per caller, timeout default 10 min, max 60 min; a separate waiter cap so waits cannot starve `open` of the 32 in-flight slots. Quit resolves every waiter `unavailable` (same path as pending open requests in SessionRuntime shutdown).
6. Agent teaching: extend the single loom plugin skill (ClaudeLoomPlugin.swift) with a short "look at sibling sessions" section; the always-in-context description grows by about one sentence (D-42 budget is about 80 tokens). Rules in the skill: only when the user mentions it or after `loom open`, binary --help is the syntax authority, `finished` is not approval, `unknown` does not prove completion, do not re-open after timeout, long waits run as a background shell task so the coordinator is not blocked.
7. Tests: reuse OpenSessionIntegrationTests/OpenSessionTests/SessionEventHubTests patterns with the fake provider (loom-fake-provider already emits Stop/last_assistant_message and background tasks). Deterministic counters, not timing: waiter resolved exactly once; replaced run cannot satisfy; /clear; background-task Stop does not finish; waiter count returns to zero and the hub subscriber count returns to the baseline.

WHAT TO LEAVE OUT (and why)
- `read --last-turn`: it moves one session's output into another's context (prompt-injection and data exposure), which is a content channel rather than status. If wanted later: only for sessions the caller opened, bounded to the Stop hook's last_assistant_message (already parsed, ClaudeHookEvent.lastAssistantMessage, and kept in ClaudeSessionStatus but not published to the hub, so it needs a small bounded hub field, not a transcript read), labelled as untrusted text. Needs the user's call (D-40 said cross-session messaging stays off).
- Event hooks file: the user can already run commands on "finished" with a plain Claude Stop hook in their own settings (hooks from user settings and Loom's per-session --settings all run; inferred from Claude's hook merging, verify in the spike). Loom-only value would be needs-approval/ticket-opened semantics, which the menu bar and approval notification (D-49/D-52) already cover. "worktree created" does not exist in Loom (no worktree feature). A hook runner would also be a new Loom-spawned process outside any run scope, which needs its own Quit kill and crash story (Process in its own process group, hard timeout, a helper-enforced timeout so a crash cannot leave a long orphan). Later at best.
- Settings > Scripting for the user's own shell/Raycast: any tokenless same-uid endpoint is equally callable by every agent's Bash tool, so the catalog must be read-only to be safe (rename/set_title/focus let a prompt-injected agent deceive the user or steal focus). Warp's broker model (peer-uid check, action-scoped grants) is dogfood-only at the cloned commit, so there is no field evidence. A read-only variant needs a discovery record (data root, owner-only) and a `loom` on PATH, which is an explicit user-initiated install step ("Install Command Line Tool") because it changes the user's environment. Only worth building if the user actually scripts Loom.
- `--explain`: nearly free later because everything it would list (activity, issue, identity, stopFailure, blockers, lastEventAt, hook-silence) is already in SessionViewState; do it as a header-pill popover first, CLI second.
- Per-session short-lived credentials (T3): redundant, see above.
- MCP server instead of a skill: adds a process or config per session and changes the agent's tool set (T3 does this; Loom's D-42 chose a plugin skill on purpose).
feasibility.ui_sketch: Slice 1 has no new surface: it is a command the agent runs, answered on the existing socket. Optional, only if it proves useful: a quiet "waiting on <session>" line in the coordinator card's meta row (reuse the S2 origin-line style from D-39), shown only while a wait is open. A Settings > General switch "Let sessions see other projects" (default off) is the only setting. Diagnostics export gets request/wait counters like HookDiagnostics. The later outside-shell variant would be a Settings card "Scripting" (off by default) with an "Install Command Line Tool" button and a plain line showing the socket record path; the later `--explain` is a click on the state pill in the detail header showing the signal behind the state.
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: PASS if built as designed. No polling or timers: the registry subscribes to the hub only while waiters exist and each waiter is a continuation, not a thread; `sessions` is one bounded catalog query per request; nothing is drawn or watched when no agent calls it. RISK: an agent in a loop calling `sessions` (add a per-caller rate limit) and unbounded waiter or buffer growth (hard caps above).
Predictable: PASS with explicit outcomes (reached/timeout/ended/replaced/not-found/unavailable), no blind retry, wait never auto-restarts.
Accurate status: PASS only if wait reuses the single derivation (move SessionIndicator into LoomCore) and refuses atPrompt/unknown/background-pending as `finished`. This is the main risk of the whole idea; herdr's #5263 shows what a loose notion of idle costs. Never report a missed transient as success (completionSeq).
Fluency: RISK. Every `"$LOOM_CLI" ...` Bash call in a session will hit Claude's own Bash permission prompt unless the user allows it; adding an allow rule in Loom's per-session --settings is a D-20-class change and needs the user. A foreground wait blocks the coordinator for the Bash tool's time limit; the design relies on background shell tasks (unverified, see experiments).
Modularity: PASS if the verb router, WaitRegistry and status derivation sit in LoomCore and the UI only consumes. RISK: scope creep into a full orchestration API and a second configuration language; hold at 4 verbs, no config file.
CLI-update resilience: PASS. Uses only hook-derived state Loom already trusts, a Loom-owned protocol version, no new CLI interface. Skill text is regenerated from source (ClaudeLoomPlugin) each app version. No pinning.
Ownership: PASS for slice 1 (no new process). The deferred event-hook runner would be a new Loom-spawned process family and would need its own Quit and crash handling, which is a reason to defer it.
User authority: PASS for reads of metadata in the same project; mutating verbs keep the approval card (open today; send would need its own card). RISK: `read` (content) and cross-project scope are authority questions for the user, and the shared token plus same-uid readable environment means scope is not a security boundary against a hostile agent. Contract §7 and D-40 ("cross-session messaging stays off") need an explicit new decision row before this is built.
feasibility.value_reason: It is the "follow the child" half of D-43 and the user's ticket-session workflow (a session opens an EDDP-* session through loom open and then needs to know when it finished or is blocked, without the user relaying), and it costs nothing at idle. But it only pays when a coordinator agent actually runs several top-level sessions, which is a narrow part of daily use, the human already gets the same signals from Cmd+J, the menu bar and notifications, and the outside-shell, event-hook and read parts that would widen the audience are the weakest or riskiest. Score rises to 4 if the user confirms they run coordinator-style workflows weekly.
