feasibility.one_line: Build the user-authority hand-off in two thin slices on machinery Loom already has (user-initiated send with hook-verified delivery first, then an agent `send` that reuses the open-session approval card), and do not build the full broker or govern the CLI's native channel, because native hold/accept cannot be made observable or user-authorized.
feasibility.loom_design:
SHAPE. Two slices plus a deliberate non-goal.

SLICE 1, user-initiated send (the contract's "text transfer" convenience, §7 last bullet; I-02+I-01+I-38 core). The user picks a target and text; Loom delivers it as the user's own prompt and reports verified outcomes.
- New LoomCore actor `SessionMessageCoordinator`, modelled on `OpenSessionCoordinator` (Sources/LoomCore/OpenSessionCoordinator.swift): in-memory, bounded (64 entries like `maximumEntries`), `updates()` AsyncStream for the UI, one one-shot Task per in-flight message (like its 85 s `replyDelay`), no polling. Record = id, source (session or user), target session, text, nonce, state, timestamps.
- States, all verified outcomes: queued (target not safe to type into yet) -> sent (bytes accepted by the run's TerminalInputQueue; explicitly NOT success) -> delivered (the target's UserPromptSubmit hook carried the message nonce) | stalled (no matching UserPromptSubmit within about 5 s; no automatic retry, the UI says it may or may not have arrived) | failed (target stopped, deleted, input queue closed or overflowed) | denied | expired (still queued after a TTL, or at target Stop/Quit). A "handled" mark can come from the next Stop of that run; there is no separate "read" state because Claude gives no read receipt (do not invent one).
- Trigger is event-driven: subscribe to `SessionEventHub` frames (already published on every hook/registry transition). When the target becomes prompt-safe, write once. Nothing runs while nothing is queued.
- Prompt-safe gate (the herdr #5263 lesson): deliver only when the target is `atPrompt` or `turnComplete`, or `waitingForInput` caused by `idle_prompt`/registry "idle"; never in Needs approval, Working, an elicitation/question dialog, or when `TerminalInputGate.lastInputDate(runID:)` is newer than the last turn boundary (the user may have an unsent draft or an open picker). Today `AgentActivity.waitingForInput` merges idle_prompt, elicitation_dialog and registry "idle" (ClaudeHook.swift lines 612-620, 744-748, 790-791), so the tracker needs a small `promptSafe` derivation or a cause tag; the registry's `waitingFor` field is not read at all.
- Delivery write: a header line plus the text, as one bracketed paste, then Enter. Header example `[Loom msg 7f3a9c21 - from you via Loom, session "Planner"; context from another session, not a new instruction]` (starts with "[" so the text can never be read as a slash command, `!` shell or `#` memory prefix; the nonce doubles as the confirmation token). Text-only, C0 controls except \n and \t rejected, NUL rejected, inline cap about 16 KiB (cmux 32 KiB; above the cap write a file under the Loom data folder and send its path, which is I-38's session reference). Write goes through the run's existing `TerminalInputQueue` (registered per run in `TerminalInputGate`), so ordering and overflow handling are already defined; today the queue is created inside `TerminalSurface.attach` (UI layer, ConversationController.adopt), so either `TerminalInputGate` gains `enqueue(runID:bytes:)` or the controller owns the call. Bracketed-paste wrapping must come from the surface's terminal mode (SwiftTerm), not a guess.
- Confirmation: `ClaudeHookEvent` (ClaudeHook.swift) already reads the UserPromptSubmit `prompt` only to set `promptIsSynthetic`; add a `deliveryMark` extracted from the first line (nonce only, never store the prompt). `SessionRuntime.deliver` forwards it to the coordinator -> delivered. Loom's own tracker then shows the target as Working, then Finished unviewed, with no extra status code.
- Stopped target: Resume with the message as the first prompt (`claude --resume <id> -- <msg>`; `ProviderLaunchProfile.claude` currently allows an opening only for `.new`, so that guard is relaxed for resume). No PTY typing at all on that path, delivered is still confirmed by the nonce.
- Idempotency: nonce per message; "Send again" is an explicit user action that makes a new nonce and says "may arrive twice". Never a blind retry (contract §7 "no blind automatic retry").

SLICE 2, agent-originated send under per-message approval (the D-43/D-46 channel, minimal form). Extends the D-40 stack instead of adding a second transport.
- `OpenSessionCommand` gets a `send` subcommand: `"$LOOM_CLI" send --to <session-id|ticket|title> (--message-file F | --message -)`. Same control socket (`LOOM_CONTROL_SOCKET`), same per-run token and `authorize` (SessionRuntime ensureHooks), same validation style (`OpenSessionInput.validated`), same reply/exit-code pattern. `ClaudeLoomPlugin` gets a second skill `send-to-session` (about 80 tokens in context per session).
- Natural first use: when `open --ticket K` returns `exists`, the agent can now `send` the brief into that ticket's session; D-40 said exactly this was "a later slice".
- Approval card = a new `OpenSessionRequest.Kind` (`.deliver`) in the existing `RequestList` slot above the SOURCE session's terminal: exact text (same 4-line preview + "Show full message"), source session, target session and project, buttons Deny / Send. The source card shows Needs approval meanwhile (already wired for open requests: `attention`, Cmd+J, ApprovalNotifier, Dock badge, menu bar), so approval fatigue is at least not hidden. Reply to the waiting agent: `delivered <id>` | `queued` (held until the target is safe; request stays in Loom, memory only) | `stalled` (do not resend, tell the user) | `denied` | `error: ...`; exit codes like open (0/1/2/3).
- The delivery step is Slice 1's, with the provenance header changed to say it was sent by another session's agent and is not from the user.
- Refuse by policy, before any card: unknown or deleted target, target == source, target in Needs approval or Working with the user typing, text over the cap, more than N waiting requests per source (one pending per source, like open requests).
- Loop guard without polling: count agent-to-agent hops since the last human-typed prompt in either session (a UserPromptSubmit that carries no nonce and is not synthetic resets the count); at 6 hops, the next send needs a fresh card even if a grant exists.

OPTIONAL, ONLY AFTER USE SHOWS APPROVAL FATIGUE: scoped grant "allow <source> to send to <target> until Stop or Quit": in memory, keyed by (source session, target session, action), dropped when either run ends, a new conversation id is adopted, or Loom quits; capped at 20 messages; not offered when the target runs with bypass/auto permissions (read `permission_mode` from hook payload, not parsed today; verify); not offered across projects. Every grant-delivered message still appears as a one-line log row in the target's detail view.

READ side (`loom:read-session`): defer. When wanted, answer only from data Loom already holds: `ClaudeSessionStatus.lastAssistantMessage` (set from the Stop hook, no transcript read) and state; a deeper read reuses the bounded tail reader pattern (`SubagentTranscriptTail`); cross-project reads need a card.

NON-GOAL, govern the CLI's native channel. Keep `"crossSessionInbound": "refuse"` (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift, claudeSettings). Reasons verified against the docs and the fact-check: explicit `hold` shows a per-message notice in the terminal and delivers nothing, emits no documented hook or event, so Loom cannot show "message held from X" as an accurate needs-you reason, and there is no dialog and no expiry; the approve/deny dialog belongs to the unset default and only in terminal sessions; `accept` and the unset default deliver automatically when the receiver prompts for permissions, which breaks "user-authorized only"; `refuse` on either side also disables native notify_when_idle, and Loom's own state, Cmd+J and notifications already cover "tell me when it is idle". The wire format for posting to the inbox socket is only reverse-engineered (documented: path, optional auth line, 30 s incomplete-line close). Claude agent teams are experimental and token-heavy; do not adopt. Channels (research preview, dev flag, permission relay) are a documented future transport, not a base.

KNOWN GAP (unchanged by this idea): a Loom session can still SendMessage to a Claude session outside Loom, and docs say Claude Code does not prompt for same-machine sends. Contract §7 already records this; a PreToolUse hook with matcher `SendMessage` (cost only when that tool fires) would close it, see experiment S4.

BOUNDS: text 16 KiB inline, 64 KiB wire (as open), 64 records, one pending agent request per source, TTL for queued messages (30 min proposed), nothing persisted (a queued message is lost at Quit and the card says so, same wording style as the `pending` line in OpenSessionReply.line), Quit and Stop of either side expire the record, deletion fence (SessionRuntime already fences a deleting session out of every list) turns a queued message to failed.

Accurate status: PASS. Only "delivered" when the target's own UserPromptSubmit carried the nonce; "sent" is never shown as success; stalled is a first-class result (this also acts as drift detection for the paste mechanism). Contract §7 stages (recorded, forwarded, accepted, completed) map to queued, sent, delivered, Stop seen.
Fluency: PASS for slice 1 (no confirmation, the user is the authority). Slice 2 costs one click per message, reachable by Cmd+J and notification; that is the price of authority; grants are deferred until the friction is real.
Modularity: PASS. New coordinator beside OpenSessionCoordinator, same socket, same authorize, same RequestList slot, one new Kind; the hook parser gets one field; no change to ProcessSupervisor, run scopes or the catalog schema (in-memory only).
CLI-update resilience: MODERATE RISK. Slice 1 depends on bracketed-paste input into the Claude TUI (de facto, not a documented delivery interface) and on the documented UserPromptSubmit `prompt` field (Loom already reads it); drift shows up as stalled, never as false success. The contract's CP3 "decisive case" wants a documented interface for idle live targets (asyncRewake, or resume with a prompt); PTY paste is allowed only as the user's text-transfer convenience (§7). Using it for agent-originated sends needs an explicit contract note from the user or the S3 result. Governing the native channel is rejected partly for this reason (undocumented posting format, no held-message signal).
Ownership: PASS. No new process; a resumed target goes through the normal start path inside a run scope; Stop/Quit/deletion expire records.
User authority: PASS by construction in slice 1; slice 2 requires an explicit card with the exact text and source, refuses delivery into Needs approval, labels provenance ("not an instruction from you"), cannot answer another session's approval (a prompt is not an approval; the target's own permission prompts still fire), and has a hop cap. RISK: prompt-injection chains and approval fatigue are the main residual risks; they argue against standing grants, against grants into bypass/auto targets, and against cross-project grants (the user has two work projects with separate contexts). A grant must never be global or persisted.

Slice 1 alone (send a session's last answer to another session, with an honest delivered/stalled result) is a large, cheap win and also the base of the side-chat and queue ideas. Slice 2 adds the planner-to-implementer and reviewer-back flows but carries injection and fatigue risk, so it is a 3 on its own; the full broker (grants, caps, read verb, native governance) is not worth its cost for one user and is where the 'L' of the original estimate sits.

S2, prompt-safe gate map (same isolated setup, plus the fake provider for unit coverage): for AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, MCP elicitation, a permission prompt, the trust dialog, /model and /resume pickers, record which hook events and registry statuses (`status`, `waitingFor`) Loom actually receives and what `AgentActivity` results. S3, only if agent-originated delivery must use a documented interface: an asyncRewake hook (exit code 2 wakes an idle Claude with stderr as a system reminder) backed by a helper that blocks on the Loom socket. Measure idle RSS/CPU of the waiter per session, behaviour at the enforced `timeout` and re-arming, duplicate waiters if registered on several events, and that the message shows to the model as a system reminder rather than a user prompt (changes provenance and the nonce check). Cost is zero when the tool is not used. Independent of the rest, but it is the honest completion of 'cross-session actions only under the user's authority'.

S5, resume-with-prompt: `claude --resume <id> -- <message>` under an isolated profile, with the nonce, to confirm the stopped-target path delivers through UserPromptSubmit and what the cold prompt cache costs; also whether `--settings`/plugin flags interact.
user_decisions: Is Slice 1 (you send between sessions yourself, verified) enough for the first release of this, with agent-originated sends following only after the S1/S2 results? Or do you want the planner-to-implementer agent flow in the same round?

For agent-originated sends: always one approval card per message, or may a later round add 'allow this pair until Stop or Quit' (not for bypass/auto targets, not across projects)? Prompt injection and approval fatigue pull in opposite directions.
Should messages between your two work projects (different tickets and contexts) be allowed at all, and should a read of another session's last answer need a card across projects?
A message to a stopped session: resume it automatically with the message as its first prompt (spends tokens, cold cache) or show 'stopped' and ask first?

A one-line Loom provenance header with a nonce will be visible in the target's transcript. Acceptable, or do you want the receiving side to see only the bare text (then confirmation falls back to prompt-text matching, which is weaker)?

The contract (section 7, CP3) says the decisive delivery case should use only documented interfaces and calls pasted text a user convenience. Do you accept PTY paste as the delivery for agent-originated sends once S1 passes, or must it be asyncRewake / resume (S3)?
Queued messages live in memory and are lost at Quit (the card says so). Is that acceptable, or must a queued hand-off survive Quit (which would need persistence rules from contract section 7)?

feasibility.one_line: Build a token-free, user-initiated, bounded session digest (snapshot file in a Loom-owned cache, pasted unsent into a live prompt or used to seed a fresh handoff/reviewer session) and skip the agent-driven /handoff automation and any live or agent-initiated reading, because the digest layer is cheap and fits every principle while the automation adds state machines for little gain over the user's own skill.
feasibility.loom_design:
DESIGN IN THREE LAYERS (each shippable alone; L0+L1 are the "light" core, L2 is optional in the same slice).

Layer A, core, no UI (LoomCore, new `SessionDigest.swift` + `SessionDigestStore.swift`):
- Trigger: only a user action (menu item, drag start, or "Start fresh session" sheet). No watcher, no timer, no hook subscription. Nothing runs when nobody asks.
- Locating the source: the Claude conversation id of the card (the same id `row.claudeSessionID` feeds "Copy Claude Session ID") is resolved to `<projects>/<encoded cwd>/<id>.jsonl` with the existing by-name finder `ClaudeTranscriptEffort.transcript(conversationID:projectsDirectory:)` and `SessionRuntime.claudeProjectsDirectory()`; then the same safety rules as `SubagentTranscriptLocation.resolve` (realpath inside the profile's `projects` folder, `O_NOFOLLOW`, regular file of this user). Today `SubagentTranscriptLocation` only accepts `…/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, so a sibling `SessionTranscriptLocation` (main file shape `projects/<folder>/<id>.jsonl`) is needed; the open-descriptor code in `SubagentTranscriptFile.openDescriptor()` can be shared.
- Reading: one cold read, bounded. `SubagentTranscriptTail` already does "last 512 KiB from a line start plus the first line, only whole lines, lines over 128 KiB skipped, shrink/inode replace handled"; use it once (no feed, no `SubagentTranscriptFeed`), with a larger cold window for a main transcript (about 1 MiB, tunable). The first line is delivered too, which for a main session is not the goal (see E2), so the digest also takes the first real user prompt from the head. Reading runs on a utility queue, never MainActor, and the read is a `pread` loop, so it holds no lock on Claude's file and cannot disturb the running CLI.
- Parsing: reuse the `SubagentTranscriptParser` shape (memmem gate before decode, narrow Decodable that never decodes `toolUseResult`, strings clipped at 4 KiB, tool results reduced to first line + line count + isError, tool calls reduced to the main argument). It must be extended or sibling-ed for the main file: it has no `isMeta` / `isCompactSummary` / `isSidechain` fields and treats every user text as `.brief`, so system reminders, slash-command echoes and the compaction summary would leak in as "user prompts". Those line kinds are hypotheses from the format, not verified here (see E2). Anything unknown yields nothing, as the existing parser does.
- Output (versioned markdown, hard cap about 16 KiB, about 4-5k tokens): header (source title, project, branch, ticket key if any, Claude session id, transcript path, snapshot time, state at snapshot, "last N of M turns", "turn in progress: yes/no"), the first user prompt (goal), the last N turns (default 8) as user text / assistant text / one-line tool calls / truncated tool results, the last assistant message in full up to 3 KiB, and "Files touched" (unique paths of Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit calls, max 30, separate from "files read"). A compaction summary, if found in range, is quoted once and labelled. Parse yields zero turns -> no file is written and the UI says "Loom could not read this session's transcript format" (journal `cli_compat_warning`), never an empty reference.
- Secret hygiene: best-effort redaction of common token shapes in tool-call arguments and text (sk-, ghp_/github_pat_, AKIA, "Bearer ", PEM headers, password=/token= values), stated as best-effort in the preview. The main leak surface is the Bash command first line in `toolCall` arguments; tool bodies are already reduced to first line + count by design.
- Store: `<data root>/handoffs/` (data root is `~/.loom` or `~/.loom-dev`; the same root as `<data root>/claude-plugin`), dir 0700, files 0600, name `<source short id>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.md`, written atomically (as `ClaudeLoomPlugin.install` does). Bounds: 32 KiB per file, at most 24 files, 7-day age, pruned on write and at launch. It is a derived, bounded digest, not a second copy of the transcript (contract section 7: "a second copy of the transcripts must not be kept"; this is the sentence to confirm with the user).
- Deletion: register with `ConversationForgetters.shared` (`ConversationForgetting.forget(sessionID:providerIDs:)`, called in the verifying step of `ConversationDeletion`) so permanently deleting the source session removes every digest made from it, idempotently, and a failure keeps the deletion open like other registered components. Digests record the Loom session id in a sidecar-free way (filename prefix), so no new catalog table is needed. Content already pasted or read into another session's transcript is outside deletion scope by contract section 8 ("Content sent to another session ... not deleted"); the preview says so in one line.

Layer B, reference into a live session (LoomCatalogUI + LoomTerminal, thin):
- Entry points: (1) "Reference in Prompt" and "Copy Reference" items in the card context menu and the detail header actions menu, next to the existing `SessionLocationMenuItems` group (Reveal in Finder, Copy Claude Session ID, Copy Resume Command); (2) dragging a card onto the terminal. For (2) the card supplies the digest as a lazily produced FILE URL, so the existing `TerminalSurface` drop path (`registerForDraggedTypes([.fileURL])`, `performDragOperation` -> `insertDroppedFiles` -> `pasteText`) inserts the path with no new drop code and no custom pasteboard type crossing the SwiftUI/AppKit boundary. The digest is only generated when the drop is accepted (NSItemProvider file representation), not at drag start.
- What goes into the prompt: one line, unsent, for example `Context from session "<title>" (snapshot 14:32, <project>): <digest path>`. The user finishes the sentence and presses Enter. Loom never writes a carriage return. This is deliberate: the contract says "Bracketed paste does not prove that the target is in the right prompt field or that it accepted the task", so Loom only claims "inserted into the prompt, not sent"; delivery is proven the way it already is, by the next UserPromptSubmit hook turning the card to Working.
- Target gating (the important safety rule): paste only into a live run whose indicator is at a prompt (Ready, Waiting for you, Finished; `SessionIndicator` in `SessionDisplay.swift`). Refuse for Needs approval (a dialog with numbered choices is listening: pasted characters could answer it), Failed, Problem, State unknown, Identity unclear and any session without a live terminal (ended screen, stopped, idle record). Never resume a stopped session just to receive a reference (no live terminal for idle records). Working is allowed because Claude queues typed text; the text still needs the user's Enter.
- Preview: a small popover (not a modal) before the first insert/copy of each digest shows the first 25 lines, byte size, "from project A into project B" when the projects differ, "snapshot; the source may have moved on", and Insert / Copy / Reveal buttons. This is the secret-leak check the idea asks for.

Layer C, fresh session seeded from a session (optional, same slice if cheap): "Start Fresh Session From This..." and "Start Fresh Reviewer..." in the same menus, one sheet with an editable title, an editable first-message template and the preview. It starts through the existing start path: a user-initiated sibling of `approveOpen` that calls `SessionRuntime.startConversation(provider: .claude, projectID: <same project>, opening: SessionOpening(...))` -> `ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(... opening:)` -> `-n <title> ... -- <message>`. `SessionOpening.openedBy` is the source session, so the card's existing origin line ("from <session>", D-39 S2) shows the lineage with no new UI. The message is short and zero-context: goal, "read <digest path>", "the source session's work is in this folder; run git status/diff yourself", plus an optional line the user types or a note path the user's own skill produced. Delivery is verified by the normal hook/state path (SessionStart then UserPromptSubmit/Working); a failed start is reported by the existing `RuntimeLaunch` error path and never retried.
- Reviewer variant: same folder, fresh context, template says "review, do not edit"; optional launch flags from `claude --help` 2.1.300 (verified present in help): `--permission-mode plan` for CLI-enforced read-only and `--add-dir <digest dir>` so the new session can read the digest outside its cwd without a prompt. Both are gated on the help text like the other capabilities (`ProviderCapabilities`), passed anyway if help drifts, journaled by the existing `missingRequiredClaudeOptions` pattern. Both change CLI behaviour, so they are user decisions (D-20 class), default off until decided.
- Not built: typing `/handoff` into the old session and waiting for Stop to harvest a path. Loom would have to parse model prose for a path (a guess presented as a verified outcome) and run a delivery-then-completion state machine across two sessions. The user's own skill already writes the note; the sheet just lets the user attach that path or text in one field.

Cost accounting for the idea as written (M stays honest): digest builder + location + parser extension + tests on fixture lines about 40 percent, store + forgetter + cleanup about 15 percent, menus/popover/drag provider/paste gating about 25 percent, fresh-session sheet + start path + templates about 20 percent. Layer A+B alone is S-M; the research's "S" for the reference alone is right only if the digest quality is accepted as is.

"Reference in Prompt" targets the session currently shown; from a card of another session it targets the selected session; a card's own menu on the selected session offers only Copy and Start items.

feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS. On-demand only; one bounded pread (about 1 MiB cold window, 128 KiB per-line cap, 16 KiB output); no watcher, timer, poll or process; nothing drawn when hidden; idle cost is zero. RISK: a per-card `.draggable` modifier on every sidebar card could add body evaluations to the list, which Loom guards with counters (`SidebarRenderProbe`, H1-D card-invalidation work); measure card body counts before and after, and attach the provider lazily.
- Predictability: PASS. Explicit gestures only, versioned digest format, deterministic caps, snapshot semantics stated in the file header ("snapshot at 14:32, turn in progress: yes"). Never changes the meaning of Enter (T3's default-on Compact chip backlash, #17467, is the cautionary tale in plans/v2-research/products/t3code.md fact-check).
- Accurate status: PASS if worded strictly. Outcomes are "copied", "inserted into the prompt, not sent", "digest written" and for a fresh session the normal verified start/Working state; never "delivered" or "handed off". A transcript that cannot be parsed produces an error, not an empty digest. RISK: transcript lines flush asynchronously (the tail comment says every 100 ms, and the power-user note says the hook's transcript_path can lag memory), so a Working source yields a stale tail; the header flags "turn in progress" and the UI says so.
- Fluency: PASS with one friction to measure. No confirmation dialogs; the popover is the only step and is dismissible. RISK: a live session reading a file outside its cwd may raise a permission prompt (to be tested in E1); fresh sessions can avoid it with `--add-dir`, live ones cannot without changing settings.
- Modularity: PASS. LoomCore holds a UI-free `SessionDigest` + `SessionDigestStore`; LoomCatalogUI adds views and the controller intents; no new target, no upward dependency; the start path is the existing `startConversation(opening:)`. If v2 becomes chat-centred, the digest layer is reused unchanged and only the menu/drag layer is replaced by composer chips (T3 pattern).
- CLI-update resilience: PASS with discipline. The transcript format is private and drifts: defensive parser (unknown -> nothing, zero turns -> visible error + `cli_compat_warning` journal), no field is required except what the digest degrades without. Launch flags used (`-n`, `--`, optionally `--add-dir`, `--permission-mode`) are in `claude --help` 2.1.300 and follow the existing help-text gating; nothing pinned. The idle-compaction toggle (v2.1.302) means a source may contain a compaction summary the parser must label, not choke on.
- Ownership: PASS. No process spawned or adopted; files only in Loom's data root, removed on source deletion through `ConversationForgetting`, aged out otherwise. The files are readable by any same-user agent that knows the path, which is not new exposure (the transcripts themselves are). Contract section 7 "second copy of the transcripts must not be kept" is the sentence to settle: the digest is capped, derived and expiring, but it is a content copy, so it needs the user's explicit nod (user_decisions).
- User authority: PASS and this is the idea's main merit. Every reference is a user click or drag; read-only; no agent can ask for another session's content in this design; a pasted line is inert until the user presses Enter. Agent-initiated or standing access is exactly what contract section 7 reserves for the CP3 channel and is not smuggled in. Cross-project note shown in the preview.
WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A VIOLATION, AND THE AVOIDANCE: (1) a live or auto-refreshing reference (continuous tailing of the source) -> snapshot only; (2) model-written summaries (Zed's New From Summary and Agent view's row summaries cost tokens/quota and are not the user's choice) -> mechanical digest only; (3) typing into other sessions or pressing Enter for the user -> paste unsent, at-prompt states only; (4) answering a pending approval by accident -> refuse Needs approval; (5) an agent-callable read tool without per-grant approval -> out of scope here; (6) harvesting the handoff note path by parsing prose -> user supplies it; (7) unbounded cache or surviving deletion -> caps, TTL, forgetter.
feasibility.value_reason: Real but second-order for this user. Multi-session, multi-project work with ticket keys makes planner-to-implementer and writer-to-reviewer handoffs common, the official Writer/Reviewer pattern is endorsed in the research, and drag-a-card is a delightful, token-free gesture that also becomes the seed of the CP3 channel (D-43/D-46). But a mechanical digest (last N turns, truncated tools) is a worse handoff than the note the user's own skill and Obsidian vault already produce ("things not to redo", decisions), loom:open-session already covers agent-initiated handoff with user approval, and a fresh reviewer is about three clicks today (New session, type the skill). If not, the fallback is path-only references (transcript path plus session id) with no digest file, which is weaker and exposes raw jsonl.

May fresh handoff and reviewer sessions start with `--add-dir <Loom digest folder>` and the reviewer with `--permission-mode plan`? Both change CLI behaviour (D-20 class); the plan-mode default and the 'read-only' wording are the user's call.

Should a fresh handoff successor inherit the source's ticket key? (Ticket de-dup picks the oldest match, so the source stays the target of `loom:open-session`; the reviewer probably should not carry the key.)
How much does the user trust a mechanical digest versus their own /handoff skill note? Decide after E3: keep Layer C, or reduce it to 'open a fresh session with this note path'.
Should an agent-readable `$LOOM_CLI read` verb (user grants access per reference, expires) be the follow-up that turns this into the first CP3 slice, or stay file-based?
If v2 moves to a chat-centred UI, are references expected to become composer chips (T3 style)? The design keeps the digest layer UI-free for that reason.

feasibility.one_line: Skip the idea as written: Claude Code already ships `/goal` (documented, CLI 2.1.300 here) as a session-scoped prompt Stop hook with a Haiku evaluator, so Loom should not build its own checker and Stop-hook loop. Adopt only a light layer that makes Loom aware of a native goal: a card marker, no false "Finished" between goal turns, and one real end signal.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
- Card (two-row): a small `◎` glyph in the existing monochrome symbol class (`LoomTheme`; no new hue, per the DESIGN.md three-status-hues rule) sits next to the project/branch row or the status text while a goal is active. The status stays truthful: Working while turns run, with no Waiting or Finished flicker between goal turns.
- Header: beside the state pill, a quiet chip "Goal · 6 turns · 41k tokens" (from `goal_status`, when known). Its tooltip shows the full condition and the latest evaluator reason. A click toggles the condition line, with no extra panel. The ⋯ menu gets "Set Goal..." and "Clear Goal" (which types `/goal clear`).
- End: when the goal resolves, the existing blue "Finished" appears once, and the pill briefly reads "Goal met" or "Goal not reached: <reason>" until the user views the session. This reuses the existing unviewed state and the Dock badge, menu bar and Cmd+J; those are not touched.
- Optional macOS banner "Goal met · <project>" through the existing `ApprovalNotifier` / `NotificationService` seam. Today banners exist only for Needs approval (D-49), so this is a new notification class and the user's call.
- Nothing is drawn or watched for sessions without a goal.
feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS for the light version. It is event-driven with no timer or poll. Parsing a prompt string is trivial. The transcript tail read is bounded (64 KiB, line-aligned, O_NOFOLLOW, regular file of this user) and runs only for sessions that have a goal. The original design RISKS this: a Loom-spawned `claude -p` per turn, plus a Stop timeout raised for every session.
- Predictability: PASS. Loom adds no behaviour to the loop. The original adds a second, Loom-owned loop that fights the CLI's 8-continuation cap, the user's own Stop hooks and native /goal.
- Accurate status: the light version IMPROVES it. Between goal turns the card no longer claims "Finished" when the CLI is about to continue. Risks to design against:
  - never show "met" unless the transcript says met;
  - a missing or unreadable `goal_status` leaves the marker unchanged and drops the hold after one idle registry sample;
  - Loom's marker says only that a goal is armed;
  - after a Loom Stop and Resume the counters are reset by the CLI, so Loom shows no counter it cannot verify.
- Fluency: PASS. There is no extra confirmation. Arming is one sheet or typing in the terminal. No new waits.
- Modularity: PASS. It is a parser, an optional tail reader, one `SessionViewState.goal` field and a few lines in `activePhase`. All of it sits beside `SubagentLedger` and `SubagentTranscriptTail`, the existing precedents for hook- and transcript-derived card data.
- CLI-update resilience: the weakest point. Documented: `/goal` itself, the Stop decision semantics, `stop_hook_active`, and the fact that Stop is the main agent only (SubagentStop is the subagents' event; internal agents such as /btw fire SubagentStop, which Loom already ignores as `.childAgent`). Undocumented and so drift-prone: the transcript `goal_status` attachment shape, and whether the slash command surfaces in UserPromptSubmit. Mitigation: parse with a narrow Decodable, treat unknown shapes as "no information", report once, and keep the pre-goal behaviour as the fallback. The `/goal` docs also name versions (v2.1.239, v2.1.246, v2.1.269), so features move; do not branch on versions.
- Ownership: PASS. No new process. The CLI's evaluator runs inside the CLI, inside the run scope Loom already owns and verifies.
- User authority: PASS. The user arms the goal themselves (typing it or using the sheet), and Loom never arms one on its own. No cross-session action is involved.
feasibility.value_reason: The walk-away loop the user wants already exists in the CLI and costs Loom nothing. What Loom adds is trust: a visible marker, no false blue between goal turns (which also protects the Dock badge, menu bar and Cmd+J across several parallel sessions), and one real end signal. That matters most for a heavy multi-session user who walks away. The arming sheet is mere convenience. The idea as written, a Loom-owned checker and loop, would add high cost and risk for little over the CLI feature. HN-style "works most of the time, not always" caveats apply to the CLI evaluator and are out of Loom's hands. These are my estimates; the user has not said whether they use /goal today.
experiments: E1, hook, registry and transcript trace of a native /goal run. Use an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, never the real ~/.claude. Run a trivial 2 to 3 turn goal such as 'create /tmp/x with one line, then stop' with a hook script that logs every event to JSONL, then read what Claude wrote. Decisions it makes: (1) Does `/goal <text>` fire UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion or neither, and does the continuation turn fire a UserPromptSubmit? That decides how arming is detected. (2) Does Loom's own Stop command hook fire on every goal turn, including turns that the evaluator then continues? (3) What is the order of the Stop hook, the `goal_status` write to the transcript and the registry 'busy' sample between turns? That decides whether the end signal comes from the transcript or can be inferred, and how long the current Finished flicker lasts. (4) What fields does the `<config>/sessions/<pid>.json` registry hold while a goal is active (is there a goal field)? That would give a documented-ish source. (5) Does `last_assistant_message` plus `stop_hook_active` tell the next Stop anything useful?

E2, Loom's current behaviour under a goal. Run the same goal inside Loom Dev (not the daily app) with an isolated profile and record the SessionEventHub frames (the `activePhase`, `unviewedCompletion` and `status.activity` sequence per turn). Decides: is the flicker real and long enough to bother the user, or does a registry 'busy' sample arrive within milliseconds? If the flicker is under about a second, piece (c) can shrink to a pure marker and the hold is skipped.

E3, can Loom type `/goal` safely? Write `/goal <text>` plus Return through TerminalInputQueue to a session at the prompt (bracketed paste versus plain typing; the slash-command menu may intercept the first characters) and confirm acceptance by the resulting hook or transcript entry. Also try `claude -- "/goal ..."` as the first message, since the open-session path (D-40) already starts sessions with a first message. Decides whether the arming sheet is a plain write or needs a verified-delivery wrapper.

Budget for all three: well inside D-04 (real-provider tests in isolated profiles, a few short turns, small-model evaluator), and the CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0 setting avoids idle check-ins during the trace.
user_decisions: Do you use /goal in the terminal today, and would you arm it from Loom (header sheet) or keep typing it? If you keep typing it, the arming sheet is dropped and only awareness (marker plus quiet status) remains.
Should Loom send a macOS banner when a goal ends (met, impossible, error)? Today banners exist only for Needs approval (D-49), so this is a new notification class.
Is a small `◎` goal marker acceptable as a new card/header element, within the DESIGN.md rule of monochrome symbols and the existing three status hues? It is the only UI change in the light version.
Should the blue 'Finished' be held back for the whole goal and fire once at the end (my recommendation), or show after every goal turn as it does now?

Does the walk-away value justify any Loom-owned loop at all? I recommend no: if native /goal's evaluator proves too weak for your work (the research cites roughly 98 % agreement for OpenChamber's own lab, and 'not always' from HN users), the better lever is a Stop command hook or a prompt hook you write in your own settings, not a Loom-owned checker.

feasibility.one_line: Technically a clean fit if cut down to read-only recipes plus one armed timer that runs only while Loom is open, but for this user it mostly duplicates Claude skills and /loop, the unique unattended value costs plan budget, and the full version (worktrees, budgets, return-to-session) is XL, not L, so park it behind the worktree and usage-by-source work.
feasibility.loom_design:
CORRECTIONS TO THE IDEA FIRST. (1) The "debates" line says Superset and Emdash advise against a cron daemon. The notes say otherwise: both SHIP schedulers (Emdash runtimes/automations: one upcoming run per automation, only fires while the app runs, recovers interrupted runs; Superset Pro automations are cloud-dispatched, at-least-once, and 'created' only means the workspace exists, not that the agent succeeded, issue #7941/#6243). The "no daemon" advice is the digest authors', and Superset's own pty-daemon problems (#7977, #5792, #8029) are the real cautionary tale. (2) Loom's own contract already says a closed app does not pick up work (LOOM-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md section 7 last paragraph), so "runs only while Loom runs" is consistent, not a compromise. (3) 'Return to this session' is already free: Claude's /loop and cron are session-scoped, and Loom already counts them as pending work (ClaudeHook.swift reads Stop.session_crons; ProviderSessionAdapters.swift adds scheduledTaskCount to pendingProviderWorkCount, so a looping session shows under way in the Active section). Do not build that variant.

SMALLEST VERSION THAT FITS (call it 'Recipes'): read-only prompts per project, run on a timer while Loom is open, results arrive as ordinary cards.
1. Store (LoomCore, new file e.g. ScheduledRecipe.swift): recipes {id, name, projectID, prompt, schedule (daily/weekly time or interval >= 1 h), enabled, lastRun, nextDue}. Persist as a small JSON beside ui-preferences.json (UIPreferencesStore pattern, unreadable file renamed aside) or an additive table opened like ensureProjectColors. Authored only from a Loom Settings page. No verb in loom-hook/OpenSessionProtocol or the loom:open-session skill can create or edit one, so agents cannot schedule (contract section 7). Honest caveat: an agent with Bash can edit a file in Application Support, so the real guard is that a recipe's permission mode is fixed in code (read-only), not user-chosen text.
2. Trigger, no polling: one armed Task per runtime (SessionRuntime owns it, like SessionLifecycleController.reschedule/timerFired with a single Task.sleep to the earliest deadline; CatalogModel.sleepUntil is the existing wall-clock sleep seam). Re-arm only on: recipe edit, runtime start, NSWorkspace.didWakeNotification, NSSystemClockDidChange (the last two forwarded from loom-app, event-driven). On fire, recompute from the wall clock (never trust the sleep), because ContinuousClock sleeps through machine sleep. Nothing runs between events; with no enabled recipes there is no timer at all.
3. Missed runs: at runtime start and on wake compute due-but-unrun slots. Policy (user decision): run ONE catch-up if the slot is within a grace window (default 12 h for daily), otherwise record 'skipped' with a reason. Settings shows 'Skipped 2 runs while Loom was closed' plainly (Desktop scheduled tasks do one catch-up within 7 days and log skip reasons; copy the honesty, not the 7 days).
4. Start path: reuse SessionRuntime.startConversation(opening:) / ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(route: .new, opening:) exactly like an approved open-session request (SessionRuntime+OpenRequests.approveOpenRequest). The user's creating and enabling the recipe is the authorization, so no per-run prompt; the approve box (OpenRequestViews) is not used. Add to the launch profile (capability-detected from claude --help like supportsEffort, drift-journaled by missingRequiredClaudeOptions, never pinned): '--permission-mode dontAsk' plus '--allowedTools' with a read-only list (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash(git log/diff/status:*), Bash(gh pr/run list/view:*)). claude --help 2.1.300 lists dontAsk, plan, auto, bypassPermissions. The scheduled run gets hooks but NO control socket and NO plugin dir (ClaudeHookLaunchConfiguration already allows controlSocketPath nil), so an unattended session cannot file open-session requests; crossSessionInbound is already 'refuse' in claudeSettings. A needs-approval stall still surfaces through the existing path (Needs approval, banner, Cmd+J).
5. Launch needs a TerminalSurface (rows/cols, ended-screen snapshot), so the UI-layer ConversationController gets a start(scheduled:) beside approveOpen (it creates the surface the same way; selection does not move, no window opens, no sound).
6. Origin and unread: add a nullable origin column (e.g. scheduled:<recipeID>) next to ticket_key/opened_by with the ensure*Columns 'added on open, no version bump' pattern, so older builds still open the catalog. Card shows a clock glyph and 'scheduled · Daily brief' in the meta row (S2 'from <session>' precedent, D-39).
7. Run end (this is the part the idea glosses over): SessionEventHub.runEnded sets activePhase to .inactive and clears status, and unviewedCompletion lives in memory only, so a stopped run today shows NO blue 'Finished' dot and nothing survives a relaunch. For an inbox the result must stay unread across the stop. Two options: (a) keep the TUI alive at its prompt until viewed (zero new state, but a ~230 MB class Claude process per unread run sits idle all day, against 'idle records cost nothing'; D-38 forbids auto idle stop but a scheduled run is a different case); (b) preferred: when the Stop hook arrives with pendingProviderWorkCount == 0, Loom runs its normal verified stopConversation, EndedScreenStore keeps the snapshot, and a persisted sessions.unread_result flag (catalog, cleared by the first deliberate view via markViewed/viewRecorded) drives a new 'unread result' indicator on an ended card. That is a real catalog + SessionIndicator + sidebar change (M), not 'reuse the machinery'.
8. 'Nothing to report' auto-viewed: do not judge text. The recipe wrapper appends 'If there is nothing to report, reply with exactly NOTHING_TO_REPORT'. Loom already parses Stop.last_assistant_message (ClaudeHook.swift lines 387/445/768) but never publishes it (ProviderWorkState carries only activity + pending count), so plumb one bounded comparison (exact match after trim) in the adapter; on match, mark read and stop. A miss errs toward showing the card unread. Label it agent-reported, never as verified status. Verify the Stop payload field against the installed CLI before relying on it (the research notes document background_tasks/session_crons for Stop but not this field).
9. Bounds: concurrency 1 (queue, drop duplicates of the same recipe); wall-clock cap per run (default 15 min) enforced by Loom's verified Stop. A token budget cannot use the CLI: --max-budget-usd works only with --print, which this design avoids. Per-session token caps need a session sum over ClaudeUsageIndex (messages are keyed by session, but no per-session query or usage-by-source exists yet), so defer them to that work. Floor: skip a run (log 'skipped: plan window under 20%') when the plan share Loom already reads from get_usage is low, reusing the footer chip's orange threshold.
10. feasibility.loom_design:
FACTS (read in the repo): (1) Loom already walks, tails and parses transcripts for Usage: `UsageTranscriptWalker.candidates(profile:)` and `isTranscriptName` (skips `.orphaned-`/`.superseded-` variants and the `memory` and `tool-results` folders), `UsageTranscriptWatcher` (one FSEvents stream over `<profile>/projects`, no timer), `ClaudeUsageIndex` (disposable `usage-index.sqlite3`, per-file offset plus 64-byte guard hash, forget digests), and `SubagentTranscriptTail` and `SubagentTranscriptParser` (partial last line held back, 128 KiB line cap, text-only entries that never decode `toolUseResult`). Catalog search is `SessionCatalog.searchSessions`, built on `conditions(for:)` in `SessionCatalog+Paging.swift` (LIKE over `loom_fold(provider|title|project name)`), driven by `CatalogModel.setSearchText` (120 ms debounce, cancel-and-replace) and `CatalogModel+Search.reloadSearchResults` (generation guard). Deletion already has `ConversationForgetters`, called in the `verifying` step with Loom id plus all provider ids, idempotent, and a throw keeps the deletion open (`ConversationDeletion.swift`, registered for usage in `AppDelegate+Usage.swift:34`). The existing U0 evidence measured the usage cold scan at about 241 MiB/s on a 1 GiB synthetic corpus (4.2 s, +14 MB RSS, warm cache) in `plans/experiments/run1-U0-usage-index.json`; a no-decode memmem-style gate should be several times faster, a decode-and-write indexer about the same speed.

DESIGN (V1, no persistent state):
1. LoomCore `TranscriptSearch` (new file, no UI). Input: the query, a candidate list, a `SearchBudget`. Candidates come from the walker (path, session stem, size, mtime; one directory pass, milliseconds) joined to catalog rows by lowercase provider id. Join `sessions.provider_conversation_id` plus `provider_identity_changes` so a /clear chain maps back to one card. Subagent files (`.../<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`) belong to the parent session. Only transcripts of catalog sessions are searched (a hit must be openable); transcripts of terminal sessions Loom never saw are out of scope (the contract §13 "import history" idea).
2. Streaming matcher: forward sequential read, newest file first (by mtime). Line splitting copies `SubagentTranscriptTail` (whole lines only, partial tail held back, 128 KiB cap; passing `coldWindowBytes: Int.max` already makes it read from byte 0). Per line: ASCII-case-folded byte gate for the needle first (like `ClaudeUsageParser.contains`), and only on a gate hit a narrow Decodable that keeps `type` (`user` or `assistant`), `timestamp`, and `message.content` text blocks (string content or `type=="text"` blocks). Skip tool_result blocks, `thinking`, `isMeta` and compact-summary lines. Re-fold the extracted text with `SessionCatalog.fold` (Turkish-aware) before the final match, so a raw-byte false positive inside a tool result is discarded. Snippet = about 160 characters around the first match (the matching line), plus role, timestamp and byte offset of the line.
3. Budgets, in the type: first pass = the newest 14 days or 512 MiB, whichever ends first, hard 2 s; a "Search older" action extends up to the CLI's retention window (cleanupPeriodDays, default 30, verified on code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory, configurable) with 8 s / 4 GiB. One search in flight, one utility-queue worker, `Task.checkCancellation()` per 1 MiB chunk. Numbers are placeholders until the spike below.
4. LoomCatalogUI: a `TranscriptSearchModel` (@Observable, owned beside `deletions` and `usage` in `CatalogModel`) started from `CatalogModel.setSearchText` after the existing debounce plus a second settle (about 300 ms, at least 3 characters, the search setting on), cancelled by the next keystroke and by `.conversationDeleted` frames; generation-guarded like `searchGeneration`. Hits arrive as coalesced batches (at most 5 per second, as `SubagentTranscriptFeed` does), grouped per session (2 hits then "+N"). Results re-join the catalog with the `notDeleting` fence at display time, so a session being deleted never shows a snippet.
5. Triggers are events only: a settled query typed by the user. No FSEvents consumer, no timer, nothing runs when the field is empty or the window is hidden.
6. Accurate status: the footer always states coverage ("Searched 63 of 214 sessions, last 14 days. Search older"), never a bare "No matches" after a partial pass. Drift: count text-bearing lines that fail to decode and show it the way Usage shows "N lines not understood" (`UsageDiagnostics`, Settings and diagnostics export); a profile with transcripts but zero extractable text shows "Conversation search unavailable", never wrong results.
7. Deletion: nothing to purge. `ClaudeDataDeleter` removes the transcript, and the search reads only transcripts, so deleted means unsearchable by construction. The same holds for the CLI's own retention sweep: a swept transcript simply stops matching, with no stale index.
8. Off switch: Settings → General "Search conversation text" (default on; it reads only on typing and keeps no copy). Per-project exclusion only if the user asks for it.
9. Step 0 (S, independent): add `ticket_key` to `conditions(for:)`. It is populated only for sessions an agent opened through the D-40 skill, so it helps with EDDP-123 only partly.

V2 only if measured too slow: a separate `transcript-search.sqlite3` (never the catalog, never inside `usage-index.sqlite3`) with an FTS5 table of user and assistant text only, fed by a second handler on the same watcher (fan-out in `AppDelegate+Usage`). The indexer would arm on the first search of an app run, collect changed paths while idle (the `UsageModel.transcriptsChanged` collect pattern), and catch up when the search field is focused. Rows would be purged when `ItemRemoved` arrives or the walker no longer sees the file (stricter than the usage index, which keeps history). Deletion would use a registered `ConversationForgetters` hook, `secure_delete`, a digest guard against re-index and WAL truncate, copying `ClaudeUsageIndex.forget`; it would not be one transaction with the file delete (the idea text says "same transaction", but Loom's real model is "forget hook in the verifying step, retry on throw"). The dry-run preview (`ConversationDeletionPreview`) would gain an index-rows line.

NOT in v1: "open at the right place". A live or idle terminal cannot scroll to a historic message, and `EndedScreenStore` snapshots are memory-only. Landing on the hit needs a read-only main-session transcript reader (windowed pread of about 64 KiB either side of the stored offset, rendered by the `SubagentTranscriptParser` plus `SubagentTranscriptView` path). That is the seed of the separate conversation-view idea. v1 click = select the session (record view with Resume, or the live terminal), because the snippet already answers "which session".

After the second settle a section "In conversations" appears below them (day-heading style, `ActivityHeading`). Each hit row is the project-stripe plus indicator slot, the session title and relative time, and under it a 2-line mono-ish snippet (secondary colour) with the match in the accent colour and a "you" or "Claude" prefix. At most 2 hits per session, then "+3 more". A footer line states coverage and holds the "Search older" link, with a small spinner while a pass runs. Click selects the session as any card click does; Return opens the first hit. Empty-state text changes from "Search covers title, provider and project" to include conversation text. Not proposed: a Cmd-K palette (a new overlay surface, and Cmd+K is the terminal clear-screen habit) and Cmd+F inside the subagent panel (Edit > Find is bound to sidebar search, `AppDelegate.swift:705`; a transcript find bar can come with the reader).
feasibility.principle_check:
Resources: PASS for V1. No standing state, no watcher consumer, no timer. A bounded burst only on a settled user query, with a byte and time budget, one worker, cancel on typing. RISK: page-cache churn and one core for up to 2 s while a session streams output; measure it against the CP5 1 MiB/s fixture. V2 would be a PARTIAL RISK: a persistent second copy plus a cold build of the whole corpus at about 200 MiB/s (a 3 GB corpus takes about 15 s of utility CPU), and the retention-purge logic.
Predictability: PASS if title matches stay first and stable and content hits are appended as a labelled section. Cursor-style "content ranked above titles" would make rows jump under the cursor as results stream in, so I reject it.
Accurate status: PASS only with the coverage footer. A partial scan reporting "no results" would be a false negative, which is the main violation to avoid. "Deleted" is verified by construction in V1; V2 needs the forget hook plus a failed hook keeping the deletion open.
Fluency: PASS. No confirmation, the existing field, and an optional "Search older" that is the user's call.
Modularity: PASS. A LoomCore searcher with no UI import, a separate model, no change to `ClaudeUsageIndex`. Reuse the walker and tail by extracting them to a shared file rather than adding a second walker.
CLI-update resilience: RISK, contained. The JSONL is internal and unversioned, but Loom already depends on it (usage, subagent panel) with defensive parsers. The failure mode is "coverage down" or "unavailable", surfaced like `linesNotUnderstood`, never wrong results. It reads text blocks only, not tool shapes.
Ownership: PASS. Read-only, no process started.
User authority: PASS as a user-typed query shown to the user. Do NOT expose this search to Claude sessions (for example a skill or socket verb): that would let one session read another's conversation, which is the D-43/D-46 channel and needs its own user-authorized design.
Privacy: snippets can show secrets pasted into prompts, so the section needs the off switch and it must not be logged (`LoomLog` public fields only: counts, durations). Contract §13 lists "full transcript search" as an idea without scope decision, so it needs a new D-entry before building.
feasibility.value_reason: The pain is real for someone with several sessions across two projects and EDDP-* tickets, and the answer is often just a snippet plus Resume. But the user's own wish list (side chat, right panel, usage, deletion, idle cost) never names transcript search; with 2-3 live sessions, the 30-day default retention and a notes vault the recall window is short; and Claude's own `--resume` picker takes a search term. Useful and cheap in V1, not transformative. The M estimate holds only for V1 (about 700-900 lines in LoomCore plus model, sidebar section, design preview, tests, evidence). The FTS5 variant is L (the reference size is `ClaudeUsageIndex` at 1,318 lines plus forgetters, eviction, schema, settings and diagnostics), and the hit reader is another M-L. Orca's L was the honest figure for the index.
depends_on: No hard dependency for V1.
Optional: the read-only main-session transcript view / conversation-view idea (needed for 'open at the hit'; V1 deliberately does not need it).
Optional: a command palette idea, if one exists, would reuse the same searcher.
A new DECISIONS entry (contract §13 lists 'full transcript search' as an unscoped idea).

So an unavailable RC is not fatal and needs no gating preflight.
- CORRECTION to the idea text: CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID is an ENVIRONMENT variable of hook-command and Bash subprocesses, set while RC is connected and removed when it ends (env-vars page, hooks page; v2.1.199+). It is NOT a field in the hook JSON payload. Today `loom-hook` (Sources/loom-hook/main.swift) forwards only stdin plus LOOM_* env, and ClaudeHookEvent.init reads only payload keys. The helper therefore has to read that env var itself.
- CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE (v2.1.181+) is checked once per push-triggering event, not polled. File exists means pushes are skipped. It is read from the CLI's start environment.

DESIGN (smallest version; cost M, not S)
A. Start switch (LoomCore).
   - `ProviderCapabilities.supportsRemoteControl = help.contains("--remote-control")`, added to `detectedClaudeOptions` like the other flags (ProviderLaunchProfile.swift).
   - `ProviderLaunchProfile.claude(route:...)` gets an optional `remoteControl: String?` (the name). It emits `--remote-control=<name>` before the `openingArguments` and before the trailing `--` prompt. Use the `=` form because the argument is optional-valued and the title can start with `-`.
   - Unlike `--settings` and `--session-id`, which are passed even when `--help` does not list them, this flag is gated on detection. It is an opt-in convenience and must not stop a session from starting. When it is missing the UI says "this Claude has no Remote Control option".
   - The name is built from the project name and the ticket key (the catalog has both), so two EDDP sessions can be told apart on the phone. Otherwise the CLI invents "host-graceful-unicorn".
   - Per-session intent is one nullable catalog column `sessions.remote_requested`, added the same way as `ticket_key` and `opened_by` (CatalogDatabase, no `user_version` bump), so Resume repeats the choice. The Settings default (UIPreferences) applies only to new sessions. D-20 is met because both are explicit user switches and the default is off.
B. Presence file (loom-app, beside ApprovalNotifier and SystemServices).
   - A `PresenceService` protocol with a system implementation and a recording fake for `--evidence`, like NotificationService.
   - Events: `com.apple.screenIsLocked` and `com.apple.screenIsUnlocked` on DistributedNotificationCenter (undocumented names, so verify on macOS 27 or fall back to CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary read at the event), NSWorkspace.screensDidSleep and screensDidWake, and the screensaver start and stop notifications. There are no timers. One atomic create or delete per event, a re-sync at launch, and delete at Quit.
   - The file lives at `<data root>/presence/at-mac`, so the dev app and the daily app never share it. Loom exports `CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE` into the launch env only when the user's Phone switch is on; it is inert unless RC is active.
   - Limitation to state: the env is fixed at CLI start, so a session that began before the setting existed is not affected.
C. Honest badge (hook path).
   - `loom-hook` adds an optional `bridgeConnected: Bool?` to ClaudeHookEnvelope. It reads only whether the env var is present and never stores or logs the value, because it equals the claude.ai/code session id in the URL. An old envelope still decodes.
   - The adapter publishes a new `.remote(RemoteState)` change through SessionEventHub, the same shape as `.subagents`. SessionViewState holds it and it is cleared on run start, detach and end.
   - Card states: none, Requested (flag passed, not yet seen), Connected (as of the last turn event), Not connected (requested, but the var was absent at the first UserPromptSubmit or Stop, or it disappeared). The last state reuses SessionIssueNotice: "Phone access did not start, see the terminal footer".
   - Wording never says "connected" without hook proof.
D. Cut from this idea.
   - Mechanism 3 (webhook, ntfy, Shortcuts push). RC already sends documented finished and needs-permission pushes, but only if the user has enabled them once in `/config`. Loom must not change those CLI settings (D-20). A second channel adds a network dependency and a settings surface for no gain.
   - A `claude auth status` preflight process. Loom reads nothing of the account today (ClaudePlanLimits keeps only the two windows). Use a pure, process-free hint from `toolchain.environment`: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK or VERTEX or FOUNDRY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC, DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK. Word it as "may not work", because settings.json env, Trusted Devices, the Team owner toggle and ZDR/HIPAA are invisible to Loom.
   - Injecting `/remote-control` into a running PTY. Loom has no programmatic input path; D-43 and D-46 leave "deliver into a session" for the cross-session channel. The menu item for a running session only shows the hint "type /remote-control".
   - `claude remote-control` server mode. It spawns sessions outside Loom's run scopes, which breaks process ownership.
   - A Loom power assertion. The CLI handles idle sleep itself while working (2.1.287 fix). The gap is a session that is waiting for approval while the Mac sleeps. That belongs to the persistence idea's stay-awake option as a separate user decision.
E. Triggers and bounds.
   - Everything is event-driven: lock and sleep notifications, hook events that already fire, and the user's click. Nothing polls and nothing is drawn when hidden.
   - Memory is one Bool per live session plus one file.
   - Cost: M. Flag and capability about S; presence service S to M; hook, envelope, hub and badge M; Settings and menu M; tests M. The flag-only version is S but gives an unprovable badge and no quiet pushes.
feasibility.ui_sketch:
- Settings → General gets a "Phone" group.
  - Switch 1: "Start new sessions reachable from my phone", off by default. Caption in plain words: "Uses Claude's Remote Control. The conversation is stored on Anthropic's servers while connected. The session ends when you stop it or quit Loom, so the phone loses it. Needs a claude.ai login."
  - Switch 2: "Skip phone pushes while I'm at the Mac", on once Switch 1 is on. Caption: "Applies to sessions started afterwards. Push types are set once in Claude's /config."
  - A short grey line shows the env-derived hint when something would block RC.
- Session ⋯ menu, with no confirmation dialog:
  - Stopped or new session: a checkable "Reachable from phone".
  - Running session: a disabled item "Reachable from phone: type /remote-control in the terminal".
  - Later, once the badge is proven: "Copy phone link", with the id kept in memory only.
- Card, bottom row: a small monochrome `iphone` symbol left of the provider icon, in text.secondary. An outline means requested, filled means connected at the last turn, and a struck-through look means not connected. No status words, so DESIGN.md §4 and the three-status-hue rule are untouched. The tooltip and accessibility label carry the words.
- Header: no new chip. A failed request reuses the existing issue notice. Stop and Quit text gains one line when a phone-reachable session is running: "The phone loses it."
feasibility.principle_check:
- Resources: PASS. No polling, a handful of OS notifications, one file write per lock event, one Bool per session. Fail condition: periodic `claude auth status`, registry polling for RC, or a standing helper. The design avoids all three. There is no Loom network code at all.
- Predictability: PASS if default off, the flag is gated on detection, and sessions started before a setting change are not affected (stated in the caption). RISK: RC makes sessions depend on network, the account and Anthropic's pairing, and it can fail silently (#34255 and #35637 open, per the persistence note). Loom must not hide that.
- Accurate status: RISK, managed. The badge is proven only by the hook env, and only as of the last turn event. SessionStart probably fires before the bridge connects, so a fresh idle session stays "Requested" until its first prompt (to be measured). Never show "Connected" from the flag alone. When a phone answers an approval, the hook sequence is the same as for the terminal, and the registry busy sample returns the state, so no new status bug is expected (to be confirmed in the spike).
- Fluency: PASS. One switch and one menu item, no modal, no startup wait. First-use text sits inline in Settings.
- Modularity: PASS. Launch rule in ProviderLaunchProfile, an OS service in loom-app behind a protocol with a fake, state through the existing hub path. LoomCore stays UI-free.
- CLI-update resilience: PASS. Only documented surfaces are used: `--remote-control`, the hook env var, CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE. All are version-tagged in the docs and degrade to "absent". Capability detection joins the drift list. Never pins a CLI version.
- Process ownership: UNPROVEN, and the decisive risk. If an RC session leaves a bridge or daemon process that survives Loom's Stop or scope kill (the Windows report #101118), the phone could show the session online after Loom said "Stopped". That is a false success. The spike must prove that Stop and Quit leave nothing and that the phone sees the session go offline. Fail condition: any survivor means do not ship, or ship only after tearing it down inside the scope.
- User authority: PASS with a caveat. A phone approval comes from the user's own claude.ai account, not from another session, so it is not a cross-session action. It is still an extra control surface, so it is opt-in per session, shown on the card, and never turned on silently. Loom's own cross-session channel (D-43) stays unrelated, and `crossSessionInbound=refuse` is unchanged.
- Privacy: transcripts are stored server-side while connected. Work projects (EDDP) may be under company or Team policy. Default off, plain wording, and no per-project auto-enable.
feasibility.value_reason: The use is real. Several long multi-agent runs blocked on approval, with the user away from the Mac, is exactly the case RC serves, and Anthropic's own pushes and approval UI already exist. But the user's own wish list (side chat, right panel, usage, reliable delete, idle cost) never mentions a phone, and the bare benefit is already available for free through `remoteControlAtStartup` or typing `/remote-control`. Loom's increment is convenience, the quiet-push presence file and an honest badge. Reliability caveats (open silent-disconnect and approval-not-reaching-host issues, a Mac that sleeps while a session waits for approval, server-side transcript storage) cap the value until the user confirms they want it.
depends_on: Spike S1 to S4 below
Optional: the persistence idea's stay-awake option, which decides whether phone approval works while the Mac idles
None of the other v2 ideas is required; it reuses the existing hook, hub and SystemServices seams
experiments: S1 Ownership and daemon (decides ship or no-ship). Needs a one-time `/login` by the user in an isolated profile (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/loom-rc-spike), because CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN cannot establish RC and the real ~/.claude is off limits. Launch `claude --remote-control=x` with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1, the way the launch profile does, inside a throwaway Loom run scope. Decide by three checks: (a) it connects (the TUI footer shows the indicator and the phone lists the session); (b) the process tree before and after shows no `claude daemon`, supervisor or bridge process outside the scope; (c) after Stop and after Quit the phone shows the session offline and `ps` finds no survivor. If it needs AGENT_VIEW enabled, or a daemon escapes, the idea is dropped or becomes a user decision under D-20.

S2 Hook env timing. Use a tiny test hook that records only whether CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID is set, for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, Notification and SubagentStart, in these cases: RC from launch, RC turned on mid-session, RC turned off, resume with the flag, after /clear. Decides whether 'Connected' can ever show before the first prompt, and whether subagent hooks carry it. If SessionStart never has it, the badge copy must say 'after your first message'.

S3 Presence file. With the phone app registered and `/config` pushes enabled in the spike profile, check that pushes still arrive with the file absent and stop while it exists, both when the Loom-like terminal has focus and when it does not. Also check whether the CLI's own 'focused terminal' suppression works at all in Loom's PTY (SwiftTerm has DECSET 1004 support but I did not confirm Loom forwards window focus). Separately verify on macOS 27 that the lock, unlock and display-sleep notifications actually fire.

S4 Naming and resume. Check how `--remote-control=<name>` interacts with `-n <title>`, whether the phone title follows later auto-titles, and whether `--resume <id> --remote-control` creates a duplicate stale entry in the phone list each time.

S5 Phone approval round trip. Approve a Bash permission prompt from the phone and watch Loom's state (PermissionRequest hook, then the registry busy sample) for a stuck 'Needs approval'. Optionally record `pmset -g assertions` while working versus waiting for approval, to see whether the CLI holds the Mac awake in the waiting case.
user_decisions: Do you actually want phone access? Your notes do not list it. If you only want to be told when a session needs you, the presence file alone is the whole value.

Which login do the work projects (EDDP-*) use: a personal Pro/Max account, or a company Team/Enterprise one? Server-side transcript storage and the owner toggle or ZDR/HIPAA restrictions apply there. Should RC be allowed for those projects at all?
Is `remoteControlAtStartup` already on in your own Claude settings? If so, the start switch is moot and only the badge and presence file remain.
Are you willing to do the one-time `/login` in a throwaway profile for the spike? It signs a session into your real claude.ai account.
Keep-awake: should Loom ever hold an idle-sleep assertion for phone-reachable sessions? This is a battery and predictability trade-off and it overlaps the persistence idea.
Default for the Settings switch: off (recommended, because of D-20 and privacy), or on for personal projects only?
