feasibility.one_line: Adopt a light version: an event-driven "what is this session running and listening on" popover and a conditional port segment, read from the run scope Loom already owns; skip the embedded WKWebView and the LOOM_PORT range.
feasibility.loom_design:
DESIGN
Why Loom can do this better than Cursor, Superset or Conductor: a session's run scope (coalition of a LoomRunHost, `RunScope.forkedMembers()` in Sources/LoomCore/RunScope.swift) is an exact, unforgeable member list of everything the session forked, including detached and reparented work. Attribution is membership, not a ppid walk, so the "shared coalition / helpers" worry in the idea's debate section mostly does not apply. Launchd-spawned members are already filtered out (`launchdSpawned`). Most primitives already exist: `ProcessTable.resourceUsage(pid:)` and `physicalFootprint(pid:)` (ProcessTable.swift, `loom_process_resource_usage` in CLoomPOSIX.c, rusage V4 with Mach tick conversion), `RunScopeTable.members(coalitionIDs:)` (one pass for many scopes), `ProcessTable.executablePath`. The dev-only `scopeAccounting` in Sources/loom-app/Evidence/EvidenceResourcePool.swift is already this inspector minus the UI and the sockets. The only genuinely new low-level piece is listening sockets: public libproc (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)`, then `proc_pidfdinfo(PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO)`, keep SOCKINFO_TCP with `tcpsi_state == TSI_S_LISTEN`, port from `insi_lport`). I confirmed these symbols exist in the local SDK headers (sys/proc_info.h, libproc.h). Nothing in the repo uses them for sockets today (the only proc_pidfdinfo use is a vnode-path test in SessionRuntimeTests.swift:858).

Pieces
1. CLoomPOSIX: one function, `loom_tcp_listeners(pid, out[], cap, &count)` returning port, family and loopback-or-any. It reads fds with a hard cap (for example 4096 fds per process and 32 listeners), fails closed with errno, and checks the reply size. It uses a public flavor, so there is no new private-ABI risk.
2. LoomCore, new file `ScopeInspector.swift` (value types plus one function), no UI import. `ProcessSupervisor` gets a small accessor that returns the session's `RunScope` handle (like `scopeWork(sessionID:)` in ProcessSupervisor+Sampling.swift). The heavy reads then run off the supervisor actor, because `loom_scopes_members` can sleep up to 50 ms per unreadable pid (RunScope.c). The result is a `ScopeInspection { sessionID, runID, sampledAt, members:[name,pid,footprint,cpuNs,listeners], totalFootprint, unreadableCount }`. Any unreadable member that cannot be ruled out makes the inspection "unavailable", never a partial total, as with the existing fail-closed membership read.
3. LoomCatalogUI: `ConversationIntents.processInspection(sessionID:) async -> ScopeInspection?` (same shape as `subagentTranscript(path:agentID:)`, with a default of nil), implemented in ConversationController via SessionRuntime. A small `ProcessInspectorModel` (like `SubagentTranscriptModel`) owns the popover: it samples once on open, then every 2 s while the popover is open AND `windowIsVisible` (the plumbing used in CatalogModel+Subagents.swift), and cancels on close. CPU % is the delta of cumulative user+system ns between two samples, so the first frame shows memory and "CPU --".
4. Pill state: a tiny `ListenerBook` in CatalogModel (not in SessionEventHub frames, so no per-card re-render churn) holds the last known listeners per live session. It is refreshed only at events Loom already handles for the branch cache (BranchCache precedent: CatalogModel.apply on `.turnComplete`, line ~1362, and `setWindowActive`, line ~1020): the Stop hook of that session, window becoming active (one pass covers all live scopes), popover open, click. There is NO sampling for "card visible". A card merely scrolling into view triggers nothing, which is the Superset lesson. To avoid a stale pill (an accuracy problem), each listener pid known to the book gets a kqueue/DispatchSource `.exit` watch (event-driven, zero polling); the entry is dropped on exit. The pill therefore only claims "was listening at last check and that process is still alive", and the popover shows the sample time.
5. "Open localhost:PORT" calls `NSWorkspace.open("http://localhost:PORT")` (localhost, not 127.0.0.1, per the Conductor note), after a single-pid re-check that the listener still exists. If it is gone the UI says "No longer listening" instead of opening a dead URL (no false success). Open is per row and never guessed from process names: ports can be Postgres, JDWP or Redis, not HTTP. Loom never probes ports.
6. Bounds: one coalition pass (~700 pids, 2 proc_pidinfo each, a few ms) plus about N members x (rusage + fd list) per sample. Max 10 live sessions x ~10 members. Memory is a handful of structs. No timer exists unless the popover is open and the window visible.

What would make it a principle violation, and how the design avoids it: (a) a periodic scanner or a per-card-visibility sampler is the Superset failure (lsof every 2.5 s, 19 short-lived processes per tick, issue #6717): no timer outside the open popover. (b) Sampling inside the supervisor actor could stall stop/launch paths for tens of ms: run reads in a detached utility task off the RunScope handle. (c) A stale "listening" pill is false status: the pid exit watch plus the 'as of' stamp. (d) Overstated totals: label as "memory footprint, approx." (contract §10 already warns summing child memory can double count shared pages) and show only scope members, never "whole machine". (e) An embedded WKWebView is the heaviest thing Loom would own: not built; default browser only.

Scope limits to state honestly in UI copy and docs: Docker, Homebrew services and anything launched through launchd/LaunchServices is outside the scope by construction (contract §6 "Out of scope"). For this backend user a Docker Postgres or Redis will NOT show, only what the agent forked (Spring Boot, node, test runners). The view must say "in this session", not "on this Mac".

Cost re-estimate: M, as the idea says, but only with the light scope. About S for the C function and ScopeInspector with a fixture test (extend loom-test-child to bind a port; RunScopeTests already assembles real scopes), S-M for the popover, model, header wiring and pill, plus docs (ARCHITECTURE, UI-MAP, DESIGN). The embedded WebView would be XL by itself (entitlements, cookies and logins state, teardown when hidden). The LOOM_PORT range is a separate S-M item (allocation persistence, resume stability, and agents only use it if told).

Tests (behaviour, not mirrors): (1) spawn a fixture in a real run scope that binds an ephemeral port and a detached grandchild that also binds one; the inspection lists both and the totals are non-zero. (2) After the scope stops, the inspection is empty and the pill is gone. (3) An unreadable member makes the whole inspection 'unavailable'. (4) The popover model starts no sampling when the window is hidden and stops on close (a counter, like CatalogHotPathTests). (5) No sample is taken on a plain list scroll or card render (statistics counter stays 0).
feasibility.ui_sketch:
Primary surface is the detail header, because the two-row sidebar card is a fixed contract (DESIGN §2 item 4: status, title, time over branch, project, provider icon), and its second row is already full.

1. Header control group (HeaderControlGroup in Sources/LoomCatalogUI/SessionHeaderViews.swift): when a live listener is known, a conditional segment appears before Stop, with the same hairline separation Stop already uses: a small network glyph plus ":3000" (or "2 ports"). The group already adds and removes the Stop segment, so a conditional segment follows the same pattern. Click opens a popover; there is no auto-open. This is a small deviation from D-53's "fixed places", so it needs the user's okay (see decisions).
2. Popover "Processes in this session": a header line "Sampled 12:04:31 - memory approx. 1.8 GB" and a refresh icon; then up to 3 top rows by footprint (name, footprint, CPU %) and a collapsed "N more"; then a "Listening" section: each row is "node  localhost:5173" or "java  all interfaces :8080" with a trailing Open button (the all-interfaces tag is free security info). Footer: "Only what this session started. Docker and services are not included." Text only, no charts, no animation, secondary text tiers from LoomTheme.
3. Entry points that need no layout change: the actions menu (the three-dot menu in the header and the card context menu in SidebarView.swift ~line 500) gets "Processes and Ports...". It opens the same popover, and works with no known listeners.
4. Sidebar card: no pill in v1. Optional later: one 10 pt glyph at the end of the second row, drawn only when a listener is known for a session that is Finished or Waiting (the leaked-dev-server case), as the cheap answer to "which stopped-looking session still holds my port". Recommend this only after the header version is used for a week.
5. Ended or stopped sessions: nothing, since the scope is verified empty after Stop. Never drawn when the window is hidden.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: PASS with the design above. Event-driven only (Stop hook, window activation, popover open, click), one coalition pass for all scopes, a 2 s tick only while the popover is open and the window is visible, nothing when hidden. RISK if implemented as "sample when card visible" (reject that part of the idea). Predictability: PASS. The same click always shows the same sampled-at snapshot; the pill never appears or disappears from a hidden poll. Accurate status: PASS if the pill is dropped on process exit (kqueue exit watch) and the open action re-checks the listener; totals say "approx." and any unreadable member makes the sample 'unavailable' rather than a partial number (matches the fail-closed style of RunScopeTable and contract §3 "not counted as success"). RISK: private coalition flavors are already in use; this adds only public libproc flavors. Fluency: PASS. No confirmation or wait; Open is one click. Modularity: PASS. A C function, one LoomCore value-type file, one UI model and view; LoomCore stays UI-free, and the dev-only EvidenceResourcePool can later reuse ScopeInspector. CLI-update resilience: PASS, the best of any v2 idea. It depends on macOS libproc, not on any Claude CLI output, hook or file format, and needs no drift detector. Process ownership: PASS and a strength. Naming only scope members is exactly 'name only what Loom started'; scope boundaries (launchd and Docker excluded) must be stated honestly in the copy. User authority: PASS. Read-only; an 'End this process' action is deliberately not included (it would be a user-initiated, verified signal via RunScopeTable.signal and is a separate decision). The contract's terminal-is-the-real-CLI rule and D-34 (no right rail) are untouched, since this is a popover, not a sidebar. D-20 is not triggered (no CLI behaviour changes). A LOOM_PORT env would be a launch-environment change; it is deferred.
feasibility.value_reason: Real but not a daily driver. Several concurrent sessions with JVM or node plus test runs make 'which session holds the RAM / who owns :8080' a genuine question, and it feeds the manual Stop decision (Loom has no auto-park; D-38 turned idle stop off). But the user is backend-focused, so an 'Open localhost' browser pill has low payoff (APIs, and Docker-hosted databases are invisible by construction); the useful backend case is port-conflict and leaked-process visibility, which the popover covers. The big productivity levers in the research (side chat, verified send, hibernate, transcript search) are worth more; this is a cheap, safe secondary feature that reuses existing primitives.
depends_on: none hard. Soft: an idle-hibernate/park idea (this feeds that decision); a verified 'End this process' action would build on it; LOOM_PORT belongs with any worktree/env-injection idea.
experiments: Listener-read spike with loom-probe or a throwaway Swift script inside an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and a real Loom run scope (never the user's real ~/.claude): run listeners as an Apple binary (/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server), a node server bound to localhost (::1 only), a JVM (java -jar or Spring Boot-like) and a reparented/double-forked listener. Decide: does PROC_PIDLISTFDS plus PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO work unprivileged for same-uid processes of all four kinds (Apple/hardened-runtime binaries are the doubt), and do IPv6 dual-stack sockets report a usable port and address? Pass: all four listed, no EPERM on same-uid processes.

Cost spike on the same setup, only when the user says the computer is idle (D-13): time one full inspection of 10 scopes x ~10 processes, and the popover's 2 s tick for 60 s. Pass: a sample well under 20 ms and under 1% of a core average during the open popover, nothing measurable otherwise; also confirm the CPU gate (40% at 1 MiB/s, contract §10) is unchanged. If `loom_scopes_members` shows >50 ms stalls from its retry sleeps, make the inspector tolerate that off-actor rather than change the stop path.

Memory-number sanity check: compare the summed `ri_phys_footprint` of a scope against Activity Monitor's Memory column and `footprint` for the same processes. Decide the label ('approx.') and whether to show only the total or per process. Do not claim better than approximate (Conductor had to fix wrong totals twice).
user_decisions: Is a conditional port segment in the header control group acceptable (a small deviation from D-53's fixed-places rule), or should v1 be menu-only ('Processes and Ports...' in the three-dot menu) with no pill at all?

Should the popover offer 'End process' for a leaked dev server, a verified signal to one scope member that the user clicks, or stay read-only and leave stopping to the existing whole-session Stop? Read-only is the lighter default.
Is 'Open localhost:PORT' in the default browser enough, or do you really want an embedded WKWebView? Recommendation: no WebView; it is the heaviest component and contradicts 'idle costs nothing'.

Is a LOOM_PORT range per session wanted at all? It only helps if your project scripts read it (for example server.port=${LOOM_PORT:8080}) or agents are told to; if yes it belongs with a worktree/env idea, not here.
Do you want the optional sidebar-card glyph for 'finished but still listening' sessions after trying the header version, given it touches the fixed two-row card contract?

feasibility.one_line: Loom already ships most of this (per-row equality-guarded sidebar with a body-count harness, offset+inode transcript tailing, visibility-gated work, session-scoped 1 s hooks, drift detection), so adopt only the missing slice: a parametrised 1/10/100 render-budget test table that every v2 per-card or per-panel datum must join, value-free hook-payload shape fixtures re-captured on CLI change, and a drift explanation string, with no bundled bad-version JSON and no network fetch.
feasibility.loom_design:
STATE TODAY (read in code, so most of the idea is already done)
(a) Sidebar budget. SidebarRenderTests (Tests/LoomCatalogUITests/SidebarRenderTests.swift) hosts the real SidebarView in a never-shown 3,200 pt window with 30 cards and counts card and time-label body evaluations through SidebarRenderProbe. It asserts: a selection change evaluates 2 cards; the minute tick evaluates 0 cards and 30 labels and does not regroup the days; an Active-section flip evaluates the moved card at most once and no others. CatalogHotPathTests covers row patches, one search query, and equal-value refresh writing no observed property. CatalogScaleTests measures catalog queries at 1,000 and 10,000 rows. The mechanism differs from cmux's: Loom uses per-row @Observable SessionRowModel with apply(...) equality guards (CatalogModel.swift ~l.101-146), not Equatable value snapshots plus .equatable(). The result is the same invariant (a change evaluates only the affected card), so do NOT rewrite to the cmux pattern.
(b) Reader regression. ClaudeUsageIndex keeps per-file (dev, ino, byte offset, 64-byte guard hash) and reads only appended bytes. SubagentTranscriptTail reads only new whole lines, holds back a partial last line, restarts on a shrink or a new inode, and cold-opens on the last 512 KiB. Tests: ClaudeUsageIndexTests.appendReadsOnlyTheNewBytes, shrinkReparses..., replacedFileWithANewInode..., tamperedBytes...; SubagentTranscriptTests.onlyNewBytesAreRead, anIdleFileDeliversNothing, aBurstOfWritesIsCoalescedIntoFewReads. Wake-ups are event-driven: UsageTranscriptWatcher is FSEvents, and the SubagentTranscriptFeed is one vnode source that runs only while its panel is on screen and the window is visible, capped at 5 reads/s. The Happy failure mode (3 s full re-read) is structurally excluded already.
(c) Hidden means no work. CatalogModel.setWindowVisible (CatalogModel.swift ~l.1034) stops the minute tick and the subagent feed. The working indicator is a Core Animation keyframe animation in the render server (IndicatorView.swift ChaseDots), documented as zero wakeups and zero SwiftUI updates, because a TimelineView re-evaluated the whole graph. SwiftTerm has hidden-window suspension (patch suspended-signal-retention). The usage model collects only changed paths while hidden (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Finished turn and usage'). Measured baseline: working indicator under reduced motion about 0.005% of a core, hidden stream1 3.5%, idle observer with one real Claude 0.044% (DEVELOPMENT.md section 7).
(f) Hook hygiene. ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings puts 9 events in the per-session --settings only (nothing in the user's global settings, contract section 9) with timeout 1, args [], and deliberately no per-tool hooks. loom-hook (Sources/loom-hook/main.swift) exits at once with a log line when LOOM_* env is missing, uses a 0.5 s socket timeout, and a wrong token gets a NAK. HookDiagnostics counts received, applied, malformed, overflow and dropped-by-reason into the diagnostics export. A hook-silence watchdog (3 s, SessionIssueNotice) exists.
(e) Drift. ProviderCapabilities is read from claude --help; ExecutableStamp re-resolves the toolchain after a CLI update; a missing required option never refuses a start (reportCompatibility journals cli_compat_warning once per version and option set); the registry reports unknown statuses once; the journal records claude_cli. This matches contract section 9 and D-45.

WHAT IS MISSING (the adoptable slice)
1. Render-budget table (extend SidebarRenderTests; test-only, no runtime cost). Make host(cards:) parametric over 1/10/100 and add table-driven rows: 'a write to field X of session A evaluates exactly card A'. Seed rows now for fields that exist (live state, subagent list update, pin, rename, title, project tone), and add one row for every v2 per-card datum when its feature lands. Add rows for writes to shared model properties. Hypothesis, not yet measured: SessionCardView.body reads model.projects (through projectName(for:) -> projects.first), model.branches (a whole dictionary) and model.viewMode, and CatalogModel.toggleCollapsed rewrites projects via refreshProjects, so a collapse toggle or rename probably evaluates every loaded card. The first table run will confirm or refute this. Then give the rule in writing: new per-card data lives on SessionRowModel with an equality-guarded apply(...), never in a model-wide dictionary read by every card body.
2. A 'live burst' case: 30 sessions with hub frames (status, subagents, activity stamp) arriving in a burst, asserting body evaluations per frame stay at or below 1 card (the 100 ms patch path, CatalogModel+Patching). SidebarRenderTests uses only idle cards today.
3. Panel gate. When a v2 right panel or chat view arrives it registers with the same visibility edge (setWindowVisible, plus an on-screen flag as SubagentTranscriptModel does: wanted = !closed && onScreen && windowVisible). One test per consumer: hidden means zero timers, zero reads, zero scheduled sleeps. SidebarRenderTests already shows the pattern (gate.requested.count).
4. Hook payload shape fixtures. Today every payload in ClaudeHookTests and SubagentTests is hand-written (SubagentTests says shapes follow 'the 12 Oct 2026 research of Claude 2.1.293'; the CLI is now 2.1.300). Add a capture mode to the existing loom-probe hook-expect experiment (Sources/loom-probe/ProviderExperiment.swift, plans/experiments/claude-hooks.json). It runs a real claude (haiku, low effort, isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) through about 4 short turns: a plain turn, a tool needing approval, a subagent, /clear. It dumps value-free shapes per event (key names and JSON types only) to Tests/LoomCoreTests/Fixtures/hook-shapes-<version>.json. A test loads the newest fixture, builds payloads from it and asserts that ClaudeHookEvent and ClaudeHookStateTracker read the fields Loom depends on (session_id, hook_event_name, transcript_path, agent_id, background_tasks[].type/status, last_assistant_message, notification_type, tool_name). A re-capture on a CLI change diffs old vs new shapes, which is the 'CLI-update surprise' detector, and runs only when the user says the Mac is idle (short real-Claude turns are pre-authorized by D-04). Keep it value-free like the other plans/experiments JSON. Approval answering is not in Loom today (PermissionRequest only detects state, the helper returns no decision), so no approval-decision contract is needed yet. If an actionable-approval idea is ever adopted, add the PermissionRequest and AskUserQuestion updatedInput captures first; the research notes that the AskUserQuestion-on-PermissionRequest path is undocumented and that CLI 2.1.300 now validates updatedInput.
5. Drift explanation without a feed. Keep one constant for the CLI version the shipped Loom was last captured against (written by the capture step). When a drift event fires (cli_compat_warning, an unknown registry status, hook_silence), add 'Claude <installed>; this Loom was last checked with <captured>' to the existing issue text and the diagnostics summary. No bundled known-bad JSON (Loom has no list of bad versions to ship, and the owner updates Loom manually, D-47). No launch fetch (it would be Loom's first network code, which D-32/D-37 avoided, and it adds a failure mode). No banner on a merely newer version: the user runs the latest CLI, so it would fire constantly and teach dismissal. T3's 'version gate' is advisory-only in code (the fact-check says it is 'graceful' from 2.1.111 and only below that 'unsupported'), so an advisory is compatible with 'never pin' only when it appears as the explanation for observed drift.
6. Perf scenario (optional, +M, idle Mac only). Add a 'cards30' scenario to scripts/cp5-d-measure.py or scripts/perf/indicator_cost.py using loom-fake-provider: 30 sessions, 5 'working', window visible vs hidden, N hook frames per second; report Loom's own CPU and wakeups and judge them with compare_baseline.py gates. The existing matrix covers terminal streaming (stream1/10, spinner1) but never a crowded sidebar.

SPIKE (decides one number): hook helper latency under load. Run the built loom-hook against a stub listening socket 1,000 times with synthetic stdin, once idle and once while swift build runs, and record p50/p95/max wall time. If p95 is far below the 1 s settings timeout the value stays; if max approaches it, raise it. A killed helper loses an event silently (the watchdog covers only 'no hook ever'), which is the same hazard as Superset's slow UserPromptSubmit (single-machine 12.8 s). Do not move the hooks to async: the code comment says synchronous is chosen so helper racing cannot reorder identity and state.

TRIGGERS AND BOUNDS: everything above is test-time or developer-time; the runtime change is one string constant. Nothing polls, and no runtime reads or timers are added. Window-hosting tests and the perf scenario run only when the user says the Mac is idle (DEVELOPMENT.md section 3); the shape-capture needs 4 short haiku turns in an isolated profile.
feasibility.ui_sketch: Almost no UI. The only user-visible change is one extra clause in an existing notice: when drift is observed, the SessionIssueNotice line above the terminal, or the Settings > About diagnostics, says 'Claude 2.1.3xx; this Loom was last checked with 2.1.300'. There is no new banner, no new settings page and no new sidebar element. The point is that the future right panel, chat view and richer cards must not make the existing UI heavier.
feasibility.principle_check: Resources: pass. These are tests and developer tooling, and the runtime adds nothing (no poll, no read, no timer, no network). A launch-time conditional fetch would be a first network dependency and is rejected. Predictability: pass; body-evaluation counts are deterministic, whereas CPU gates are noisy, so use counts in tests and CPU only in idle-Mac measurements. Accurate status: pass and improved; shape fixtures catch a silent payload change before it makes a status wrong. Risk: a fixture frozen at 2.1.300 can falsely reassure, so the capture date and version must be stored and the test must name them. Fluency: pass; no new prompts or waits. Modularity: pass; the budget table sits beside the existing SidebarRenderProbe and the capture lives in loom-probe, which is dev-only, so nothing lands in the release tree (check.sh --release-tree must still pass). CLI-update resilience: pass if the advisory stays an explanation attached to observed drift. It becomes a violation only if it gates a start by version or ships a hand-maintained known-bad list that Loom then trusts (contract: 'versions not pinned', 'no result inferred from an unknown event'). Ownership: unaffected. User authority: unaffected, because there are no cross-session actions. Risk: the heavy runs (window tests, perf scenario, real turns) must follow the idle-Mac rule or they cause the heat the user's policy forbids. Standing decisions D-34 and the 'terminal is the real CLI' rule are not touched.
feasibility.value_reason: It is protective, not a feature. A v2 chat-centred UI, right panel and richer cards are where the daily-use properties (no beachball with 30+ sessions, accurate status, low idle CPU) are most likely to regress, and the shape fixtures plus the table give early warning at low cost. It is not a 4 because Loom already has the hard parts (O(1) card patching, incremental readers, hidden gating), so what remains is mostly discipline and a test table, not new capability. It rises to 4 if the chat-centred UI renders transcripts in SwiftUI, which is the largest new CPU risk.
depends_on: Any v2 feature that adds per-card data, a right panel, or a transcript-rendering chat view (each adds one row to the budget table)
D-04 pre-authorization of short real-Claude turns, and the idle-Mac rule, for the shape capture and the perf scenario
experiments: Run the extended SidebarRenderTests (1/10/100 cards, shared-property writes) once with the user's idle-Mac go-ahead. It decides whether a project collapse or rename, or a change to branches, evaluates every loaded card as suspected. If yes, move projectName, tone and branch label onto SessionRowModel as equality-guarded fields. If no, the hypothesis is closed.

Hook helper latency: 1,000 loom-hook runs against a stub socket, idle vs under a concurrent build, p50/p95/max against the 1 s timeout in ProviderLaunchProfile.claudeSettings. Decides whether timeout 1 stays.

One real-Claude shape capture on 2.1.300 (about 4 haiku turns, isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) diffed against the hand-written payloads in SubagentTests and ClaudeHookTests. Decides whether any assumed field is stale; this is the first value of the fixtures.
Optional cards30 CPU scenario with loom-fake-provider, window visible vs hidden, to confirm that a crowded sidebar stays well under the 40% gate and that hidden costs about nothing.
user_decisions: Is it acceptable to add a small 'last checked with Claude X' constant that is refreshed whenever the shape capture is re-run, given that the user publishes Loom releases by hand? The alternative is no version text at all.
Should the capture and the perf scenario be part of the release checklist (run on each CLI minor bump) or stay an on-demand tool the planner runs? The first costs a few real turns per release.
If the chat-centred UI goes ahead, should its transcript renderer have a hard budget (rows drawn, bytes parsed per second, hidden means zero) written into the contract before the design is chosen?

directions.name: Loom Cockpit
directions.thesis: The real Claude Code terminal stays the centre of Loom. Loom v2 makes everything around it the best attention, context and review instrument for a person who runs 3-6 CLI sessions across two work projects. Every session answers four questions without being opened: Does it need me? Why, in one line? What did it change and what state is it in (context size, branch, PR/CI, plan pace)? What is the one key that acts on it? Loom stays a native host that owns the process, proves outcomes and draws nothing it does not need. It adds read-only views (a Conversation view, a Changes view, the existing subagent panel) and a very small, verified, draft-first send path. It does not add a chat engine, a worktree orchestrator, a browser or a daemon. Anthropic is absorbing the breadth (Desktop diff, side chat, agent view); a light local app can only win on triage, truth and cost. The product rule is: terminal for doing, Loom for knowing, one key to get from knowing to doing. Chat-style rendering is used only where it is read-only or clearly cheaper than a live terminal (idle, stopped and catch-up reading, search results, side questions). Evidence-led escape valve: if the Conversation view becomes the way the user reads most of the time, a composer-led direction is reconsidered in a later round with data, not now.
directions.day_in_the_life:
08:40 Berke opens Loom on the Mac. A banner row in the Active area says 'Ended with Loom: 3. Reopen all / Dismiss' (I-21). He reopens the two EDDP-* sessions and dismisses the experiment. The sidebar shows the In work list (I-18) with yesterday's four tickets; two cards carry a ticket chip (EDDP-412, EDDP-415). The footer shows '1.1M today, 5h 22%' with no pace warning.

09:05 He presses Option+Cmd+N, the new-session sheet appears (I-33), the EDDP-415 chip is already offered from recents, preset 'plan + high' is selected, he types the first message and presses Return. The session starts in plan mode. He continues in the real terminal. Keep-awake (I-20) is on, so the Mac does not sleep while it works.

10:30 He is deep in a terminal reviewing a plan. The menu bar badge turns orange. The card of EDDP-412 says under its title 'Bash: git push origin feature/EDDP-412' (I-14) and the Dock badge says 1. He ignores it until his thought ends, presses Cmd+J (next session that needs me), lands in that terminal, reads the real dialog and answers it with the CLI's own keys. The banner for an approval carried the command text too, so he knew it was safe before switching. A second card turns blue: 'Finished, unviewed'. Its second line shows the tail of the last message: '...want me to keep the old endpoint, or remove it?'. He knows it needs a decision, not a read.

11:10 A third session, EDDP-415, is Working for a long run. He opens the right inspector with Cmd+Opt+S and types a question into Ask Aside (I-09): the real CLI forked from that session in plan mode, nested under the card, nothing enters the main thread. While it answers, a long answer is catching up: the header shows 'ctx 412k' and the state pill says 'Working, 2 subagents'. He clicks a subagent row: the existing read-only transcript replaces the terminal in place (unchanged).

12:20 EDDP-412 finishes. The card shows '+120 -8 in 5 files' and a PR token '#482, checks running' (I-28, I-31). He presses the header Changes chip, reads the diff in the right inspector, selects two hunks, writes two comments and presses 'Stage in prompt'. Loom pastes one structured block into the session prompt without pressing Return (I-29 over I-01 draft-only). He looks at the terminal, edits one word and presses Return himself; the card then says 'Delivered' once the hook confirms. He did not use a chat composer; the CLI prompt is still where he types.

14:00 He quits for lunch with two sessions mid-run. Quit stops everything, verified. At 15:00 reopening shows 'Ended with Loom: 2'. A stopped session opens in the Conversation view (I-05): rendered markdown, folded tool rows, readable without a process or live terminal; Resume is one click. He searches 'idempotency' in the sidebar and a section 'In conversations' lists three sessions with a snippet (I-41).

17:40 The footer chip turns orange: 'at this pace the 5-hour window ends around 18:30, resets 20:15' (I-25). He parks the lowest-priority work: Mark Done on two In work items. Cmd+Q: the quit sheet names the Working sessions (I-17). Nothing leaks, nothing polls.
directions.layout:
Three columns; the centre is always the terminal (or one of the read-only views in the same slot). Right inspector is collapsed by default (nothing drawn, nothing watched, no PTY resize while closed) and has one tab per tenant that exists: Side (a forked real CLI), Changes, Conversation. It narrows the detail pane (480 pt min), so the auto-collapse of the sidebar at small widths is the default; SIGWINCH on open/close is coalesced to one resize.

Header fixed places (D-53) plus conditional chips that drop right-to-left when narrow: state pill+reason, project+branch, Changes chip, PR chip, context figure, Stop, ... menu, inspector toggle.
Menu bar item: Needs-you list with reason line per row (and Allow/Deny only if I-15 passes its spike), 'Keeping Mac awake' line, Quit-sheet text names Working sessions.
Menus: Session > Next Needing Me (Cmd+J), Ask Aside / /btw, Send Text to Session..., Show Changes, Mark Done, New Session... (Option+Cmd+N); Dock menu mirrors Needs you.
Overlays: new-session sheet (palette style, opacity only), send popover over the terminal (draft default), ended-with-Loom heading row, quit sheet.
design_pattern_changes: D-34 (no right sidebar): lifted for exactly one purpose, a collapsed-by-default right inspector hosting side session, Changes and read-only Conversation. Still no left rail. Why: the user wanted this panel since Herdr Desktop and a fork/diff needs a place that does not replace the terminal.

Contract/DESIGN 2.6 'terminal is never replaced by a custom chat UI' is reworded to 'the live session is always the real terminal; Loom adds read-only views and a draft-first send path'. Why: allows the Conversation view for stopped/idle sessions and the live catch-up toggle without making chat the primary surface. UI-MAP 'No chat UI' changes in the same way.

D-54 point 3 (stopped session shows the last terminal screen, ~4 MiB snapshot): the Conversation view replaces the static ended-screen snapshot for sessions without a terminal, if the user agrees, with the snapshot kept only if it proves useful for pending dialogs. Why: searchable, lighter, no snapshot held in memory.

DESIGN section 2.4 two-row card: kept, except a conditional third line on attention-state cards only (asking / last said). Why: 'who needs me and why' is the product; the row is drawn only while the state holds, so a quiet list stays exactly two rows. The never-drawn status label rule is unchanged.
D-53 header fixed places: header keeps its fixed places for pill/chip/controls but gains conditional chips (changes, PR, context) with a strict drop order, rather than new always-visible controls.

D-52 (banners only for approvals): approval banners gain tool and command text; an opt-in, default-off 'finished or failed' banner when away. Why: reason in the banner is triage; opt-in keeps it quiet.
D-38 (idle sessions never stop): unchanged by default; an opt-in 'Sleep' for idle sessions (I-19) is added only after the resume-fidelity spike, with the setting off.

PermissionRequest hook stays decision-free in Phase 1-2. In Phase 3 it may change to a held, decision-returning hook (I-15) only if the hook/dialog race spike passes; this needs a new DECISIONS entry and an amendment to the CP2 text in the contract. Otherwise approvals stay answered in the CLI.

D-43/D-46 (cross-session channel wanted, undated): given a date only for the read side (I-36) and user-initiated send (I-37 slice 1) in Phase 4, and only after the I-01 spike; agent-initiated sends stay behind a per-message approval card.
D-20/D-32 wording: the per-session --settings may later carry more than hooks only if a statusLine bridge is adopted; not planned here (I-24 excluded).
Header 'Stop' stays the only Loom-originated process action; no new action may report success without a verified outcome (send uses queued/pasted/delivered/outcome unknown vocabulary; never retried).
Resource rules gain a budget table (I-44): every per-card or per-panel datum must pass a 1/10/100-card render test and a hidden-means-zero check before it ships.

phases.name: P0 Evidence week (no UI)
phases.goal: One isolated-profile Claude session of hook recording and probes answers the questions that decide later phases, so nothing speculative is built. Uses loom-probe HookRecorder, a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and a few short Haiku turns (D-04), never the real ~/.claude.
phases.exit_criteria: Written findings with fixtures for: hook payloads (Notification text, PermissionRequest tool_input, AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode path, Stop last_assistant_message shape, permission_mode); send matrix and modal visibility (I-01 E1/E2: is 'submit' allowed or draft-only); hook/dialog race (I-15 E1); fork flags, cache and residue (I-09 E1-E6); main-session JSONL shapes and window size (I-05 E1, I-23 E1/E2); resume fidelity (I-19); goal trace (I-39 E1); input-fidelity checklist run when the Mac is idle. Each later phase item is marked go, draft-only, or drop with evidence. No code ships.

phases.name: P1 Triage: who needs me, and why
phases.goal: Make the sidebar, header, menu bar and notifications answer 'does it need me, for what' without opening it, with truthful status and almost no new cost.
phases.exit_criteria: Sticky Failed, pinned regression sequences for resume/compact/background work, and a 'Why this status' readout shipped; attention cards show a bounded memory-only reason line (tool+command or last-message tail) only while the state holds; subagent rows name which subagent asked and never stay 'running'; approval banners carry tool and command text with a setting; away-aware viewed state, opt-in finish banner, Dock menu and quit sheet naming Working sessions; keep-awake setting with indicator; context figure in tokens (percent only where the window is known); plan pace on the footer chip with stale marker; a menu item that types '/btw ' into the terminal; I-44 render-budget table (1/10/100) and hook shape fixtures in CI; CPU gate unchanged (40% of a core at 1 MiB/s), hidden window still evaluates zero cards.

phases.name: P2 Memory: what happened and where was I
phases.goal: Read-only views and cheap derived state so a stopped, idle or forgotten session is readable, searchable and resumable, and a ticket is one thread.
phases.exit_criteria: Conversation view ships first for sessions with no terminal (stopped, stale, after relaunch), then a live Terminal/Chat toggle after real use; cold open reads <= ~1.5 MiB, hidden/stopped view holds no descriptor or watcher; '+N -M, K files' chip with Copy Patch / Open in Editor from an owned bounded git read; opt-in GitHub-only PR/check chip via one bounded gh call at existing events; ticket chip, search by key and New Session from Ticket; In work list (one flag, Done key); 'Ended with Loom' reopen offer; 'In conversations' search section on a budgeted scan; Usage cards By project/source/ticket; header-menu 'Processes and Ports'; goal marker with no false Finished (if the spike says needed); opt-in Sleep for idle sessions (only if fidelity spike passed). All cost checks pass at 1 MiB/s terminal load; no polling added.

phases.name: P3 Act: one key from knowing to doing
phases.goal: Turn the knowledge into verified actions on the real CLI, always draft-first and never claiming success without proof.
phases.exit_criteria: Send primitive (hook-gated, bracketed paste into the prompt, UserPromptSubmit-confirmed 'delivered', never retried) with 'Place in Prompt' default and 'Send' only if the P0 matrix passed 20/20; per-session 'after this turn' queue strip with edit/cancel and honest outcomes (memory only); new-session sheet with JSON presets and permission-mode chip; roll-up row of opened sessions under the parent with one capped batch approval; if and only if the P0 race passed: Allow/Deny from the approval box and menu bar with 'handed back to terminal' on timeout, and AskUserQuestion/plan read cards, otherwise approvals remain in the CLI. Opening a send path never writes into a dialog (checked on the modal matrix).

phases.name: P4 Inspector: side questions, review loop, cross-session reads
phases.goal: Add the right inspector and the review loop on top of verified send, without letting the panel become a second app.
phases.exit_criteria: Right inspector (D-34 lifted) with a Side tab as a forked real CLI in plan mode, nested hidden under its parent card, with Discard (verified delete, cascade with parent) and Bring Back (paste into the main prompt, user presses Return); a Changes tab with read-only diff and batched comments staged as one draft; read verbs sessions/status/wait on the existing control socket for coordinator sessions; user-initiated Send to Session with verified outcomes. Pane closed means nothing runs; opening costs one coalesced resize; Changes pane only ships if Claude's own /diff proves awkward in Loom's terminal.

excluded.id_or_what: I-06 (chat lens with composer over the live PTY) and I-03 (native composer overlay)
excluded.why: Cockpit keeps typing in the CLI. A composer would need the same unproven write path plus a stray-Enter risk. The read-only half (I-05) and the small send popover (I-01) cover the real needs; revisit only if usage data shows the Conversation view replacing the terminal.

excluded.id_or_what: I-07 (Chat mode: stream-json child per session)
excluded.why: XL engine, billing/policy exposure for headless use, parity gaps (skills, MCP, TUI dialogs). It is the right engine for a chat-centred Loom, not for a cockpit.

excluded.id_or_what: I-13 (OSC 7501 receiver)
excluded.why: Value 2; most of the reason text already comes from hook fields. Revisit if Claude emits it in hook-silent states.

excluded.id_or_what: I-24 (statusLine bridge)
excluded.why: Takes over the user's statusLine and may hide CLI footer hints; transcript tokens (I-23) and gh (I-31) cover most of the gain. Hold until a spike shows the hints survive.

excluded.id_or_what: I-30 (per-turn checkpoints)
excluded.why: Git snapshots per turn, storage and deletion duties, and the chip from I-28 gives most triage value. Later.

excluded.id_or_what: I-32 (worktree-backed sessions)
excluded.why: Contested value; collisions are rare in a 2-3 session practice and Claude's own worktree support exists. Ask the user how often two sessions collide before spending M.

excluded.id_or_what: I-38 (session digest / handoff)
excluded.why: Keeps a second content copy of transcripts, conflicts with contract section 7; the user's own handoff skill covers it.

excluded.id_or_what: I-22 (supervisor/Run detached), I-42 (Remote Control), I-40 (scheduled runs), I-27 (multi-account)
excluded.why: Break Quit-stops-all or add ownership/plan costs, or the user never asked for them (phone, second account). Later or on request.

excluded.id_or_what: Daemon/PTY multiplexer, SDK/ACP/Node host, TUI scraping, notch overlay and mascots, relay/push server, embedded browser, auto reviewer agent, kanban/task runner, plugin marketplace, auto-commit and in-app accept/reject, polling dashboards, agent-teams concept
excluded.why: Standing skips from the catalog: each breaks process ownership, update resilience, or the resource principles that define the app.

risks: The send path (I-01) is the shared foundation of P3-P4 and rests on undocumented TUI behaviour (paste, delay, modal visibility). If the spike fails, the cockpit still works as a read/triage product but the review loop becomes copy-patch only. Mitigation: draft-only default and P0 first.

Anthropic keeps absorbing features (Desktop diff and side chat, agent view, Remote Control); the defensible core is cross-project triage and truth, not any single feature. Keep the plan to what a light local app does better and drop items Claude's CLI ships well (/diff, /btw, /goal).

Header and card crowding: conditional chips plus a third attention line push against the two-row contract. Needs a design preview round and strict drop order; if it fails, move the data to tooltips and the inspector.
Reason lines expose commands and paths on a locked screen and in notifications. Needs Settings switches and bounded memory-only text; never persisted.
Right inspector narrows the PTY and the Claude TUI reflows (SIGWINCH). Mitigation: collapsed default, one coalesced resize, auto-collapse sidebar; a slide-over or tab fallback if it feels bad.
Hook drift: status accuracy depends on documented but subtle hook semantics (Stop vs interrupt, idle_prompt, background_tasks). Mitigation: fixtures per CLI version, drift advisory, never pin.
Scope creep from the Conversation view into a chat product (markdown, diffs, composer pressure). Keep it read-only and gated by evidence of use.

Several ideas depend on the user's unanswered facts: GitHub vs GitLab, tickets and worktree habits, permission mode used, whether they hand-type /goal. Wrong guesses waste M-sized items; ask before P2.
Resource creep: gh, git and transcript scans are the first work Loom does off its own files. Each must be event-driven, bounded, cancelled on Quit and visible-only, with a render and CPU test.
Reopening D-38 or the contract's chat rule requires the user's explicit decision, not an agent's.
directions.effort: Roughly 3.5-4.5 months of solo agentic work, mostly S/M items. P0: ~1 week and some real-turn spend; P1: ~3 weeks (nine S/M items, mostly pure state and hook fields already received); P2: ~5-6 weeks (I-05 is the only L, with I-28 chip, I-31, I-41 as M); P3: ~4 weeks (I-01/I-02 M, I-15 M if it passes); P4: ~5 weeks (I-09 and I-10 are L, I-29 is L). Each phase ships on its own and P1 alone changes daily use.
directions.identity: Orca, cmux, Conductor, T3 Code and Claude Desktop are workspaces that own the agent: a worktree orchestrator with embedded diff and browser (Orca, Conductor), a terminal multiplexer with browser panes (cmux), a chat shell over the SDK or ACP (T3 Code, Conductor), or the vendor's own engine and cloud (Claude Desktop). Loom Cockpit owns only the process and the truth. It hosts the unmodified CLI in a verified run scope, reads the documented hook, registry and usage surfaces, and presents attention, reason, change, cost and context across projects on one screen, with outcomes it can prove (delivered, stopped, deleted) instead of optimistic UI. No daemon, no worktree manager, no embedded browser, no model call of its own, nothing drawn while hidden. Where the others render the conversation, Loom keeps the CLI and adds an instrument panel and a draft-first, never-retried send path. Its edge is being the light, native, always-correct second brain for several sessions, not a better IDE or chat window."

directions.name: Loom Lens (conversation-first hybrid)
directions.thesis: The conversation is the front door, the real terminal is the engine room. Every session opens as a native, readable conversation rendered from the transcript of the SAME real Claude CLI process Loom already owns (no second engine, no SDK, no Node), with a composer, approval and question cards, and a right panel for side chat and subagents. One click switches the centre to the real PTY, which stays authoritative for everything Loom does not model (slash menus, pickers, dialogs, skills, MCP). The bet is that most of the user's day is reading, triaging and giving short follow-ups, which a chat view does better than a terminal, while the 'real CLI is always there' fallback keeps update resilience and the billing/policy posture intact. The chat default for LIVE sessions is earned, not assumed: it ships behind spike results (send fidelity, dialog discrimination, hook race). If those fail, the product degrades gracefully to 'excellent reader + draft-only composer + terminal for dialogs', which is still a better Loom than today.
directions.day_in_the_life:
08:50 Launch. Quit stopped everything yesterday, so Active is empty, but the sidebar shows a 'Reopen what was running (4)' offer (I-21) and an 'In work' shelf with EDDP-412 and EDDP-415 (I-18). Stopped sessions open instantly as readable conversations, no terminal and no process (I-05): I skim yesterday's EDDP-412 review thread, hit Cmd+F 'idempotency' and find the right session by a content snippet (I-41). I Reopen only EDDP-415; it resumes and shows 'Resuming'.
09:10 New work: Option+Cmd+N sheet (I-33), project=api, ticket EDDP-418 (the sheet de-dups against existing EDDP-418 sessions, I-34), preset 'plan mode, high effort'. The first message goes in as the launch argument, so no PTY injection is needed. The session opens in Chat view: markdown answer, tool calls folded per turn, an Edit row with +32 -8. The card shows '412k' context once it matters and, while Needs approval, a third line 'Bash: git push origin feat/EDDP-418' (I-14, I-23).
09:40 While EDDP-418 works I want to know who calls revoke(). Cmd+; (layout-checked) opens the right panel at Side chat: a forked real CLI session in plan mode, seeded with the parent's context (I-09). I type the question in the panel's composer; it answers as a conversation in the panel, while the main thread is untouched and keeps working. I click 'Bring back', which puts a two-line summary as an unsent draft in the main composer. The main chat never saw the side thread. Closing the panel with Discard deletes the fork with the verified-deletion machinery.
10:15 A notification: EDDP-415 needs approval. Cmd+J jumps there; the Chat view shows a card 'Bash wants to run: <full command>', with 'Answer in Terminal' always available and, only if the hook-race spike passed, Allow/Deny (I-16, I-15). An AskUserQuestion appears as a real question card instead of a TUI menu. I answer and the card turns into 'Sent, waiting for Claude to continue' then disappears when the hook shows the turn moving.
11:00 EDDP-418 spawns four subagents. The sidebar tree shows who is running; the one that asked for approval carries the attention glyph (I-11). I click one and its live transcript opens in the right panel BESIDE the main conversation (no terminal resize because the centre is native), with tokens in its header.
11:30 EDDP-418 finishes: blue Finished, the turn footer reads '5 files +120 -8 / Copy patch / Open in editor' (I-28 light). I review in the IDE and type a follow-up in the composer: 'Place in Prompt' (draft) or 'Send' (enabled only when hooks prove a clean idle prompt); the card shows 'delivered' only when UserPromptSubmit confirms it (I-01). For EDDP-415 which is still Working I queue 'after this turn: run the migration tests' (I-02), visible and cancellable above the composer.
14:00 The footer chip warns 'at this pace the 5-hour window ends about 15:40' (I-25). I Stop one low-value session; Stop is verified. A long answer from yesterday needs the real thing, so I press the Chat|Terminal segment and use /resume and a skill in the actual TUI; the panel auto-hides while the terminal shows, and comes back when I return.
17:30 Quit stops everything (as today). Tomorrow every ended session is still a readable, searchable conversation costing nothing.

RIGHT is a new collapsed-by-default inspector (NSSplitViewItem inspector, remembered width 340-640) hosting exactly two tenants at first: Side chat and Subagent transcript (a third, Changes, only if I-28 phase 2 is ever built). Terminal mode: centre = today's PTY surface, composer/queue strip hidden, right panel auto-collapsed and restored on return (the only place a PTY resize can happen is the switch, coalesced once). Stopped/ended sessions: Chat view only, with a Resume action; no live terminal, no 4 MiB snapshot. Overlays: new-session sheet (popover-style, Option+Cmd+N), Send-text and quick-queue popover, pill popover 'Why this status' (I-12), Quit sheet that names working sessions. Menu bar: item and Needs-you list unchanged; Session menu gains Toggle Chat/Terminal, Ask Aside (Cmd+; if typeable on Turkish Q, else a letter chord), Toggle Right Panel, Send Text to Session, Queue. Dock badge, Cmd+J, notifications unchanged (approvals only, D-52).
design_pattern_changes: DESIGN section 1 item 6 / UI-MAP 'No chat UI' / contract core-experience row: 'the terminal text is the real CLI, never replaced by a custom chat UI' becomes 'the live session is always the real CLI process in a PTY Loom owns; Loom adds views of it. The terminal is one click away, is authoritative, and is the fallback for every dialog Loom does not model. Loom never emulates CLI features (slash menus, pickers, plan/model switchers) and never scrapes the TUI.' Why: the user is now open to a chat-centred UI, and a lens over the same process keeps update resilience, ownership and billing posture.

D-34 (no right sidebar): lifted for exactly one collapsed-by-default right inspector with two tenants (Side chat, Subagent transcript). No left rail is added. Why: the user's long-standing wish, and the chat-centred centre is native so opening the panel does not SIGWINCH a running TUI.

D-54 P1 (subagent click replaces the terminal in place): the transcript opens in the right panel beside the main conversation; in Terminal mode it still opens in place or the panel auto-collapses. Why: P1 existed to avoid resizing the PTY; a native centre removes that constraint.

D-54 point 3 (stopped session shows its last terminal screen): superseded by the Chat view as the default for sessions with no process; the static snapshot (~4 MiB in memory) is dropped after one release unless the user misses it. Why: reads better, is searchable, and reduces memory for idle records.
D-53 header fixed places: two new fixed slots (Chat|Terminal segment, panel toggle); state pill may become a popover trigger ('why this status', I-12). Header remains one control group.

DESIGN two-row card (section 1 item 4): a conditional third line only on attention-state cards ('Bash: git push ...', 'asking: ...'), memory-only, shown only while the matching state holds; tooltip-first if a preview shows it is too heavy. Context figure and ticket chip join the second row only when relevant.

Terminal-never-input rule implicit in today's app: the app may now write text into a session, but only through one primitive (SessionInputSender): hook-gated, draft-only by default, 'delivered' only after UserPromptSubmit, 'outcome unknown' when unproven, never retried, refused during approval/dialog states, degrades to draft-only after two unconfirmed submits. No other code path writes prompts.

Return key semantics: in the composer, Return inserts a newline and Cmd+Return sends (decision to confirm); in Terminal mode Return belongs to the terminal as today; no Loom button is the Return default over a live approval (existing rule kept).

Resource rules extended (I-44): the Chat view joins the render-budget test table (1/10/100 rows, shared-property writes); hidden or stopped Chat views hold no descriptor, watcher or timer; reads bounded (cold window ~1.5 MiB, backwards paging); no whole-file parse; live text per block, never per token.
Notification/attention policy unchanged (D-52 approvals only, no sound); finish/failure banners remain an opt-in question, not part of v2 core.

Hook decisions (contract section 9 and the 'helpers return no provider decision' comment) change only if the hook-race spike passes: PermissionRequest/PreToolUse hooks may then hold and return allow/deny with soft-timeout hand-back to the CLI dialog. Needs a DECISIONS entry; otherwise unchanged.

D-38 (never stop for inactivity) stays untouched; idle auto-park (I-19) is not part of this product. D-43/D-46 (user-authorized channel, undated) gets its first slice: user-initiated send between sessions through the composer, with agent-originated sends only after approval-card design.

phases.name: Phase 0: Truth first (cheap fixes plus every spike the rest depends on)
phases.goal: Make the status data the Chat view will show trustworthy, protect the resource budget, and answer the unverified questions before building any UI on them. Run all isolated-profile real-Claude spikes in one batch under the D-04 allowance.
phases.exit_criteria: Written spike results with go/no-go per later phase: (1) main-session JSONL fixtures captured on CLI 2.1.300 (record types, line sizes, resume/clear/rewind/compact semantics, hook-to-file latency) from I-05 E1; (2) send matrix and modal visibility E1/E2 from I-01 with the 20/20 bar or an explicit 'draft-only only' verdict; (3) hook-race E1 from I-15/I-16 decided (hold, hold-when-away, or terminal-only approvals); (4) fork spike E1-E6 from I-09 (card identity, plan mode holds, cache cost, residue, picker pollution); (5) Notification/PermissionRequest/Stop payload shapes recorded as value-free fixtures. Shipped: sticky Failed and pinned regression sequences (I-12), keep-awake switch (I-20), render-budget table and shape fixtures (I-44), input-fidelity checklist run (I-04), /btw menu shortcut as a terminal-mode nicety (I-08). No new views.

phases.name: Phase 1: Conversation lens, read-only (the new front door)
phases.goal: Every session can be read as a native conversation built from the real transcript. Ship first for sessions with no terminal (stopped, stale, after relaunch), then the live toggle. Search and card context ride on the same reader.
phases.exit_criteria: Cold open reads at most ~1.5 MiB; backwards paging prepends with no scroll jump on a 2,000-turn fixture; 50-100 MB synthetic transcript opens without whole-file parse; hidden or stopped view holds no descriptor or watcher; total CPU stays under 40% of a core with Chat visible during a 1 MiB/s terminal run; the row model is source-agnostic (a TranscriptSource protocol) so a later stream-json source can feed it; unknown records render as raw collapsed rows and a drift notice, never a crash; fixtures per CLI version pass. Stopped sessions default to Chat. The user has read real sessions in it for at least a week and says it is better than the snapshot. Content search shows snippets and opens the session at the hit. Context shows as tokens first (percent only where the window is known).

phases.name: Phase 2: Composer, queue and approvals in the conversation
phases.goal: Let the user act from the Chat view without ever claiming a success Loom cannot prove, and make the live default the chat only if the evidence allows it.
phases.exit_criteria: SessionInputSender ships draft-only; 'Send' is enabled only if the E1/E2 bar passes (>=99% verified delivery, 0 unexplained results, 0 stray-Enter-into-dialog cases in the dialog matrix) and the gate proves a clean idle prompt; otherwise it stays draft-only and the product states so. Delivery states are queued/pasted/delivered/outcome unknown, confirmed only by UserPromptSubmit. 'After this turn' queue is memory-only, editable, cancellable, dropped at Quit with a warning. Approval cards show the full command or diff and always offer 'Answer in Terminal'; AskUserQuestion card and plan panel ship only if hook-form and plan-semantics spikes pass; Allow/Deny only if the hook-race spike passed, with hand-back to the CLI dialog on timeout and release when the terminal is answered. Subagent attribution names who asked. Decision gate recorded in DECISIONS: live sessions default to Chat (pass) or stay Terminal-default with Chat one click away (fail). No ticket for I-03's Ctrl+G bridge; the composer is the native one.

phases.name: Phase 3: Right panel, side chat and subagents beside the main thread
phases.goal: Deliver the user's two oldest wishes in one panel: a ChatGPT-style side thread and subagents/subtasks next to the work.
phases.exit_criteria: A side chat is a normal hidden child card whose run is a plan-mode forked real CLI (claude --resume parent --fork-session) rendered by the Phase 1 view with the Phase 2 composer; fork identity is verified with no duplicate card; the parent is untouched; Discard performs verified deletion including the fork's data, and deleting the parent cascades; usage does not double-count the fork; collapsed panel draws and watches nothing; opening or closing the panel causes no PTY resize in Chat mode and at most one coalesced resize on terminal switch; Bring Back only pastes an unsent draft into the main composer; a bounded user-initiated session digest can be referenced into another prompt. A context-size hint shows before the first aside, since every fork and reopen re-reads the context.

phases.name: Phase 4: Start, ticket and review light-loop
phases.goal: Make starting the third parallel task and judging a finished one take seconds, using ticket keys, without building an IDE or a diff engine.
phases.exit_criteria: New-session sheet (project, mode from the documented hook field, effort, first message as launch argument) and JSON presets work with the existing launch path and ticket de-dup; ticket chip and search-by-key work; a bounded, owned git read (plain Process, 5 s timeout, caps) gives '+N -M, K files' on the finished turn footer and header with Copy Patch and Open in Editor, with no per-turn polling and no FSEvents; PR/CI chip only if the user's work repos are on GitHub and the gh contract spike passes (default off); review comments (I-29) stay a go/no-go: built only if the user wants an in-app Changes view after trying Claude's /diff inside Loom, and then only as stored comments staged as an unsent draft.

phases.name: Phase 5: Day rhythm and the first slice of the channel
phases.goal: Triage and lifecycle polish that make Loom the place the day is run from, plus the first user-authorized hand-off between sessions.
phases.exit_criteria: In-work shelf (opt-in or prompt-opened, one-key Done, 15-day falloff) and a launch-time 'Reopen what was running' offer derived from existing records; Quit sheet names working sessions; away-aware viewed/banner policy decided by the presence probe; plan pace on the footer chip with stale/unknown marked; usage by project, source (main, subagent, side chat) and ticket; roll-up row of opened sessions under the parent card with a capped batch-open approval; read-only in-session verbs (sessions, status, wait) on the control socket after the D-46 date is lifted by the user; user-initiated 'Send to session' with verified outcomes reusing the composer primitive. Process-tree/ports popover only if a header-menu-only variant is accepted. No new background timers or watchers.

phases.name: Phase 6: Gated and optional (decide only on evidence from Phases 1-3)
phases.goal: Revisit the heavier items once the lens and composer have real usage, instead of committing to them in advance.
phases.exit_criteria: Opt-in Chat mode (stream-json child per session, PTY default and fallback, mode switch = verified stop plus resume, exactly one process owns a session id, killable if billing posture changes) proceeds only if all hold: the user keeps reaching for the terminal mainly for token streaming or approvals Loom cannot do via hooks; the S-07a/b/c/d capture, round-trip, resource and parity spikes pass; the support-article billing language is re-read and acceptable; and it reuses the Phase 1 row model unchanged. statusLine bridge, per-turn checkpoints, worktree sessions, native /goal awareness and an opt-in 'Asleep' hibernate (a D-38 amendment) are each separate user decisions; none is a precondition for the product.

excluded.id_or_what: I-07 as a v2.0 deliverable (Chat mode, stream-json child)
excluded.why: Right engine for token streaming and authoritative approvals, but an XL build with a headless-billing exposure, parity gaps (skills, MCP, plugins, TUI dialogs, agent teams) and an unanswered replace-vs-convenience question. Kept as Phase 6, gated on evidence. The Phase 1 row model is source-agnostic so this stays cheap to add later.

excluded.id_or_what: I-13 OSC 7501 receiver
excluded.why: Value 2; most of the promised 'reason and message text' is already in hook fields Loom drops (covered by I-14). Needs vendor patch and a wire-capture spike; revisit if hooks prove silent in states that matter.

excluded.id_or_what: I-19 idle auto-park (hibernate)
excluded.why: Reverses D-38, which the user chose after a 60-minute stop surprised them. The Chat view already makes ended sessions cost nothing and be readable, so most of the wish is met without it. Opt-in 'Asleep' left to Phase 6.

excluded.id_or_what: I-22 Claude supervisor lane / Run detached
excluded.why: Later: low value for sessions that live in Loom, an unmeasured side effect (agents --json may start Anthropic's supervisor), and detached runs break Loom's hook channel and D-40. 'Reopen what was running' covers most of the benefit.

excluded.id_or_what: I-27 multiple Claude accounts
excluded.why: No evidence the user has two accounts; the real cost is per-session profile plumbing. Build only on the user's word.

excluded.id_or_what: I-40 scheduled runs with triage inbox
excluded.why: Duplicates skills and /loop for this user, costs plan budget, XL honestly. Parked behind worktrees and usage-by-source.

excluded.id_or_what: I-42 Remote Control toggle
excluded.why: Not in the user's notes, untested against Loom's launch env, and sends the conversation to Anthropic's servers while connected; privacy question for the work projects. Skip unless the user asks.

excluded.id_or_what: I-39 Loom-owned Goal mode
excluded.why: Claude Code ships /goal natively; a Loom loop is redundant. At most a later goal marker and no false Finished between goal turns.

excluded.id_or_what: I-03 as a separate overlay and its Ctrl+G compose bridge
excluded.why: Absorbed: the Phase 2 composer is the native editor. @file completion, persisted drafts and auto-open dropped; the bridge would change EDITOR/VISUAL inside Loom sessions for little gain.

excluded.id_or_what: I-24 statusLine bridge (early)
excluded.why: Takes the statusLine slot and may hide CLI footer hints; Phase 1 gives tokens-first context without it. Gated until the footer-hint spike.

excluded.id_or_what: I-30 per-turn checkpoints, I-32 worktree-backed sessions, I-29 as a default
excluded.why: Large, contested (power-user research says they scale what users cannot absorb; ten product reports say the opposite) and they overlap Claude Desktop. The turn-footer chip from I-28 gives most of the triage value. Worktrees and review comments stay user decisions.

excluded.id_or_what: Daemon or multiplexer that survives Quit, SDK/ACP/Node engine for the main session, TUI scraping, notch/mascot/AppleScript jumping, Loom-owned relay or phone app, embedded browser, undocumented OAuth usage endpoint, auto reviewer agent, kanban/webhook runner, plugin marketplace, per-repo polling
excluded.why: Per the skip list: each breaks process ownership, 'Quit stops all', update resilience, cost transparency or low resource use, and is where competitors report their worst CPU, leak and policy failures.

excluded.id_or_what: Token-by-token streaming, syntax-highlighted side-by-side diff, in-app accept/reject hunks, a Loom emulation of slash menus/pickers
excluded.why: Not achievable honestly from the transcript lens (writes land per block, ~100 ms behind) or they duplicate the IDE and the CLI. The Terminal segment is the answer, by design.

risks: TRANSCRIPT FORMAT: the main-session JSONL is CLI-internal (the SDK typings say so), not a documented interface. A CLI update can change record types, ordering, branches after rewind, resume/clear id changes. Mitigation: tolerant decoder, unknown rows shown raw, fixtures per CLI version, drift notice, Terminal always works. Residual: Chat view can be wrong or empty after an update while status (hooks) is still right.

LIVE FEEL: the lens updates per content block with a ~100 ms flush lag and no token streaming; it will feel less alive than T3 Code or Claude Desktop. Only an opt-in stream-json mode fixes that, and it carries policy exposure. If the user's expectation is a streaming chat, Phase 1-3 will disappoint.

WRITE PATH UNVERIFIED: 'never press Enter into a dialog' is not documented anywhere. Loom's 'Waiting for you' cannot tell an idle prompt from a question dialog; a composer Enter can approve a highlighted option. Mitigation: draft-only default, hook gate, user-keystroke epoch, auto-degrade, 99% bar. If the bar fails, the composer is only 'Place in Prompt' and the user must switch to the terminal to press Enter, which weakens the chat-first claim.

APPROVALS: whether a held PermissionRequest hook races the CLI dialog, whether a terminal answer cancels the hook, and whether AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode are hookable are all unmeasured. If they fail, approvals stay in the terminal and live sessions should default to Terminal; the Chat view then mostly serves reading, queued follow-ups and side chat.

DUAL SURFACE CONFUSION: two places to type (composer and the TUI draft box). A half-typed TUI draft or an open picker can be overwritten or mis-targeted. Mitigation: composer disabled with a reason when the terminal is dirty or in a modal; one writer per run through the existing input queue.

POLICY/BILLING: the PTY path is on the safe side (unmodified CLI, user's own login). Anthropic's metering and SDK/headless policy changed several times in ten months; Chat mode and any headless side chat are exposed. The existing 1 s headless get_usage call is already a small instance of this. Re-read the support article before each release; keep Chat mode killable.

FORKS: a fork re-reads the whole context (cache-cold cost), shares the working tree (plan mode is CLI-enforced but some read-only Bash will prompt), only sees flushed turns, may pollute the resume picker, can double-count usage, and mid-turn forks may carry a dangling tool_use. All unverified until the Phase 0 fork spike.

RESOURCES: markdown/diff rendering of long sessions, backwards paging with variable-height rows and prepend scroll stability are real SwiftUI/AppKit risks; a visible Chat view plus a visible right panel plus live terminal surfaces for many sessions can break the CPU gate. Mitigation: render budget table, bounded reads, hidden = zero, no snapshot memory, reuse of the existing per-file vnode feed instead of new FSEvents streams.
IDENTITY DRIFT: one Loom session can span several conversation ids/files (resume, /clear, fork, rewind branches). The view must follow Loom's adoptConversation logic or it will show a stale thread.

SCOPE CREEP AGAINST ANTHROPIC: Claude Desktop already ships diff, side chat, preview, PR monitor and Routines. Building a Changes pane, PR dashboard or scheduler makes Loom a worse copy. Mitigation: keep to chips, links and triage; leave review comments and worktrees as user decisions.

EVIDENCE QUALITY: much of the research is single-user anecdote and several mechanisms are explicitly unverified. The plan therefore front-loads spikes and gates phases; a failed spike changes the product shape, not just the schedule.

TWO-PHASE DECISION DEBT: this direction needs user decisions recorded in DECISIONS (contract wording, D-34, D-54, hook decision-making, default view for live sessions, naming of the toggle, Return semantics, whether prompt text may be stored). Building before those are recorded would repeat the old pattern of design drift.
directions.effort: XL overall. Rough single-developer, heavily agentic estimates: Phase 0 S-M (about 1.5-2 weeks, mostly spikes); Phase 1 L (4-5 weeks, decoder + markdown rendering + paging + search); Phase 2 L (4-6 weeks, send primitive, queue, approval cards, conditional hook channel); Phase 3 L (4-5 weeks, inspector shell, fork lifecycle, cascade deletion, bring-back); Phase 4 M-L (3-4 weeks); Phase 5 M (3-4 weeks across many small items); Phase 6 XL and optional (6-8+ weeks if Chat mode proceeds). About 4-5 calendar months for Phases 0-5 if each phase's gate passes; Phases 1 and 3 are independently shippable, so the first useful release is the end of Phase 1.
directions.identity: Loom Lens renders the user's real Claude session instead of replacing it. T3 Code, Conductor and Zed-style chat UIs drive the model through an SDK or ACP engine and re-implement the CLI's features, so they lag the CLI (hidden slash commands, pinned or bundled CLI versions) and carry SDK billing exposure; Loom's chat is a lens over the unmodified CLI in a PTY, so every skill, MCP server, plugin and dialog works on day one via one click to Terminal, and it never pins a CLI version. Orca, cmux and Warp-style hosts show terminals and worktrees but write to the PTY without proof (Orca/Superset report 'delivered' blindly); Loom's edge is verified outcomes (delivered only on the UserPromptSubmit hook, Stop and delete verified, 'outcome unknown' stated) and run-scope process ownership with no daemon. Orca and Superset pay for daemons, polling and Electron; Loom stays a light native Swift app where hidden means zero work and idle records cost nothing. Conductor and Claude Desktop centre on one workspace, diff and PR flow (Desktop in Anthropic's environment); Loom centres on triage across many local sessions and two or three projects: status accuracy, attention routing, the subagent tree, ticket-keyed sessions, a side chat that is a real forked card with verified discard, and a user-authorized cross-session channel. It does not try to be an IDE, diff reviewer or scheduler; it hands those to the user's IDE, GitLab/GitHub and Claude itself.

directions.name: Loom v2 "Lean Cockpit": the terminal is the engine, Loom is the instrument panel
directions.thesis: Loom v2 does not become a second agent client. It stays a light native host over the unmodified Claude CLI and gets better at the three things only a host that owns the process can do: (1) tell the truth about each session (status, what it is asking, usage pace), (2) let the user catch up on any session without a live terminal (read-only Chat view of the same session, a one-click 'reopen what was running'), and (3) give the user the side thread they have wanted for months by forking a real session, not by building a chat engine. Every feature either surfaces something the CLI already ships (hook fields Loom already receives, /btw, --fork-session, transcripts, get_usage) or reads a file Loom already knows how to tail. Nothing in v2 holds a new standing authority, adds a runtime, or watches anything while hidden. Three small releases (0.5 Trust the dot, 0.6 Read it without the terminal, 0.7 Ask aside); each ends with a measured CPU/render gate and each later release is gated by evidence from the earlier one. The highest-risk write-path ideas (submit-into-PTY composer, answering approvals from Loom, cross-session send) are deliberately not in v2; they are replaced by draft-only paste, which the user confirms with Return.
directions.day_in_the_life:
08:40. The user opens Loom. Quit stopped everything yesterday, so Active is empty, but above the day headings a quiet row reads 'Ended with Loom - 4  Reopen all  Dismiss' (I-21, derived from the catalog: runs that ended at the last Quit or crash, no new state). They press Reopen all for EDDP-412 and the api session; the other two they ignore. Cards go Working; Cmd+J still jumps to whatever needs them.

09:15. Needs-approval banner (as today) now says 'api - Bash: git push origin EDDP-412' (I-14) instead of just 'needs approval'. They glance, know it is the push they expected, switch with Cmd+J and answer in the real terminal. The pill's three-dot menu has 'Why this status?' when a dot looks wrong; Failed cards no longer turn into 'Waiting for you' 60 s later (I-12). Footer chip: '1.2M today - 5h 62% - ~2h left at this pace' turns orange only when the pace will run out before reset (I-25).

10:30. Mid-task in EDDP-412 they wonder whether the retry should be idempotent. Cmd+; opens 'Ask aside' (R3): a plan-mode fork of the session appears nested under the parent card as 'Aside: retry idempotent?', the detail swaps to its terminal (parent header status stays visible, parent is not resized). They talk with it for six turns. 'Bring back' pastes a short summary into the parent's prompt as an unsent draft; they edit and press Return. They discard the aside; its data is verifiably deleted. Before R3 existed, the same moment was a one-key /btw (I-08).

11:45. They run a long test suite session and close the lid for lunch; with 'Keep the Mac awake while sessions work' (I-20) the run finishes, and the menu bar item shows one blue Finished. The Mac holds only while Working; it let go when the session went to Waiting.

13:30. A teammate asks what was decided about pagination last week. They open the ended session; it opens in the Chat view (I-05 slice A: rendered turns, folded tool calls, nothing running, no process, no live terminal) rather than a frozen screenshot. In R3, sidebar search for 'pagination' also lists 'In conversations' hits with a snippet (I-41, budgeted scan, no index).

15:10. A multi-agent workflow runs. The subagent row that is blocked on a permission prompt shows the attention glyph and its name, so they know which of the five is asking (I-11 tier 1); a finished subagent never sticks on 'running'.

18:00. They Quit. Loom lists the two Working sessions by name in the quit sheet (I-17), Quit stops everything as always, and tomorrow's 'Ended with Loom' row will offer them back. The day used no extra process, no daemon, no new watcher while the window was hidden.
directions.layout:
Information architecture: the shell does not change. Left sidebar (activity/project view, search, footer) + one centre detail panel. No left rail and no right panel in v2 (D-34 holds). The centre panel gains exactly one alternate body: Chat (read-only transcript), selected per session by a 2-state 'Terminal | Chat' segment in the existing header control group. A forked side session is an ordinary child card whose detail replaces the parent's body in place (the D-54 P1 pattern the user already chose), not a split. Overlays: the existing approval/open-request boxes (richer text), one small 'Ask aside' popover, 'Why this status?' as a three-dot menu item. Menu bar item, Dock badge and Dock menu stay the attention surfaces; the Dock menu and quit sheet get names.
