Notes: only attention cards get the extra grey 11 pt line (or tooltip first); all other cards keep exactly two rows. Header context figure ('412k') sits in the project chip tooltip/popover, not on the card. Menu bar: unchanged list; keep-awake shows one disabled line 'Keeping the Mac awake'. Menus: Session > Ask Aside (Cmd+;), Ask a Side Question /btw, Show Chat/Terminal; Dock menu lists Needs-you sessions.
design_pattern_changes: Contract core-experience row, DESIGN section 2.6 and UI-MAP 'No chat UI': 'the terminal is the real CLI; it is never replaced by a custom chat UI' becomes 'the LIVE session is always the real terminal; Loom adds read-only views of the same session'. Why: this is the user's opened door, and a read-only Chat view needs no engine, no composer and no write path. Typing, approvals, slash commands, skills stay in the CLI. Needs a new DECISIONS entry.

D-54 point 3 (a stopped session shows its last terminal screen as a static snapshot): superseded for sessions whose transcript resolves; the Chat view becomes the default body for stopped/stale/after-relaunch sessions and the 4 MiB snapshot is dropped once it works. The snapshot stays as the fallback when no transcript can be resolved. Why: readable, searchable, cheaper in memory, and the first honest chat-centred step.

D-34 (no left rail; right sidebar deferred) is NOT lifted. Side chat uses the D-54 P1 'swap the body in place' pattern with the parent's state mirrored in the header; no resized PTY, no third split item. A right panel is revisited only if, after R3, the user says in-place swapping hurts (measure SIGWINCH reflow first).

DESIGN section 2.4 'two-row card': amended narrowly. Cards stay two rows. Only cards in an attention state (Needs approval, Waiting for you, Failed) may show one extra 11 pt secondary line ('Bash: git push origin EDDP-412', end of the last message, 'API error: rate_limit'), memory-only and gone when the state clears. Ship as tooltip + banner text first (R1) and add the line only after the user has seen it in a preview. No new hue.

DESIGN section 6 header contract (D-53 fixed places): one new fixed slot in the control group for the 'Terminal | Chat' segment, shown only when a transcript resolves. The state pill is NOT made clickable; 'Why this status?' lives in the three-dot menu and in diagnostics, so the pill contract stays as is.

D-52/D-49 notification scope (banners for approvals only, no sound): unchanged in kind; the approval banner body gains tool + command/path text behind one Settings switch 'Show details in banners' (default off for lock-screen privacy until the user chooses). No finish/failure banners in v2.

Status language (DESIGN section 4): Failed becomes sticky until the user's next prompt (a later idle_prompt Notification can no longer downgrade it). Subagent rows get the attention glyph when their own approval is pending. No new status colours or labels; 'Background work' label deliberately not added.

Vocabulary rule ('session' in user text, 'conversation' only in code): the toggle label is a user decision. Recommendation: 'Chat' for the segment (it is what the user asked for), 'session' everywhere else; check-user-wording.sh gets one allowed term.

D-38 (no idle auto-stop) and D-40/D-43/D-46/D-20: all unchanged. The PermissionRequest hook stays decision-free, no statusLine takeover, no new per-tool hooks, no cross-session channel. One small addition to settings: Settings > General 'Keep the Mac awake while sessions work' (default off), consistent with the system-integration switches.

Resource contract (section 10): add a rule that every new per-card, per-header or per-panel datum must join the 1/10/100-card render-budget table (I-44) and that a hidden or stopped Chat view holds zero descriptors/watchers/timers. This is an engineering rule, not a visual one, but it becomes part of the acceptance checklist for each release.

phases.name: 0.5 Trust the dot (S-sized, no new surfaces)
phases.goal: Make what Loom already knows visible and correct, and add the cheap lifecycle wins. Zero new windows, zero new watchers. One 'recording day' in an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with loom-probe's HookRecorder (a handful of short real turns under D-04) answers the open questions of I-12, I-14, I-25 and I-08 at once: StopFailure then idle_prompt, background-task Stop fields, Notification and PermissionRequest payload fields, last_assistant_message shape, what /btw does to hooks and the registry. Build order: I-44 guard table first (so everything after is measured), then I-12, I-14-light (banner text + tooltip, memory-only), I-20, I-25-light (pace + '~' stale marker; no new limit state), I-17-light (quit sheet names Working sessions, Dock menu with Needs-you list; away-aware 'viewed' only if the presence probe S-1 shows it is a one-line change), I-08 (menu item + Cmd chord that types '/btw ' into the live terminal). I-04 is a hands-on checklist run once when the user says the Mac is idle, plus whatever small fix it finds.
phases.exit_criteria: (1) Render-budget test table (1/10/100 cards, shared-property writes) is green and joined by the new per-card datum; if a project rename or branch change evaluates every card, that is fixed before release. (2) Regression fixtures exist and fail without the fix: Failed not downgraded by a later Notification, resume/compact/clear never producing Finished-unviewed, background-task Stop keeps Working, hook payload shape fixtures re-captured on the installed CLI. (3) Approval banner and notification show tool + command/path when the Settings switch is on; text is memory-only, gone after the state clears and after a relaunch. (4) 'pmset -g assertions' shows the idle-sleep assertion appears on Working, releases on Waiting/Finished/Quit/force-quit, with a 6-8 h cap and Low Power Mode pause; display still sleeps. (5) Pace tooltip appears only when the projected run-out precedes reset; a stale limits answer is marked. (6) CPU gate (40% of a core at 1 MiB/s) unchanged with the sidebar visible and with it hidden. (7) The user has used /btw for a week; their verdict is recorded and feeds the R3 go/no-go. (8) I-04 checklist done: image paste, drag-drop paths, Fn-Fn dictation, and a decision on /voice microphone attribution recorded.

phases.name: 0.6 Read it without the terminal
phases.goal: Introduce the read-only Chat view of the SAME session (user's opened door toward a chat-centred UI) and fix the 'morning after' problem, reusing machinery that already ships for subagent transcripts (location rules, tail, feed, model, in-place swap). Order: E1 fixture-capture spike (main-session JSONL record types, line sizes, resume/rewind behaviour, write latency) and E3 resource check on a 50-100 MB synthetic transcript first; then I-05 slice A (sessions with no live terminal: stopped, stale, after relaunch, replaces the ended-screen snapshot); I-21 (derived 'Ended with Loom' offer with Reopen all/Dismiss, one launch lifetime, resume only, no injected text); I-11 tier 1 (name the subagent that asked, deterministic closure so no record stays 'running'; E1 recording decides which closure rules ship); I-23 as a tokens-only context figure for live sessions in the header chip tooltip, riding the existing usage index. Live Terminal|Chat toggle (slice B) ships only after slice A has been used for a couple of weeks.
phases.exit_criteria: (1) Cold open of a 50-100 MB transcript reads at most about 1.5 MiB, never parses the whole file, and a hidden or stopped Chat view holds no descriptor, watcher or timer (openDescriptors-style test). (2) Total Loom CPU with the Chat view visible stays under the 40% gate during a 1 MiB/s terminal run; scroll position is stable when an older page is prepended. (3) Opening any stopped session shows rendered turns, folded tool calls, Edit diffs as folded rows (no diff pane), and 'Resume' still works; the snapshot is removed only if every stopped session in the user's catalog resolves a transcript, otherwise it remains as fallback. (4) The 'Ended with Loom' offer is derived from catalog facts, appears only for runs that ended at Quit/crash newer than the previous launch, and is covered by tests for crash-closed, Quit-closed, user-Stop and later-run cases; Reopen all is capped and staggered. (5) A subagent blocked on approval shows its attention glyph; after Esc/kill/idle a subagent never remains 'running' in the E1 recording scenarios. (6) Context figure shows tokens only (no percent, no amber) unless the window is learned from history; it resets on the documented compaction hook. (7) DECISIONS entry written for the contract amendment (live = real terminal, read-only views allowed) before the toggle ships; the user picks the toggle label and default view per session. (8) Own markdown block renderer is acceptable on a 20-answer fidelity sample, or the user explicitly approves a swift-markdown dependency.

phases.name: 0.7 Ask aside
phases.goal: Deliver the long-standing side-thread wish as a forked REAL session (plan-mode PTY child, nested under the parent, in-place swap, verified discard) once the evidence says it is worth its cost, plus the cheap search that the Chat view enables. Go/no-go: the user's week of /btw (R1) and a one-day isolated-profile fork spike E1-E6 (does --fork-session accept --session-id and a positional prompt, SessionStart source value, mid-turn fork behaviour, cache_read on the fork's first record, residue/deletion coverage, picker pollution). If /btw covers most side questions, R3 shrinks to the shortcut that already exists and the budget goes to the user's next pain point. Build: I-09 (ClaudeRoute.fork, side_of link, nested row, Cmd+; popover with one text field, plan mode by default, Discard through the existing verified deletion, Promote to a normal session, parent deletion cascades), the draft-only subset of I-01 for 'Bring back' (bracketed paste into the parent's prompt only when hooks prove an idle prompt, never an Enter, outcome shown as 'placed in prompt' or 'not placed: reason'), and I-41 stage 1 (on-demand budgeted transcript scan as 'In conversations' in sidebar search, no index, no palette) only if the S1 corpus measurement says the scan fits.
phases.exit_criteria: (1) Spike E1-E6 pass: fork gets a verifiable child id without a duplicate card, plan mode holds (no edits) in the mid-turn case or Ask Aside is refused during Working/Needs approval, the cost hint is honest about re-read tokens. (2) Verified Discard: after Discard, ClaudeDataInventory.plan on the child leaves no residual, the parent's data is untouched, usage dedupe does not double count the parent's message ids. (3) A side session never counts toward Cmd+J, Dock badge or menu bar unless it needs approval (user decision recorded); Quit stops it like any session; no idle timers. (4) Bring back places text only at a proven idle prompt and never presses Enter; refused with a one-line reason in Needs approval and in any dialog. (5) Search: 90-day scan p95 under 3 s warm, budgeted (default recent window), cancelable on keystroke, zero work when the field is empty, and snippets come from text-only decoding. (6) After a week of use the user states whether in-place swapping is enough or a right panel is wanted; if wanted, that becomes a separate, measured D-34 decision, not part of 0.7.

excluded.id_or_what: I-01 submit/Enter path, I-02 prompt queue, I-03 composer overlay, I-06 chat lens WITH composer
excluded.why: The whole family rests on the unproven claim that a stray Enter can never land in a permission or question dialog; Loom's 'Waiting for you' cannot distinguish a prompt from a dialog. The user has not named typing pain as a problem, only reading and catching up. v2 keeps draft-only paste (user presses Return) where a hand-back is needed. Revisit only after the I-01 E1/E2 matrix passes and the user confirms they feel the pain.

excluded.id_or_what: I-07 Chat mode (Loom-owned stream-json child), SDK/ACP/Node
excluded.why: XL, unbounded, billing exposure to headless use, breaks 'real CLI hosted unmodified', and its own spec says to wait for I-05 to prove the user reads Loom's chat. Reconsider after 0.6 only if the Chat view is used daily and typing in it is the missing piece.

excluded.id_or_what: I-10 generic right-hand panel / tab host
excluded.why: The subagent half is already solved by the sidebar tree plus the in-place transcript (D-54); a split resizes the PTY (SIGWINCH reflow) and narrows the TUI. One tenant (side chat) does not justify a new layout item. Side chat uses the in-place swap; right panel is deferred until measured pain.

excluded.why: All fail the fit test: idle cost, process ownership, update resilience, authority, or accurate status. The field's loudest CPU and drift failures come from exactly these.

risks: I-05 is the long pole and is honestly L: main-session JSONL is CLI-internal and undocumented (record types, branches after rewind, compaction, resume spanning ids), markdown rendering and prepend-scrolling are easy to get wrong. Mitigation: E1 fixture capture and E3 resource check before building, per-CLI-version fixtures, unknown record types render as raw/folded, slice A (no live terminal) first, snapshot kept as fallback.

Hook semantics are subtle and some answers are unmeasured (StopFailure then idle_prompt, background_tasks completeness, whether PermissionRequest carries tool_input for AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode, subagent closure on kill). The R1 recording day may shrink I-12/I-14/I-11. Mitigation: all rules have fixtures; unknown values render as 'unknown', never as success.

Fork-based side chat (I-09) has unverified card-identity, cache-cost and mid-turn behaviour; a fork re-reads the whole context (plan-window cost) and shares the working tree (plan mode is guidance plus CLI tool limits). Mitigation: R3 is gated by the /btw week and the E1-E6 spike; context-size hint before the first ask; refuse during Working/Needs approval if the mid-turn test fails.

Contract/design amendments (live terminal wording, snapshot removal, attention line on cards, details in banners) are the user's decisions; building before they are recorded would drift the product. Mitigation: each is a DECISIONS entry before the dependent build, and the card line ships as tooltip first.

Privacy of surfaced text: last message and command text can contain secrets or work-project content on a locked screen or in screenshots. Mitigation: memory-only, bounded, cleared with the state, banner details behind an off-by-default switch, excluded from diagnostics exports.

Keep-awake and 'Reopen all' touch battery and plan budget: staggered resume of several large contexts re-reads caches; keep-awake can pin the Mac. Mitigation: caps, Low Power Mode pause, release on Waiting, stagger and count limit on Reopen all, off by default.

Scope creep from the catalog's gravity: ten high-convergence ideas (composer, diff, worktrees, approvals) will keep looking attractive and Anthropic keeps absorbing breadth (Desktop side chat, diff, routines). Mitigation: the exclusion list with named revisit conditions; compete on triage, accuracy, idle-zero cost and verified outcomes.

CLI drift between releases (Claude ships near-daily; mods and /btw behaviours change). Mitigation: the existing drift detection plus the I-44 shape-fixture recapture on each CLI minor bump; Cmd+; chord and /btw typed text checked against the Turkish Q layout.
The user may not feel the pain assumed by some R2/R3 items (context figure, search). Mitigation: I-23 and I-41 are explicitly conditional and drop out without hurting the thesis.
directions.effort: Overall roughly 9-12 weeks of agent-assisted work, no XL item. 0.5: about 2 weeks (all S, plus one recording day and one idle-Mac checklist; I-14 and I-17 are the largest at S/M). 0.6: about 4-5 weeks (I-05 slice A is the long pole at L; I-21 M, I-11 tier 1 M, I-23 tokens-only S-M; live toggle slice B is an extra 1 week only if used). 0.7: about 3-4 weeks including the fork spike (I-09 L, draft-only paste S, I-41 stage 1 M). Real-Claude spend: about 100-150 short turns in isolated profiles across the three recording/spike days, inside D-04. Each release runs the full suite and the CPU/render gates once, only when the user says the computer is idle.
directions.identity: The competitors are all workspace managers that grow upward into orchestration: Orca, Conductor, T3 Code and cmux centre on worktree-per-task, a diff/review loop and (for Conductor and T3) a bundled or SDK-driven agent; Claude's own Desktop app is the vendor's full client with side chat, diff and routines. Loom v2 is the opposite bet: the lightest native cockpit over the unmodified CLI, competing on trust rather than breadth. What is distinct and kept: (1) verified, honest status and outcomes (hook-driven state with watchdog and drift detection, sticky Failed, 'why this status', verified Stop/Quit/delete; the others write to a PTY or show a dot without proof); (2) process ownership with idle cost near zero (run scopes, Quit stops everything, no daemon, nothing drawn or watched while hidden, a CPU gate in the contract; the others carry resident daemons, pollers or Electron); (3) a read-only Chat view of the same session plus 'reopen what was running', so catching up never needs a live process; (4) a side thread that is a real forked session with plan mode and verified discard, not a second engine or a billing-exposed headless child; (5) honest usage (plan pace, stale marked) and never reading credentials; (6) the user's own authority stays in front: Loom never answers an approval or sends text into another session for them. It deliberately does not try to be an IDE, a worktree manager or an orchestrator."

scores.notes: Best fit with the fit test: every item is triage, truth or read-only, and the P0 evidence week plus per-phase go/draft-only/drop gates are the right discipline. Weaknesses: P3 and P4 (send path, queue, Allow/Deny, inspector, Changes pane with review comments) lean on the unproven I-01 write path and on I-15, and the Changes pane duplicates Claude's /diff and Desktop. Effort (3.5-4.5 months) is dominated by P4 (I-09 L, I-10 L, I-29 L), which should stay gated. Right inspector is the user's long-standing wish but is built last, after a SIGWINCH cost that no spike has measured yet.

Most ambitious and the most distinct identity (a chat lens over the unmodified CLI with verified outcomes). But the front-door bet rests on three unverified things at once: the CLI-internal main-session JSONL (catalog says L and undocumented), the composer write path (I-01 'never Enter into a dialog' is undocumented, I-06 is XL), and the hook race for approvals (I-15). Live feel is capped (about 100 ms lag, no token streaming) so a chat default would disappoint against T3/Desktop. Phases 2-3 (composer, right panel, fork) stack on those. Its good parts (read-only I-05 first, source-agnostic row model, stream-json gated as Phase 6, SessionInputSender rules) are worth keeping, but not 'chat as default for live sessions' now.

Lowest risk and effort (9-12 weeks, no XL item, three small releases each gated by evidence from the previous one). Every item either surfaces fields Loom already receives (I-12, I-14, I-11, I-25, I-20) or reuses shipped machinery (I-05 reuses the subagent tail/feed/model, I-21 is derived, I-09 reuses launch and verified deletion). Productivity is lower because it defers the review loop, the send path and the right panel, and the user's own notes want the right panel and side chat; keeping side chat as an in-place swap is a deliberate tradeoff. Its 'live=real terminal, read-only views allowed' wording and its exclusion list with revisit conditions are the cleanest of the three.

judge.recommended: Recommended v2 = "Lean Cockpit with a Conversation view", delivered as gated releases. Product rule: the live session is always the real Claude Code terminal; Loom adds truth (status, reason, cost, context), read-only views (Conversation view for sessions without a terminal, existing subagent transcript) and a draft-first, never-retried send path only after it is proven. Spine: Lean's three releases (0.5 Trust the dot, 0.6 Read it without the terminal, 0.7 Ask aside) because they are the only plan where every item reuses Loom's shipped machinery and has a measured CPU/render gate. Taken from Cockpit: the P0 evidence batch up front (one isolated-profile recording day decides which later items are go, draft-only or drop), the attention-card reason line (shown only while the state holds, tooltip/banner first), 'Ended with Loom' and In-work, ticket chip and new-session sheet, the '+N -M' chip, the budget table (I-44), and the right inspector as a LATER, evidence-gated item rather than a v2.0 commitment. Taken from Lens: the source-agnostic transcript row model (so a stream-json source can plug in later), the SessionInputSender rules (hook-gated, draft-only default, 'delivered' only after UserPromptSubmit, outcome unknown never retried, refused in approval/dialog states), and 'unknown records render raw, never crash'. Explicitly NOT in v2.0: chat as the default for live sessions, a composer that submits, Allow/Deny from Loom, stream-json Chat mode (I-07), the Changes pane with review comments, worktrees, cross-session send. Rationale: the three directions share one backbone (I-12/I-14/I-05/I-09/I-44) and disagree only on the high-risk write path and the right panel; both depend on spikes that have not been run. Anthropic is absorbing Desktop diff, side chat and agent view, so Loom's defensible edge is cross-project triage, status truth, idle-zero cost and verified outcomes. Side chat gets the wish-list treatment (I-08 now, I-09 as a forked real CLI in plan mode, nested under the parent, verified Discard) first as an in-place swap; a right inspector (D-34) is opened only if the user says in-place swapping hurts after a week and SIGWINCH reflow is measured. If a week of using the Conversation view shows the user reading mostly there and wanting to type there, the composer-led direction (Lens Phase 2, then Phase 6 Chat mode) is reconsidered in a later round with data.

No agent-set note.

user_questions: Contract wording (needed before 0.6): may 'the terminal is never replaced by a custom chat UI' become 'the live session is always the real terminal; Loom adds read-only views'? Options: (a) yes, read-only views only (recommended); (b) yes, and also reserve the right to a composer-led live view later after data; (c) keep the old wording and skip the Conversation view.

Stopped sessions default view (D-54 point 3): Options: (a) Conversation view replaces the ~4 MiB ended-screen snapshot once every stopped session resolves a transcript, snapshot kept as fallback (recommended); (b) Conversation default but keep the snapshot for pending dialogs; (c) keep the snapshot only.

Right panel (D-34): Options: (a) keep deferred; side chat uses the in-place swap, revisit after a week of use with SIGWINCH measured (recommended); (b) lift D-34 now for a collapsed-by-default inspector with the side tab; (c) never.

Side chat scope: Options: (a) use /btw for a week first, build I-09 only if it is not enough (recommended); (b) build the fork now regardless; (c) /btw shortcut only. Also: plan mode by default with promote-to-edit, persistent child with explicit Discard, cascade on parent delete, may Discard skip confirmation.

Writing into sessions (I-01): Options: (a) draft-only 'Place in Prompt', you press Return, permanently or until the send matrix passes (recommended); (b) allow a gated 'Send' only if the matrix passes 20/20 and the dialog matrix shows 0 stray-Enter cases; (c) no write path at all. Do you actually feel typing pain, or is the wish mostly reading and catching up?

Approvals (I-15/I-16): which permission mode do you normally run (auto / acceptEdits / manual)? Options: (a) answer approvals only in the CLI, Loom shows what is asked (recommended); (b) allow Loom to hold the PermissionRequest hook and answer, only if the race spike passes, amending D-20-class and CP2 text.

Card density: Options: (a) a third 11 pt line on attention-state cards only, after a design preview (recommended); (b) tooltip and banner text only; (c) keep exactly two rows. And should banners show tool+command by default (lock-screen privacy) or behind an off-by-default switch?

Opt-in safety valves: keep-awake default off or on-while-working; may 'Ended with Loom' Reopen all be capped at N sessions; is opt-in finish/failure banner wanted at all (D-52 limits banners to approvals)?

Facts only you have: are the EDDP-* repos on GitHub or GitLab; do you use one worktree per ticket or several sessions in one folder; what tracker and key prefixes; do you hand-type /goal; do you run your own statusLine. These decide I-28/I-31/I-32/I-34 and whether to spend M-sized effort on them.

Cross-session channel (D-43/D-46): Options: (a) leave undated until the send primitive is proven, then start with read verbs I-36 (recommended); (b) date it now for the read side only; (c) date user-initiated send first. Messages between the two work projects allowed or not?

Toggle naming and default: label for the Terminal|Chat segment ('Chat', 'Transcript', 'Conversation') versus the vocabulary rule that user text says 'session'; and Cmd+; or a letter chord on the Turkish Q layout.

Spike budget: approve about 100-150 short real-Claude turns in isolated profiles under D-04 across the recording day, the JSONL fixture capture and the fork spike; and say when the Mac is idle for the CPU/render gates and the input-fidelity checklist.
Own markdown renderer vs adding swift-markdown as the first third-party dependency (vendored-only policy); decide after a 20-answer fidelity sample.
spikes_first: One 'recording day' in an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (never the real ~/.claude) with loom-probe HookRecorder, Haiku, low effort: StopFailure then idle_prompt; background shell/cron Stop fields; Notification and PermissionRequest payloads (Bash, Edit, Write, MCP) and whether AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode fire PermissionRequest; Stop.last_assistant_message shape; permission_mode field; subagent closure on Esc/kill and agent_id on permission events; /btw effect on hooks and registry. Decides I-12, I-14, I-11, I-16 scope and the shape fixtures for I-44.

Hook/dialog race (I-15 E1): does a held PermissionRequest hook delay or race the TUI dialog, does a terminal answer cancel it. Decides whether Allow/Deny exists at all or approvals stay in the CLI. Run in the same isolated profile.

Send matrix and modal visibility (I-01 E1/E2): bracketed paste plus separate Enter, delays 50-1000 ms, sizes up to 30 KB, leading / ! @ #, UserPromptSubmit prompt digest, behaviour in permission, AskUserQuestion, plan, trust, picker states, bracketedPasteMode as a signal. Bar: 20/20 and 0 stray-Enter-into-dialog, else draft-only permanently. Needed before 'Bring back' ships.

Main-session JSONL fixture capture (I-05 E1) plus resource check (E3): record types, line-size distribution, resume/clear/rewind/compact id behaviour, hook-to-file latency, a 50-100 MB synthetic transcript with cold open <= ~1.5 MiB, no descriptor/watcher when hidden; then the scroll/prepend prototype (E2) with the Mac idle. Decides the 0.6 go and the turn-builder complexity.

Fork spike (I-09 E1-E6): --resume --fork-session with --session-id and positional prompt, SessionStart source value and duplicate-card risk, mid-turn fork and dangling tool_use, plan mode holding, cache_read on the fork's first record, residue and ClaudeDataInventory coverage, usage dedupe, resume-picker pollution. Gate the 0.7 build on this plus the /btw week.
Context and compaction signals (I-23 E1/E2): model string for native-1M vs [1m] vs DISABLE_1M, whether SessionStart(source=compact) fires on idle compaction; decides tokens-only vs percent.
Presence probe (I-17 S-1): occlusionState and screen-lock/screensaver notifications on this macOS 27 build, to decide whether away-aware viewed is a one-line change.

Render-budget test run (I-44): extend SidebarRenderTests to 1/10/100 cards with project rename, branch change and collapse writes; run once the Mac is idle. Also the idle-Mac input-fidelity checklist (I-04) and the 1-minute user-run corpus size count for I-41 (du/file count of transcripts in the last 14/30 days).

missing_ideas: Hibernation by count or memory pressure, and a manual Sleep, are absent from the plan and the question list (cmux, supacode, orca, conductor, persistence-remote-orchestration). The cmux fact-check says its hibernation is not an idle timer: it only evicts the oldest idle background agents above 12 live terminals. Supacode keeps the 3 most recent live and sweeps on memory pressure. Both avoid the D-38 surprise of a 60-minute auto-stop. The catalog's I-19 is time-based and opt-in only, and the synthesis puts it in 'later' behind a resume-fidelity spike that is not in spikes_first. No user question asks about it, although 'idle sessions cost nothing' is a stated long-standing wish and five sources converge on it. A manual Sleep (a Stop that keeps the tab) needs no D-38 change.

Memory-pressure and recency policy for hidden-but-Working sessions (supacode TerminalsFeature). Loom keeps one TerminalSurface per live run, selected or not (I-13 facts in the catalog). The plan only discusses idle records. Hidden Working sessions still hold renderers and scrollback, and nothing in the plan or in I-44's budget table covers them.

Documented `http` hook handler (attention-surfaces and persistence-remote-orchestration, 'Missed by the report'). A hook that POSTs to Loom's local endpoint would remove the per-event loom-hook helper spawn (about 4 ms CPU each). It would also avoid holding one helper process per pending PermissionRequest, which I-15 needs. The catalog only measures helper latency (I-44) and never proposes this. It fits the CPU and process principles better than the I-44 budget work alone.

Claude Channels `claude/channel/permission` is a documented, build-your-own approval relay (persistence fact-check 'Missed'). It is a research preview that needs the dev flag or an allowlist and costs one MCP process per session. The synthesis files Channels under 'standing skips/gated' and makes Allow/Deny depend on an unverified hook race. The research corrects the 'undocumented' framing, so the I-15 decision should at least name Channels as the documented alternative.

The idle_prompt semantics decision (I-17 decision 1) is missing from the plan and the questions. The cmux fact-check says cmux HEAD maps idle_prompt to a reminder and suppresses needs-input for completed or background-pending sessions. The catalog says this one choice 'matters more for badge trust than any ordering change'. Today, about 60 s after a turn you already viewed, Loom shows an orange 'Waiting for you' that counts in the Dock badge, the menu bar, the project dot and Cmd+J. I-17-light and the 13 user questions omit it. S-2, the idle_prompt reality check, is also not in spikes_first.

Cache-cold hint and prompt-cache countdown (usage-tools, orca CacheTimer, t3code). I-25 splits it out as 'a separate spike', and the spike is not in spikes_first. The plan adds I-21 'Reopen all', which resumes N cold sessions. It also never mentions the silent idle-compaction token spend at 54 min on 200K+ contexts, or the `idleCompaction:false` switch (claude-official fact-check). Users get no cost warning before the first prompt of a resumed session.

A per-turn approvals counter and Enter/Esc approve/deny (codex-app, 'Keyboard approval and per-turn circuit breaker') were dropped without a word. The judge's skip list says 'A per-turn approvals counter (I-15) is the cheap substitute' for the auto-reviewer, but I-15 contains no counter. The Enter-approves part conflicts with DESIGN.md 'Return never approves while a live terminal is shown', so dropping it is defensible but should be stated. The counter is a cheap, no-model-call piece that does not depend on the hook race.

Fork-from-here and rewind points (happy, 'listClaudeRewindPoints' and 'forkAndTruncateSession' with a hard-fail rule). Not in the catalog and not in the skips. It is only a possible future use of the --fork-session work in I-09, but it is the research's cheapest alternative to a checkpoint UI.

`claude agents --json` as a documented cross-check source (claude-official, zed, cursor 'Missed'). It gives state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, status and a waitingFor enum, and lists kind:interactive rows. Loom's status relies on the registry file `sessions/<pid>.json`, which the code comment calls 'a private CLI capability'. The principle says documented interfaces are preferred. I-22 dismisses the idea as a visibility lane and never evaluates it as a drift cross-check. The cheap test (does it work with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1, which Loom sets) is only inside I-22's E1.

Per-type filtering of Stop.background_tasks (superset fact-check: PR #8114 counts only subagent and workflow tasks because shells and monitors can run indefinitely; conductor 'waiting on background task' with a timer). The catalog never proposes filtering by task type, a visible 'waiting on background work' wording, or a timer. See the principle_violations entry on the same point.

The outbound cross-session gap named in the contract (LOOM-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md section 7): `crossSessionInbound: refuse` blocks only incoming messages, so a Loom session can still SendMessage to non-Loom sessions. The catalog has it as I-37 S4, but it is in neither spikes_first nor the plan nor the user questions. Q10 treats the channel purely as a future feature.
shaky_claims: 'Delivered only after UserPromptSubmit' and 'prompt digest/hash match' (I-01, I-02 S1, I-03, the judge's send path). The review-git-loop and warp fact-checks weaken this in four ways. (1) The hook's `prompt` has pastes expanded or wrapped in <pasted_content>, and invisible Unicode is stripped on Enter, so exact hash equality is overstated. (2) Loom does not retain prompt text. (3) UserPromptSubmit also fires for turns Claude starts on its own, so it proves 'some prompt', not 'my prompt'; a nonce or normalisation is needed. (4) Slash commands are swallowed by autocomplete even when sent as short constants. The '50 ms' delay is only Orca's renderer note path; the main path uses 500 ms plus a size term. The catalog sometimes says 'digest compare' without the caveat.

'Draft-only Place in Prompt' is called the zero-risk mode, and 0.7 reports 'placed or not placed with reason'. Nothing in the research gives Loom a way to verify placement. The contract (section 7) says bracketed paste does not prove the target field accepted the text, and chat-ui-paths rejects screen scraping. Until the user presses Return there is no UserPromptSubmit to confirm anything, so 'placed' is only 'bytes accepted by TerminalInputQueue', which is 'sent, unconfirmed'. Whether a paste into an AskUserQuestion or permission dialog is inert depends on whether the TUI keeps bracketed paste mode on there. That is I-01 E2, which is unrun. A paste of numbers or newlines into a dialog is not obviously harmless.

'Loom's defensible edge is cross-project triage.' The power-user and cursor fact-checks say Agent View already has `--cwd` project filtering, grouped states, a Ready-for-review group, PR/CI labels, PR-number search and peek/reply. Cursor adds that Claude's agent view 'overlaps Loom's sidebar and was not discussed'. The edge that holds up is status truth, verified outcomes, idle-zero cost and the subagent tree. The judge's wording is stronger than the evidence.

'The /btw week is the baseline for the I-09 go/no-go.' /btw is a single-answer, no-tools, in-memory answer in the TUI (chat-ui-paths fact-check). SubagentStop also fires for it (claude-official). It cannot measure demand for the user's actual wish: a persistent, multi-turn thread that 'can do most things except spawn subagents'. A week of /btw can show how often side questions happen. It cannot show that a tool-enabled persistent thread is unnecessary.

Hook-only status is presented as the stable base. The herdr fact-check says herdr moved away from hook-driven state for Claude after stale-hook bugs and now strips its hooks. Supacode and Paseo conflate permission_prompt (about 6 s delay, only when the user seems away) with idle_prompt (about 60 s after finishing). Per-session --settings mitigates the herdr failure mode, but the new items (I-12, I-14, I-20) depend more on Stop, background_tasks and Notification semantics. Several of those are unobserved on the installed CLI, and the unrun recording day is the only verification.

I-05's 'Stop-hook-to-JSONL about 100 ms' and the live-view plan. The warp fact-check quotes the hooks docs: the transcript file 'isn't guaranteed to include the final message at Stop time on all versions', which is why last_assistant_message exists. This does not hurt slice A (stopped records) but it does affect slice B and any transcript-based confirmation. The plan should say the live view needs Stop.last_assistant_message to reconcile with the file.

Allow/Deny and the AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode cards (I-15/I-16, listed as 'later, if the race spike passes'). The attention-surfaces fact-check shows that answering these by hook in an interactive session is an inference. The docs frame it for -p and PreToolUse only. 'The CLI does not reap the pending hook when you answer in the terminal' rests on one user's report (Vibe Island #245). CLI 2.1.300 now drops unknown updatedInput keys, so older CodeIsland-style answers fail. The synthesis gates these correctly, but the I-14-light banner already assumes PermissionRequest carries tool_input for AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode, which is unverified. The permission-mode question also stays open: auto mode (2.1.283+) makes approvals rarer than the older statistics suggest.

'The CLI waits and continues by itself at a usage limit (2.1.234+), so drop Continue-at-reset and the Limit-reached state' (I-25). The same item says the hook order and Loom's state during that wait are unobserved. The simplification rests on docs, not on a recorded sequence, and the sequence spike is missing from spikes_first.

'Prompt-cache TTL tier readable from transcripts' and 'idle compaction fires SessionStart(source=compact)' are both unverified (usage-tools, claude-official). The synthesis ships the context figure in 0.6 with 'reset on SessionStart(compact)'. The I-23 E2 spike is listed, but the I-25 TTL spike is not. The statusLine `context_window_size` field is documented, so the 200K-versus-1M uncertainty exists only on the transcript route. The tokens-only fallback is sound, but 'reset on compact' is not yet shown to work for idle compaction.
contradictions: Scope of 0.5. The plan says '[0.5, ship alone, about 2 weeks] I-44 first', then lists I-12, I-14-light, I-20, I-25-light, I-17-light, I-08 and I-04 under '[0.5]' as well. It is unclear whether I-44 ships alone as a mini-release or the whole list is 0.5. The recommended hybrid has no effort estimate or score of its own. It is called 'Lean as spine' (9-12 weeks), but it adds Cockpit and Lens items (the P0 evidence batch, I-14-light, I-25-light, I-20, I-04, I-01 draft path, I-41, the quit sheet) that Lean's estimate did not include.

The spike sequence is not tied to the release sequence. The recording day is said to decide I-12, I-14, I-11 and I-16, yet the 0.5 items I-12 (sticky Failed), I-14-light and I-20 are described as shipping first. Several 0.5 and 0.6 items need spikes that spikes_first omits: I-21 Spike 1 (kill mid-turn then --resume), I-19 resume fidelity, I-25 hook order at the usage limit, I-20's assertion check, I-28 E1 (run /diff in Loom's terminal), I-13's 7501 capture, and I-37 S4. The recording-day agent_id-on-permission-events question was already settled by FB2-6 per the I-11 correction. Only the 'id equals SubagentStart id' part is still open.

I-12 'sticky Failed until the next prompt' (0.5) interacts badly with I-25's own finding. The CLI auto-continues after a usage-limit wait, so there may be no new user prompt. A synthetic continuation (promptIsSynthetic) does not start a user turn in Loom, so the card could stay red while the session is working again. The two items are scoped by different judges and the interaction is not mentioned. The I-25 hook-order spike would settle it but is not scheduled.

I-14 says title precedence is 'already satisfied', but its own experiment 5 admits it does not know whether a mid-session /rename reaches the OSC title Loom reads. The catalog treats it as done and the synthesis never mentions it.

The user's wish is a side chat that 'goes inactive after a while'. I-09 recommends no timers at all (D-38) and I-10 asks the same question, but the final 13 questions drop it. The plan also makes the side chat read-only (plan mode), while the wish says 'can do most things except spawn subagents'. Promote-to-edit exists, but the gap between the wish and the plan is not stated.

The synthesis says the Changes pane is built only 'if Claude's /diff is awkward in Loom's terminal' and keeps the +N -M chip in 'later'. The research's main thesis (power-user-workflows) is that review is the bottleneck. Its tier-2 list includes light review aids: diff-stat chip, open in IDE/GitLab, fresh reviewer. None appears in 0.5-0.7, and the cheap zero-code /diff check that gates the decision (I-28 E1) is not scheduled.

The catalog (I-37) says Loom should not govern the CLI's native messaging because hold/accept cannot be made observable. The persistence fact-check shows why: explicit `hold` only shows a notice and delivers nothing, and the default rule delivers automatically. The conclusion 'broker over the control socket' is consistent. But the plan's text 'cross-session send ... later' ignores that today's un-gated direction is outbound, not inbound. The research's recommended delivery model (cmux: deliver through hooks, not by typing into the prompt) differs from I-37 slice 1's PTY paste. The contract says the decisive delivery case should use documented interfaces only.
principle_violations: Accurate status and predictable behaviour: I-12 pins 'background-task Stop keeps Working' as a regression sequence, and I-20 holds the Mac awake on 'background tasks counted'. Loom's ClaudeHook.swift counts every entry of Stop.background_tasks with no type filter (collectionCount). A background dev-server shell or monitor can run indefinitely, so the card stays Working forever and the idle-sleep assertion is held up to the 6-8 h cap (battery). Superset deliberately counts only subagent and workflow tasks (superset fact-check, PR #8114). The tasks have a type (shell, subagent, monitor, workflow) per the cmux fact-check. The plan should filter by type, or show a distinct 'waiting on background work' wording, before building the assertion on it. I-20's own Cron check does not cover the shell case.

Verified outcomes: 'placed in prompt' (I-01 draft-only, 0.7) and 'Bring back' report a result that no documented signal confirms (see shaky_claims). Without a screen-state check or the later UserPromptSubmit, the honest vocabulary is 'sent, unconfirmed' (the research's own wording for the part of Orca not to copy).

Process ownership and verified deletion in I-09: 'Discard' may skip the confirmation, children are cascade-deleted with the parent, and persistent forks accumulate. Contract section 8 requires a dry run and a verified result for permanent deletion. The fork child also holds a copy of the parent's history, so an unconfirmed Discard can destroy a promoted or edited side session. This is only a user question, not a design rule.

Low resource use: I-41 stage 1 scans up to 512 MiB of transcripts per query (14-day window) after the 120 ms debounce, on a 'budgeted scan, no index' design. It is bounded and user-triggered, so it is not polling, but each new character starts another scan and the first gate is S2, which needs an idle Mac. Snippets can also surface secrets pasted into prompts, and the scan reads transcripts of sessions beyond the catalog. The plan adds it to 0.7 only 'if the corpus measurement says so', which is fine, but the privacy side has no setting yet.

Privacy at the card level: I-14-light puts the last assistant message and the tool+command in tooltips and (after a design preview) a third card line, and only the banner has an off-by-default switch. Screen sharing and a locked screen can still show card text. The privacy question in Q7 covers banners only.

Cross-session actions under the user's authority: the known outbound gap (Loom session to non-Loom session through the native SendMessage) is documented in the contract but nowhere in the plan, spikes or questions. The plan adds 'Reopen all', batch open and a future send path while the existing open gap stays unmitigated.
other: The recording day and most spikes need a logged-in isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (I-11, I-13, I-42). Logging in is a user-only action. It signs the user's real claude.ai account into a throwaway profile and spends plan quota. Q12 asks for turn budgets (D-04) but not for the login or who does it. The spike plan is blocked until the user is asked.

The judge scores are unweighted sums (cockpit 20, conversation 16, lean 21). The recommended plan is a hybrid that was never scored. The user's stated goals are 'main development app' and 'boost productivity'. The three wishes the notes name most (right panel, persistent side chat, usable remaining usage) arrive late or gated. Release 0.5 is almost entirely trust and truth work, and the first productivity-additive item is the read-only Conversation view in 0.6. This may be right, but the choice is not argued against the user's goal.

The plan calls the new view 'Conversation view', while D-37 asked for 'session' and Q11 raises the naming only as a question. The scan of the user-facing nouns (Terminal|Chat, Reopen, Ask aside) is not applied to the plan itself.

The 128 KiB line cap and skip in the subagent transcript parser (I-05 E1) would silently drop big main-session records such as tool_result lines. 'Unknown records render raw, never crash' needs an explicit rule for oversized lines. Otherwise the Conversation view shows an incomplete transcript as complete, which is a false-completeness risk.

Evidence quality: many competitor performance numbers are single-user, nightly-build or Windows-specific (cursor whoami finding, herdr #5289, cmux #14308 historical, orca 11 GB, happy #1902). The synthesis uses them as failure classes, which is right. But the 'lessons' text does not flag that several are unreproduced, and vendor-authored comparison pages (runpane, superset compare, favtray) are interested parties.

Version assumptions: statusline `prompt_cache` needs 2.1.251+, `agentType` in subagentStatusLine 2.1.293+, onFailure 2.1.295+, mods 2.1.287+, OSC 7501 2.1.295+, crossSessionInbound 2.1.224+, `idleCompaction` 2.1.290+. The plan says 'never pin' but includes no capability-detection step for the fields I-14-light and I-23 rely on. The tests should degrade to 'unknown' when a field is missing, and I-44's shape fixtures should record which CLI version introduced each field.

OSC 7501 (I-13) is dropped to 'gated or on request'. Its half-day wire capture could be folded into the recording day at near-zero extra cost, since it is the same isolated profile and the same CLI. Only attached background sessions and tmux send nothing, which does not affect Loom's PTY. Supacode's maintainers plan to add a receiver, so Loom could become the odd one out.

Good points to keep: the deliberate drops (Interrupted state, bundled bad-version JSON, severity re-sort, skills browser, auto reviewer) are all supported by the research. The 'Do not copy' lists match the fact-checks. The budget table, the per-phase go/draft-only/drop gates and the reuse of SubagentTranscript machinery are well grounded in the code (checked: ProviderLaunchProfile sets DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1 and crossSessionInbound:refuse; the hook parser counts all background_tasks).
